recentReviews.comment: Bring hemorrhoid cream for after she's done with you. Be prepared to learn most all chapters on your own, she provides videos that are such a bore, you will  be tested on everything so nothing is optional. Godspeed.

EVERYTHING is Honorlock proctored. Multiple attempts on quizzes (Honorlock setup each time though). Questions on tests and quizzes worded in a way meant to trip you up. Time limit on them isn't the best either. Lectures are for grade- have to answer questions throughout and no skipping ahead or speeding it up. Not truly asynchronous.

The class average could be failing on an exam and she will not give a curve And the exams are super heavy on your grade You will have so much homework and the lectures don't help at all as she lectures like you know the curriculum already making her lectures less of a lecture and more of a review. shes as bad as the 150+ negative reviews say she is

The professor is the only one that teaches intermediate 2 at utsa so you have to take her. she does an inverse classroom which means she doesnt teach and just does revies of her lectures which are just reviews. every week you will have to spend 8+ hours of your life to hw and the exam are worth a massive amount. find anyway to learn but from her
Impossible to follow during the lectures and constantly locks assignments and exams for limited times while being an asynchronous course.

Very nice professor, and very effective in how she teaches. However, by the second week of class there were already 12 assignments due by Sunday and the majority of them are tedious, repetitive, and boring online textbook slop assignments.

there was a set in person class time but she used it like student hours, so you went to class if you needed help. three projects all pretty easy, you do present but its only worth 5 points so you can chose. everything is open from day one and you complete the assignments as early as you want

Overall, a very nice person. Excellent professor to take as your introduction to accounting, as both she and her husband are accountants. I'm not an accounting major, but she made the profession seem very intriguing because she brings accounting professionals to give lectures and gives resources for internships/experience in accounting.

This is my second class with this professor, and she is very effective. There is a significant amount of reading and homework, which is expected for the course. Her lectures are clear and help connect concepts to real world accounting. Her experience and examples make the material easier to understand.

Since this is an online course, you don't get much interaction with the professor outside of emails. The course itself is fairly manageable, but there is a lot of homework, and it can be very time-consuming. Quizzes are proctored, so make sure you have a device that can run the proctoring program. Overall, it's a great course! I really liked it!

Very difficult course considering the professor was unable to teach clearly.  Exam are worth 60% of overall grade on a point-based system, so if you fail one, consider passing the course to get very difficult. Homework takes around 6 hours a week, and the quizzes and tests are monitored online on Proctorio. Few extra credit opportunities.

The teacher is super unorganized and has no idea about the content he is teaching. Has no care for students even with valid circumstances and proof. I had to teach myself the whole course. Attendance isn't mandatory for the class at all as all homework and tests are online. Uses Proctorio for tests and quizzes. The textbook is required.

Worst college professor. Her English isn't very good and she speaks very quietly, even if you sit in the front row. Has issues explaining the material and trips over her words a lot during the lecture. Homework takes 2-4 hours per assignment, and you receive 2-3 each week. On top of that, you get an online quiz every week which is proctored. AVOID

No guidance, 0, Proctored everything which isn't a end all be all but it is when all you do is read. She says you will spend almost 20 hours a week reading/studying. Ridiculous when you are a full time student. if you miss a quiz or get below 50% she will drop you. Worst account department I've seen after looking at other ratings.

She is your run-of-the-mill accounting professor in my opinion. She can be apathetic to her students but that is just how the accounting department is. Good professors in the accounting department are few and far between so if you do take her go ahead. The only problem with her is that she does have a thick accent which can be hard to hear.

READ THE SYLLABUS! You will get dropped if you miss an assignment, failing is ok. This course is based on getting as many points as possible! Accounting itself is hard so do your best to not slack. Im a huge procrastinator so it was hard for me but I barely passed. If i can so can you! You will study, eat, sleep accounting so good luck!
Prof. Jiang is not a good accounting professor, somewhat regularly struggles with her own material and is very slow at teaching. Difficult accent to understand and pretty unwilling to work with you.

Prof. Pendarvis lectures are all over the place and at times will spend the entire lecture on just one question. She also doesn't help much on the homework and often get frustrated with her own students. Also be ready to pay for your homework, as you will be required to do so. If you aren't willing to teach yourself the course, then don't take her

Took this professor because of limited registration options. Lectures led nowhere, made questionable remarks about students in the class, basically switched to online halfway through the semester, made announcements and hw help videos at 3-4am that are difficult to follow, etc. Taking this course with this professor is every man for himself.

Her lectures are all over the place but informative. No real lecture structure in the beggining. If anyone takes her class I urge you to really participate in the lectures and speak with her often. She is very open to questions and help. You need to actively read the source material an go above and beyond for this class.

Class is spent trying to figure out how to use technology and not teaching. Most students stopped coming to class. Exams are extremely difficult. You don't have enough time to ever finish. Most of the class bombed every exam and the prof always puts the blame on the students. She will never take accountability and gets triggered by everything.

Dr. Deborah Pendarvis read off slides and got sidetracked very easily. This professor rarely helped on any homework assignments, and all her quizzes and exams were proctored. Please don't take this professor! So much homework and tests.  Each lecture consisted of reading off slides and her overcomplicating material. (Sucked at working Technology.)

I took her online course with a set time.She is a good professor and does explain the material but a lot of the material I had to learn on my own with the homework. My biggest qualm is that she does not open the quizzes or exams so I never knew what I missed. If you take this class prepare to spend the majority of your week on accounting homework.

As a non business major pursing my masters in business, I was very concerned about taking accounting. Professor Christiana is very knowledgeable about the subject and cares about the students wellbeing. 

A few points:
-tests can be alittle hard BUT STUDY
-attendance is mandatory for participation points
-tons of extra credit opportunities!

This class is obviously not just an easy class to take, but Professor Christiana doesn't want any of her students to fail. She gives many opportunities to improve your grades. There are 4 exams in total. This course is run through McGraw. She also gives reviews before each exam which are really helpful to know what is on the exam.

Wonderful Professor! This class can be hard but she is usually accessible outside of the class and is ALWAYS super willing to help. If you don't understand everything right away the homework helps which you get 2 attempts on and quizzes you get 3 attempts and she is willing to go over both with you. If you're willing to get help you'll be fine.

Multiple attempts for everything except tests. Plenty of practice for you to complete before tests (chapter quizzes and then bootcamp quizzes). Some extra credit (attendance and some other assignments), but the multiple attempts should help you get a perfect score. I understand accounting may be difficult, but this was a great introductory class.

recentReviews.comment: Love this guy. Lectures are entertaining and he teaches the concepts well. Easy A if you have a solid foundation in accounting and you read the book.

Once your into or in the middle of your upper-division accounting courses, you realize how well Prof. Lee teaches and explains accounting concepts compared to the other professors. Going to class was very helpful, but the tests are pretty hard to get an A on. He makes the class fun tho and entertaining with the fact that you're learning accounting.
You will probably spend many 13 hours to do this class. and his exams are proctored and you have to have the lock down browser. and his exams are also only open during a small window .. so good luck

Good professor! Genuinely cares for his students by my reading. Very dry sense of humor, but I enjoyed his lectures. 

As for work, it can be difficult. But it's very manageable as with any other course.

Although intermediate Accounting as a whole is extremely difficult, he tries to do his best to make sure you are prepared. Although he tries to go over as much material as possible in class there's just so much you gotta prepare to learn outside of class and cover a fair amount of material on your own. TLDR: do hw's and reading's and you'll do fine

Dr. Chen is an overall pretty great professor who's quite knowledgeable in accounting and wants to help. I thought it was a straightforward class but she made it even more so enjoyable with short, digestible lectures (online) and accessibility outside of class for questions for exam reviews

Overall good professor, but I will say, the midterm and final exams were pretty hard. Managed to do well on my group project and did all the smart books to boost my grade to barely get an A. Study for exams. Two exams total. 

ACC 3163

She is kind, but personally, did not work as a teacher for me. She was difficult to understand, and the material was taught to be more complicated than it actually was. I went from a B to a D at the end of the semester after she finally imputed my grades which left me no opportunity to try and raise them! She was only option left when I registered.
She is a great professor she is always willing to help and answer questions you have overall had a great experience.

This is a very challenging course with a lot of assignments, but Professor Chen is very caring. She promptly responded to my emails and provided detailed answers to my questions. All of the in-class notes and materials she provided were extremely helpful!

I'm not the best at accounting but professor Lopez made it easy to understand. I liked that we use Excel together to work through the problems in real-time, it makes grasping the concepts a lot easier. Study for the exams, he will still give you formula sheets though.

The course lacked clear organization, and communication was inconsistent. Emails were rarely answered in a timely manner, and much of the instruction appeared to rely on student aides. More structured lectures and improved responsiveness would make the class more effective.

Great professor, this class was very easy to understand. provided materials and in-class examples to study from. Exams are weighted heavy but very easy; 15 True / False and 25 multiple choice. Professor is open to helping students after class or even during class when you miss/don't understand something.
Professor Lopez is pretty funny and takes joy in teaching his lectures. Taking him in-person as an accounting major was very helpful and by attending the lectures you'll get an easy A.
He offers no extra credit or cares for your well being. So if you experience any heath problems during the semester he will say oh well maybe drop the course.

Intermediate Accting II. Lectures are high-level overviews with minimal info. You can pass the class w/o reading book if you study his example solutions and homework explanations (available after the due dates). Lectures are lackluster and insufficient; the real professor is the examples/homeworks. Class Test Ave 1-68%, 2-57%, 3-69%, 4-79%.

Honestly WORST professor I have ever had. I did self taught ACC 1 & 2, I believe this is a step down from that. Two homework assignments are due per week that have nothing to do with the three major exams you have. To pass exam, you have to watch boring pre-recorded lectures. Not helpful when asking for additional help or information. Don't take.

Okay, this class is... tough. Doesn't matter which prof you take, they'll all be hard. I worked to the bone for an A-. Rules are against you: Proctorio, no notes allowed, no toggling btwn questions. 5 lengthy hw's weekly, expect to devote half the week to it. My only saving grace was this: ASK FOR HELP via email & be specific with your questions.

Every one bombed the first test, wouldn't offer extra credit but would replace the grade with what was received on the final (class average was 70% so higher than the 1st test but still not any better). Lectures consisted of him working out the problems he had posted already on blackboard. Didn't post any extra problems to help with understanding

Every week we have to read, a Smartbook activity, 2 homeworks, quizzes, and lecture videos and example videos. I spent at LEAST 1 one hour on this class everyday. The homeworks were different from the quizzes, and the quizzes were different from the tests. I studied all week before tests and the highest grade I got was an 82 including the curve.

Professor Howard is clearly very passionate about tax. In his clear lectures, he outlines what is expected in terms of learning and retention. His examples highlight the important points of each topic. His style of teaching sets students up for successful careers as he teaches them how to find an answer instead of memorizing rates and figures.

If you do not get an A in this class, you did not try. The recipe for success is to skim the chapter, print the PowerPoint slides, and watch the lectures taking notes on your slides. The tests are open book/note. He wants to make sure you understand how to think about taxes and not memorize tax rates, since they frequently change.

Super cool and chill dude. Easy grader, if you do your work you should get an A. Tests are open note and he only tests you on what's on his powerpoints. He gives lots of extra credit opportunities, overall not a stressful class. He does take a while to respond to emails sometimes, but other than that I loved the class and actually learned!

AWESOME professor. i'm really disappointed he's not teaching next semester because i had told basically everyone i know to take him. you'll get to use any notes you want on exams. he keeps things quite surface-level so while tax is really tedious, the class wasn't that bad. he's funny and a really awesome lecturer. seriously such a great professor.

Professor Howard is AmazingEasy A! He explains the material so well and his Power Points condense each chapter, makes tax easy! He allows you to use ANY notes on the exam which includes reviews he creates with exam examples. There are 2 tax returns and 1 tax memo  project but you can work in projects. TAKE HIM to pass tax and enjoy the material

Not sure why of many bad reviews, the status of the class really depends on the students efforts but a lot don't show up or give their full attention in class. Get introduced to Power Bi and Tableau and more excel practice but all isn't difficult. The weekly labs are time-consuming but not hard. Professor is smart, nice, and prefers participation.

This is the worst professor I have ever taken. Lectures are not helpful at all, as what's covered is on a video in McGraw hill. She makes her super easy class a priority last week of class with two confusing projects due in that same week. Look forward to acing this class next semester with a content professor.

Large disconnect between lectures, homework, and exams. The things you're doing on the homework will mean nothing on the exam as they are all concept-based questions. The projects are fine but 1) cannot get away with just a Mac or COB's computer lab (UiPath), 2) very short amount of time to finish, and 3) the rubric is virtually nonexistent.

Overall course material is super easy, but she comes out with a ridiculously confusing set of two projects right at the end of the semester. You can be a straight A student and attend class all semester but it won't matter. Not enough time to study for final exams in intermediate or other difficult, key courses because of this. Stay away.

She is very caring and nice, but her lectures were pretty pointless when you have the textbook and homework already do it for you. The midterm and final were Honorlocked. We only had a week to do the UiPath and final projects which was abysmal. I would find another professor for this class if so.

Professor Philip explains things clearly and gives helpful resources. I liked her teaching style, and going to class helped me understand the material better. You just have to stay on top of the work.

I wish she would let us at least use an index card on exams. Quizzes are all calculation problems and exams are mostly multiple choice. EC assignments are there, but with them being only 1-3 points it barely makes a difference.  Final exam is optional and will replace your lowest exam grade (even if you score lower on the final).

Accounting 1 is a hard class overall. While a lot of time is needed outside of class to study, professor Philip is patient, kind and supportive. It is a lot of hours and work but she does help in class and gives necessary resources to succeed

This professor is great and tries her best to make everything clear for the students. Although attendance isnt mandatory I would strongly suggest you show up and pay attention because the tests are proctored online. There is 2 homework's and a quiz a week but they're timely so you cant procrastinate. If you pay attention in class you will succeed.
Was a great introduction to accounting as someone who had no idea what they were doing. Very understanding and has real world experience with accounting industry.

recentReviews.comment: So much reading and quizzing per week. Quizzes aren't made well and are difficult to understand. Studying for this class every week will take you at least 12 hours a week.

The questions on the quiz are all worded oddly, and some of the questions ask for the most obscure information that wasn't even in the lectures or textbook. You can pass, but getting a high grade won't come easily. An absurd amount of reading; 12 quizzes, 2-3 a week, and ~5-6 hours of reading required for each quiz. You may get away with skimming.
Some questions are worded weird.

HOLY MOLY. Some of the questions are super tricky, and I don't even think some of the topics were covered in the lectures. Honorlocked. 20-40 Questions, 1 minute per question, no backtracking. Again, a lot of these questions on the quiz are WEIRD. Medians were 85-95. Lots and lots of reading.

Dr. Canon makes modules and lessons really easy to navigate. This course has a quiz for each chapter. He gives us a week to do them and we have NO EXAMS. So that is awesome. He gives you a chance to make up your lowest quiz grade at the end of the semester which is nice. Overall great professor.

I took this class this past summer as a 10 week course. He always makes it a point to read the textbook (I only ever looked at the slides posted) so the material can "stick" in the actual lecture. Exams are multiple choice but most of the points come from the short questions at the end of each exam. Come prepared each class and you will do great!

Knowledgable professor but very hard class and tough exams. It wasn't fun at all, but at least he gave extra credit after each test (which makes it worth going to class). Be prepared to have a high level of critical thinking to answer questions. No study guides, you either have to go to the lectures, learn the HW or from the textbook yourself.

Attendance is not mandatory but i highly recommend going because he will give extra credit opportunities after exams which really helps. he also does examples in class to solidify the concepts. Exams are hard but not impossible even for laid back students

He is good as a lecturer but tough as a grader on exams. His exams, especially the open-ended questions, require a high level of concept understanding to answer questions. To make it out alive, you have to know your materials to the T.

Ignore all the negative reviews. The lectures are him talking to us not at us, we are encouraged to interact in class which actually does help understand the material a lot more. The material is hard but the professor makes it so much easier to understand. I would definitely take him again. He doesnt even grade open ended exam questions too harshly

If you need BLaw, take his course! Super easy, exams are open notes relevant to the lectures and textbook. Professor Bohac was very understanding and accommodated students. Great professor, id take him again if I could.

Very easy professor with extensive industry experience and knowledge. The grade consists of 5 online open book, open note tests that are very easy. The lectures are mandatory due to new UTSA policies, but there are no lectures the week of the test. Overall, the class is very easy and his lectures are interesting. Attendance is mandatory though.

Attendance is not mandatory. There are only 4 exams and a final. The final is not mandatory if you are satisfied with the grade you currently have. Pretty easy A. His lectures have nothing to do with what is on the exams. He will provide an 'outline' of what will be on the exam. Just study that and you'll pass.

recentReviews.comment: Its a very straightforward, easy class. You just need to show up when attendance is required and complete the straightfoward assignments online. Hes a professor who genuinely wants all his students to succeed. If you need anything ask him for help he is a very nice man!
Great online class. There are no tests, just quizzes, and some discussions. It's super easy to pass. He lets you work ahead, so this class is easy to finish early. I would definitely take it again.

If there was a 3.5 rating, I would give it to this professor. His tests and quizzes can contain errors which make the overall reliability dubious. Additionally, his questions over topics, especially the movies you watch, are tedious and unnecessary. However, he does seem passionate about what he teaches.

Can be time consuming and is hard to learn and retain subjects of ethics when most of the professor's assignments are based on inconsistent short/long lectures or videos/movies that are outdated or cost money. Textbook can be found for free online and assignments aren't proctored so online resources and video transcripts will be your best friend.
Amazing Professor and lovely response time! Overall amazing and great class!
This guy does not know how to teach. He just says "You should have already learned this." and then wonders why half the class drops after the first week and the rest fail every exam he has.

He's a very good professor. He offers extra credit and curves some assignments, which has helped me a lot. He provides great feedback and is always willing to explain anything when students have questions. You definitely need to show up to class to pass because he covers a lot in each lecture. Overall, I'm very glad I had him as a professor.

This professor mainly relied on you already knowing a lot about economics, even before you took the class. Quizzes had only a few questions so it was pretty easy to fail, and they were 25% of your grade. Pretty forgiving as he dropped the lowest grade for quizzes and exams. DO THE ATTENDANCE QUIZZES, they will save your grade.

Pretty easy class, and this professor was very communicative, but grading is heavily reliant on quizzes. Grades also start at 0% and you have to work your way up to a letter grade, so get ready to ace every assignment for the first week.

His lectures just go over the slides that he posts online, you get proctored for the weekly quizzes that can ONLY be taken the days that they are due, practice tests he gives out do help a lot. Class is going to take up a large amount of your time if you want a A

recentReviews.comment: Straightforward power points and lectures. Attendance not mandatory. Tests do take up a large portion of grades but, they are taken online. Just make sure to do the homework and look over the published slideshows, and you'll be fine.
Very kind and lenient and made class really really easy. Take him if you just need to get a credit over with honestly. 3 hws and 3 exams it isn't hard at all just complete work on time.

He will only give 3 exams and three homework assignments all semester. Going to class is pointless he only reads from slides that he posts anyways. If you do take him prepare to learn for yourself. If you do not take him good luck finding an easier econ course.
Only assignments are 3 exams and 3 review assignments for the exam. He mumbles like no other and even in the front row you can barely understand what he is saying. Going to class is pointless.

It was a low effort class. We had three assignments and three tests that you could take home. The assignments are a little long but managable if you read the slides. Attendance is not mandatory, and most of the information can be found on the slides. The lectures can be a little boring, but it is easy.
There is a lot of McGraw hills, but overall it is easy to take his class, what brought my grade down is not attending to class very often.
Enjoyed this professor, assignments are easy and made lectures interesting

He made the class easy and didn't teach the book much during lectures, but world-related economics which made learning it actually interesting, he is not like most professors and that is what I loved about him.

This class is a mixed bag - the professor tends to go off on tangents, but the assignments are pretty straightforward. Definitely rely on the textbook and study tools like unstuckstudy to supplement the lectures. Attendance is mandatory, so just make sure to show up and engage with the material.

He is the main reason why I made this account in the first place. His lectures don't help at all with the homework or test. At best he might say, "this page is important for your next test." and that's it. The homework and test are not hard but take some time and attendance is mandatory. I urge anyone to NOT take him unless you absolutely have to.

He is a poor professor at best. What he teaches in class is almost always the exact same as what is in the textbook. If you don't understand it from him you won't understand it from the textbook. The class is also graded in such a way that you can get 23/24 questions right every week and your grade still drops. There are 0 chances for extra-credit.

Dr T's classes are well organized and he explains things clearly. He uses Powerpoint slides and involves students in discussions during classes. I especially liked that his assignments are online. You may wanna sit in the front though. Sometimes his mike doesn't reach the back side good.

Myfavorite professor at UTSA. He is approachable, nice and genuinely interested in helping his students. He takes his time during office hours and even offers activities like weekly coffee hours and field trips. His assignments are moderately difficult and the two exams have weight on the grade.

Temel is very knowledgeable and he explains economic concepts clearly. He uses lots of practical examples and it helped me connect the theory to situations in outside world. I also liked the discussions in classes. Not a difficult class, but you gotta go to classes although he doesn't require attendance.

He doesn't allow laptops or phones during the lecture. Requires an online $140 smart book rental. Exams are 65 percent of the grade, "which will be on the contents that are taught in classes only -they won't be in the book or lecture slides in enough detail"
He gives a lot of homework, which is all McGraw Hill pretty much every other day. The class is easy, but it is very time consuming.
Gives a lot of homework. Be ready to do assignments and quizzes almost each day. Class is easy.

Overall this class was not difficult if you are ready to do a lot of work. 4 modules each had around 3 chapters consisting of a reading (very lengthy), homework assignment, and a quiz with a test at the end of each module. The class uses McGraw Hill so test questions usually showed up on the assignments and quizzes so study those questions.

he's just a normal professor. He teaches good, he gives good examples, always asks if there are any questions or problems with the assignments. The thing that was difficult tho was the reading. It's so much reading and the read and comprehend assignment are super long but it's a free 100. There are a bunch of assignments but just make time for it

Took his class during the summer, honestly he wasn't a bad professor, I only gave him a 2 because of the sheer amount of homework he gave. There's also mcgraw hill every other day which is kind of annoying. His lectures weren't mandatory, but I showed up to a few, but stopped because one, it was unhelpful, and two it was very boring.

Felt like he dumbed down in class lessons that didn't compare to hw questions/quizzes, had to learn almost by myself the whole semester. His accent is very thick which made it very difficult to understand him most times. He did curve most of the exams due to the low grades most earned.

Professor Arslan made microeconomic concepts easy to understand and was very accessible outside of class. The homework could be challenging, but it was extremely helpful in preparing for exams. As long as effort is put into the class, you should have as good of an experience as I did.

Professor Arslan is a great professor. He is very accessible outside of class due to limited resources for higher up economics courses. I am very thankful to have learned from him this semester and if I wasn't graduating soon I would take his class again.

This guy's notes/lectures are pure nonsense and for our first test 2/3 of the class failed so he gave us a 13 point "one-time" curve and on the second test one classmate calculated he gave us a 20-25 point curve because he cannot teach at all. I get he's from Turkey but when test grades look like that cmon. I got an A- but I wouldn't take him again

Cool guy for sure but the course absolutely lacked structure. There aren't enough assignments or anything that actually TAUGHT you the course material. The lack of regular/HW assignments plus how the exams are weighed was also annoying. If you don't do well on an exam expect it to tank your grade. No curves, no make-ups, no REAL extra credit...

Best economics professor I've had at UTSA.  Explains concepts clearly and thoroughly and is extremely helpful during office hours. He also cares about his students and their success more than any other professor I've had. He truly motivated us and made sure we didn't get discouraged by setbacks in his class. Kind, encouraging, and caring professor.

Beheshti is great. He explains everything thoroughly and if you still don't understand the material his help is very accessible outside of class time. Econometrics is a hard course, but the professor laid out his expectations for us very clearly. He doesn't make this class easy, but if you put in the work you will pass and/or get a good grade.

He's does not allow phone usage during the lectures, which are mandatory to attend and will add points to your grade. The exams are based on the lectures we do in class. He will call you out if you're distracted and not let you in if you're late.

Professor Beladi is a good instructor who provides clear expectations for the class. The only grades were test grades, but they were easy as long as you attended lectures. He does tend to joke around a lot during lectures and point out certain students.

Excellent professor. He teaches in a way that will help students clearly understand what he is teaching, and will test you in that understanding through his exams. However, there are not many grades in his class, with only 2 tests and a 10-page paper. Students MUST ATTEND CLASS, as they directly help you pass the tests. He is otherwise very funny.

Amazing Econ Professor, he really cares about his students and cares about you learning the material and not just memorizing it. We had two mid term exams and he made the final optional. Attendance is important so make sure to be there and on time. He'll notice if you're not there and only show up for exams.

Hes a very sweet guy, offered extra credit for showing up to lectures. However, you won't pass if you don't show up!! So... in addition to passing the class because you learn from his lectures... you also get extra credit. We had three assignments all year which were all tests so definitely study the textbook

recentReviews.comment: One of my favorite professors! We worked with R for this class and it was my first time using the program, but he made it easy to understand/use on your own. I would definitely take this course if you're looking to get a your Econ electives done!

This class was interesting, the whole topic of mobility is what he specializes in. He is very informed about this topic, and will answer your questions in a clear and concise way. He is understanding about when life happens and will give you an extension if you ask. The class is very code-heavy. Make sure to practice R before taking the class.

Prof Williams basically uses Pearson online learning to do your homeworks with a few assignments done thru blackboard. There is quite a lot of homework, but the assignments are extremely easy and you can grind thru them quickly. I only spent about 1 hour a week doing this class and got a B despite not reading any of the online textbook.

recentReviews.comment: Terri Davis is a kind person, but the class is challenging due to lack of organization. Lectures often go off topic, assignments are inconsistently structured, grading is slow, and emails are not always answered. Exams are tricky, and some course examples are outdated.

If you're looking for a course that will leave you feeling fulfilled or prepared in understanding applications then I suggest you look elsewhere. Course is disjointed, with little to no help from the professor. No slides in class, projects are strictly graded, & most of your time will be spent hearing the professor speak about "corporate America."

Lectures are so off-topic it's hard to justify going. Nothing covered is available outside of class. Code works, outputs the correct thing, and follows all her standards; you're guaranteed nothing. No re-grading, no make-ups-- zero for even one line of code out of order. To pass, you have to meet with her outside of class. BEWARE, take anyone else

She is not the worst professor at UTSA and outside of the tests the class isn't hard, but her tests have questions can be quite difficult and she doesn't really prepare you all that well during class for the tests. Her other assignments/projects aren't really that difficult, but she has unclear guidelines and is very a harsh grader for everything.
Worst professor I have taken at UTSA. Not helpful and makes this class miserable. DO NOT take her.

recentReviews.comment: Professor Teneyuca was great. His class is pretty self explanatory and he reminds you every week what is due. I loved seeing his inspiring messages throughout the semester. All assignments were due sunday and are easy.

one of the best prof i have ever had clear assignments easy and clear labs i took this class in my first semester with no cybersecurity networking or IT knowledge and still managed to get an A leaves feedback on all assignments fair grading reading a quiz and a lab weekly very manageable
Super easy class and the work is due on Sundays, which can be a lot if you wait last minute to do it.

Professor Teneyuca is awesome, simply. He's extremely fast in responding to emails and questions or concerns. He does expect you to go into more depth when it comes to lab assignments, but this just helps you grow and conceptually grasp the material better. Take him if you can!

Fairly easy class. Textbook is provided for free digitally through the UTSA library although you can get by well enough with just the slides he posts. He does expect you to put more effort beyond the written lab instructions. Often this means typing out some of your thought process and adding pictures despite not being stated in the instruction.

He's not bad, but he's not good. The lectures seem outdated, and it's unclear what he expects in the lab findings. There are times I would spend hours to find what im supposed to look for. I didn't have much of a choice since he was the only one for this class, but if there's someone better, take that chance and take them.

This should be a required class at UTSA—great content and lectures. Labs are extensive and require critical thinking and experimentation. Always go to office hours before the labs are due, as he explains how to do them and gives guidance on common struggles. Attendance isn't required, but trust me, you will want to attend every minute of it.

Second attempt with him, first: getting C's on assignments, dropped, took with another and finished A+.  Only option for this class. Same lecture style, not real clear as to what he wants in labs.  You can find the answer, but it isn't what he was looking for so deduction.  Standard answer "join office hours" even if you're not available.

One of the better profs I've taken at UTSA. He is ALWAYS avail which was heaven sent! He will get back to you in a few hours. He grades pretty harshly but he is fair. Yes, he has an accent but it's VERY obvious what he is saying. I've learned a ton in this class. Only gripe is the lectures are outdated and do need refreshing. I enjoyed this class!

Great professor! Lectures are informative. However, there is a significant written language barrier, causing a lot of assignments to become unclear and unnecessarily difficult. Furthermore, (this might be a more personal thing), he uses bad analogies to explain things, which doesn't help comprehension too much.

His instructions are often the most clear I have had from a proffessor, so long as you show up for class and do the work it's smooth sailing. His humor might be geared towards older generations but if you are willing to look past that and talk to him he makes it worth while. If you show up to class early he will show you fighter jet footage

His class is great for preparing for fieldwork and focuses on what's important, cutting out unnecessary info. The labs are clear and helpful. He knows his stuff and is always available during class to answer questions. It's refreshing to have a professor who genuinely cares about our learning. I'd definitely take another class with him!

Prof Pugh is one of the worst professors I have taken at UTSA, he is downright mean to students and refuses to work with you to fix anything. If you show up to class you will score well, DON'T MISS DUE DATES, NO LATE WORK NO ACCEPTIONS, no office hours, by appointment only, constant down talk to his students, "do you even know what a floppy is?!".

I agree with whoever said people complaining are lazy. The class was very well structured and simple to follow. He is 'old school' but not in a bad way, more in a way that you would expect people to be when you enter the workforce. There was 1 lab where the word count was long but he is not a very hard grader. Exams are easy if you attend lectures.

Most people complaining never showed up to class even on exam days which he made very clear were in person. Overall, great professor his labs, assignments, lectures all fantastic. Tests were not difficult and honestly if you just put in an average amount of effort you will get a high grade. I would take him again if I could. (He is a slow grader)

Took this class online in Fall 2022 and I had a hard time grasping the information, so I dropped it. I retook it this semester, in person, and it turned out to be one of my easiest coding classes. There is 3 homework, which are fairly easy to complete. Quizzes &exams are open notes. Attendance is not mandatory but his coding lectures help out a lot

Dr. Z is very knowledgeable about database systems and if you read the book and watch the lectures you will be ok. Just know you will have to write SQL scripts at the end of the class and if you haven't been paying attention to the lectures then you will have a hard time at the end of the class.
Not bad. Weekly lab report, quiz, and coursera module due. She provided the reading material. Course is tied to IS 6113. Would take again

easy course & not a bad prof. Hard to reach her over email but she held weekly office hrs via zoom (after we reminded her, first 4-5wks students were waiting for her to show up). Weekly lab report, quiz, and coursera module due. I have 0 cybersecurity experience & I was able to manage the labs. They weren't too difficult but are time consuming.
Amazing Professor and lovely response time! Overall amazing, informative and great class!
Great and easy professor, Gives a lot of time for Labs and other assignments.

Great professor. Very easy to follow the online course. Usually its pretty typical - Read and study chapter - Take practice quiz - Take real quiz each week, with a few projects thrown in here and there. Each project she assigns has step by step instructions, easy to follow. I would recommend this professor if taking online.

Dietrich seems like a nice professor outside of class, but the learning experience wasn't great. He mainly reads from PowerPoint, lacks engagement, and speaks monotonously, especially challenging for a 6pm class. Low test averages and minimal participation made it less impactful. Would not retake.

You can tell that this professor loves what he teaches. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is highly recommended! His lectures are informative. There were a few instances where it was hard to hear, but he was happy to repeat himself. I recommend reading the text in conjunction with his lectures; it will help you pass the exams.
very monotoned. unclear. speaks very low. reads off slides and gives no additional information. very hard to retain anything if you have a short attention span or not an auditory learner.

Take this professor if you want to learn absolutely nothing. He doesn't care about students and their knowledge. His lectures are boring and go over everything you already learned from the textbook. You can easily pass the exams by studying quizlet flashcards. You can take quizzes at home. No extra credit, no help on labs. He doesn't care.

Knowledgeable lecturer -- interesting if you're into the material. My only criticism is that the weekly quizzes are based on the reading material from the publisher quiz banks and awful and focused on trivial minutiae and jargon rather than real theory and concepts. The labs are much better and not terribly time consuming or difficult
Great professor for my learning style. Very relaxed on grading as long as you complete the work. Not super available outside of class so if you have questions attend his lecture.

This professor lacks a simple sense of urgency. He doesn't input grades for assignments till weeks or months later while still assigning other assignments, so you won't know your errors until it's too late to do anything about it. The lectures are not very intuitive & never refer to the homework or explain what's expected in it.
This is the second week of class and he has already broken down topics that I couldn't grasp in other classes. Even though this is an asynchronous online class, he has lots of helpful lectures

Same story. Was missing for the first 10-13 weeks. He did not grade anything until like late October or early November. It does not look like Huddleston is coming back. He cant be avoided. I will give a big tip and that is join his Slack channel early in the semester and ask questions. He was very available there.
Avoid at all costs. Did not teach material, tests were difficult and so was his grading. Took months before grades/feedback were given and we only covered a fraction of course material.

I would def not take this professor she gives 0 on assignments after flagging you for AI on an assignment you spent hours on she shouldn't be a teacher in my opinion and im surprised they gave her a teaching license to accuse kids of ai rather than grade them properly,

Guys, please do not take this class take another professor she gave me a referral for using AI when I did not use AI and I did the whole assignment myself for four hours. I wasted my time just for her to write me a script talking about how I used AI she is one of the worst professors in my opinion. Do not take this professor for ur own sake

She accused me of using AI when I did not and reported me to the Code of Conduct Center. After my Code of Conduct meeting, it resulted in NO use of AI, and caused her to give me a re-grade… which she still gave me a bad grade. She then gave me ZEROS for the entire rest of the semester for “AI use.” I reported her to the dean.

Really frustrating experience. I'm a 4.0 student and had my work flagged as AI when it wasn't, which led to going through the academic dishonesty process. I was extra careful on the next assignment and followed everything exactly—and it still got flagged. Felt like I couldn't win in this class.
She's an okay professor, but she's incredibly harsh when it comes to allegations of AI usage. She relies on faulty AI detection and ruins people's lives. I didn't cheat or use AI.

Just a stellar professor, made the class enjoyable to go to even though it was a night class, and made concepts easy to understand by connecting them to everyday concepts. Very easy to get along with and even helped me apply for an internship just because I asked for advice. 10/10
Love this class! Easiest summer course I've ever taken and it was honestly fun, professor was really easy to work with and to understand.

Easy class, he does make the quiz questions harder than they need to be but, if you're just looking for credit I would go for it. That said he is very bad with outside communication. Granted, he does respond it just takes him a week or two. I believe this is one of those cases where he is more a full time researcher part time teacher kind of deal.

Professor Valecha has been absolutely amazing. It is apparent that he cares about his students and wants them to be successful. He is extremely intelligent and connects everything to a professional setting.

No structure via Blackboard, nor clear guidance in his syllabus. The lab instructions are terrible, no clarity and his "walkthrough" via recorded lectures aren't helpful. He just reads the lab instructions. He throws in trick questions on a timed quizzes with only one attempt. It's opened notes but he does not make it easy.

I'm not gonna lie, I did not learn in his class. Maybe that was just me, but everything is online... like everything. His lectures are tedious and he's not very inspirational. If you want an easy A, take this guy, but I guarantee you won't learn much. And in this field, you need to know what you're doing to get a job. So, do with that what you will

One quiz (2 attempts) and a discussion post or Case Study due weekly. 5 labs and 3 exams. Lab reports are automatically generated through JBL which is a time saver. Prof. Jennings does not interact with the class often but was understanding and extended a due date when JBL went down. Would recommend for a solid, not very difficult online course.

I loved Professor Jennings. He is very knowledgeable about his stuff and laid back. Plenty of grades to cushion you throughout the semester. If you don't know too much about networking, then it might be a struggle for you, but he explains things very well. 10/10 recommend to anyone for an easy grade.

I don't come from a tech background so this class was pretty hard for me. The professor was great and gave useful and effective feedback. There were lots of labs but I learned a lot. Lectures were provided as well for this online class so that helped break down confusing topics. I would take him again if I could.

He's a good professor, if you have questions he will answer them. Make sure to watch the lecture videos, those will help break down important and confusing concepts. They're short and easy to follow. The labs were tough, but he gives great feedback. I would definitely take him again if I could.

This guy gives no clear feedback on labs and is just another lazy professor who does the bare minimum for his students. We had an open note midterm and the final USED to say it was open note and then he changed it last minute to being NO notes. The tests are proctored and are very hard because there are way 2 many things to retain from the material

Here is the thing... If this Professor is the only one available for Intrusion Detection.. Wait for another semester for a different professor. His grading is ridiculous to the highest level. He will say things like "I barely saw 4 pages" in a 4-6 page requirement lab. However, in my case I literally had 9. Its like he doesn't even read them.

Most of this guy's lecture slides are 20 years old and not updated since, a lot of their content is irrelevant with todays standards and technology, which he tells us all the time.  He makes you write a 7 page book report on a book about hackers from the 1980s. his lab instructions are extremely vague, and 4 page min report for all. all sing. space

The worst professor I have ever taken. Does not teach at all. Has 4 Labs that are 4 page minimum, 1 book report 7 page minimum, both single spaced. Labs barely have any instructions. His lab instructions have nothing to do with course work. No advice or walk through on how to use software programs.

CONTINUED... you have to basically google and youtube your way through this class and self teach yourself since he doesn't take the time to give out clear instructions or even step by step guidance as to what to do so ... you will also be surprised about your lab grades because he's a tough grader and grades ridiculously so DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!

Professor Menard is a nice guy. There 5 labs due throughout the semester which are easy, 3 exams, and a weekly quiz. Pretty easy class to pass. Lectures could be a little more informative because when it was time for a test, I feel like we didn't go over a lot of material, however he has reviews for them so you can just go back an review the slides

Knock this class out as soonnnnn as possible! Don't leave it all till last minute, average professor but the work is what gets you. It's an easy A, but you won't learn much unless you actually take your own time and read, take notes, and follow along in the... self guided online "class." Good luck!

This is one of those classes YOU teach completely to yourself! I highly suggest knocking all of it out ASAP to concentrate on any other class you may have. Strongly recommend to take this as a summer class.  Also, the lack in direction is severe! Don't lose your mind, breath and read the syllabus.

In this online class, all content opens at the start and closes at the end of the semester. You can retake module quizzes and labs, but not the 3 tests. It's an easy A, but you won't learn much unless you read the material thoroughly.
Had a great experience.
Average course. Consists of online labs (essentially participation graded) and some quizzes/exams. Not a difficult course easy A+.

Writing long reports is a big part of cyber but I did not value the content of these labs. The last lab, which I purposefully did not do, required you to do an 8-hour scan in Wireshark and also describe the history of Wireshark. Because of the labs, I don't think I learned as much as I should've. Also, he only reads off the slides in lectures.

Definitely not bad. Doesn't go too much in depth in lectures, but it is helpful to attend class for hints he gives. Mostly self-taught with labs, but Gives PLENTY of extra credit and even allows for re-submission on labs (w no deduction), and extensions within reason. Lab reports are long, but other profs for this course make them even longer.
there's probably better profs you can take

Professor Wooldridge is a decent guy. His lectures are boring, but not in a particularly offensive manner. However, the amount of writing for this IT course would leave even the most talented of writers feeling like their time was wasted. Long writing segments murder enthusiasm for a subject and the time would be better spent doing anything else.

This class was way more writing-heavy than I expected. It honestly felt more like a writing class at times, with constant write-ups, reports, and formatting requirements that took the focus away from learning actual technical skills. The assignments were clearly structured, which helped, but there was very little flexibility.

This professor has one bright spot, he answers your emails quickly. Other than that he has the labs worth more than the exams meaning if you do bad on one lab it tanks your grade for the rest of the semester. He also expects you to know things in the lab that he doesn't go over at all and it all felt DIY by the 3rd lab.
Great professor, the labs can get a little tough since their are no instruction but I really learned a lot this way.

Just another professor that acts like we have no other classes and our whole life is just this one class, 7 page paper due on a book within the first month on top of the homework, labs, and long lab reports and The exam, It is not hard, just a lot, but why so much right off the bat?

This class is honestly ridiculous weekly discussion board posts about what you do for the internship are fine. But he randomly tacked on a 5 page single space paper about SOCs that has nothing to do with my internship and expects me to link the two. No syllabus, no rubrics, reachable outside of class but doesn't grade until last minute. Just dont
very good, for practical learning..

This course has one paper, four labs, and three exams. You are expected to complete one lab a month and a book report within the first month. Book report is seven pages single-spaced, and lab reports are four pages single. If you paid attention throughout your degree, you shouldn't have a problem. Attend his meeting times if you need assistance.

I took this class last semester, but I did not leave a review. Absolute gem of a professor. He genuinely cares for his students and wants to see us learn. Class was tough, but the class was designed to be that way no matter who you take. It will put you on track to secure a job. This class is great when paired with ICS security.

One of the best professors I have ever had the pleasure of learning from at UTSA Cares deeply about student success and is always reachable The course is quite difficult and attendance is 20% of your grade but in office hours he is incredibly helpful I would highly recommend this professor 4, 4-6 page single space reports, a book report and 3 exams

Professor Munoz is an outstanding instructor—approachable, humble, and highly available for students who want to dive deeper. He covers class expectations thoroughly and is a great resource for building a professional network. If you want to learn about cyber and make key connections, he's the one to take. Being funny is a strength, not a flaw!

Weekly quiz over each chapter, 3 exams, 4 labs, & 1 book report. If you are looking for an easy grade, take him. If you want actually to learn cybersecurity, dont. He gives answers to the lab/quiz/exams. He cracks too many jokes & allows students to talk over him about topics not cybersecurity related making attendance pointless. Easy grade tho.
One of the few professors in the cyber security teaching realm that has up to date information and real world experience.

100% try to get in his class! He gives lots of extra credit, prepares you VERY well for exams, guides you through the labs, and genuinely cares about your development as a young professional. Does learn names and pays attention to who shows up to class and attendance is part of grade. This class is hard! This prof will make all the difference

Spring 2022: Wonderful and caring professor! He truly tries his best to help each student succeed in this course and outside of it. Many opportunities for extra credit! His lectures are very engaging and interesting.  Furthermore, there are 3 exams, 4 labs, and a dozen quizzes, where the exams and quizzes are based off the PowerPoints (open-note).

Weekly 5-question quiz (2 attempts), 3 exams, 7-pg book report, and 4 SimSpace labs. Overall Prof. McCulley is understanding, and the workload is good. The biggest con is the labs because other students can interfere with your work and not all tools work in SimSpace. Limited feedback makes it difficult to know what went wrong or how to improve.

This class was a great introduction to the legal world with a cyber spin.  Great understanding on what it takes to become an attorney or understand law within this profession.  Nothing too difficult, but definitely a lot of fun.

Great class and learned a lot about agile. The grading structure is a little weird, we really only had 2 grades in the gradebook. Part of it was mostly based on participation/attendance even though there's no sign in sheets. There are a couple of group projects but I thought they went good. It was a different a structure but I preferred it!

I took this class Fall 2020, when the universities were closed and the class was taught 100% online. His homework assignments and projects were not specific and I would lose simple points because he was learning to navigate the applications we would use for homework. I would eventually get the grade more or less after I explained that I did it
There is only a midterm and final. He does a few true/false quizzes. Hes a great professor and his a very lenient grader.
Make sure to attend class. While not mandatory, there are several in-class assignments and ample opportunities for extra credit.

Charles Liu is the MAN!! Such a nice guy and really really cares about the students. Decent amount of HW but not too bad. He gives sample questions in class for each chapter-- these questions will be the same questions on the test almost exactly!! Gives random extra credit attendance points as well! Overall great class, highly recommended!!
Consist of 10 Quizzes and 10 homeworks all online and easy. 3 exams as long as you study thew review and sample questions he gives you should do fine. Would take again. Big extra credit project.

I don't know why only one class is available to choose from the course code, this was for IS-4463. Coursework is outdated, from 2019 and parts of it broken. All assignments graded like participation, 0 feedback, another student confirmed that our semester of work was graded in an 8 minute window. You want to learn and grow? This is not the class.

Wish I got to meet the professor in class this semester due to his career background. If you are taking this class online just don't be afraid to send emails, ask questions, and go to his office hours for the labs. It was pretty cool that we got to see the log4j exploit being shown in action.
I really liked this class. There are 5 labs, but they're really neat. Expect weekly quizzes and discussions.

Mr. Sellards is one of the best professors I've had in my time here at UTSA. He takes the time to break down complex subjects into bite sized chunks that are easy to digest and understand. As long as you put effort into the class and ask questions there is no reason to not pass this class. He is easily approachable and will always attempt to help!

Props to Professor Sellards for really caring about his students this semester, he was totally willing to cooperate with students on due dates and other things and the way he taught the class was very polished and the exercises very interesting. At one point he pointed out the goal was to learn and understand, not meet a due date. Lots of respect.

About a quiz and discussion post due each week. Plenty of time to finish 4 SEEDLabs and provides necessary information to complete them through helpful slides. Allows colloboration on labs. Final is a 5-8 page paper. Textbook is free and fun to read. Always responded to my emails. Some lab instructions were not always clear, but overall fun class.

IS 4473.courseName: Cyber Security Policy, Compliance, and Risk Assessment

Fall 2026.title: Cyber Security Policy, Compliance, and Risk Assessment

recentReviews.comment: 100 percent recommend!

This is my second class with Thomas Ervin and he's amazing!! Genuinely cares for his students and works hard to make sure they understand the material and pass. If you can take one of his classes, definitely do it, it is because of Thomas Ervin that I have finally found what it is in Cyber Security that I love, digital forensics.

I took this as an elective, and I love this guy because the energy he brings into his online lectures is wonderful and engaging. Especially with the assignments, I love the situations he comes up with, it almost feels like Im an actual digital forensics investigator. He's very caring, so I 100% recommend him if you get the opportunity to!

Amazing professor, definitely cares about the material and the students! Always available to help. The assignments are very interesting and easy to pick up even if you don't watch the lecture videos every week.

This professor is truly one of the best professors i've taken at UTSA. He is helpful, knowledgeable and works with you anytime. I would recommend this professor to any student. Truly a privilege to have taken this class.

Chelsea Hicks is very knowledgeable in digital forensics. However, she is a tough grader, and her lab rubrics do not clearly explain the format she requires or mention required items, and she takes points off for this. The labs themselves are very easy, but I would add in everything you see, even if it doesn't seem important or relevant.

Dr Hicks is a very good professor. While not a huge stickler for small errors, there is always feedback provided. Dr Hicks is always willing to help and is very humble in her approach. While the class is online, she is ALWAYS available and will get back to you in a short time. She makes it easy to do an online class and you will feel supported.
Very accessible and very helpful professor. W prof. Class is a little difficult if you don't pay attention, but overall I really don't have any complaints.

I would not recommend taking her online. The lectures average under an hour however they are extremely boring and she pretty much just reads off the slides without actually explaining what things mean. It is a fairly easy class and definitely passable but you'll have to do most of the work teaching yourself with different more engaging resources.

Previous ratings were promising, however in the new world of COVID this course is not fit for online. Lectures are ok, too much reading, too many articles per module. Labs and exercises seem all over the place, often felt lost. Instructions were not always clear. Quizzes were not too tough. Save yourself, take in person class if possible.

Stauffer is passionate about digital forensics. Class consists of lectures and guides on the labs. Inside the class, he's a great professor. However, his out of class behavior was poor. In office hours, he'd swear under his breath and slam devices down. Uncomfortable environment all together, made it seem like a burden to be there needing help.

A very valuable class for any students interested in Digital Forensics and Incident Response. Lectures and Assignments were always engaging and informative. Assignments are modeled based on the work a Professional Forensic Analyst would be performing in the CS industry. If you put in the time and effort the course requires, you will be rewarded.

Really great professor. Cares about his class and gives detailed lectures on what we are learning for the week. 100% of this course was hands-on learning (we basically had a lab a week) but he goes over them with you and what is expected. Class isn't "mandatory" but GO TO CLASS, YOU WILL MISS OUT ON INSTRUCTIONS FOR YOUR LABS.

Great, no-nonsense professor. Very clear about requirements and expectations. Lectures are engaging and effective. Classwork is challenging but rewarding. Plenty of materials are provided to supplement your learning. He has real-world experience, which he incorporates into the class. I recommend him to anyone seriously interested in DFIR.

There is a lab due every weekend. There is no lecture videos, just slides and requires you to get 4 textbooks and recommends 5 more.Get ready to teach yourself! The labs are not long, but with the little of effort he actually puts into the class is insane.The way he formats the class on BB also makes it hard to find anything. Take another elective.

THE worst professor I've ever taken.  The book was archaic, the tests were uninformative, the labs were not even graded, I mean, why even pay for this class?  YouTube videos are what you get. The cost/benefit is severely on the negative factor, where I HIGHLY suggest you look to take this class somewhere else! Such a shame! Don't expect to learn!

A great professor, of course the material was hard (its about reverse engineering malware that includes assembly and C so its gonna be tough) but he structures it in a way that makes it easier to learn and apply it. If you keep up with the readings, quizzes and labs will be easy, he's very chill so he'll always help you if you message him.
This professor makes learning easy! Thank you!

10/5. Lectures are recorded specifically for us this semester and youtube videos are complimentary to lecture. Feedback on EVERYTHING. "Disorganized" - course work is given and expected due in ~4 days, can be done in 5-8 hours. Semester project is great. This course IS difficult, you DO have to work, but Prof. Mireless warns you at the start.

This class exceeded my expectations. JM is accessible and provides clear videos. Labs are straightforward, and taking notes is essential for assignments. The project lets you explore your interests. If you want to learn cybersecurity, this class is for you. He's dedicated and expects you to put in effort. I learned a lot because of him!

seems like an okay dude but most of his labs are just taking other people's youtube videos and just making a short lab on it. while i do thank him for pointing us in the direction of youtube videos that cover great topics, i dont believe that a professor should be doing just that. some of his lab work are also outdated

Professor is a nice guy who is accessible, the course however is a disorganized mess. Try harder is the main philosophy in this class which actually seems to mean I wont actually teach you how to do things so you better scan through the dozen Wikipedia articles/man pages I provide or you are going to have a bad time. Don't trust the reviews!

CS 4493.courseName: T: Red Team Concepts and Opera

Spring 2024.title: T: Red Team Concepts and Opera

recentReviews.comment: Group projects + HTB labs themselves not bad. VERY unclear about point deductions; will deduct points for silly reasons. For example, took off points because my screenshot extended a bit too far down by an inch. He needs to chill with the grading and leave point deductions for reasonable matters.

Prof. Anderson was decent, I only wish he wasn't so stuck-up on a lot of things. He makes mistakes but blames the students, stating "I'm disappointed" repeatedly. Expect to write a long 1500+ word essay at the beginning of the semester, with mini-essays after. Lastly, you'll have a semester-long group project interacting with a small business.

Professor Anderson is the best prof. I've had in CS! He really cares for students & pushes them to take initivite in learning- the cyber world requires attentivness. PAY ATTENTION to announcemens & instructions, put group project on resume- class is a breeze! Students who dont care give him a bad rep, reach out in office hours he is very nice!

Repeatedly blamed students for his own mistakes (EX: incorrectly set up exam questions, not posting submission instructions on the actual submission page). The information he teaches is very good and informative but he is absolutely grating. 
Be prepared for a semester long group project, and the scheduling issues that come with that.

I really enjoy his classes, they were fun and interesting. He likes what he is teaching and explain the class material pretty well. If you are hoping to cheat on the assignments or test, then yes he is not the professor for you. However if u want to learn and the lectures to be interesting and not heavy at all Professor Anderson is great on that.
