This is an online class, so I can't say too much about Dr. Marlow, but the class wasn't bad. I prefer in person classes, but she had a very good and clear structure for the class. Quizzes, homework, and tests are open note, so just pay attention and you'll do fine. She uses McGraw Hill for most work.
Very straightforward class. No complaints as long as you take good notes you'll be fine.

Professor Albanian was honestly one of the best professors I've had since attending UTSA. She responds to emails in a timely manner and she is caring. We had 14 quizzes for this class only, 1 per week, so if you read the chapters you'll be fine.

Prof. Albarian does not engage whasoever. She rarely puts updates on Blackboard/sends emails so you feel like you missed something. She records lectures that literally repeat what you just read in the textbook, which is annoyingly redundant. Also, she took points off because I submitted wrong but didn't give feedback as to why until mid semester.

Professor Albarian expects you to read the chapter, but doesn't take attendance, so in a class of 80 only 10 people show up. All quizzes and the midterm are online and open notes with multiple attempts, which is nice. However, if the semester goes as planned, the final is closed book/notes and in class. So you are not adequately prepared for it.
This Professor is a great teacher . Not only does she teach well she has a lot of experience. She explains the material thoroughly so dont be afraid to ask questions. Gives points for participants

ALL GROUP WORK! If you feel comfortable relying upon other students in your class, then this is the class for you. Heavily weighted on everyone doing their part. He offered quizzes, which were 5 minutes long and difficult to finish in time. SAME FOR MIDTERM! 60 minutes for 60 questions, most students ended up randomly picking answers due to time.

He was such a different prof than any other that I've had. The way the class is set up is very ambiguous and he doesn't do a good job of explaining anything. He sends you into breakout rooms to discuss a case study but its hard to figure out what we really need to talk about. Toward end of sem, we realized it's just about participating. Easy enough
Not prepared, teaches the same things in multiple classes. Boring.

This class was one of the best classes I've taken at UTSA. This professor was so enthusiastic and extremely knowledgable, and taught from his experiences which was really cool. As an international business major, it was fairly easy and super interesting. The cases to read were about 15 pages long, you must read to earn participation credit.
Favorite professor at utsa. Just show up to class and participate in lectures.
no homework or textbook. He just does lectures and posts them on canvas. His lectures are really interesting but sometimes he lacks nuance. Overall, his class is super easy and I enjoy being there.

He is very clear in the guidelines and a very fair grader. He covers a lot of information and provides a study guide that students can use during the exams. However he made some disparaging and insensitive remarks when describing other cultures or countries. As an educator, he needs to do better to ensure he does not perpetuate stereotypes.

Professor Walsh is the man when it comes to international management. His lectures are up to date with the different countries and has personal experience in each and every one of them. 3 exams, 1 case study paper and presentation (short and easy) and attendance makes up your entire grade. Know the study guides he gives out and youll ace the exams

Professor Walsh is the best. He knows a lot about almost every country. Attend class even if you don't want to, he cares so much. Tests are based of the study guide and the research paper is easy if you follow his outline. I wish I could take him again, I learned so much from him!

Great Professor, I highly suggest taking this course! The class consists of 2 exams(20%), 1 Case study Paper(20%), attendance(5%) and final(35%). Each day of class, he presents a different country, talking about its history, geography, business behavior, and his own experience. His presentations are constantly updated, and he is extremely knowledge
I 100% recommend her class. If you do the work you'll get a good grade!! You just have to keep up with assignments and she does allow late work. She also is very sweet and engages with everyone.

Heather was a good professor. Work was sometimes tedious but as to be expected for a class not in my major. Would take again. Beware of tons of group work. If forced participation isn't your thing, maybe choose another professor.

Took class last fall. Prof Staples burdens you with many assigns. Each week you read 2 texts & then 2 discussion posts, 2 different quizzes, plus work in teams. 2 exams. Have to watch videos of her reading the text you just read. Never says why your answer was wrong & won't correct when she makes an error! Slow email reply and to grade anything.

She was very nice and made class interesting. There were quite a few group projects, and you want to make sure you read directions carefully because she will take off points for the little things done incorrectly. I learned a lot and am taking her again for another class.

Professor Staples is a tough grader for no reason. She doesn't explain exactly what she wants on the assignments and grades you like she does. While she is nice, she is not the best professor and needs to be more concise in what she expects from students when it comes to assignments. This class is definitely a GPA crusher, be warned.
I would say check your assignments and the comments she leaves. She contradicts a lot. She also misses things that affect assignments.
I did like the class, but she contradicts herself a lot. She does not like you doing your own approach even if the outcome is the same. I found myself getting tense when she would come around

Took this class in the Fall and was one of my favorite classes. She has really great lecture and is very understanding. There is a group project in this class so be careful on who you pick. It was a big problem for me but if you talk to her she will be understanding. One of my favorite classes I've taken at UTSA.

This professor is very insightful and provides great information about entrepreneurship. However, she has a tough grading policy for no reason. There is a group project for this class. She does allow you to choose, so make sure it is with reliable people. Not the best but not the worst.

If you are serious about learning business, Dr. Chawla will get you there. She teaches the undergraduate class Innovations and Entrepreneurship. This class was very insightful. It is in person and you are required to participate heavily. I have learned a great deal of life long information for this course that will help me in the long run.

I absolutely loved the format of this class. He would lecture for the first half, and then have us do an activity to understand the material rather than just reading slides. He has reflection posts at the end of the week so write some notes that stood out to you. At the end there was a group project to create your own activity. Posts the slides.

Prof. Cerecedo-Lopez was great. He has a strategic course design that is built to help you learn the concepts through real-life examples. He is super understanding, relatable, and eager to help at any moment. The assignments are just mainly writing assignments. A lot of fun interactive group activities, take his class!!!!

He is amazing professor, you can tell how much he loves teaching and helping other student to success. Used lot of real life examples to make you understand the concept. Fast respond with email, give you enough time to do assignment. Lot of extra credits opportunites
Great professor and always in a good mood.
Dr Xu was a great professor. Attendance is mandatory, so be sure to go to class, but other than that her class is easy enough

Dr. Xu is a phenomenal professor. She is caring, clearly explains concepts, and gives ample time for her end-of-semester project. I thoroughly enjoyed her course. The only thing about her class I did not enjoy were the exams, as the questions (usually 50 of them) are too long to even read given an hour timeslot. Therefore, you resort to rushing.
Most pointless class, dos not need to be this hard. The professor makes this class very hard with the assignments she gives. Nothing new to learn.
Stay away from this professor, if you need a good grade in this class.

Does not make sense, when speaking, very difficult to understand even a single word. The tests are too hard, so no point in studying if you're not going to learn or gain any knowledge out of it. This class is not meant to be difficult as it is one of the most pointless classes that is required, but the professor makes it harder than it actually is

Professor Xu is an awesome professor. 3 exams, 3 quizzes, 2 homework assignments, and two group projects, all of which are very easy if you simply pay attention in class and study the PPT slides. He offers easy extra credit and genuinely wants all his students to learn and succeed. One of UTSA's finest, honestly. Easy, fun capstone course.
She is great. No need for materials, just need $20 for one simulation and $12 for another

Great and easy class! Just participate and youll be ok. Chapter quiz once a week. Midterm, final, and Final presentation with a group. Participation matters and she cares enough to learn your name. Super easy to email and talk to.
Wayyy too passionate about her capstone management class.
Does way too much. Wants you to fully participate in class to fully get attendance points. Not just answer a few questions but interact with the whole class and constantly ask questions.

Look, this class is horrid. The grade criteria is against you. UTSA should either revamp this class or get rid of it. All I learned was how much a horrible class can ruin your 4 years in one semester. If you didn't have to take this class, DON'T. Unfortunately, I have to and I hate it. I thought I had a bad class b4, this one tops it! Awful!!!!!

Tough class, but Unstuck study was a lifesaver for exam prep. Lectures are just PowerPoints - you'll need to really engage with the textbook. Exams are proctored and cover a ton of material, so definitely don't slack on the Smartbook readings.

HW and Smartbook per week. All HW is open at the start, so can finish HW early which is great. Mid-term and final were proctored, but reversed policy for the final by some Christmas miracle. Relies heavily on McGraw Hill, but is responsive to email and sends announcements. Curved grades at the end. Tests are hard, so do well on HW to have buffer.

Last class to take as an online B.B.A Cyber Security Major with a minor in Digital Forensics. Worst exam structure ever in life. 2 proctored exams worth 300 points each out of 1000 points total. Ridiculous. Memorize (don't try to learn) ALL of the information - if you want to do well. Absolutely horrific. Good Luck folks, may the force be with you!

He is one of the worst teachers i have ever taken. Made us pay 200 dollars for mcgraw hill, made smartbooks unbearably long and difficult to the point it took me 3 hours to complete. Not only that this dude made our exams proctored and put all the chapters we did into 1 exam, we had to study 6 chapters for our midterm with no review. Plz avoid.

Professor Clark has been by far the best business professor I have ever taken. I took his asynchronous class only needing us to attend class every 4th Fridays. Classes always included case studies which we would collectively as a class talk about and get graded as a whole. Very easy class assignments were reasonable but informative.

This was a fully virtual class and I never interacted with the professor. WEEKLY, He posts 3 discussions, mod. notes quiz over notes, a really long case study you have to read, then test over case study. End of semester you have to do a really long simulation that takes forever. No final though. You do have to pay for the simulation platform.

2 weeks per module. Slides are online for course & you get points just for reading it. Quiz is always more easy points. Uses Packback that you have to pay for but there's no text and you get a grade for it too. Has a case study for each module & does a review before the quiz on it is due. Very nice professor &d cares about his students. No exams!
Great professor. Light on the assignments and gives 2 weeks for each module. A HUGE relief when you are taking multiple classes. Recommend him for sure!
The case studies are really hard but prof is really nice and the class has easy timelines if you stay on top of it. Hate that he makes you buy all this extra stuff tho

Professor was 20+ mins late to the first class, teaches very fast, assumes prior stats knowledge, and is hard to understand. Homework was the most help. The tests aren't tough but unfair. Timed at 90 minutes with multiple lengthy problems that could take 15 minutes. Two lowest homework grades and one test are dropped at the end of the semester.

Would be 20min late to class and taught quickly. It was hard to understand him because of his accent. Homework helped the most in understanding the material. The tests were 90min long with questions that could take 15min each. Strict about due dates and doesn't accept late work, but drops a lot of assignments at the end. FINAL EXAM IS OPTIONAL

Professor Kone is a good teacher. The thing about him though is that he teaches Basic Stats as if we already know everything about stats, writing symbols and saying words without explaining what it is or what it means, jumping straight into difficult problems without going over easier ones. He has an accent to so prepare for that. Great person.
Learn it yourself type of class. You definitely will need other resources for this class if you want to be successful. If you don't do well in stats do not take this class.

I loved taking this class, he was a great professor. He was engaging and he always made sure you understood what he taught before moving on to the next thing. This is not for a class. Today, I took my comp exam for my master's degree, a requirement I need to pass and graduate. However, things were turning wild a bit. Online course with almost no instructor presence. Never spoke to him all term. Zeros posted prematurely, then told to ignore them. Unapproachable.

I only survived because the class is online but if you're going to take it in person, it's a lot more difficult. The good thing is that he gives extra credit, the class is difficult, so prepare to give your 1000%
easiest class i've ever taken fr

Never had issues with a professor until Prof. Karimi. Def on a high horse and does not care for students.

Overall Professor is very nice. He has lots HW each week, and two case projects. Be prepared to work on his class for multiple hours every week. You can get a good grade by doing the assignments on time.

Prof. Karimi is very knowledgeable. I have always had a hard time passing stats classes and this is the first one that I will be earning an A. Although there is A LOT of homework, we have multiple tries and he goes over similar problems in class. The best thing is that there are no tests, so I guess that makes up for having hw every week.

Professor Karimi was an excellent professor who offered 5% extra credit for submitting homework on time, which motivated us to stay on track. His recorded lectures on Canvas were extremely helpful for completing assignments. As long as you watch the videos and complete the work on time, you should do well in the class.
Although he was a difficult grader, he cares for student learning. Just be prepared to do homework and quizzes weekly. He also helps a lot in office hours on assignments.

Terrible professor, wasn't primary professor for my section but for a different section. We used common exams where each professor graded portions of the exams. Crazy stupid points taken off for things like not showing how minutes convert to seconds in a problem. Dude is terrible. Avoid, avoid, avoid.

MBA 5413

Prof. Karimi is very knowledgeable. I have always had a hard time passing stats classes and this is the first one that I will be earning an A. Hard professor and lots of homework. If you stay on top of it and don't just use Chegg to find the answers, then you will do well on exams and the project.

Lectures are terrible. Cares way too much about derivations rather than teaching how to solve problems. Better to learn from textbook and/or lectures from other professors on YouTube. Often will assign homework and take home quiz at same time. Both usually very long. Only saving grace is his exams are usually fair and grades them fair as well.

Take him, especially for online! I took him in the summer and was completely online. Literally got extensions on tests and hw whenever I asked, and my grade was an easy A without even trying! Probably doesn't know they're granting us free credit, but it was a blessing on my GPA, so I am not complaining! You literally have to try to fail this class!

This is the most flexible teacher I've ever had. I was granted extensions on homework and tests every time I asked without question, and I got a higher grade than the grading scheme indicated I would get. The tests are literally the same problems as the homework, and there's a few case studies you have to do as well.

I had to drop this class last semester because it was so hard for me, so I took it as a 5-week class over the summer. By the 2nd week I thought I would have to drop it again because I tanked the first test. I still don't know how I got an A, my grade should be lower according to the grade criteria, but defiantly recommend, you can do it!

The material is statsII, you know it is dry. However, the instructor's approach to teaching is great &  will get you through the class. You will learn how to use M$ Excel well, important to be successful. The tests are just like the homework, so take your time to get through them and you will get an A. *Do the in class exercises and cases.*

Very nice and responds quickly to emails. A group project for graduates (3 papers, presenting 1 of them). He is vague on instructions in the syllabus but will answer questions to clarify. Weekly quizzes with multiple attempts. 2 exams made up of quiz questions. Easy if you study. He lectured maybe once, the rest of the classes were presentations.

IF YOU NEED TO TAKE STATS 2 (Also known as MS 3043/BAN 3043) TAKE HIM. Unlike stats 1 professors this guy tests you in a way that makes sense. Instead of forcing you to memorize equations he teaches you how to do things in Excel, which gives you the answer immediately. He allows you to use Excel, Homework, etc on Exams. He is a great prof 10/10

I took this in the summer, completely online. It's not hard if you spend time studying. Everything is at your own pace, so you could technically finish the whole course pretty fast if you dedicate time. The professor is easy to reach, overall, would take again

He knows the material and delivers thoughtful lectures that truly engage you to learn as a college student and not just self-teach yourself the entire course. By going to the lectures he gives shows you "Cheat-sheets" (Excel) to help you out with homework and exams which are all open-book. He emphasizes the success of business students to not fail.
His class was kinda boring but it was helpful. Attendance was not mandatory but extra credit opportunities were class only towards the end. Homeworks and exams were online.

This class was promoted as the main core class at UTSA that business students fail. If you go to more than half the classes you will be fine. He shows you how to do the problems step-by-step. I would definitely recommend taking him. The late points aren't too harsh either!

Prof. Massaro was very caring. Lots of homework but it is manageable. Tests are exactly like the homework problems. Attendance isn't mandatory but its stats so it's best to not miss class. There are extra credit opportunities. The only thing I'll say is I did have to pay $100 for one semester for the website she uses for homework.

One of the best professors I have had. The class itself can be a little confusing at times, but if she notices that the majority of the class isn't grasping the concept, she will re-explain. The professor was nice, and gave a lot of extra credit. The material might be hard if ur not good at statistics, but otherwise it should be easy.
Terrible! Weighted grade is way lower than the grade calculated in canvas. He does not teach!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU VALUE YOUR SANITY. The homework had every single one of us students with faces of abject horror. This class is hard, like very hard. ChatGPT struggles to help you. You may ask why you need this class; no one knows. The math is hard, and you'll never understand it.

The lecture videos are about 30 years old, so THAT is my biggest gripe. There is a bit of a language barrier but he is always willing to help you out if in need. His Teaching Notes are incredible and helped me fly through his homework assignments.

I can't speak highly enough about this professor. It was refreshing to take notes by hand, using examples step by step rather than on Powerpoint or McGraw Connect. Even though he was a caring professor and did absolutely his best to ensure every student in his class passed. It didn't change the fact that you need to study very hard for his exams because they are not a piece of cake. Lots of problem sets as well but overall he is a well rounded professor.

Good guy, really cares about his students. Offers lots of extensions on the homework, curves the exams to make fair for everyone. He loves to teach, so it makes the class interesting. This class is easy if you attend lectures. While he does not take attendance, you will only pass this class if you attend the lectures. He allows corrections on HW but there is a good amount that you will need to keep up with. He has no clear schedule and takes forever to grade. Overall good professor for a difficult course.

Knowledgable and speaks clearly.  Good feedback, allows HW corrections.  But...he overcomplicates, long winded, and pre-grade takes over from grading.  Coming into the final week, there is still 4 ungraded assignments.  Believes he is doing you a favor by assigning 2 HW 2 weeks before finals and have it due the next week. No schedule of assignments
Best professor I've had at UTSA and probably ever.

He is literally an award-winning professor and teaches the honors section during the fall & spring for a reason. You can't fail on the homework because he can check it before you submit. The lectures were a little slow for me, but that is because he wants everybody to understand and pass.
Excellent, highly experienced instructor! He teaches you everything you need to know and doesn't force you to waste your time and money on arduous textbook readings.

Amazing professor. Made a difficult subject easier and understandable. He cares about his students and is willing to stay with you after every class to help with homework. I recommend him to anyone who has the opportunity to take him.

BEST PROFESSOR AT UTSA!!He genuinely cares about his students, lectures are entertaining and fun! I really enjoyed Dr. Koyuncu's course. It was well-structured and paced perfectly. The only issue was the length of the recorded lectures, as some were from in-person sessions. I took this course in Spring 2024 and found Professor Koyuncu's class to be informative and engaging. Vern is the MAN!!!! Really great lectures. Makes you not want to miss his class, super funny and interesting. Truly cares

Wow really one of the best professors I've ever taken so far. He makes lectures fun and engaging, so even though attendance is not mandatory, you just want to attend. Vern was WONDERFUL. So nice and just a great dude. Made the course interesting. So much extra credit you don't have to take exams. No textbook.

Great professor, teaching, very easy class and understandable. So much extra credit opportunities you can get that you can be exempt from the finals. Optional textbook and all assignments were in discussions and were easy to go through.

I hate math classes but, Vern is a great professor who is extremely lenient in his grading. One of the nicest and easy-to-understand professors. Assignments were discussions, but they were easy (use ur resources). Didn't have to purchase anything for the class and lots of extra credit! Enough to be exempt from exams and hw!! Book can be found online too, if needed. RECOMMEND!
he is an awesome teacher

Professor Campbell has his assignments through Cengage. If you do not pay attention to his videos or heavily study,you may fail. The course work gives you multiple tries which is good, but it will come in handy if you aren't strong in math. As long as you give time in the course you will be okay.

Prof. Campbell obviously knows his stuff, and is pretty good in teaching it, and has good recorded lectures. Great professor. Very clear on the grading in the syllabus, I took the online class and it was literally all assignments on Cengage, very easy A.

Literally was so unreachable, and never graded anything. Finals are over and has yet to even grade my final. Please avoid at your discretion.

He gives out so much reading that you cannot keep up. Lectures are vague, so the only way you actually learn is if you read which you have to do because he has pop quizzes. He also grades you on attendance and won't put in grades. Grades were due two days ago and we still don't know what we received from him. Nice guy but a difficult professor.
2 tests and a final with attendance and group presentation make up your grade. He may curve the grade after each test. Always follow his exam reviews because they are the key to each test

She does not post the modules on time, there were weeks of radio silence. And the instructions are confusing for the projects. then grading was vague and left me frustrated because I was following the rubric.
Was a great teacher super kind and supportive. Easy to turn in makeup work.

Professor Luna is a super sweet lady. She has clear guidelines for the class and it is manageable and the workload is not much. Some of the quizzes are a little tricky but there is a retake for each quiz. Good class and learned some cool new things.

Great professor! All the work is easy and fun! The only thing I disliked was the group work and the Google certificate program that's due every 3 weeks and takes around 3 hrs to complete. There's a couple of written assignments in the program that is graded by other peers. If you don't get graded your whole assignment is a 0. Which is irritating.

Professor Luna is amazing! She's SO sweet and really loves to hear what students want to say. We had 3 big projects and 1 group project but they were all really easy and fun to do. The textbook is free and all the readings are pretty short and interesting as well. She's also extremely lenient with late work. Take her!

recentReviews.comment: Dr Duffey is great. She is caring, has great lectures, and is helps us in class.  HOWEVER!!!... she does not post grades and hasn't this entire semester. We have no feedback and grades to show and we have one week left of classes. She also has a cumulative final exam. Be aware

She would upload random assignments on the same day with no notification, she would randomly change the assignment date without any notification. She wasn't well at communicating to her online class at all! The material and assignments were informative but she didn't communicate with her students.

I lost my grandma during the semester. I wrote her an email informing her I may fall behind due to the amount of stress and grief I was feeling. She asked me to write a paper about my grandma instead. She wrote such beautiful kind words on all of my assignments in the notes and comments. It was so kind, and it helped me to grieve in a healthy way.
she has very vague instructions. She doesn't grade assignments she just marks them as complete so you will never know your grade in this class. Regardless this class is an easy A

You are pretty much writing essays for all your assignments. VERY vague instructions but a very easy grader. You can submit assignments late. She will NEVER reply to your emails and only input grades around midterms and finals. I was very close to getting a perfect grade but I lost 20 points but that was completely my fault
Really good. Everything is easy, and he explains stuff well

He grades weirdly. Even if you follow the criteria, you will never receive the maximum grade, even though it's not design which is something that is based on taste. This is very straightforward stuff. He's very nice and works with you if you need it. His class is pretty interesting as well.
Good teacher, easy class. Do your work, and you'll get a good grade.

Nice professor! Easy class to take, just make sure to do your notes before the deadline, only because it is a bit of paperwork to do, and it would be kind of hard to do it last second, but everything else is very easy. Would take this class again if I could!

Overall, Professor Matiella is a good professor. My only notes are that he assigns graded Cornell notes that take a long time if you wait until the last minute. Also, he grades very slowly for example one of my assignments was graded a month and week after the due date.
If you have another option for a professor take them instead. It doesn't matter who it is.
one way ticket to dropping out. might question your will and your life choices and your major.

RUN! Do not take her unless you want to spent way too much time on assignments just for her to change her mind every 10 minutes. She gives unclear feedback and loses track of what she wants or what she's talking about that leaves everyone confused. My blessings if you have to take her.
She is very tough and strict.

I like to think of this class as a filter for people who want to know if this is really what they want to study. Professor Blizard is well informed in the class content and real life experience. She was late every class 15 minutes but compensated with rich projects and complex assignments. Our class was really advanced compared to other classes.

Moved the class without warning to start 30 minutes earlier, overlapping with one of my other classes. I'm not watching your lectures and spending more time out of class to catch up to fix your mistake dude.

honestly my favorite architecture teacher so far. he's the only teacher that has allowed me to truly explore design and he doesn't give too much work. he's very understanding and funny. he gives good feedback and gave us the freedom to decide what we wanted but also guiding us in the right direction. would 100% take him again.

Professor Ali fostered an engaging and inclusive learning environment. His well-organized lectures connected theory to real world examples, making concepts clear and relevant. He encouraged participation, gave detailed feedback, and challenged us in positive ways. I grew academically because of his teaching.

Professor Alireza is an excellent instructor. He explains material clearly, answers questions thoroughly, and truly cares about his students. His assignments helped reinforce key concepts and made learning easier. I gained a lot from this course and would definitely take another class with him. Highly recommended!

I truly appreciated this course. Prof. Ali was consistently well prepared and provided us with access to the lecture slides outside of class. His presentations were clear and detailed, and I found the assignments both engaging and enjoyable.

Shes alright, shes unclear with all her lectures though. She won't explain a project properly and then gets mad at you for not understanding. She says she's too busy to answer any of her emails so good luck if you need to communicate with her. The projects are fairly simple, but she takes favoritism.
Honestly nice and whole-hearted professor, but take if you want an easy semester just don't expect to actually learn anything.

Dr. Singery is a great professor at UTSA! Instructions may be unclear at times, but she reiterates her instructions to fully understand her assignments. Gives great ideas and help when designing, allowing you to be inspired! Her field trips are great too!
Best professor!! She cares about her students and pushes you to think outside the box. Enjoyed her class so much!!

This professor is nice. In terms of teaching, I'd definitely say she could be more clearer. Plus, she may seem easy-going, but she's that type of teacher that doesn't 'hand out easy grades'. You could do a simple assignment correctly and expect an A, because there's not much to it, but she'll be the type to give you an 89 instead of the 90.

Temple is like a tornado. If he starts talking, you have no choice but to stand there and get sucked in. However, the things you hear while in the tornado are interesting/helpful and oftentimes will contribute to a clearer design. He also gives really good critique, and cares about his students understanding the material more than the grade.

If I've come to understand correctly, you can only take him the first year of architecture before gateway. Take advantage. He inspires you to think more about your designs and works with you through your progress. Definitely recommend.
Really good professor but the only problem that students complain about is that he talks a lot but actually he doesn't. Each word he says worth a lot if you will take him seriously.

As one can tell fro reading all the other comments, he's a chatty teacher, but defiantly enjoyable & solo helpful in setting a foundation to become a good quality designer. Definitely take his craftsmanship critique into account in all your projects b/c he becomes a harder grader towards the end; also time management is key!
you will learn a lot.

He knows Rhino, but we actually did very little during the entire semester, focusing on the same project.  He was hardly ever present in class; It's seem he doesn't care. He was rude to me when asking questions. Overall, I recommend the class if you're looking for a relaxed pace; but if you're looking to learn, there are better instructors.

He's a great guy and very understanding. Sometimes it can be hard to understand what he asks because he's not the best communicator. His classes are rhino based, and you will almost not draw at all. He cares a lot about the graphic elements of your work. I learned a ton from his classes and recommend him, especially for more software experience.

He is an ok guy but professor wise is not good. When asking for help he doesn't really explain well and not only that he just rushes through. Gives busy work and does not really sit there with you and teach. Homework wasn't hard just didn't understand the concepts and wished he was more engaged with the students

Amazing professor. May seem intimidating at first and his projects will come off as a lot upon introducing them, but trust his process. He emphasizes the quality of your design and teaches you to have a purpose for every decision. Learned a lot of practical and actually useful skills. Take if you want a fresh perspective on architecture.

He's a great professor. I enjoyed attending his class and the projects he gave us were always fun and interesting. What I liked most about his teaching is that he was always honest about my designs and he helped me think outside of the box.
He stole videos from other professors. Gives the wrong answers and then corrects them after someone says something. Doesn't actually teach.

I don't honestly think he could care less about his classes. The entire class was taught with videos from another professor and youtube videos. Weekly tests contain awful typos and strange language. When I asked him about a problem with a test malfunction he said that he didn't see anything wrong.
Be prepared to not be taught and learn off of nothing but YouTube videos. Wouldn't recommend if you value good type of learning like how it should be.

If your expecting to be taught, this isn't the class for you. Low expectations and low results and all done independently through Youtube videos. If you want an easy A this class is for you, the professor is very sweet and understanding but you wont remember a single thing.

Very nice person, but a very poor teacher. Very good about being flexible if students have an issue with technology or not understanding a concept. Lectures about something completely different from the assignments which leaves the students confused and not knowing how to complete the assignments or understand their concepts.

Very unprofessional. Does not properly utilize time set aside for him to provide students with critiques on their work. Instead, he spends that time asking students about very personal information about themselves.
Just no, horrible, does not respect students.
100% awful. Nosy, weird, not a good professor or person. Be prepared for personal questions to be asked instead of talking about your project, which he will never criticize.
This professor was supposed to catch a flight to Urbino next semester, but instead, he caught a case. I had low expectations for him, and he still failed to meet them.
He is the best professor you will have. You will learn, and you will be able to design and explore yourself as an architect.

She is an awesome professor, and I really enjoyed the architecture firms she had scheduled for us. she really cares about our opinion and what do we think. She is also willing to help people including outside of class hours. She is a big fan in model making, if you enjoy making models, you will enjoy her class.

Very great professor! As long as you reach all requirements in a project you can expect clear grading. Aside from that, he also encourages students to dive deep into their designs, encourages freedom when designing. He has also helped develop a positive synergy amongst the students and led to a very positive overall studio culture.

He is like a washing machine and in the middle of projects that he gives you 2 days in class to do even though they should take 2 and a half to 3 weeks to do; he will give you more assignments! He changes the requirements for projects on the fly when you might already be half way through and now have to start over.

He only uses sketch-up, because it's easy. He likes to keep things "simple" but just rewards bare minimum work. If you want to actually learn something or be challenged to be a better designer in any way, do not take this man. He's an ok guy but a bad professor. Terrible time management and fostered no studio culture. Just mediocre overall.

Professor Johnson's class was very hands on his critiques were always geared towards helping you to get across what you want your design to communicate instead of him pushing his own ideas on you.  Overall I think he is one of the top architecture professors in the university and highly suggest aspiring architects to take his class.

Professor Johnson became my favorite professor, after I took his class. He actually engages with his students with a different approach than other professors do. He is fun to be around and with crack jokes with you. He usually does about 2 big projects and a 1 week projects. He is a fairly easy grader, just follow the checklist he will give you.
He should not be an architecture professor.
He is very unprepared of what he wants to say in class, so he wastes a lot of time. I don't think he should be a professor.
Avoid at all costs. The worst studio professor.
Wasted a lot of time; he is unprepared and just talks to not be quiet. Avoid him if you can.
Avoid at all costs

recentReviews.comment: Professor Lombardi is a good teacher who's teaching a hard class. The textbook is very boring, but she gives out videos to help us understand the content before the next test. She has us take notes and draw on a specific type of notebook. She's very lenient with classwork though, and you have multiple attempts on tests and quizzes.

She's awesome!! So kind and understanding. I loved taking her class and recommend her to everyone. There are a lot of notes, and your notebook will be a grade, but it really helps to remember all the information.

Beautiful Soul, very caring and amazing teacher. I only didn't achieve an "A" because I can't drawl and that is part of the class on me not her. The class was very informative and I wish I could take another.

She's very sweet and understanding of any issues. I would recommend her to anyone. Her accent may be hard to understand initially, but after a while, I think you get used to it. Tests are open-note, and your notebook will also be a grade.

She was a sweet and caring professor. She's very passionate about the subject &does her best to make the class enjoyable and somewhat easy. She grades you based of your notebook submissions which include notes and sketches, weekly quizzes, attendance and exams. Overall, I think she is a great professor, and you can learn a lot by taking her class.
DO NOT take him, can not stress this enough. It is his world your just an assist.

Took him for the first time as a masters student. Challenging, but very rewarding class. He provides resources and helps guide you through your project. Think of him as a project architect and you working together in a firm, and you'll be fine.

He is hard to understand. When you do not understand, just ask him. He will come off as rude but comes from a good place. He is a really tough grader so be careful. Depending on his mood, he makes me want to kms. He doesn't teach and is not motivating which is something I look for in a professor.

This man is absolutely awful. As a design student, we are naturally creative and expressive people; But how Nishimoto runs his studio, you and your project become a Nishimoto production. It felt like he was turning us into his mindless assistants in his conquest for a authoritarian design world; ruled by the man himself. N I S H I M O T O.

This class was confusing online. His teaching methods take some getting used to and they don't quite make sense at first. By the end of the semester, it was easier to understand him but the beginning was rough. If you take this class, ask a lot of questions so the projects are more clear, he goes more into depth when you do that.

recentReviews.comment: He never really post the information you need to know for the exams but rather says it very shortly in the class, he has the monuments list posted but sometimes he wont add that information to the exams, the online lectures that he post are from like 2015 and seem very pointless to me that he only gives you a certain amount of time to view them.

The only reason I withdrawal from his class was the lack of preparation he gave me. His canvas is like a desert, nothing to study or look upon, he would post maybe a few notes from his lectures but wants you to take the “ initiative”. He's class was all exams and mini quizzes. No assignments or extra credit. I would suggest a different professor.

As long as you actually attend all of the lectures and take notes that you truly study before exams you'll do fine. He does a pretty good job of letting you know what's important to remember. The research paper he assigns is a big chunk of your grade, as if the final so put in effort on those. He's a tough grader when it comes to any writing.

hard to stay focused through his lectures. Tests are extremely hard and when you go into his office for help he basically says go read your notes. He's a bit rude. He gives out participation grades throughout his lectures. He'll ask questions and whoever answers will get extra points but doesn't ask for the names and gives points to random people.

Had one big paper, please cite everything correctly. He's a super smart professor and i like his lectures (that is just me). Its a super interesting class that is really enjoyable topic for me. There are class discussions and at the moment, half of it is online (1.2 hour lectures).

Professor Bastian is not your traditional Architecture professor he's really into innovative things and parametric design. He will incorporate as much technology as possible wherever he gets the chance! I really enjoy his classes but the only downside for me is that his critiques change very drastically sometimes from  one class to the next!

He is very knowledgable and passionate about what he is teaching. But all the grades are based on 4 quizzes and 3 exams and that is it. The quizzes consist of 4 questions and a written response (graded heavy) while the exam is 25 multiple choice and 25 T/F questions which are worded in a way that is difficult to comprehend. Nice, but very monotone.

Second time taking this professor. First of all he never put grades in, so you will never know if you are passing  or failing. Second he dont grade by quality of work but instead he grades based of his own interests.

I've taken 3 semesters with him back to back, and at first it was dull sure, his lecture get lengthy, and it is hard to follow along, but overall his intentions to help and teach are there, he cares and is very helpful outside of class, helped me a lot outside of class. He cares if you show you that you care for your work as well.

I like him as a person hes clearly very knowledgeable and experienced in Architecture. He tends to get passive aggressive when hes frustrated which I find a bit disrespectful but given the circumstances of online class I get it. There are few projects and each one you have a lot of time, and he gives little instruction so we can be creative.

This teacher is more concern with the structure of his rules than genuinely interacting and helping the student to excel. It is all about him selfish and self center expects perfection, but when he makes mistakes do not correct and acts border by it when confronted. His lectures are boring and long and quite honest he is not a good teacher
I wish this class was in person

I didn't have a problem with him all year. He is a tough grader given that he doesn't provide feedback, he just gives you a grade. I am ticked off that he made an extra credit assignment for a grade rather than add points individually. I had a high A that dropped to a B because he didn't say whether it was optional or not.
Very mid. Hope he would've let us have more decisions on OUR project but he decided to prioritize his preferences and it just ended up being something that many people felt dissatisfied by.

Digital Design Studio was overall a good class but very out of touch with modern architecture software which I wish I had known. Araiza uses Rhino 3D and sure it's a nice extra skill to have but all students should be learning software like Revit which is what literally every firm uses. Taking this class held me (and many others) back.
The best!

The class encourages strong student engagement, and discussions are often active. However, the weekly reading load is very heavy and can feel overwhelming. Class time sometimes runs past scheduled limits. The strict no-technology policy can be frustrating, but it does help keep students focused.
One of the most inspirational and motivational people Ive ever had the pleasure of knowing. So grateful to have had him for my first ever design course

What I like about his class the most is that it's very challenging compared to other classes, yet our class seems to have learned a whole lot from all the challenges he gave us. His feedbacks are always amazing--he'd tell you the positives and the negatives and where to go from there. He's also very inspirational and caring for his students.

He does give a lot of homework to us, for example, 1 model and 5 different drawings/renderings which you can only work on for 2 nights. However, he gives really good feedbackshe tells you where you succeed and where you fell over, so youll know what to improve on the next time you do homework. Ask lots of questions if instructions are unclear.
Great, but difficult teacher. you should have many deliverables each day. if you think you did a lot, do more. All projects are continuous so you will never be done. Accept that.

Bagarozy is a very detail orientated professor that is not afraid to give harsh critiques and sometimes break your soul. BUT HE IS AN AMAZING PROFESSOR that has prepared me for my next design courses. It is worth getting through tears and sleepless nights to gain the skills you get from this class. Don't miss this opportunity!

I wouldnt take his class again, but it doesnt discredit his teaching. He understands the material very well which is comforting but sometimes he doesnt explain things in the best way for his students to completely comprehend the matter. Im sure his class wouldve been way better in-person, but having to be taught virtually ruined experience.

I had this professor the first year he came to UTSA. He is a good professor along with his partner Paola. Dennis focuses on design details mainly, and Paola gives really good feedback when it comes to design and presentation documentation. I really enjoyed their class and they make an effort to connect to their students. Always have stuff to show!

After presentations they hardly gave me critiques so I thought everything about my project was good until the final presentation day came and they failed me and blamed me for not knowing better after they never corrected most of my work. Never specified what they wanted from the us. Was the worst at communicating and always had the class confused.
He is one of the best professors I have ever taken, I learned so much from him. He genuinely cares for his students and wants you to succeed.

Professor Patmon has been one of the best professors I've had so far! He is very knowledgable in the field of architecture and answers questions you may have about architecture. He is a professor that wants his students to succeed and do well and gives great feedback on your projects.

He has deep knowledge of architecture, working full-time as an architect and often giving detailed lectures on various topics like structures and systems. However, his dual role caused scheduling conflicts; he'd leave in the middle of class for meetings, and he gave little time to complete our project by sharing the program a month before pens down
very helpful

Greatest professor I've had during my time as an ARC student. I had never received instruction like this before. Very well-organized, very informative, and very motivating. No one at UTSA is educating on the topics she is and should be taking notes. In a matter of months, I learned Revit. She genuinely cares about her students and is just awesome

His class was awesome! Took him during the summer. He took us on field trips to learn about the city's architecture. He gives really good feedback and criticism on your designs. Learned how to go about the design process in a completely different way than I used to. Would definitely recommend anyone considering his class to take it.

Arguably the best studio professor at UTSA. He will definitely critique your work harshly but he is very objective and you can really tell he does it because he cares about your work. He is the type of professor to back off during work time but I recommend you seek him out, he will give you the guidance you need.

Professor Fish was the best!  His weekly architecture tours around the city were very helpful and inspirational.  He was very easy to talk to, often times giving a much better answer than anticipated! I wish I could have professor Fish for all my classes!

Ive had him as my professor more than once now and I can honestly say hes the BEST studio professor Ive ever had!! Likes students who have constant work flow but is also very understanding when students get stuck or frustrated, and gives very detailed and insightful feedback on your designs!! He has helped me improve as a designer so much!

HE'S AMAZING! Both hard and fair, but he pushes you to be a better designer and student. He gives lots of homework, but its for your benefit. Make sure you have some knowledge of Revit, he gets frustrated with some questions, but he always takes the time to explain if you ask him. I wish I could have him every semester.

Professor Diego is a delight! I like how she uses real projects that she is working on or has finished as context for what she is teaching. She is very understanding if you ever need an extension on a project and she cares about everyone's well being.

I love Professor Diego! She does a great job at relating course content with real life situations, which makes learning more enjoyable. She uses her own projects to illustrate how to apply the content learned in each class into our own designs. She does give group projects, and although frustrating at times, think I learned a lot from them!

I really like the class there's a lot to learn however, professor Diego isn't big on helping students achieve how to fix your design beforehand. Also, on her wall, there is a bare painting that is very sensual/erotic which is disturbing to look at. The slides have a lot of information for future reference to keep for later on in the studios.

I have really nothing to say other than be prepared for group projects (we had two and boy oh boy they were hard to organize on our end) and if you can, turn your camera. She likes to see people's faces. Her lectures are really insightful, but they do always span the entirety of class time. So don't expect to get out early. Have not had quizzes

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! She gives amazing lectures and her tests are easy if you study. She uploads all power points online so you can miss class but you wont want to. She gives group projects that are fun! its like a scavenger in San Antonio. You will present these to the class. Take notes and you will get a high grade. We also had 2 field trips.

So far, Dr. Appleford has been one of the best professors I've had. - He keeps lectures really interesting and thought-provoking. - He's willing to help students in and outside of class. - He is very considerate. Throughout the semester, he'd move deadlines and test dates around to accommodate for everyone's different schedules! - Class is tough.

Dr. Appleford is one of the best professors I have encountered thus far in my BME journey. He helps you both with in-class questions as well as career/field questions. He is eloquent, always available to answer questions, and cares a lot about his students. He inspires me as a BME student. I wish all professors were like him.

This class is hard, but he is a good lecturer. Really passionate about the subject. Lots of extra credit. DONT buy the book (you need the book), ask a prev. student for a copy of it. All the homework is hard and the book is not so helpful, no joke. So make friends to find solutions. Participation is essential.

Cell Biology second semester is a very busy class and make sure you always stay on top of your reading and do all the assignments he tells you to do in lecture before the class. For the Lab make sure you are always writing your papers thoroughly and following directions in the lab. Do not procrastinate on the lab reports and have a good partner.

Appleford is a fantastic teacher, but both Quantitative physiology and cell bio for engineers are very tough classes. Lectures and notes are clear, but tests are very tough despite being multiple choice. Likes to give Dr. Who and other nerdy bonus questions. Overall great professor

recentReviews.comment: Professor Tang is all that I want in a teacher. He shows up early, explains the lecture in several different ways with several examples, and takes questions with no offense taken. Though he has a slight accent, he is still a great lecturer. Dr. Herbert's slides and practice exams are fantastic - use them!

Straight-forward professor, knows the matieral for EA1 and can help you understand the material. Don't be shy to ask questions, he will help you. This course is time consuming, so be preapre to study almost everyday.

Fantastic professor, had her for BME Labs (1-3), Biomaterials, Topics in Biomechanics, and Senior Design. She takes time to get to know students and is always accessible outside of class. She tends to grade generously for students that participate in class and actively engage.

Dr. Gaviria is an amazing professor especially for the senior design curriculum and she emphasizes what she wants for each milestone and also looks at your need statement and specs. Each design depending on the team and also the mentors for senior design will also be input for you to have the best senior design experience.

She is a very informative professor who is very knowledgeable in her specialization. Her lectures are intriguing and inspiring, and the grading is very lenient as long as you participate and show improvement.

You will need to read a lot to pass the class. The grade is based on standard deviation so if you are below the 50% mark at the end of the year you will get a D or F in the class. Tests are 100% of the grade and essay based. The very specific so read the chapters a lot. Not a fun class to take, requires multiple hours a week of studying to pass.

Professor Jacobs is a wonderful person who shows compassion to all of his students. He does assign a lot of homework, and I do mean a lot. To make up for it, he makes the exams open notes and also has extra credit opportunities on every exam and some homework grades. I found his class to be very hard, but that could just be a skill issue on my part

I enjoyed Professor Jacobs Intro to Chemical Engineering course. 
There are many group projects (answering questions on a packet), but the questions are straightforward & easy to divvy out. There is also one major paper but you have the entire semester to write it. I'm taking him for another Chemical Engineering course and I'm looking forward to it
I took this professor during the Spring 2022 semester and Dr. Jacobs is absolutely amazing! He cares and wants to see his students succeed! I would highly recommend taking him.
You can just tell he wants students to succeed in his class and it does it with delight. Very accessible outside of class and is willing to help you out!

He is a very great, understanding, and helpful professor. Professor Jacobs has helped me out when I am stuck on a topic relating to this course and does it with great attitude. Would definitely take him again.

Funny professor, but an extremely unprofessional one. Took this professor for 2 classes and he graded fairly the previous semester but this most recent professor it was completely different. Pop quizzes and no excuse if you cannot make it. If you fail an exam or don't do good in the class you will be picked on and embarrassed for not doing well.

Was late to class one time because of a car accident. When I made it to class, he had a random pop quiz. After I explained the situation to him he said “Oh well”, and I got a 0. Sums him up as person.
Was late to class b

This is a chemical engineering professor, chemical engineering courses are hard. Dr. Ramirez-Hernandez teaches two of the hardest courses in the major and is always willing to help you understand. Disregard the negative comments from people who aren't willing to learn and practice the material and expect every professor to throw As at them.

If you don't have experience with Matlab or don't enjoy coding then the class might be difficult. The start of the semester is enjoyable and easy to follow but eventually got complicated. above average

Don't take this if you're bad at Verilog and/or have a busy schedule. We were doing lengthy Verilog and Virtuoso assignments, yet were lectured and tested on MOSFETS. Took him for Electrical Circuits. It was one of his first years teaching and as such didn't have much previous content to fall back on. I was weary of taking Dr. Shadaram, after I heard he is very difficult. I found however that his class isn't that bad. The textbook was a free PDF. The homeworks were a lot, but the recitation TAs were helpful. Professor is a good lecturer, he always stops to ask if we have any questions. He gives extra points to your grade for asking questions.

Dr. Shadaram teaches a very tough course. The reviews here are students who just got their first shock of what it means to be an Electrical Engineer. Dr. Shadaram made sure we understood the content if you asked questions and was even more helpful in office hours. His teaching put me leagues above my classmates that took the "easier" professor.

Professor was not an effective lecturer. I managed to get a grade of an A- purely from outside resources not provided by his class. Blames class for bad grades but every semester I hear from other peers that he lectures poorly and blames students for lack of quality teaching and understanding.

Shadaram refuses to be a decent professor, with only reading off of ppt with little to no explanation on the process. He also does not like to be contacted outside of class even though he has stated he doesn't mind. Does not provide a review for exams, and all exams are in person unlike other 2423 classes. He does not care about you passing.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. He simply does not care about you. He will fail majority of the class without thinking twice and will tell you to quit engineering if you don't understand the material even though his "lectures" are just reading from a ppt. He doesn't care to explain his work or show it, he just says do it on your own. Worst prof in ECE

One of the best professors I have had. I took him for his Wireless Com (graduate level) class and he's a great lecturer! He makes complex concepts  easy to understand. Nice professor if you want to learn something new....:)
Dr. Akopian is one of the more likable and responsive professors in the EE dept

recentReviews.comment: Professor Millwater is one of the best diff EQ teacher ever. He's so so nice and teaches very well. If you like to learn through example problems and not just through slides go to him! His examples are what helped me so much. He records his lectures too! Extremely chill guy. Go to class and do the problems with him and ask questions and you'll pass
He takes notes with you so you don't get lost and he explains everything he does. Will answer questions efficiently and is very caring to his students. The GOAT of EA1.

Dr. Millwater is great. He focuses on how to do something, and not as much as to why. He helped me in this regard as I don't grasp conceptual lectures that well and EA1 is essentially lots of mathematical principles. He focuses on understanding, and is helpful and straightforward. If you put in the effort, he can help you do well.
Very strict when it comes to homework and tests. He won't budge on homework assignments and very tough with partial credit. He does give a good amount of extra credit on exams though.

First, EA1 is a tough course. However, Millwater gives you a VERY fair chance of passing the class. There are deadlines, you are expected to meet them. Millwater knows the material and gives TONS of examples for you to follow. In addition, there is a lot of HW but it makes sense as the more practice you do, the better prepared you are for the exam

He was a bit of a mean person and made his final exam a little harder than it needed to be. For the most part, it was a pretty hard class, but nothing new for engineering courses. However, from what I saw, most people failed just because of the final alone, so be careful. Overall, just angry at life, but you can still do well with effort.

The course itself wasn't to difficult, but the course and the lectures were extremely boring to me. The lab aspect is pretty interesting and a little bit of fun, but physical drawing seems pointless with so much technology and very repetitive. The class was pretty simple, exams weren't too hard.

While the lectures can be dull, he breaks things down in a simple, easy-to-understand way and never moves too fast with the different things covered. But during the exams and quizzes, he does throw a lot of curveballs that might be a little unfair, and he does not hesitate to grade harshly. Take someone else if possible, but definitely manageable.

Not bad by any means. I will say lectures are pretty boring, and homework can be hard. There's not a lot of feedback so it's hard to know what you're doing wrong. Exams/quizzes are similar to homework, no real curveballs there. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Lectures/ gives iClicker questions after class ends pretty regularly.

The one star reviews our unfair, and the 5-star reviews simp too much. When he teaches the material he teaches it well, the only problem I have is that is 10% of the lecture. It is very hard not to fall asleep in his class as he will go way too far into detail about subjects while engineering related, aren't related to the class.

additionally does +4 extra credit to your grade if you show up 90% of the time and do two short surveys. would recommend.

The homework assignments are easy if you follow along with the slides. The tests are similar to the homework assignments, but they are still difficult. Make sure you understand the concept, and you'll be good. Test 2 will be the hardest, so make sure you study ahead of time. The first and third will be easier, but make sure to prepare.

try your hardest to take June instead. He only teaches off slides with no examples and the recitation sessions are a waste of time. You will know when you have an exam 1 week beforehand. Luckily the exam is 80% of what the homework looks like but will deduct any points he can. if youre messy with your equations hell take off points. steer clear

start the homework early. Homework 3 I believe was the hardest. He gives hints at what is on the test & hw is a lot like the test. no set test dates. Very understanding if you just communicate through email. Review Calc 3 material as half the class is calc 3 & linear alg. use word to fit everything on 1 side of cheat sheet, final is 2 sides.
Good professor and fair but you will have to teach yourself

this course is only mandatory for ME majors and its pretty tough. hws are very tough & worth 20% of ur course grade. pop quizzes are given every 2-3 weeks which are usually easier than the hws but still tough. exams are MC and no partial credit, but 2 attempts. if u take this class with this professor u will prob need tutoring

Dr. Eghbal is a poor professor. Lectures are general and theory based, so not as useful in doing problems for HW, Quizzes and Exams. Lectures are from years ago, Exams are MC(no partial credit). He shows NO passion or care and is lazy. The office hours are useless too. My recommendation: Take this class at a community college -- And I got an A lol.

Dr. Morad was a solid lecturer. Circuits isn't the easiest class for ME's and to be fair he doesn't really help. His lectures were average but he didn't seem to enjoy teaching. He had pretty standard HWs and exams with the occasional pop quiz to see if students are paying attention. He had to offer an EC project worth +15 overall bc of low grades.

Morad gets a pretty bad wrap but I felt that he knows what he is talking about and is trying to improve his teaching. If you study hard (out of the book) before exams you will be fine but his reviews dont match with the exams that well. do the HW early so you will do well on the pop quizzes and finally, take advantage of the EC project.

Honestly get ready to teach yourself if you want to do well. Her lectures weren't horrible but the exams and homework are nothing like what you learn in lecture videos. I suggest going to her office hour zoom meetings as often as possible, it's the only place you'll get help with homework, and it's where you can bring up concerns to her.

I have two cousins who are math wizards and professional civil engineers... somehow I still got a C. Yeah this class is that terrible. Tests are NOTHING like the assignments. Very poor instruction. I don't understand why the architecture department has let this go on for so long when it's the same thing every semester. Clearly it's not the students

She doesn't let you ask questions during exam. She makes things complicated. She makes her own examples that has no real life application; I didn't know what to do for any of her homework. And I had to watch so many videos for her class! She also says some material won't be on the test but it showed up a lot! Take somebody else. Good luck!
This class is honestly the worst class that I have ever taken at UTSA.

Ridiculous. I am basically paying to watch youtube videos. Every week theres at least 5 videos to watch INCLUDING her lecture videos. Grading criteria sucks, she doesnt explain math well and assigns wayyyy too many quizzes and homework a week (at least 4-5) and its not enough time to understand what the heck were doing. Hate this class.

The lecture is pointless. Especially when you can't understand what the professor, who mumbles a lot and talks extremely quietly. The lab is good and useful, depending on the TA. He takes a long time, or never answer emails. 2 exams for lecture and 2 exams for lab, group project for lab. Attendance mandatory for both lecture and lab. Good luck

The lectures can be dull and it's hard to retain what he goes over, despite him trying to be engaging. That said, the tests aren't that hard if you spend a lot of time preparing on your own using the slides & homework. There are a LOT of different assignments making up your grade. Nothing's that hard individually but can pile up in a tedious way.

Geez, everyone hates on this kind old man. He's a really good guy; his exams though are pretty long and it's a race when you take them. Exams are mixture of openended and multi choice. IMO, when you get to the lab reports, write the abstract and results + discussion. These are the most tedious YET BENEFICIAL sections for your learning.

He's a good person; he gives a lot of extra credit. Materials is not a very easy class, everyone kind of blew it off; and it was okay. We all got a 60-ish average for the first exam, so he gave an online exam retest of 20% extra credit. If you listen in class and answer questions he will respect you. He's funny and cares about his students.

Dr. Rao is easily the most unorganized and incompetent professor i've ever had the displeasure of taking. My advice is to just read the textbook to learn the topics as it's much less confusing that way. Expect homework assignments that do not work, exam and quiz keys that are incorrect, and a good amount of extra credit required to pass.

I LOVED HIM. Not just in class, but overall such an amazing man/professor. Had him for an elective class, very friendly, office hours open, gives not just help, but advice, willing to go into philosophy with you, self introspection, and so on. Happy to have met him early on, definitely worth meeting.

Took him for ME elective- amazing, hilarious, knowledgable, invested in student success and will help you get excited about your work and support your growth. Highly recommend, in my opinion he is the best of the best at UTSA.

Great Lecturer, also has all lectures online recorded for you to go back and watch to get a better understanding(did this a bunch). Honestly wish this guy taught more courses I would definitely take them. Learned a lot from this man. If you need this course definitely take him.
Great professor, advisor, and mentor! Thankful to have him at UTSA, definitely will recommendation his class lots to learn about applicable medical research teamwork, and leadership

one of the best professors ive ever had. hw and exams are very fair, and he seems to genuinely enjoy teaching if you interact with him in class. grading on exams is very smart; they grade based on if you know the process rather than the actual numbers. would take this professor for every course if i could.

Professor Cobb is a pretty chill guy. Teaching isn't his day job, he just does it for enjoyment. He provides an exquisite equation sheet for exams and makes homework completion grades. His lectures are pretty good. He doesn't just read off the slides and will work examples.

One of UTSA's best professors. Lectures are really interesting if you show up & the exams are very fair (just use the equation sheet). The lab section is tough, so make sure you find a good group bc thats where your time will go. I wish more classes were taught the way Cobb teaches his lectures, & hes very reasonable when it comes to grading.

She's great for the controls lecture. It's every other week and usually takes us less than an hour, then we just have 2 weeks to write a report about it. She walks you through everything and makes the whole lab really easy.

Dr. Crom is a phenomenal instructor who did a great job breaking down complex topics into easy-to-understand concepts. Her office hours and recitations were invaluable for getting practice and feedback on long problems before exams.
Don't take Crom
When 50% or more of the class is failing, then the problem is not the students.

Ridiculously strict grader despite not actually lecturing or teaching any materials. Thought providing a weekly two hour video lecture which provided no explanation outside of her reading the slides was a substitute. Homework might as well not count for anything. Tests are 90% of grade.

Uses old lectures from publisher of book. Inconsistent grading of similar mistakes between students. Long times to receive response. Uses a lot of Spanish with grader during exams. Exam, quizzes, and homeworks are repeats of previous years but easy if you just read the textbook. Grading and response takes a long time.

I'm currently taking the class (as I type this), and Dr Rincon is awesome! She's super inclusive and considerate of student's issues and is a great teacher. Expect a lot of slides every class. 3 exams + final. Attendance is mandatory and iclicker grades can be the difference between two letter grades, also A LOT of extra credit. Good luck!

Lectures were great and I was never lost about anything she went over. You have to memorize quite a lot of stuff for the exams as her equation sheets are very short and involved many conceptual stuff. Lots of HW, quizzes and in-class work too. That said, nothing egregious overall. She's also very nice and accommodating about due dates and grading.

She's very nice and does a good job at explaining materials. Not a hard class and she makes it easier. Tests are pretty light but actually study to do better than just passing. Offers plenty of extra credit. Grading is fair too and is very accessible. She's also very talkative…beware.

She's very nice, maybe more than a bit disorganized. Exams were really easy and there was tons of extra credit. She provides a huge list of study topics making studying the day before quite easy, but the formula sheets, curiously, are very thin.

He's a pretty okay lecturer but that's because its thermo 2 - a course with repeat material. He is pretty helpful in showing you the easiest way to do a problem as long as you understand the concepts. He does NOT curve so you get what you get. try to do well on the first 2 exams, because the last one will be much more difficult.

Dr. Abidin is a great professor. Thermodynamics is a tough course, so it obviously won't be easy with any professor. Abidin's exams were fair and related closely to the homework and recitation problems. People rate professors badly just because they were lazy and did bad in the class.

He's a decent professor. I do not recommend taking him if you can. He clearly knows his stuff, but struggles conveying it. Be prepared to study YouTube and the book. The exams are tough and the practice exams do not help. Focus more on studying the homework and recitations. Again, I do not recommend taking him.

Dr. Abidin is a good professor. He really likes Thermo and it comes out in lecture. Its pleasant to have faculty still be excited. Especially after working all day and teaching at night. I would recommend you come to class, he short hands his examples but I like that. I have to tear my notes down afterwords which makes me understand processes

Dr. Zainal Abidin is a poor lecturer (death by ppt). The material is brutal and having a poor professor makes it even worse. The Exams are very tough --a majority of the class failed the 1st Exam or dropped from the course. I recommend watching Youtube videos and/or going to Herberts Lecture instead. Be prepared to teach yourself!!!

Dr. Pineda is amazing! His lecture slides are very informative and easy to follow. I went to most of his office hours and he answered every question in extreme depth. His lectures go over a lot of the theory but he takes all the notes on his iPad and posts them. He also records all of the lectures along with posting recitations.

Professor showed great interest in ensuring understanding of the subject material. Fluid Mechanics is a difficult course, yet he managed to lecture in a format that was easy to understand. Gives many helpful assignments and at-home labs to demonstrate concepts.

Dr. Pineda delivers his lectures in the form of note taking, which gives students a good chance to take notes along with him. He gives decent examples during lectures and has more examples in a recitation that he posts online. He's also pretty helpful if you go to office hours.
Dr. Pineda stands out among any professors I have had. He genuinely cares for his students and is an expert in his field.

Professor is great at teaching advance topics. He clearly reads the book himself and takes out the important stuff from the book and makes amazing powerpoints to clearly inform their students. He is not concerned with students making basic math mistakes in exams but rather see that the student has a good understanding of the topics. recommend!!!
