recentReviews.comment: Easy A for Solids, but only if you don't want to learn anything. His slides are handwritten and completely illegible, and he doesn't finish half of his sentences while teaching. His exams are insanely easy, though, and you don't have to take the final if you pass the two midterms.

His lectures aren't the best and you'll likely have to teach yourself a bit (I recommend looking up his Youtube channel), but he does try to be engaging and cares about his classes a lot. HW and quizzes barely matter to your grade and the exams are almost absurdly simple. Just go over the basic concepts and processes. He also offers extra credit.

Always shows up to class in a good mood to lecture. He doesn't always go step-by-step for example problems but he likes to bring demonstration props to class, which makes up for that. Exams feel a little long but are not too bad and are graded fairly. Homework is VERY hard and MUCH harder than the exams, but makes for good study material by itself.

Great professor! Do the HW's, the quizzes, and solve extra problems. His exams are fair if you put in the effort to pass the class. Lectures can feel monotonous/boring, but he does his best to answer questions/concerns. Also, he provides the textbook in canvas.

Dr. Han is one of the more fun lecturers in UTSA engineering. He makes a difficult subject more understandable through use of props and imagination. His class is more engaging than most labs i've taken, which says a lot. Homework assignments were extremely difficult, but worth very little. Just focus on lectures and exams and you'll do fine.
Exams were VERY easy with examples taken from the lecture slides and homework. The project, however, while relatively straightforward, was time consuming and graded tough.

It's hard to follow the lectures, mostly due to his accent, but the material isn't that bad and the tests are doable if you keep up. He does grade harshly though, so be careful and don't expect an easy A. The group project isn't unfairly hard either, but is still a lot, lot, lot of work so find a good group and get started as early as you can.

Good professor for a hard class, considering he hadn't taught this course in 10+ years. Lots of homework, but important to understand it. Tests are modified homework problems and really only over the fundamentals. He outlined what was important to know for exams during lectures, which I liked. Would take him again.
Very great speech!

Honestly Zeng makes this class much simpler than other professors. #1 thing to do is SHOW UP TO CLASS. its not the most entertaining, but hes pretty helpful in explaining things & tells you the most common mistakes so you dont do the same. Exam grading is hit or miss. The class project is the hardest part of the class, so try not to procrastinate.

Not a bad professor, very knowledgeable and helpful in fact. He makes class manageable, exams are fair, and he doesn't overload you, but exams are 97% of the grade. Very strict and can be REALLY condescending when something inconveniences him. My advice: keep office hours strictly about course content and don't expect much flexibility.

He's literally running social experiments on us like lab rats right now. Our exams are 97% of our grade and the class average for exam 1 was a 50. He's trying to do research on if there's a correlation between doing Take Home Exam Problems worth 2% of our grade and getting better exam scores. Had to admit after exam 1 it wasn't true. I'm a lab rat.

Professor is rude and unaccommodating if you are unable to attend class for any reason. Tends to talk down to people using his tone. He is knowledgeable and good at teaching but I would not recommend taking his class.

No complaints. He breaks things down in a super easy-to-understand way, does lots of example problems and is just very engaging in general. I even look up his Youtube lectures for classes I take with other professors. The exams are 95% of the grade and, other than him being a bit nitpicky when grading, are simple and very similar to the homework.

His last name is derived from low German, meaning "Man" (man) and "Düvel" (devil).
The lecture style was non-linear and quick, which made it difficult to follow and take notes. This led to frustration during class that I haven't had with other professors. There was limited flexibility in addressing student feedback or receiving additional support.

Enterprise Engineering: Dr. Wan is an amazing professor. Great lectures that are very informational. Graded by 1 group project, homework & quizzes. His exams are pretty difficult. Best way to pass his class is to make sure you do good on the quizzes, homework's and group project! Very kind, helpful and will work with you.

Hands down, he is the best professor I have ever had as a student. He had a clear plan of how he wanted to conduct the course and he did that brilliantly. Yes, he gives a lot of homework and quiz's, which only keeps the students up to date with the course works. So, when the midterms and finals come, the students were well prepared.

Wan is one of the better professors I have had. He mostly goes over problems in his lectures, but he posts a lot of material online to study from; he even record his lectures online. I recommend getting the textbook, any edition, and reading the material when you get the chance. The material is tough, so be prepared to study a lot.
If you want to teach yourself, take him.

Dr. Wan is a very nice professor who will try his best to answer your questions. Study his PowerPoints, and take advantage of his office hours. He gives partial credit as well as bonus points on exams. I would have possibly received a better score if I had studied more in his class.

I never understood a single thing this man said. I was confused the whole semester. He would say one thing, then change his mind. His class is a total disaster. I wonder who hired this person as a professor. He was also sarcastic at times. This may get deleted but this dude is a piece of garbage.

You are better off not going to class and teaching yourself by reading the book. I'm ngl I fumbled this class and got a B- because I didn't figure out how to take notes until the last exam lol. He mostly lectures by TALKING about the topics (no slides) and has a very simple notes outline. I recommend voice recording lectures to fill in notes later . Overall he's chill and knows a bunch of sci-fi references.

Very frustrating. 85% of your grade is your exams, one assignment per week that barely helps your grade. His notes are very difficult to understand because he often does not elaborate over topics that should be elaborated upon, and then proceeds to put said topics on his assignments and exams. Decently funny guy, but his lectures give me a headache

All the people complaining most likely put in very minimal effort. His lectures are actually engaging and interesting. He does his best to explain and use examples we would understand. There's a quiz every week, and you can retake it until you get a 100. The exams are very lecture-heavy, and if you take good notes, you will pass them.
He was a very tough grader, but if you go to his office hours, which I found helpful, he doesn't mind breaking things down one by one to help you. Loved his lectures I found him funny

I really enjoyed this class. It was pretty tough, and paying attention in class is essential. He gives terms in an outline, but you have to define the terms yourself or you won't understand. The textbook reading is very helpful, but they tend to be lengthy. It's challenging, but a very interesting class and I really enjoyed.

I took his course last semester, I really enjoyed it, very knowledgeable professor, not easy lectures but very fair grading. In retrospect when I compare to other lectures I took, it was one of the best.
He would go through lectures fast and speak as if we knew what he was talking about most of the time and he had a thick accent so sometimes it was just harder to grasp

Only grades are four exams out of five, quizzes are merely bonus points to your grade. You can tell he is very passionate in his teachings. At times, he would ask for a volunteer for an demonstration of the topic, and those were fun to watch. Exams are open notes (on paper) and has exam review days before the exam--can tell he cares

His first time teaching effects of sleep on memory and learning. He's very passionate about the topic! Lectures were engaging and there wasn't too much out of class work. Quizes after each unit and points from other assignments are used as extra points towards the final (which was cumulative). Wasn't a hard class, but still go to class!

I took his asynchronous course so it is partially my fault for this unenjoyable experience because online classes aren't exactly my jam. However, about the course the only grades are five exams (which are open note, and your lowest grade gets dropped) which are very difficult.

run. teach yourself EVERYTHING by textbook. If you have a question he says "Look at the textbook" ONLY reads off of slides for over an hour in class. Your "study" material is the slides he already read off of. The only grades are quizzes and test. I dropped this class so fast because my GPA is high and this would have flunked it. save yourself

He made us buy our own scantrons and than if someone forgot he would make them leave class the day of the exam to go buy some at the school store and have them comeback rather than just lending them an extra one

Only a few lectures in and I hate it. The guy isn't necessarily rude but he's not at all engaging and just reads off a projector for an hour and a half, and requires mandatory attendance. Feels like a waste of time.

He clearly gave up halfway through the semester. He was constantly late to class and never actually lectured just read straight off the slides all while making our attendance mandatory. Very much felt like he didn't respect our time. Additionally, he showed a serious lack of respect towards students when addressing in-class issues.

He's a very intellectual individual, but would read off the slides and was never able to answer questions students had during lecture. Most of your grade is based on the exams he gives along with in class quizzes.

Only a few lectures in and I love this professor. She's pretty hands on and teaches in a way that I can understand. I can tell that she actually enjoys teaching, unlike a lot of professors I've had. Would definitely love to take a course of hers again.

She's very thorough by explaining what's happening for this week! She's a great professor if you listen to her lecture videos. Exams she lets you have notes which are super helpful! I've had her twice and I've had no problem whatsoever with her. Would definitely take her again.

Dr. Scott is a fantastic professor. This class was done hybrid remote, so we met once a week and had pre recorded video lectures instead of a second weekly class. I don't particularly care for this format, but I learned a lot and got what I needed from the course. Be prepared to devote a decent bit of your time to the outside lectures and reading.
Literally one of the best professor's Ive ever had!!
not letting me submit comment

One of my favorite profs. Really understanding and wants to help you understand the topic. Actually really funny, I didn't dread going to class at all. In-person is graded with 4 exams and attendance, so GO TO CLASS! He lectures the whole time, but he's not boring. Would take a class from him again if I could!

The class was easy but what he would lecture about, you'd go home not have learned anything. The class was for nothing, he would lecture about things we learned in elementary school which was frustrating. Attendance was a heavy grade. Easy grade overall but would not take with him if you want to take anything away from the class

There are 4 exams, that's it. Watch the lectures and you will do fine! He responded to all my emails promptly. I had internet issues and one point and he was very accommodating. His recorded lectures aren't boring and he has a great personality so it's not a painful process lol. If you don't like being on your own so to speak, maybe not for you.

This class only has 4 exams that make up your grade, so missing one will be damaging. Tests are open for a few days so there's no reason not to get them done. The tests are not difficult if you do the reading and listen to the lectures. He has a great personality so the lecture videos aren't dry or boring.

DO NOT TAKE HER! If you can avoid her as a professor, do so at all costs. Never have I dealt with a professor who is as passive aggressive and as rude to students as she was. She will stop lecture to single students out in class rather than discussing issues privately. Will talk to you like you're five years old, too. Course itself is too easy.
No!! Just no!! I would not recommend her at all unless it's a last resort! She holds on to your grade for ever which is beyond weird!!

The course content is pretty basic and not complicated. I however dislike the way exams are done. You are forced to go question by question and you can't go back, which goes against good test taking strategies and increases testing anxiety. Since you are graded on so few things this could be a big deal for someone who is not a good test taker.
You are graded by a few things so it's a make or break. She's very test heavy as the course mostly consisted of tests. She takes forever to grade as well.

PSY 3303 with Ms. Zawacki was awesome. She was available during both class and student hours. Lectures were great and easy to understand. Attendance isn't mandatory (online platform), and the book was needed. If you have the opportunity, take her class. 10/10

recentReviews.comment: Lectures are fun, but he'll often place into groups and have someone present findings. Tests are easy, and structure of the class makes it easy to receive a high grade.

Professor Brown didn't have a good schedule to follow, almost never had when assignments were due and couldn't submit late work for point deduction, probably included 40% of what was due which made it hard because you constantly have to be checking in on your own. The only reason I'd take his class again was because the work wasn't too difficult.

Professor Denver Brown is an amazing professor. His lectures are fun, he is very caring, knowledgeable and helpful. I love how he emphasizes the many routes you can take within the field of psychology!
Dr. Brown this class less scary. Amazing professor!

loved dr brown! his class was easy and he seems to care a lot about students / the course. it is pretty lecture heavy and he does use inquizitive, but attendance wasn't counted and the assignments weren't hard. i do recommend going to the lectures though. highly recommend!

She knows the material, but is not a good teacher. No homework or practice just tests with questions where multiple answers seem correct, but you have to guess her best answer. Lectures are full of mumbling and unrelated rambling. Also constantly threatens to sue students for recording or taking pictures.Would never take again if I had the choice.

I would not take this professor if you struggle with notes and find it hard to focus during someone's rambling. She makes examples she gives in the lecture apart of the exam but she talks so much about things outside of the subject you don't even know what examples to take note of. This class mentally drained me like no other and it is astounding.

Please do not take this professor. Someone took a picture in class and she screamed at them. She told us how she died for 18 minutes but I guess that doesn't revive your heart. Lectures from memory but doesn't remember much. No assignments, grade are entirely dependent on your tests but provides no materials on Canvas to study with.

She comes off harsh to some; that didn't bother me. I work fine with that kind of person. She has high standards for students. She knows her field extremely well. Her personality is unpredictable, which makes it hard to feel safe asking questions. You wanna leave early/show up late to class? Sit near the door, be quiet, and let her know beforehand.
RUN!! no online slides, only exams, you have to be the Benjamin Franklin of taking notes if not you better buy that $40 lecture guide and you have to sell your spleen and liver for a B.

Miss Porter was fantastic, very relatable, and chill. I've always struggled with scientific writing; she showed us her old undergrad papers to make us feel better. All the material was very clear and easy to understand.

Carah was overall, so sweet. She was very straightforward about assignments and how she graded and she gave fantastic feedback to guide us through our assignments. It was very obvious that she wanted all of us to succeed and was very understanding and personable. She also made herself available outside of the classroom for guidance.

Carah was one of the most down to Earth professors I've had. She was super clear and concise when it came to assignments and grading. She was personable, understanding and made herself available outside of class. The class was primarily based on group work and iclicker quizzes, and she also provided many opportunities for helpful feedback.

I'm very happy I had Professor Porter as my Experimental Psych Lab & Projects instructor. As long as you complete your work on time and listen to her feedback on assignments you will get a good grade. She is also a very understanding and kind instructor.

Professor Porter is a very kind professor, and her assignments are of reasonable length, and if an assignment is unclear to the student, she offers assistance and explains in a one-to-one level. She does give a reasonable amount of time to complete any of the assignments. Overall, a great class and professor.
I really enjoyed taking experimental projects and design with Sanders. She cares about the work you are doing and any concerns you may have. Her class was enjoyable!

A great teacher of experimental design. She gives us good information throughout her lectures and is readily available to answer any questions or concerns. She makes every student feel welcomed and establishes a no-judgment zone. I would definitely take another course with this professor.

She is one of the best professors I have ever had, and if she ever decides to teach another psychology course, I would definitely take it. She is very responsive and gives the best feedback on your assignments, so you know what you need to fix. She is also available outside of class and will accommodate her time to help you out.

Instructor Sanders is amazing! She cares a lot about individual success and is incredibly clear with instructions. She is very understanding and her lessons are always interesting, definitely my favorite class this semester. She also goes out of her way to make sure everyone is doing okay in class and understand the assignments.

Professor Jenna was the best professor for this class. She is very understanding when it comes to the workload for this class and will be there for you every step of the way. If you need any help she is accessible all the time even after office hours.

SO MANY group projects. Enough work for 4 classes. Funny and kind teacher. Helpful outside of class. The directions and examples for assignments are confusing and unhelpful. Very hard class. SUPER dry textbook. Lots of quizzes.

Professor Jones-Rincon was an amazing Introduction to Psychology professor. Her lectures are easy to understand and she made psychology very interesting. She talks about her husband and cats a lot and it's awesome. She also studies video games, so that appeals to her gamer students. Excellent professor!

Professor Gonzalez is knowledgeable and kind in his teaching approach. This course has a heavy workload, but he makes it manageable and is not harsh about grading (and provides great feedback so you know what to improve on next time). A lot of the course was group work, but you can choose to work alone. He's great! And has a cute cat.

He's knowledgable and polite/flexible but rushed through summer course. Lots of groupwork(in class), individual assignments & quizzes. Easiest to communicate w/ 1on1 or in groups. Not an easy A, but doable. Got so lucky w/my group - it's essential that you're all present. Other groups struggled when members were absent. Recommend taking w/PSY 3403.

This class had a lot of papers/projects to complete. There was a lot of solo and group work to complete. With that being said, he was a great professor. He explained the material in a practical and applicable way. He was always willing to meet with me and check my papers. I learned SO much in this class. Make sure you ask questions if needed!!

Overall his online class was fun you got to interact with classmates through group projects. members are assigned through a survey so we all had some interests in common. we had a quiz after every class which are fairly easy.We have one major paper due at the end and he walks you though it most of the work you had already turned in as "group work".

Very friendly and approachable, laid back professor who made this class easy for me. Lectures consist of powerpoints and tons of extra credit opportunities. You are assigned in groups based on similar interests for your research. Lots of work but tons of feedback. One of the best professors I've ever had!

This is one of the most difficult classes I have taken, but Prof. Larios is an amazing professor. There are 1000 points in this class broken into group projects, daily quizzes, a huge paper, and some others. The research paper and project are very intimidating but he breaks it down a lot to help, the group work also helps so much. I recommend him.

The class itself is difficult, there's a lot of group projects and written assignments that can take a few days to complete, but Prof Larios really helps make the work manageable. There are quizzes every class day, but they're fairly easy if you pay attention. He gives meaningful feedback to written assignments, and truly wants students to do well.

All tests and quizzes are based strictly on the readings and focus on memorization over conceptual understanding. Lecture attendance is required, but the content isn't tested on, it feels like a waste of time. She grades the research paper easily, but due to her disorganized teaching and bad test/quiz design, I wouldn't take her again.

Was her first time teaching this class, but it was interesting. Lots of group conversations but you're graded mostly by attendance and weekly quizzes and a few reflection papers. Start the final project early and get with your peers to study for the mid-term and final exams trust.

Taken for family & couple psych. Enjoyable class! Dr. Eads is funny and very engaging. Doesn't go over textbook in class; group activities based on chapters are done instead (not graded). Graded on attendance (mandatory!), online quizzes, semester project, in-person midterm/final. She is funny and informative, not too difficult in my opinion.

enrolled in her memory class excited, but was thoroughly disappointed with the structure of the class.
she teaches straight out of the textbook and doesn't even have slides. we do pointless activities then we are tested NINE chapter units and expected to remember every little study mentioned in the textbook. DO NOT TAKE!!

Some people know the material well and thats great and all but that doesn't mean they should teach. She doesn't have powerpoints she just talks and expects you to take in the information and the stuff she talks about isn't related to the exams. Not a good professor.

Please save yourself the struggle and listen to the other reviews. His lectures have nothing to do with the actual content of the class and rather just ramble on from the PowerPoint however, it's gonna be the same three PowerPoint the whole semester so it's very repetitive just not worth the money. He also changes the syllabus regularly

The lectures focus more on empirically based clinical practices than the textbook so I didn't read most of it. He is repetitive at times but i think the class is meant to be student led. The course is flexible and values students' input. I'd recommend if you're genuinely interested in clinical psych/grad school as he encourages class discussion.
If you want to learn, do not take him. He is easy to take, but if you want to learn, he is not going to help.

There's a paper to sign at the end of every class and its for a grade so go to class. My only complaint is that his lectures would hardly go over the power point and he would repeat the same info we learned in the last class but for WEEKS. Kind of hard to understand through his accent but it gets easier. He gives quiz answers after quizzes.

Dr. Osman was such a caring and funny professor. He always wanted all students to be comfortable in class and encouraged questions. He would take his time and break down answers to quizzes. You would have to try really hard to not get an a in this class. He does have a heavy accent which he jokes about and advises us to ask if we need any repeated
Really can't miss his lectures. They are definitely worth going to otherwise, you may fail the class..

I enjoyed this professor and have taken him before for my intro course. In this class it was test heavy the tests were 30 minutes and all free response so be aware if that my first test was 13 free response questions 10 were fill in the blank and three we had to respond 3-4 sentences. The tests progressively got easier.

DOES NOT ANSWER EMAILS! Will purposely make confusing questions, no matter how good your notes are. Most of my class is frustrated and unsatisfied. Lectures are very clear so I do not understand why he has to make tricky questions, it doesn't help us learn about the content just to be weary of how he words things. Dumb prof
This course is harder than anticipated and you'll get little to no help from the professor. He did not reply to my emails and it's the only class I ever had to withdraw from. Highly do not recommend.

THIS IS NOT A DRILL!!! DO NOT! I REPEAT DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! This is by far the worst class I have taken in all my years of being a student. It is more difficult than Experimental Psychology! Quizzes have mistakes and are extremely difficult. Passing seems near impossible in this class. Save yourself a weekly mental breakdown, and don't.
he's honestly just a really nice guy his assignments are very straightforward and he's very easy to reach id definitely take him again

It was a long class, but the topics and lectures were amazing. The atmosphere of the class was comfortable and I genuinely learned a lot. Attendance isn't mandatory, but highly encouraged because questions from spoken lectures are on the tests and slides are on canvas but are very simple, so she explains them in class. Would defiantly recommend!

Although her class was once a week, she shortened the class period and gave us an intermission break. Very easy to get through, but the quiz won't show up on canvas as an assignment to turn in. Many people missed the quizzes entirely bc of that (just read the syllabus!). She's not very tech savvy, but a sweet lady.

The class is very long, but very informative if you pay attention and take notes! Very sweet professor, and offers extra credit plus one interactive assignment at the end of the year that is easy. There are only 5 online exams, and if you study and take notes you will be good (intro to psychopathology)

A very informative class. It can be challenging, especially with the brain material, but reviewing the slides, using the extra resources, and reading the assignments will keep you on track. The professor is caring and a great teacher. The class consists of three small writing assignments (150 words or less) and exams. I recommend!

Dr. McNaughton shows real interest in what she teaches and in her students. Her lectures were never boring and she explains everything clearly. She is very helpful if you ask her a question. Her tests come from the book and her powerpoints. She is just a very sweet prof.

Asked for help regarding test and was brushed off and told to use critical thinking and intuition which can be frustrating when you're already struggling. Test and quiz questions can be confusing. Slides are word heavy and impersonal I would make sure to pay attention as best as possible. He clearly enjoys the subject I wouldn't recommend though.

Prof Golob is very passionate and excited to share his work with his students. I believe he sometimes forgets to tailor to his audience because of this fact. If you don't come to class, you WILL fail. His exams are process over content; each question requires higher-order thinking. The curves are very generous because they are difficult. (PSY-4193)

This was one of the more challenging classes I've taken and could easily be considered a capstone. The professor is clearly passionate about the material. Exams are application based and require a solid understanding of the concepts. He does offer extra credit opportunities. It's an interesting class, but harder than most PSY courses.

Honestly tried to be positive about the class but when emailing the professor, he would completely skip over some of my questions and give me unhelpful feedback. It's very frustrating when the professor is not that involved with his students as he does appointment only when needed to meet outside of class which is based off his schedule.
Hard grader but it all gets curved.
He's hard to follow and doesn't care if you understand or not

Dr. Pillow is a very good professor. He wants you to succeed so he is always willing to help. I have always struggled with math, but he was always willing to help me truly understand concepts. His lectures are great and really as long as you go to class you will pass.

Prof. Pillow is one of the best instructors I've had. His lectures were well-organized, and clearly explained. The material was a bit challenging for me but I felt like I actually learned something from this class for the semester. I highly recommend taking his class if you get the chance

This professor has helped me understand math and stats to a new level. I had taken two stats classes before psy stats and failed both (in hs and in freshman yr at utsa) but I am currently thriving with Prof. Pillow! Go to class and do the extra cred if needed. there are also online videos and diff resources available. Plus brings his dog to class!
Such an amazing professor. He is a great teacher I enjoyed his lectures a lot as a visual learner.

She is extremely nice and genuinely wants students to succeed. The class is easy and teaches a lot about getting involved in leadership. She is very knowledgeable and always able to answer questions. As long as you attend class and complete the assignments, you will be fine.
Nicest professor on campus! I love Gina!!!
Professor Amatangelo was very kind and helpful when it comes to helping with assignments. I really enjoyed the content she presented and she provided all the resources needed to complete assignments.

Amazing professor and counselor! If you have a problem, as long as you contact her right away she will work with you! Assignment are usually just writing a few sentences on what you learned in a practical assignment. At times, you may be assigned to do off campus work, which is mandatory. But that's where the difficulty stops!

Professor Amatangelo is awesome! She seems very personable and caring, I really wish I had her class in person as mine was online, she made an effort to connect with students as best as she could. During lectures, we would be expected to participate. I took the class as an elective and found it to be very informative.

Dr. Jaramillo is the best PAD professor I've had. I think the material she gives and teaches is helpful for our future careers. She gives great feedback and offers to read our essays days before they are due to see if we're on the right track. I've learned a lot in class. She's also understanding and well-prepared.

Take every class you can with Dr. Jaramillo! One of the most supportive and understanding profs I've encountered. She puts in extra effort to pull together readings so you don't have to buy a book. She will call on you to participate in class, so at least skim the readings before class! This class is writing intensive, but you will learn so much.

I came into this class not even knowing what it was or what I was going to be getting from it, but I actually now love this class. Our morning discussions are always entertaining and Dr. Jaramillo is such a nice professor.

This class is centered on group discussions, she splits the class up into groups of 5 almost every other class. The content is fairly easy. Your grade is based on making a policy memo on a topic you chose, she gives good feedback when she grades papers. There are pop-up class assignments, so while class is not mandatory it is highly encouraged.

There is a lot of group work in class and a lot of in-class participation things that she uses for grades. So if you don't like talking in groups, I wouldn't take her. However, she offers a lot of extra credit that really helps you on exams. Her exams are half multiple choice and half an essay that you submit before the exam class period.

Professor Jaramillo made my days downtown after professor Pina enjoyable and especially with my freshman year experience with AIS. She is a laid back teacher and very caring for students in the AIS curriculum. She really cares for her students and wants students to their best. She is an awesome AIS professor and does not stress us out!
Great Professor!

recentReviews.comment: she's super sweet, if you were lost its mainly if you weren't paying attention or avoid doing any readings she gives, even if you are lost she is willing to help in any shape or form she can. she basically hands us the assignment done with all the links and examples she offers. she's considerate in making the class understandable.

Although the homework is very difficult to do and understand, she drops the two lowest grades on assignments. She also understanding and willing to help. Attendance is mandatory to pass the class with a decent grade.

Dr. Romero is an AMAZING professor. I am taking another of her classes this semester. You can't skip class and expect to do well. Her lectures are interesting and she is happy to clarify if necessary. Participate, read the material and take notes! She doesn't read off slides, she actively teaches. She is understanding and wants you to learn.

Seems like an easy class, you show up and youll learn nothing pretty much. All semester I was super lost. We had two different books. When it came down to a test she would pull questions from both books which made it difficult to study. If you can take another professor please do so.

If you have other options, take a different professor and course. She never updates grades into Blackboard. I had to submit weekly journals that were just never up par in her eyes. Really have to work for my grade. Btw, civic engagement is such a boring subject to learn about. Trust me.

Dr. Delgado is very strict when it comes to the syllabus and grading, so he will not be lenient when it comes to late/missed assignments, and he will not clarify anything he will just tell you to go back to the syllabus. The class was fairly easy, just short weekly quizzes and no exams or projects.

Easiest class ever. There were ten total assignments. They were all quizzes composed of 5 or 10 questions. He gave two attempts on most of them and three on some of them. He provides a PowerPoint that essentially goes over all the questions on the quiz. Would recommend this professor.

super easy class, and he makes the expectations clear in the syllabus- weekly quizzes and no final exam. all the quizzes have multiple attempts and esp in the beginning i really didnt even have to read the ppts to do well. if you want to actually learn you can def do it with this class, but if you just want an easy A this is the class for u lol

Professor Delgado is an amazing teacher, though his assignments can be a bit much if you allow yourself enough time to get the assignments done, you'll be fine. He is very homework heavy and can sometimes be confusing, but as long as you ask questions, you will definitely pass. He is amazing and I can not wait to take him again next semester!

The work itself is not bad. It is long and writing-inclusive. The reason for my bad review is that there is no way to contact this professor. He says he is reachable by email but he has only once replied to one of many many emails. He says he will allow us to re-submit work but there is no option to. Due to this I feel as if I was graded unfairly.

recentReviews.comment: lecture is simple and so is the homeowrk

Don't buy textbook, I did not use it. I studied with the lectures. Get a good seat and people around you, you will be doing work with them the whole semester. Tests aren't difficult nor are the assignments.

extremely test heavy. he has a test every 2 weeks, and it's also so much information. he uses honorlock and gets mad when it doesn't work, even tries to blame it on the students. rarely, if ever, replies outside of class. avoid this class if you're an anxious test taker. and all of his lectures aren't even done by him.

I had him for 2 classes and I got an A+ in both. Theories of Health Behavior online and Human Disease Etiology, Treatment and Prevention in-person. There should be no reason you should not get an A as long as you do your work and follow the instructions. He's a good professor and gives out extra credit. Tip would be to always cite your sources.

Super kind professor. There were on average 3 assignments a week, 3 total exams, and one group project at the end of the semester that counts as the final. He offers several extra credit opportunities. He is very understanding of personal situations and cares about the well-being of his students.

Dr. GB was a great professor. Lectures were weekly with in class assignments. You definitely need to attend class to earn a good grade, as there are attendance grades and in class assignments. He explains things well and gives great feedback on assignments. Exam reviews definitely help. Just attend class and you'll do well.
This is the perfect class where you can you have easy weekly assignments and the chapter quizzes take less that 5 minutes. Failing this class would require you to not show up and turn nothinh in.
He is literally the best professor. He does take attendance but going to class helps so much. Overall he is my favorite professor and I will be taking him again next semester.
Professor Baniya is amazing!!! I recommend taking him! he is a great guy.

One of the nicest professors I have ever had. He is so caring and strives for our success. There is a lot of extra credit opportunities and there are a lot of group assignments so you get to know the people around you well to help for the final project. He is super accommodating for the assignments. I loved having him as my 1st-semester professor.

She is SO sweet and caring! If you are struggling, reach out and she WILL help you. The course was also very easy and tests were online and open note. Attendance is technically mandatory but she helps you if you miss anything. AMAZING professor!
Super sweet professor. Everybody never missed class, even though attendance wasn't technically mandatory. She is totally understanding and cares about her students.
Just not good. #rude

I honestly really enjoyed this class. Very project heavy but when started are really easy to complete and understand. I was able to get very ahead in this class because I would knock out projects weeks in advance but overall I would say this is a pretty easy A class and I think the professor makes it really hard to fail.
You receive an automatic 0 on any assignment that is a minute late. No point deduction, no make ups. And although she uses AI to explain assignments she still some how manages to make them confusing.

Personal Health is a class UTSA makes you take that is designed to waste both your time and money. The instructions for a lot of the assignments are unclear and there are no opportunities to fix an assignment that you messed up. If you get the chance to take this class with another professor, do it.

I've taken 2 classes already with Professor Doyle and would recommend her!! There is quite some work but it's very easy. Just don't do it last minute because she's strict on deadlines and how she grades. Also no exams and no final which is also a plus.

Took her for Survey of Health and Drugs, but it wasn't on here. Pretty easy, just don't slack off. She does let you submit things a little late, even though the syllabus states otherwise. If you abuse that though she will give you a zero. Overall easy class.
not much going on in this class. a few discussion boards and thats like it. no web cams, no set times. Have fun!!

She has poor communication skills and speaks to students in a condescending tone. Her attitude creates an unwelcoming learning environment. As for grading, he's lets you know exactly what your work needs to ensure the best grade possible. I absolutely would take the class again.

Absolutely loved Prof DeLeon's class on Satan and the Occult! I hope he is able to teach this course again so others can experience! This class isn't for everyone due to subject matter, but if you want to put a little more thought on the duality of good and evil and the devil and witches, this class will leave you a lot to think about!

Highly recommend for all the pre-meds out there because the amount of information learned by the different cases is astronomical. No final btw
Super sweet guy. Just show up and take notes. The exams are derived from the slides. He takes at least 2 breaks per class. I highly recommend if you are interested in premed

Only graded based on 3/4 exams. Attendance not mandatory but it is a must because he shows images that will be tested on. Tests are 50 questions multiple choice. Only meet once a week for 3hrs. We would get two breaks each class around 10/15 mins each. We would also play Kahoot and some of those questions would be on the exams.

A lovely, gentle guy with lots of golden nuggets and stories throughout class. If you're not interested in medicine, this class will bore you (very long!), but I LOVED this class. Easy A as long as you attend, take notes, study the handouts, and pay attention to the photos (they are NOT all provided in his PPTs, but WILL be on the test).

Lectures were pretty dry and a little hard to pay attention to. No textbook use, and outlines are posted ahead of time. While attendance isn't mandatory, he often shows images as "cases of the day" that will be on exams. He's a little soft spoken, but not too bad. Only grades in the class are 4 exams, and the highest 3 are taken. An 85+ is an A.

Dr. H does NOT let you fail his class. While the content is difficult, he alleviates it by offering online lectures the class before an exam, extra credit GALORE, and interesting food related mnemonics. Talk to him, come to class, and study hard!

Dr. H is amazing. His tests are difficult, but he drops lowest exam. Attendance is mandatory but you get 4 skips before it affects grade. Extra credit for every exam. Weekly assignments but lowest are dropped. Does detailed reviews before exams. He is really passionate and interested in our success!!! TAKE HIM!
Best anatomy professor
This class was rigorous but fair. And he gives out extra credit for exams.

Tests are difficult however super similar to what youll see when youre testing for entrance exams. Dr. H just likes to prepare his students for real life through his courses. Attendance is mandatory but he makes learning fun. Also creates review sessions for each test.I've taken him for both A&P l and ll and have really appreciated him as a prof.

Punches above her classes' paygrade, Will grade assignments months after assignment, will humiliate students for asking questions she doesn't like, and will give a 0 for any assignment missed if not present for class without exception, deflecting blame to higher ups and making it "out of her control"

Class is easy, but the way it's run is frustrating. If you miss a day, you're basically on your own because she won't go over what you missed. She also posts essay assignments a day before they're due, which is stressful. She can come off as rude and is really picky over small details. Not a hard class, just not a good experience.

Wonderful professor! Most definitely would take this class again if I could! I highly recommend taking this class if needed for a credit, however showing up to class, good communication with Collen Witt, doing assignments are important for this class. However, this class is easy no need for stress for this class.

Dr. Witt had a very organized class with clear expectations. The class is entirely graded off of participation and attendance. She was very entertaining to listen to and she cared so much about each of her students individually. If you can take her, I would 100% recommend her you will have a blast and it will be an easy 100!
Professor Witt is amazing! You can tell that she truly cares for her students. This class was super easy and stress-free. I %1000000 recommend Professor Witt. Very easy class and a great professor.

I took this class in Spring 2021 and it was super easy and laid back. While mostly discussion based, we did have one group project with a partner and an essay we had to write. Just make sure to read the required materials and have something to discuss in class. The schedule and structure is super flexible.

Theres only two assignments all semester & the rest of your grade comes from attendance & participation. Very lowkey class and a super chill professor, but he can be kinda all over the place so sometimes his requirements are a little unclear. Overall a cool dude and fun class but be prepared for a very loose schedule and curriculum.

Graded based mostly on participation, one group project (in pairs), and one essay. Class is mostly just discussion of the assigned book or articles. He would cut class early a lot because we looked sad, haha. Lot's of discourse and political talk (between students); he's overall really chill and understanding.

Super informal guy with a great sense of humor. Since he's an Honors professor he can generally rely on the students to do their own work. He gets distracted easily so lectures can be uninformative but if you read the assigned material you will learn everything you need.

Brent is a solid dude. He jokes non-stop, but usually gets through his lecture info. If not, it's all pretty easy stuff. Just study the book, if you have it, or quizlet for the tests. He likes to give out extra credit when attendance is low, so make sure to be there if you need it. Also, watch the movies, they end up on the tests.

recentReviews.comment: Took her GenderRep & if you dont like to talk dont join her class. We sat in silence for 5 minutes at a time bc she would have "the talkers" not talk bc she wanted the quiet ones to talk. It was uncomfortable & many times she came off as playfully rude. By the end of the semester most of us didnt want to go to class bc of how she spoke to people

Professor Glover is great at facilitating important discussions and isn't afraid to help students challenge their preconceived notions. I respect her so much for that! Her grading/teaching style isn't for everyone i guess, but I personally got a lot from this course. 10/10 for her!

Professor Glover is a good teacher; however, she makes a 3 credit class have the workload of a 6 credit class. There were 4 written essays, each had to be written in 35 mins each, as well as an oral exam and 30 reading guides. Overall a good course, but a HUGE time sink. Useful if you want to learn self-awareness, but beware of the workload.

Horrible class, her grading criteria is so confusing and she offers no help. The exams were impossible to do well on and were worth more than everything we had done over the semester. this class felt so long and overwhelming

Professor Glover knows a lot about different things, but I really disliked this class. We had weekly readings that were quite long and whereas reading shouldn't be an issue in university, this is a one credit hour class with a course load of a three credit hours. Moreover, each reading had short answer quizzes. She also grades incredibly slowly!
online course, very fun and interesting. Lectures are fun to watch and it was not overwhelming. Good elective

Easiest class ever! You must watch the lectures to receive participation points-- but they are so interesting! There are quizzes every Friday unless it is an exam. I absolutely love this class and the way Professor Hamilton teaches it. I would take another class of his if I could.
Quizzes every Friday minus exam days, lectures count as a participation grade. 3 exams, 4th is optional if you're happy with your grade. Pretty easy going class!

I took this class as an elective and it was surprisingly fun. I did not think I would find much interest in this field but watching the weekly videos seemed to peak my interest. As someone who struggles with classes that fall under the subject of science: I think I did pretty well. Most of the grades depend on quizzes but they are fairly easy.

Anthropology 1013 is an intriguing class. Professor Hamilton has really detailed lectures. It is great because he allows multiple attempts on quizzes. There is a quiz every Friday except on test Fridays. Information is to the point. Very fun class if you love anthropology.

If there are any other instructors you can take, please do. She causes unnecessary stress due to the amount of times she changes instructions and adds on new specifications. I don't think I will ever take this professor again.

I would never take this professor again. She isn't as helpful as she claims to be, and overcomplicates tasks. Although she states she makes everything clear, she often contradicts instructions she's already given.

Funny, open-minded, very clearly passionate about what she does and cares a lot about her students. Attendance is graded and you learn much more from being in class than just reading off the slides at home, but I found class so engaging I didn't mind attending! I felt actually prepared when doing tests for this course. Great teacher, great course.

She was ok. Her lessons were great and engaging, but she's very strict. If you do an assignment and forget to print it you will get no credit. Her tests have to do with the last 5 lessons so try your best to study or you'll be cooked

I had to take this course for credit but I absolutely loved Dr. Moon. Her lectures are very interesting and she's super down to earth. Only thing that could be intimidating is that there's absolutely no electronic use in the classroom.

This class is manageable. Professor gives good lectures but sometimes the information is hard to remember since its most likely the first time learning about primates, etc. When it comes to the tests, you have two chances to take it and it is always open note. Lab reports take a bit of time but are well guided by her instructions.

Straightforward and easy class. She can be awkward at times but her lectures are pretty informative. Weekly module and quiz with a few tests and assignments. I really recommend getting the textbook as the modules and quizzes revolve heavily around the weekly chapter. Overall easy class if you read the book and attend lectures.

She can be a bit awkward at times but you get used to it over time. Class is mostly just lectures and then a group activity which counts as attendance at the end of class. Exams follow lectures so honestly the textbook isn't needed (except for maybe the homework modules). Weekly homework modules and like a 3 question quiz. Pretty easy tbh.

Prof. Barkwill Love- Pretty steady class and only four exams. She is a bit awkward sometimes but you will get used to it over time. She does do group activities as a participation grade and for attendance. Her book was not needed and her tests came straight from the lectures. Lectures were pretty interesting as an intro course. Overall, fairly easy

Professor Barkwill Love is an AMAZING professor, at times she can go off on tangents but she is so passionate about her subject. If you show up to class and participate in the iclicker points then you will defiantly pass. I didn't buy the textbook and i passed easily, but she does have the book on reserve at the library.
Robert was a very sweet guy and very passionate about the course, but the hybrid format was a little confusing. I fell behind and lost motivation. Don't be like me.

i loved this professor! we had a hybrid class, so we had to do a lot of textbook reading. but he gave extra credit and was clearly very passionate about his work. graded the written exam really harsh however. he does use iclicker quizzes but they're easy

This Professor only grades by the 5 QUESTIONS he does at the beginning of class and feels like he only gives 20 seconds at most to answer before moving on. there had been a few cases where students weren't able to answer in time and that will be an automatic 0 points given for that question out of 5. nonetheless he is a good person.

Dr. Hard is great! He's been in the business of archaeology for a long time and it really shines through his lectures. I took intro to archaeology with him and the course was a great balance between the science of archaeology and the humanism of anthropology. He cares about his students and he's always available to answer questions. Go for it!

Professor Hard has good intentions but this class simply isn't organized. There's miscommunication between Hard and the TA which causes confusion among students. The tests rely a lot on lectures which are hard to follow. I suggest to read the book and try to comprehend it as best as you can because you're going to be teaching yourself a lot here.
If you need a science credit, take this class!!! It is super easy yet interesting and will not cause additional stress. I would highly recommend.

Professor Holdbrook is very passionate and knows a lot about what she teaches. Going to every single lecture will give yourself the best chance in doing well in this class because not only will you understand each unit better but will also be very astonished in the material you learn, in my opinion.
She makes the class interesting even if you aren't into science really.

She was a very good professor, but she just read from the slides and she didn't make much eye contact; she was mostly looking at the wall behind the us. Her lab assignments are very extensive and require a lot of time, which most of us don't have, but if you contact her, you can work things out. Quizzes, labs and exams are online.

Professor Holdbrook's passion for anthropology translates into engaging lectures. She is also great to work with (I submitted the wrong data sheet with my lab report and she let me fix my mistake for full credit). Textbook is free online and attendance is for extra credit (up to 5 pts added to final grade). Overall, loved her and loved this class.

I rated the difficulty a four, mainly in the context of this being an online course. It wouldn't be anything out of the ordinary of an in-person course. Class was easy to get an A. The labs take a lot of time, you just have to buckle down and put in the work for them. Like I had to stare at primates and jot everything they did for an hour. not fun.
TA grades everything. Research project is worth half your grade. Quizzes are pretty difficult, they're timed and you can't go back once you answer a question. Not a big fan over all

The quizzes have nothing to do with the lecture videos. She rewords the questions on purpose to try to trick you. Also, her grammar is all over the place, and she has an issue with misspelling words on quizzes, which makes it harder to understand the questions.
This class was super disappointing. You don't really learn about primates, you just learn the general behavior all of them share. Super boring class wouldn't recommend.

Professor Wikberg was very informative and it was fun to get to learn so much from someone so passionate. The class was well structured and I always either knew what I was doing or knew that I could reach out to either Professor Wikberg or our TA for help. Great class, would recommend if Biological Anthropology sounds interesting at all!
Super easy class. The professor is very passionate, and the material is interesting. Quizzes and exams are straightforward, and as long as you complete everything on time, you'll be fine.
Great class.Great professor.

I took this course online and it's the easiest course I've ever taken. The workload looks like a lot, but it's not that bad. You can tell the professor really cares about anthropology and makes lectures interesting. The quizzes and tests are not proctored. There's only 2 labs and they look hard at first, but not too bad. Overall super easy class.
super cool prof and interesting class his assignments were intimidating but nothing crazy

his quizzes are all from his provided lecture material, but his test are a little all over the place.  he will work with you on late assignments and exams, just communicate with him.  i would take his class again.

recentReviews.comment: Really great professor who cares about students.

This was a fabulous class. I decidedd to major in anthropology because of this class. I'm still not sure if I'll go into archaeology but Dr. Bria has inspired me to think much more broadly about my career and the possibilities for it. She is such a wonderful and inspirational teacher.

Everyone's thinking it, but I'll be the one to say it: This woman is hot as hell.

Good professor too.
Professor Bria is pretty great. Super understanding and really goes above and beyond to help you do well in class.

I really enjoyed taking this class with Dr. Bria. I was not really interested in archaeology at all before and I was kind of intimidated by the science of it allbut she did a really good job of explaining everything and giving us examples from her own research. I hope to go on Dr. Bria's field school when she teaches it again because she's so good.

This “research professor” hasn't presented in almost 2 years! Yet, she has an incredible ego that supersedes her unwillingness to post a photo of herself. With such a small number of faculty available, you'll be forced to take her classes. Beware, she is dangerous.

Second class w/ her. Reading, lecture video, and open book quiz per week. 3 open-book take-at-home exams, Excel group project, and 2-page paper. Chance to work with artifacts. She does helpful reviews for the exams and helps for final project. Attendance is a must. Lots of reading, and lectures can be boring. Pay attention in class and get easy A.

Dr. Levi is an incredibly caring professor and is very kind hearted overall. Her class was not very interesting and was lecture heavy, but her lectures had all the answers to any tests/quizzes we had to take. Her assignments were simple and she often had videos where she talked you through how to do the assignment or just gave the answers.

Overall good professor. Weekly readings and quiz plus two tests and one-page paper. The paper/quizzes/tests are easy and open book. Tests are taken at home. Gives lots of time to complete assignments. Readings are long. Attendance is mandatory. Lectures can be boring for some but are useful. PowerPoints are provided. Slow grader. Easy extra credit.

I would avoid taking her class for ANT2043, I have never struggled with a class as much as this one and I have straight A's. I ended up dropping this class because the material was confusing and she made it hard to understand and was not helpful. Pre recorded lectures, she is very monotone, might be better in person if that is an option for you.

A lot of writing assignments. As time goes on in class, the assignments got less interesting and more busy work-like. Takes forever to put grades in, even with TA help. Finals and other large projects are unnecessarily time consuming and difficult. I learned that it doesn't matter if I write well, it matters if it looks like AI.

Professor has her office hours available yet constantly changes them. Her and her TA grade assignments every 3-4 weeks after submission and locked assignments so you can't re-submit or withdraw work. Accused me of plagiarizing on work based on a personal experience, and when contacted, already took off full credit for two assignments.

This class is ridiculously demanding for an intro level course. The readings are interesting but heavy. She's strict with deadlines. I accidentally turned in the wrong doc for part of one assignment and she showed no mercy and my grade plummeted. RIP my 4.0. Work is dull and repetitive. Take someone else, she killed my interest in cultural anthro.

Not sure why initial review got removed.  If this class wasn't mandatory then I wouldn't have taken it with this instructor.  She grades on her own curve and or opinions despite it being supported personal viewpoints. She doesn't seem to tech savvy for an online class.

I actually took her death and dying course and it was the worst course I have ever taken at UTSA. Her assignments are very lengthy and unreasonable. Her grading style is trash and she doesn't have a clear grading style, not to mention I never received any feedback on why I received the grades I did. I absolutely DO NOT RECCOMMEND!!!

I took this class as an elective, it's difficult to say how hard it was because it's actually pretty easy but has ALOT of assigned reading, it's actually important too because it's discussed I groups in class and is a big part of the exams which are written in person. If you don't mind reading or class participation this class is fun and easy.

A lot of readings but if you happen to miss any they are talked about during class and easy to understand roughly what they were talking about. If you miss any classes it is hard to understand in the next class. He talks a lot but makes it funny and interesting. That being said, you can miss the first 10 minutes and not miss any material.

Overall my favorite professor so far! He makes class very interesting and cracks jokes a lot which made class very engaging.There is a lot of readings but the readings are actually interesting and they explain a lot. Super chill and little to no homework and the test are extremely easy as well!

Professor Gallagher is a great professor, but there is a TON of reading. Overall, his lectures can be a little boring but not all the time.

One Tip: Make sure to keep on top of your readings because once you get behind it is almost impossible to catch back up...

Definitely attend class and look at his powerpoints. There are biweekly quizzes and SAQ's for each module and a few exams. It is definitely a good amount of free response and not too much multiple choice when it comes to exams. There is plenty of reading that is required daily.
