recentReviews.comment: To find a professor who puts in as much effort as Dr. Cepek is RARE and hard to find. I'm not an Anthropology major, but his class was intriguing and thought-provoking. He is truly a wonderful professor, and I would highly recommend taking his class.

Mike is great. He really cares about his students, and he doesn't make his class overly difficult. Its best if you show up for his class but the tests are based off powerpoints only so you arent penalized for not making it to class.

Professor Cepek is an amazing teacher. He is extremely passionate about what he teaches and he will meet you where you are at. His TA Moureen is also amazing and she is suer helpful. The class is honestly so eye-opening and he made me love anthropology. All his classes are great and I recommend them all. Especially Cultural Anthropology.

Cepek is a good guy who obviously cares about what he does and cared about his students. Biggest assignment is a five page paper describing three books, so be sure to actually read them! Other than that, very easy class, easy 100s for weekly discussions and he allows 3 missed posts and replies without penalties. Definitely recommend him!

Professor Cepek made me fall in love with Anthropology! His lectures are always engaging and he is wonderfully laid back in class. He assigns lots of readings but they're honestly not hard to get through and you could even get away with skimming over them. He will support you if you need help so don't be afraid to ask! 10/10 would recommend

It is pretty straight forward, the syllabus is pretty self explanatory about what the schedule will be for the semester. "Not reading", some people were not reading the question correctly - all tests and quizzes are open book. Take notes of what she says, as these might be on those quiz/tests. She's teaching at 3 diff places. Would take again.

Prof Clemmons was AMAZING and this has been my favorite college class I have ever taken. The class isn't an easy A, but as long as you go to class and study the bare minimum you will do fine. She does require sketches each week but they are an easy grade. She is extremely knowledgable and truly cares about forensic anthropology. TAKE THIS CLASS!

This professor definitely made my first semester of college a living hell. She is TERRIBLE at responding to emails or questions being asked. Her grading criteria makes no sense whatsoever . Be ready to be super stressed when taking this class because you have to be DEDICATED as she said in order to pass this class.

Unaccessible. Doesnt communicate with class. Study material doesnt prepare you for exams or quiz questions that are mostly open ended. I dont recall having any multiple choice questions all semester. Easily offended and rude.

Doesn't seem to care at all. Posts weekly assignments and quizzes late so you don't get the whole week/day to work on them. Says class isnt mandatory but punishes students for not going. DOESNT ANSWER EMAIL. I've never had a more UNaccessable prof. Was super excited to take this class and she ruined it for me.
Great guy, show up and you're pretty much guaranteed an A
Super entertaining lectures, and he was clearly super passionate about what he teaches. Made me actually want to show up to every class.

Pretty cool guy, you can tell that he really enjoys his job and is super passionate. Open-note weekly quizzes are very much based on the videos and lectures from the week, tests are super similar. Being on time and present in class I'd say is important, and every now and then we would look at physical artifacts brought in.

Dr. Kosiba is super sweet and nice! Super easy class, all of the quizzes and exams are online and he makes a point to make it as easy on you as possible. Attendance is mandatory, but lectures weren't too bad or anything.

Dr. Kosiba is a great, caring professor. Exams are super, super easy and attendance is mandatory but he is super lenient and gives you 4 freebies. 100% take him for your freshman year anthropology class :)
Prof. Halvaksz is an amazing lecturer. He tells fun personal stories and is clearly very passionate on the subject. The class will be easy if you pay attention and take notes.

Halvaksz is a great professor for anthropology. He responds very promptly to emails and offers good feedback on assignments. His lectures and assignments are super neat, we watched many interesting films

I loved taking Dr. Halvaksz' "Media, Power, and Public Culture" class. He is extremely entertaining and his lectures were great. The workload is manageable and the films we watched were very fun to watch. There's a lot of reading but it's all pretty easy to read. I'm an art history major and this class was a lot of fun.
Dr. H is one of the best professors Ive ever had! His lectures are really cool and actually fun to attend. homework is basically minimal reading or watching a cool film.
Dr. H is awesome. Hes a great professor and loves to help his students. He genuinely loves his job and loves to see students succeed!! ANT2053 was a fun class definitely would take it again

Love Dr. Brown. Took her for Frauds, Myths and Mysteries. The lectures, and readings were so interesting. It was the most fun class I have ever took at UTSA. Dr. Brown is funny, engaging, and caring. No h/w, only 1 or 2 major papers and I believe 4 Exams. She gives a study guide and study review sessions before exams. I am taking her again.

Great professor and rather easy course. You have a textbook, but she posts it on bb, so no need to buy it. You really don't even have to touch it, all tests are based on lectures. The tests are rather easy and she is a generous grader for the essays. She is available outside of class and responds to all emails in depth. Very interesting course too.

Lectures are everything and are very interesting. Not alot of reading at all. Exams are difficult and consist of essay component. But if you study off the review and pay attention to notes you can do well. She is extremely nice and helpful with any questions and encourages everyone to learn.

Dr. Brown was an okay teacher. Her voice is nasally and kind of annoying but she is brilliant! Her lectures were very entertaining and informative and this was a really fun class. BEWARE that 90% of your grade is exams and they're MC, TF, and both short AND long essays. KNOW YOUR STUFF. There's 1 paper worth 10% of your grade. Lectures not on BB!

Great professor! She really loves what she does and it shows in the lectures. The tests a bit more work than the average (25 multiple choice plus a short and long essay, all having to be done w/i the 50 minutes) but if you know the material, you'll be okay. She really cares about her students grades and was always willing to meet up.

took it as an online course, lots of homework for an elective class, felt like busy work especially as there were 3 major assignments throughout the semester. Exams aren't hard as they are fully online and study guides are provided

Professor Pozzi's class was very simple and easy to understand. Everything is straightforward - highly recommend if you need a GPA boost or a easy science to knock out. Just make sure you submit your assignments and such on time and you should be good!

Great professor that shows a strong passion for anthropology. His lectures are easy to follow and assignments are given clear grading instructions. 10/10 would recommend taking this class with professor Pozzi
Very understanding professor and lectures are very interesting. Would 100% take again!

He's really a good professor. He explains everything so well and wants students to succeed. He's always available if you need help. His class is always interactive and a discussion rather than just powerpoint which I really enjoyed. 10/10 recommend!

Professor Rosenberg is awesome! Just make sure to pay attention in class, keep up with the quizzes, and reach out to her if you need any help. She is really helpful and if you happen to miss an assignment there is enough extra credit to help make up for it.
Super easy class. we did a museum project and when with our group to the san Antonio art museum

Very fun, easy to talk to professor. She shows a lot of care towards her students and remembered all of our names in her class. Tons of extra credit, very lenient on due dates, always willing to help her students.

I honestly loved this class because you could tell she was really passionate about what she was talking about, so it was easy to follow along. Of course, there's going to be a lot of reading, it's a literature class but the texts she provides are usually not hard reads or when they were there are free audiobooks on YouTube.
I love Prof. Rosenberg's classes! The subject matter is always interesting, and her delivery methods are always fun and engaging. If it were possible I would take a new class from her every semester.

Professor Masten is a great professor, very knowledgeable about art history. Her class has quizzes at the end of every week. She has in person activities that count for credit. These activities are listed in the syllabus so they're easy to keep track of. Overall easy class, just keep showing up.

Super caring and knowledgable professor! It's clear she knows a lot about her subject, and lectures are always interesting. Attendance isn't mandatory unless there's an assignment in class, but I'd suggest going anyways as there are weekly quizzes based on the lectures. No textbook needed. Really easy and fun class

The only thing I would warn future students to do is remind yourselves for the quizzes due every Sunday. They are super simple and quick to finish with only 8 questions that were covered in lectures and slides, but super easy to forget!! Attendance is not mandatory, but the activities are only done in class.

Professor Maten is an excellent professor, she has a true passion for her course making her class very entertaining and interesting. Attendance is not mandatory unless there is an in class assignment. Amazing professor absolutely take her!

Her class structure really didn't make sense with the assignments we had to do. She would lecture over topics for us to not use them. The whole class was centered on a presentation that she wanted us to submit for the COLFA showcase. She had a reader-grader that left confusing points off and she would end up having to grade it herself anyway.

She is a good professor, though her TA grades everything so it takes a second for her to get back to you regarding assignment grade. There's videos to watch each week, things to read, etc. It very hard failing this class because the quizzes reflect a lot of the videos. Discussion posts can be heavy sometimes but not hard.

The class was enjoyable! Even though I'm not a big lover of the subject, it was still fun. There is no reason why you shouldn't receive an A if you simply watch the videos and read the content. The group conversation can be challenging and need well-considered answers, but everything is doable if you don't put it off.

Easiest class you can take online. Around 2-3 assignments that are so easy and quick to take, exams are 20 questions that aren't monitored. She is also very nice and genuinely likes teaching, but if you do not care about art, easy A on her class

Whatever you do never take this class with this professor. She honestly takes too long in grading the assignments making you wait for weeks to a month. You are given only a week to write an 8 page essay completely for the final. Also the weekly discussions slowly  dwindling down to a couple of people who have survived in this class.

This course online is not ideal. Discussion posts and replies are fine and the readings behind them are interesting, but the amount of information given per week is ridiculous. Feedback is very vague and the "museum visits" are annoying. Not the worst class or professor but u gotta be on top of things for sure.
Provides clear instructions for assignments & gives great feedback!

Katherine is a good professor her assignments are well organzied and her grading criteria shows what she is looking for in her submissions, However your'e assignments are all discussion boards and muiltple peer reviews in every submission. The TA was probably the worse when it came to this class she would take off points for silly reasons.
This class requires you to do “Mood Boards” she doesn't provide feedback if you get a bad grade, so be prepared to keep asking for feedback

If you're dealing with a tough situation at home, I wouldn't recommend this class. I reached out to Prof. Deck-Portillo about personal issues affecting my attendance, as advised, but never received a response or meeting invite. Other professors responded promptly and showed concern, but she didn't acknowledge my email, which was disappointing.
This was a very interesting class, I learned so much about art history. I enjoyed it. Although it was an easy class, it was great.

I enjoyed Professor Johnson's Art of the Holocaust course online. She's a great online professor and the class is flexible. Professor Johnson gives you weekly assignments, but it's at your own pace to where you could get things done a bit early if you wanted to, which helped me. Also, she gives detailed feedback. Highly recommend.

The entire class was based off of about 10 discussions where we had to use the text that she chose for that week (we had to buy about 3 books ourselves aside from the textbook, the rest she provided). Even when I used information that was only found in the resources, I still lost points. The only extra credit provided was multiple page book review.

I loved this professor! It was an online class though so there was a lot of self-teaching, but she gave good feedback on discussion posts and had interesting content. I took her for both "World of Vermeer" and "Art and the Holocaust," and made an A and A+. Great online professor :).

Be prepared for weekly essays and extremely long chapter readings. Each chapter reading averages about 25 pages of dense, incomprehensible, and highly pretentious writing. Additionally, they're PDF formatted - you can't use the "find" button to easily find information, and if you hate squinting at your screen to read tiny letters, buy the book.

Overall she was okay. I ended with an A+ from learning everything on my own. Half of this course was online so wed have weekly mini essays I had to look up everything on my own to understand it. Khan Academy and youtube videos will be your best friend to comprehend the content.

This is a decade over.  But I need to speak up.  When I took this professor.  I was dealing with a SA report. She is knowledgeable and there is an interest in my culture and my people but in the lens of from a European perspective. I missed more than enough classes. She talked me out of withdrawing. (1)
attend the lectures, read the syllabus - you'll do well. easiest class ive taken and her lectures are nice to get through. very passionate about art which i liked!
I was able to reach the prof via email and office hours which was very useful. As long as you attend lectures you will pass.

(Took an upper level class with her) She is very knowledgeable and has information-heavy lectures. However, she loves speaking with students about their thoughts on the lecture or art history in general. There is a bit of reading, but assignments are completely manageable. I learned the most in this AHC class than any other class!

Dr. Eckmann is a wonderful professor. Very easy to communicate with and understandable. Treats students with respect and expects students to do the work. There is a lot of reading required for this class to understand the material being covered. Lectures are posted on Blackboard. Wants students to succeed!
The best of the best!
He is actually  the GREATEST PROFESSOR EVER. He is so inspirational and makes it so easy to understand his course while expressing your passion for art.

One of my favorite professors ever! I don't know why he has such low ratings. He is extremely easy to talk to and his class is very well organized. He may change the syllabus sometimes but it's nothing unnecessary. I wish I could take all of his contemporary art classes. He's extremely supportive and inspiring. Take him if you love art history.

No one could even get in contact with him the whole semester via email or blackboard. We had to message the TA for our problems, I felt like she was the professor instead of him. His instructions arent clear, a lot of the work still has the dates from the Fall 2020 semester so it's hard to see when something is due (timewise and date wise).

I took his summer course, and while it isn't a hard course, it is a bit dull. He really enjoys listening to himself talk, and he often starts to get so immersed in talking about a piece that he gets behind on his syllabus. Not necessarily a hard class, but not really an enjoyable AHC course. Be prepared for lectures to run past the end of class.

Dr. Wiersema is an amazing professor. Graduate work is often difficult but her courses make grad school fun. Her course on Andean art history was extremely interesting. There were lots of lectures and some fun group assignments, as well.

I had Dr. Wiersema 4 times at UTSA and I honestly wish I could've taken her more. She is so understanding and makes her lectures easy to follow. If you have any interest in Pre-Columbian art, you should take her courses. My grades were completely dependent on how much I worked that semester, two A's in AHC 4423/AHC 4933, and two C's in AHC 4933.

I loved taking her class and I really learned a lot. Yes, there is a lot of reading.. There is also a lot of writing, but she makes the prompt pretty clear so it's not that difficult if you read and pay attention to the material. She also takes the time out to give feedback and answers emails quickly. I really liked her.

Assignments due every day 4 days out of the week, each day you have to read at least 10 pages-full chapters out of the textbook (she recommends setting aside 4-5 hours per day for reading) and write a 250 minimum discussion post, and respond to two other students. You're allowed to miss 2-3 discussion assignments without it affecting your grade.

There are only 5 classes in this class but that's because it was a hybrid class. Definitely go to class since it's only one time a week. You can tell she is truly in love with Art History. I loved hearing her lecture every week and I wish I could take her for every Art History class. She also influenced me to change my major to Art History. :)

ART 1143.courseName: Art for Non Art Majors: Paint

Fall 2022.title: Art for Non Art Majors: Paint

recentReviews.comment: hiromi is a amazing professor, i had her for foundations one and drawing two and while she runs a tight ship she is 100% the best professor ive had she has really pushed me to be a better artist

Be prepared to draw A LOT. She expects you to dedicate all of your time to her class as a full-time student, which is unrealistic. She is very project-oriented and assigns them on a weekly basis. It's super frustrating because a lot of students do not finish them on time with the heavy workload. It's not easy to communicate with her either.

Hiromi is really great, I made my Rate My Professor account to give her a 5/5. Very knowledgeable about everything covered in the class as well as great at helping you improve your work. She is really charming and a joy to talk to. You will need to do a lot of work outside of class, but all of the projects assigned are great practice and enjoyable.

Hiromi was an amazing instructor. She truly cares about her class and she expects you to always be in class. She allows three absences until it will start to affect your grade. She expects that you are truly committed to her class and that you always should be working outside of the time you meet. She's truly caring and wants everyone to exceed!

Hiromi is great. She wants you to do well and you can tell. It was hard with online since explaining techniques is hard but it was a great class still. She was so supportive and her personal experience was the last push I needed to change my major to art.

This guys a legend man. He gives lots of time on assignments and is very understanding. even posts make- up exams towards the end of the semester to help you out. Too bad it was just a art class, he's a good guy and professor.
Professor Saenz is a good professor to take since his exams and quizzes are straightforward and based off of his PowerPoint notes. Easy A if you pay attention and complete all the assignments.

Work is not particularly hard, but it is tiring and there's a lot of it.  Not a lot of room for unique spins on project ideas.  Professor can be picky about subject matter, so just stick to painting photographs or completely abstract pieces.  Don't miss class more than 3 times or your grade will take a huge hit.

I absolutely dreaded her class. She would introduce the project but then change her mind later in the week after several had already started working on it. It was obvious that everyone in the class, me included, collectively put in less effort into their projects as the semester went on because she asked for too much.

This class was okay at first but then she started to strip away creativity. She will always find something to critique even if your project looks near perfect. Critiques on Mondays and then sketches for the next projects. You will work on the next project on that Wednesday. Then repeats each week! Don't expect easy 100s.

Lots of reading gives good feedback, graded returned quickly, and 3 opportunities for EC. Do her papers her way and you will be fine. She tells you exactly what she wants. Easy A if you do the work and you can guarantee an A with all the EC opportunities.

PSA: THIS IS STILL A COLLEGE CLASS! I'm not a history major, but I'm still expected to write a coherent paper and know the answers on the test. If you do the work, it's not hard to get an A.  Most people expect an easy A for minimal work. The downside is that this is a three hour class and if you're already good at drawing, you will be very bored.

This professor did not have any clear instructions or seem like he knew what he was doing. Half the time, he was being corrected by his TAs, who also did not really grade fairly. He also made attendance mandatory and we would sometimes sit there doing nothing until the literal very end to open up the password protected quiz.

At first I was intimidated by the content of the class and her in general, but by the end of the semester my mind was changed. Very casual professor and genuinely wants to help with making sure you are familiar and set up with the skills to do well with digital art.
I didn't appreciate her class at all. Very restrictive in terms of what she thinks "art" is and has a closed mind to student's work.

She is the most organized, thorough, helpful, understanding, and inspiring Professor I've ever had! On top of the in-depth lectures, she provides lots of demonstration videos, helpful handouts, and references in order to guide and inspire the students to do their assignments well. You can expect to do well and have fun as you follow along!

I took this professor multiple times over the past couple of years, and I have heard mixed reviews regarding the way he teaches and his overall personality. Surface level, he is a chill prof with an easy going classroom, however he can be inappropriate and stubborn, so I say proceed with caution and just be weary if you take any of his classes.

He was basically my father figure the entire semester I took him. He explained things in a way that was understandable and easy. I miss taking his class because of how caring he was towards me and other students. He was fun and talked about exciting things about art. He is (so far) the best professor I have ever had.

Professor Rodriguez was a joy to have! Very funny and passionate. He is a little disorganized, but does his best to make everything as easy as possible for his students. 4 quizzes, 3 exams (3rd one is counted as the final), all open note, attendance not mandatory.

This teacher made me not want to stay in my major. At first, I thought he was going to be a fun zany professor, But then found he's unclear, unhelpful, and not be inappropriate at times. I wish I never took this class.
Professor Rodriguez ROCKS! The best professor I've ever had and very inspiring. He KNOWS art and makes me want to know it too. Kudos on every level!!

Professor Patterson is a super chill funny guy. You can tell you really loves animation, as well as many other types of art. Really good at helping you when you're stuck. Personally I was not a big fan of the final two projects, but if you're big into animation you'll love it. Great guy, great artist, great professor.

Easy Visual Arts class. 18 quizes and 2 create an artwork project. Easy art projects and quizes can be found online. Don't need to buy book. I took this class in the second 8 week but can be done in 3 weeks.

Took him for Foundations 3 (Art 1023) and it was one of my favorite classes! Attendance is *mandatory however he works with you if you have any conflicts and gives work days where you don't have to meet in person. Really easy with a few projects and small assignments, and lots of time to work on everything!
Great professor, class is not hard, the art styles is easy to learn so at longest you read textbook you should be okay.

Textbook is free, online art class with only 20 quizzes and 2 tests to grade on a 2 week span for 10 and 1 consecutively, it doesn't get better than that, enjoy taking his class, not difficult imo, just literally manage your time and you will be fine, tests are mostly questions from quizzes and quizzes are mostly important topics from textbook.
I took his 4-week long course and it was super easy to follow. The quizzes took no more than 5ish min, and the test no more than 45 min - 1 hr. Overall, I liked the class

This class was actually Art1014 three dimensional foundations, we had three sculpting projects this semester along with three artist research papers (1 page). very easy, Ryberg gives great and helpful ideas throughout the semester. attendance is mandatory as well as critique participation. this class is only as hard as you make it in my opinion.
The textbook can be found online and is easy to read. The tests are majority of your grade, but simple. The class only lasts half the semester. No extra credit.

An easy class with multiple McGraw hill assignments with a test at the end of like 4 or 5 chapters. In total of 4 or 5 tests. Extra credit was going to an art museum and taking photos of yourself there. Another was the survey at the end. very simple class and easy A! 10/10 I would take the class again.
Lets you go at your own pace for everything. You need the textbook for the quizzes. Everything assigned is super short and quick.
an older version of the textbook can be found online and provides the info youll need for the course.  very easy to achieve the grade you want in this course.  recommend and would take again

Hes a cool professor, but hes very particular about your projects and that they shouldnt be simple, and hes a tough critic. But hes very nice, and very understanding, he help his students out and explains well what he wants from you.

Prof. Graybill (aka BUSTER) is a great teacher! This class is so cool because he pushes us to make art out of our comfort zone. It was really cool working with materials I've never worked with before, like wire and wood. He's very talented and skillful in his craft and I would love to take another one of his classes. The workshop is badass!
Very kind and knowledgeable professor. Helps every student until they have a clear understanding of tasks. Needs to work on keeping up with grades, other than that awesome prof. Would take again.

ART 1143.courseName: Art for Non Art Majors: Paint

Fall 2022.title: Art for Non Art Majors: Paint

recentReviews.comment: Beth had just received this course last minute so things were kind of hectic. She was very lenient about attendance and understanding of circumstances. It was hard to understand the grading criteria but she was always open to help.

Makes the work harder than it should be. When you email her with questions, her response is always read the instructions even though you do. Can never just give you a helpful answer. She expects too much for a professor that doesnt teach. Do not recommend her even if you are an art major.

Took her for ART-1143 Digital Photography. Makes it difficult for no reason. For a non-art major especially not focusing in photography, this class probably is not for you. Not an easy A. Not interesting either. Lectures are long and boring. The entire semester is posted at once, but goes on a weekly basis.

Loves seeing creativity and effort in photos and assignments. Clear about what she wants in each assignment and gives plenty of examples. Encourages "experimenting" with concepts in class with the use of school's lab materials. Always able to reach her outside of class time and is always offering new ideas for photos. No tests, just critique days!

It was difficult to understand what the professor was looking for in out pictures.  Don't think this is an easy class because it's for non art majors she really expects you to think outside of the box no matter what your background in art is. okay teacher overall.

Professor Wuest provided a fun learning environment this semester and I am a big fan of the extra credit opportunities. I highly recommend this course and professor to anyone in need of an elective course or is interested in visual arts in general.

She cares about her students and tries to lessen the end of semester stress (which was super helpful.) You do need to buy the textbook for the online homework, there's extra credit, and there's fun exercises. The exams were easy if you read and payed attention to the reading and questions in the textbook.

By far the best experience I've had with a professor. Online textbook required $ through McGraw Hill. Majority of assignments are McGraw Hill, some quizzes, and some exercises. She grades on Complete/Incomplete (EXERCISES ONLY), so unless you truly are putting zero effort into your assignments, you will pass this class with flying colors.
Not a very difficult class at all. Most of the answers in the chapter quizzes tend to be straight out of the online textbook, and the professor is easy to get in touch with.

Want an amazing experience on your first semester at UTSA or any semester for that matter? Choose Mary! She is the most caring and inspirational professor (don't call her professor) you can get! She makes her class fun and enjoyable and it was the highlight of my every week. Her projects are well explained and she will guide you through each step!

You might have a hard time if you´ve never done printmaking before. Lectures can be unorganized and hard to follow. He once assigned a group project that was not optional or for a grade even though we were on a tight deadline with other assignments for this course. You'll be fine if you work hard, take notes, and stay focused.

Super fun and casual. He offered to break dance for us. He also told us if we are stressed to "not panic" and instead just "go to HEB, buy some stuff and make a stew"??? So make of that what you will... Idk who gave him one star but they probably just failed his class because they can not draw for the life of them and blamed it on Juan...

Juan Mora is a very passionate professor that tries to help anyone that's in his class, he pushes anyone to be a better artist but expects you to be on top of your work and make the time commitment for the studios. He is hard to reach outside of class, but his projects were really  off the wall and very fun just show up to class and make an effort.

Juan is an excellent printmaker who thrives best in that class, but I took his Drawing II class where he was average, probably because he was less passionate about it. He tends to be late to class and can be unorganized. He explains things in confusing ways sometimes too. His critiques were good. He's a goof who can be awkward sometimes haha.

It is a fun and educational course. Paying attention to lectures and taking notes will help a long way with assignments. Each assignment will have weekly deadlines and/or progress checks, so staying productive is wise in order to pass. Moreover, always ask questions or feedback with Juan during class and he'll help the best he can.

I created an account just to praise Christie! As long as you come in with a open mind and are willing to try things that you aren't familiar with, you'll do great! If you're trying ,and completing, the work you'll pass this class. She is always willing to give feedback. The only people I saw have a problem her were people not willing to branch out.

She's incredibly patronizing and contradicts herself constantly. She has an intense need to be needed by her students, leading to unwarranted advice that is frustrating for everyone involved. She's an easy grader, so you won't fail so long as you do the work, she's just an incredibly difficult person to speak to and function around.
Amazing professor, I would 100% take her again. The quizzes are pretty easy and you have plenty of time to complete them.

Blizard definitely cares for her students. You'll have to do a LOT of painting (so much you get sick of it), but she's an easy grader and gives amazing tips and feedback throughout the process. Stay on top of it, and you should pass with an A!
One of my favorite professor I've ever had. Very understanding and flexible. He wants to see students excel past graduating and is open to curating the projects to your career interests.
Great teacher.

Definitely one of my favorite professors. Understanding and constructive with his material. He is not afraid to speak his mind and also has a humor side to him. Extremely helpful in critiques and easy to talk to. Unfortunately he will not be at UTSA anymore =( I was looking forward to taking more of his classes.
Justin is helpful, knowledgable & fun. Highly encourages experimentation.

He is a very understanding professor. He has a lot of knowledge in his field and will share it with you if you ask. If you take his class, just work hard, be present and turn in your assignments and you will pass. I enjoyed his class and his teaching style.

The class is split into modules, one each month. It is completely doable and he gives decent instructions. The textbook is quite helpful too. Other than the occasional email from him, I never heard from him though.

Easy class but he would never respond to emails. People in our class group chats were constantly not knowing what to do because he wouldnt answer anybody and we had to guess on what to do. Easy work though, only 4 due dates with a couple things to do in each one.

He's an artist and that is the perspective he teaches. He emphasizes that we need to think in terms of our own concepts and incorporates that into the assignments. He doesn't allow slackers to run the class and tells them to do the work. He is available for questions and help. He didn't pick favorites like other profs do.  Wish he'd teach advanced.
If you need an art credit this is a perfect class, very easy asignments and lectures are very clear to the readings he provides!

I took him for Advanced Photography. I'm so happy that he is in the photography department at UTSA. He is an artist and teaches that perspective, which is a change from the other instructors. He offers experience and insights on how to think of photography in a different way. I reccommend him if you are interested in making art beyond your degree.

This class was super easy. She's super lenient with attendance as long as you complete all your projects within the given time. She allows you to come whenever outside of class time to complete/work on projects. She super chill and is very nice.

As an art major, Verena is so willing to go with anything you want. She explicitly explains her project outlines and expects you to read them. None of the projects are "due" until the final week, so you have the entire semester to complete any work needed. She does her demonstrations at the beginning of class, so be sure to get there on time.
Humiliated my piece in front of class. Not impressed.
I had her for basic ceramics (art for non-art majors) and I loved the class! She was very caring and helped when you asked.
took her for honors ceramics pretty chill class would rather take ceramics than an actual compartive humanitive studies class

One of the best professors I've had at UTSA. I took him for two classes and both were well organized and fun to take. If you have a chance to take him for either an art class or a senior seminar, definitely do it! He is extremely understanding and easy to talk, not to mention very easy to contact about any situation. One of the best prof's at UTSA!

Well organized and thorough for virtual learning. Not only does he provide well in-depth lectures for us to learn, but he gives helpful references and past student examples to help guide us through every assignment. We also receive great feedback whenever we check-in for our progress on the assignments or having any issue on concepts. An easy A!

I love this professor! He seems to genuinely care about his students and the topic at hand. The sketchbook and project requirements can be overwhelming and difficult to understand in the beginning but it gets easier as time goes on. There is a lot of work to be done but it is always fun and the professor makes it known that he's there to help.

Nice instructor. Explained that I wasn't an art major, but that his class was an elective that I needed. He said not to worry that I would be fine as long as I understood the assignments and achieved the color that was needed. My pictures were literally circles and squares. This class will make you see color in a whole new light. Learned a lot.
Super cool and down to earth! understands that life happens. Always gives time to redo projects if you arent happy with your grade. Wants you to be better and gives you the tools to become better

Had him for Advanced Painting and I  strongly discourage his class if you have a clear idea of who you are as artist and what art means to you. he'll  disregard your ideas and push you to make art how he wants you too. If you don't do exactly what he says he'll get mean. He never even read my project proposal.

We didn't work well together, to this day Idk why I almost failed. In his advanced class, my artwork was transforming and he didn't like the path it was taking. I was putting in more time/work than the others, but he was still butthurt. Treats one student different than the next when it comes to standards and grades. It's a gamble not worth taking.
a very good professor

He is very helpful and understanding, but ONLY if you come to him about it. If you don't ask for his help or show him that you would like his input, he won't really say anything. He does grade on the skill level you have shown him, but i wouldn't call him hard, i got an A and didn't even turn in a few things. very understanding with personal probs.

This teacher does expect alot from you but will grade on your skill leval, so if you show him your good and then drag off it will effect you. Need book for quizzes. Teacher is extreamly supportive of all ideas but will let you decide. You will need to put time into work
Class is straight-forward. Textbook is necessary. 9 quizzes, 2 mid-terms, and a final. Quizzes open on Friday and are due by Sunday. I would recommend the professor!

Professor West is hilarious, making me excited to go to a class I originally didn't want to go to. There is one major project, but he is lenient since it is a freshman class. He does mention things in class that are on the midterms that aren't in the textbook, though.
He is a super cool guy

I absolutly loved this professor. 10/10 my favorite teacher by far. He made this class enjoyable even though it was a morning class. There is one major thing and it's the presentation. He clearly explains everything required for it. I recommend this class and this professor to anyone that needs this class

Professor West is passionate about his topics. I took Mass Media&Law and he could relate every topic to something from his experience or ours. Only 2 tests, (3 in syllabus but entire class chose a 5th essay) and 4-5 essay assignments (easy). Gives extra credit for showing up to every class. Would recommend to com majors looking for electives.

Professor Johnson is very slow to grade your work, which is a bit annoying but she's a really easy grader. She also opened the class like 5 days late which sucked. The textbook and quizzes were through McGraw so be prepared to do a lot of reading and dish out like $150. If you don't care about the tedious work take this class for an easy A.

EXTREMELY unorganized. Takes forever to respond to emails. Took her class online and it felt like she didn't even think about us or the class at all. Due dates were from the last semester, she had to be reminded to assign us groups for a group project, and none of my assignments have been graded yet and the semester ends in less than two weeks.

Disorganized and did not communicate on the assignments at all. Removed two weeks off the online course for grading purposes. Feedback or grading does not occur until after the class is over. You will have to live with the grade you receive. Unnecessary busy work such as connect quizzes, her quizzes, then two exams.

Overall easy class if you stay on top of deadlines. Total workload: 14- 10 question quizzes, 2 exams, 9 McGraw Hill concepts, 3 discussion posts, and 1 reflection paper. The McGraw Hill concepts took the longest, so don't wait until the last minute.

Very kind professor, willing to work with students. The course was fun and on the easier side because you get to choose your writing/video topics. 
The ONLY thing I have to say that I did not like...and it greatly upsets me is that with only a few weeks left in this semester, none of my assignments are graded.
3 smartbooks a week with a 6 person presentation that you get a week to prepare for in a class most people take for free grades is absurd.

his grading is VERY clear. if he wants 5 sentences in a paragraph: he's counting. He's very thorough in instructions though and its easy to get ahold of him for questions. he does allow for late work but his tests are scheduled kinda weirdly. overall he's very fair, and thats that.

Allows late work with points off, one group project, one essay, I never gave a speech. sends out reminder emails that were a great help. Assignments were really easy but the test were kind of tricky though.

Easiest class ever. Just know that when he says he grades grammar strictly on essays or projects that he is not joking, so triple-check your spelling etc. There's one major group project, but it's not that hard. There's online practice for exams. Rubrics are super clear and specific so you know exactly what he's looking for on essays/projects.

The course load wasn't bad at all; extremely manageable. Professor Harris is really responsive with emails and course messages, which was a plus. The only negative thing was how harsh he grades. Despite the grading, the course content was extremely beneficial and I would take this class again.

Prof. Hullinger was not the best communicator or teacher. Given that we attended class 3 times weekly, I expected real lessons from him rather than watching a youtube video, which could have been watched at home. For in-person speeches, his judgement is inconsistent. It felt like he was trying to make it hard to get an A in an elective class.

Literally would just put videos on the projector and do his own thing. After that, he'd do a rundown of a PowerPoint and that would be it. My class did super well on one of the exams and once everyone got their grade, he immediately asked if we cheated. I felt attacked. If I were you, I would stay away from this professor.

Step 1. Gives rubric to follow for grade
Step 2. Follow rubric to a tee
Step 3. Get a 40 on the assignment
Step 4. Profit
Step 5. Never pick this professor

Difficult to understand verbally due to a medical issue with his tongue, not clear at all with grading rubric and his expectations for assignments. Nearly everyone from both of his classes failed exam 3 and he still had the audacity to blame the students over taking any blame for the study material being 2 weeks behind the test.

Will fail you if you didn't follow the rubric he never explained EXACTLY and will take off points unnecessarily. Puts on YouTube videos and then spends the class on his phone but gets upset when students don't give their undivided attention. Overall a very negative experience for a class that is supposed to be enjoyable. I do not recommend.

Class is very easy, based mostly on chapters that she provides, with weekly quizzes for each chapter as well as 3 speeches, speech outlines and one essay. Accessible outside of class and very understanding when I had problems with the submission of my assignment, 10/10 am very grateful for her.

Fairly easy class and completely online. There are 16 short 10-question quizzes and four theory analysis paper/essays. Assignments are straightforward and not hard just stay consistent and don't fall behind. Quizzes are completed through McGraw Hill.

Class consisted of textbook reading and 4 short papers. I like how the class was set up and I got good feedback on the assignments. The only downside is having to pay $90 just to submit homework because of McGraw Hill.
Took this class fully virtual, so I never once talked to the teacher. But, every week you would either do a discussion, or a 500 word essay over that weeks topic. Super easy. No textbook, no final.

She is a really great professor! She is so nice and really cares about her students and it shows. The class has a nice structure, super easy to follow along. One or two assignments per week, not difficult at all! She posts grades in a timely manner and always provides good feedback on assignments. Passed with an easy 100. Highly recommend!

I LOVEEE prof gonzales. She is an absolute gem. Very understanding because she's a master's student, so she's easy to talk to. Tests are easy and there's only 3. I believe 3 speech's, including the final which is a group speech. Grades fairly easily on speeches. Take her, you'll love her.

Terrible professor that couldn't care less about actually teaching any material. Doesn't respond to emails, grades assignments last minute and doesn't elaborate on anything described in the syllabus. Kinda ironic how a communications professor has no concept of actually communicating with her students. It's an easy A but nothing will be learned.

This is a class taught by a textbook. The professor never does what she says she will do, and she does not grade what is outside of the textbook until the very last minute. There was one intro video posted, and then she practically vanished for the rest of the semester. The class is OK and you can pass easily, but you won't really learn much.

There is literally nothing commendable about this professor. Not only does she give vague instructions, she also doesn't respond to emails. She is very last minute, unprofessional, and just an overall inactive professor. The content is easy, but that means nothing when the professor doesn't give proper instructions. I don't recommend her at all.

This is the worse unrealistic class I done ever took in my 5 years of college. He to literally unrealistic with the work he give out to complete in the short time frame. He grade absolutely hard and just make assignments extremely difficult. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!

She is queen! Amazing professor and communicator. She treats students with fairness and love, it feels like having a friend

shes queen

One of the best. Introduction to media class was a breeze and fun at the same time. Grading is fair and semi-lax, and assignments are easy if you plan them out well. Amazing! The way she broke down the major assignment throughout the 8 week-long class was so helpful. Professor Kang's class is very easy to follow! He gives one week to submit each assignment that he uploads with new lecture information. Mr. Kang is one of the most personable professors I have ever had. He would record short videos as feedback on assignments which shows he really cares. My only issue with this class was that I didn't feel as though the assignments corresponded with the readings. Very easy and fun assignments too!

Great professor. Easy-normal difficulty depending on whether you do his homework assignments. Made very clear instructions for eash assignment. Easy to contact and is a fast responder. Understanding with deadlines and late assignments.

I enjoyed taking this class so much. Professor Kang was incredibly understanding. He really wants you to succeed and gives you really good feedback. I wish i could take him for other classes. 10/10! TAKE HIM! Hands done my favorite Professor Ive taken at UTSA.

Professor P. is great! She really cares about teaching and is always available to answer any questions. She brings in speakers and makes the class very interesting and I can say I learned a lot. She is an easy grader and I would totally take her again if I could.

Dr. P is one of the best professors that I have ever had in my college/university career! Profesor Passalacqua is one of the best professors I've had during my university time!  The lectures and topics covered in this course are extremely interesting. Prof.P is a phenomenal teacher! She has a ton of first hand experience to what she teaches. Shes clear in what to prep for in quizes and dosen't give out that many excessive papers other than the notes! I would have taken her twice if I could!

Heavy lectures on everything in her personal life that has nothing to do with class. She is completely clueless on how to instruct on topic. Out of all my classes for my semester, this was the class that never stressed me out. Had a lot of time to do assignments and enough assignments to swing my grade back up if one assignment hadn't done so well. I did actually enjoy learning a handful of things in the assignments.

Save yourself and your GPA. This professor claims that "students learn better when given parameters for a project and then allowed to explore and learn on their own" which is a nicer way to say that she is going to give you vague assignments with little to no instruction, and then fail you with 0 feedback. I found the majority of this class to be a little boring & overkill on the "here's how to be a college student" handholding. at least for me she's being pretty difficult, she doesn't do extra credit, in the announcement there's not details about how so supposed to be done the assignments, i explain that i got my laptop late because i didn't have a lot money at tame to pay for it. i'm currently trying to change my professor i cant i'm just going to drop-off my class.

Professor Tokunaga is a good professor and tries his best. However, sometimes the way he explains or words things is complicated. great professor who cares about his students. although this class is 100% online, prof tokunaga is very accessible and replies quickly. his course may seem threatening, but he makes the content easy to digest + gives multiple chances to pass. overall, he's a great prof who doesn't neglect his students or class despite it being online.
Professor Tokunaga was a super cool professor. Very understanding and super helpful when I had any problems with quizzes or projects. Would take again.

Dr. Tokunaga is a nice professor and gives good feedback. I took the summer, 5 week accelerated course. He is a tough grader.

Dr. Tokunaga is a great professor, he gives a simple quiz and reading along with a weekly lecture. I definitely recommend taking him

If you can't avoid him, figure him out. He is very willing to give feedback on everything. Use his objectives to study, you can cut and paste from his readings and slides. Professor is fair. Just do the work.
Toughest grader

The toughest professor I have ever encountered, and his feedback on assignments comes off as rude and belittling. If you do not think how he thinks, then you will have a tough time in this class. He is extremely intelligent in this field, he has too high expectations for everyone else to be on his level.

Absolute garbage of a professor. Tells you to focus on "objectives" but the quizzes and exams have little to no relevance to them. He should not be a professor ANYWHERE. AVOID THIS MAN AT ALL COSTS, SAVE YOURSELF THE TIME AND STRESS.

She is one of the best professors I have ever had!! The class can be a little challenging at times however is straightforward, but every day I truly looked forward to going to class. Super engaging and fun to listen to. You don't feel like you are just being thrown information, you are able to talk and ask questions/give opinions all the time.

One of the best professors I have had. Actually seems interested in what her students says. She has very engaging lectures and group discussions that make you feel like you're really learning. Got to access new opportunities I would not have normally done.

Professor Deturk is an amazing professor who thoroughly enjoys her field. She gives great lectures and has plenty of open discussions that are interesting to engage in. Prof DeTurk lectures are interesting, though clearly politically biased which could be kind of irritating since we were in a research class, not politics. Prof Deturk managed to make a 3-hour weekly class engaging and fun. The projects for the course aren't easy, but she breaks them down so you do a little at a time and that helps a lot. I took this class because I needed the credit, but ended up learning a lot and really enjoying it.
Professor was nice and gave great feedback. The class was not hard and very informative!

Super easy class. Only three 25-question exams (not proctored), 16 short module/ slideshow with a few questions after, two individual essays, and seven short discussion posts. Very manageable workload, finished with an A+.
Great teacher!

Professor Hajek was a great professor! I'm pretty hands off, but he was readily available to help if I had questions. Not a tough grader at all and has some interesting feedback and stories.

I would recommend this graduate professor to a friend. The grading was mostly based on the three projects we did throughout the semester. There is little grades other than that. There is chapter readings, but no quizzes. He was really nice and understanding! 
Definitely recommend this course. He makes the content easy to understand.

Tough but fair class. Only three tests 30 Questions plus two big projects, so staying on top of research and deadlines matters. Content is manageable but requires lots of studying/reading. Some language barrier due to his thick accent, but overall knowledgeable and organized.

Professor Zhang is so responsive and caring!!! His assignments are very straight forward, they just take some time to complete. Professor Zhang is very responsive and helpful. His assignments can be pretty confusing but you just have to watch his lectures for certain assignments and reach out to him if you have questions. I think in total, there were like 5 or 6 assignments (tests included) throughout the entire semester. It was a pretty easy course.

Professor Juyan is a very enthusiastic professor with an obvious passion for his field. His classes have a lot of reading and writing/powerpoints. Professor Zhang is so sweet and very clearly cares that you pass his class. He will be stern with you when needed, but he is very understanding and wants you to do well. His lectures and power points were easy to follow, and the tests are easy as long as you study them. Great professor!

recentReviews.comment: Jonathan Gutierrez is an excellent professor. Not only did he interact respectfully and kindly with me and the other students, but he actively tried to learn about us as individuals. required to take this class but the teacher is amazing. very caring and wants to form relationships with the students. easy grader and was not a lot of homework.
New class over a very interesting topic. I enjoyed the assignments, but I wish I could have received more feedback from the professor.

Awesome professor!!! There are tough assignments sometimes but he's understanding, unlike other professors! Instructions are clear, open discussion, communicates well, cool, & his dig. med. prod. class is fun &informative! I would definitely take this professor again!

Great professor. His instructions are clear and the assignments are not hard at all. I learned a lot in his Digi. Production class. He is also very understanding. Class is a waste of time. Warmups and group work drag far longer than needed because you spend most of class waiting on him. Textbook isn't needed; he just shows his copy anyway. No real learning is done in this class.

Kanso is a very knowledgeable professor; he is clearly compassionate and cares for all his students. There is a syllabus to follow but this is a difficult course, as it's a capstone. Jamie is a laidback young professor who is good at his job and passionate about his subject. He takes attendance with clicker questions. Tests are easy breezy as long as you pay attention in class, homework is minimal (couple 4-6 pg papers). Definitely recommend.
This is one of my fav profs.  He's funny and clear.  He's so interested in what he does and it really comes across in his lectures.
She's nice, but she really values participation. Overall the class is easy, but the work is a bit tedious.
She is very nice and explains the texts well, just make sure you read the assigned reading before class and you'll be fine.

Professor Adamina really knows what she's talking about, and she presents the information in a way where you don't even realize you're learning. Very understanding.

Such a sweet, intelligent, and genuine soul. She is very articulate and her lectures are not only compelling, but they are also very fluent and eloquent. She makes the class very fun and interesting and the group work is very impressive. I would definitely want to take her again because she is now one of my favorite professors.

Very enjoyable class! Mrs. Adamina has a passion for film and literature that shows whenever she is lecturing. As a hybrid class, her in-person lectures were stress-free and enjoyable to be a part of whenever it came to watching and analyzing genres, camera work, and reading poems. She is an amazing professor with very minimal and doable homework.
I can't even fit everything I did not like about taking this class with this professor in this box.
She is so full of energy and loves what she teaches.

The class tag should be ENG 2413, but it is not included on the list. This class is an easy A, however the way that this professor grades is off putting. The best professor I've ever had. No one is more prepared, knowledgeable, and qualified as a literary analyst and lecturer. If you desire knowledge, she's the best. Dr. Schoellman is incredibly understanding and loves what she does. She really goes the extra mile to make sure you're not only progressing but comfortable in her class. Dr. Schoellman is one of the best teachers I have encountered at UTSA. She is an interesting person and a fascinating lecturer. She cares about her students and appreciates their efforts. Despite the readings and homework, taking her 2253 and 3073 class is the best thing I've ever done. She's not like many other professors cause she made her class fun for us. Love this professor so much! She has a very calm, soothing voice and is the sweetest, most caring, and most compassionate professor that I've ever had. Her lectures are so compelling and fluent. Dr. Gentry is really kind and caring, very easy to talk to. There is a textbook for this course but I didn't use it once. She isn't a tough grader at all, as long as you put in a little effort you can easily get an A in this course.
Great professor. I feel she is how other teachers should be. Very understanding. Take her!!!!

Overall, I'd argue that Dr. Gentry is one of the best teachers on campus and I thoroughly enjoyed her class despite generally not liking writing classes. Professor Gentry was fantastic! She is so nice and understanding and makes the material interesting. She wasn't a hard grader and gave really kind constructive criticism when necessary. She also replied quickly to emails. I would definitely take one of her classes again, one of my favorite professors so far at UTSA.

If you have the opportunity to take writing and with Professor Gentry definitely take it she is very clear in her assignments and she provides A LOT of opportunity to get the highest scores on assignments. You will have to purchase a small textbook that cost around $30-40

Easily one of the best classes I've taken at UTSA. He provides any textbook style materials you'll need for the class, so you don't have to worry about buying textbooks for this class. He's a great professor, usually laid back and the only exam is the final.
Tech writing seems a little dull on the surface, but he really makes it fun with class discussions! I feel like I actually got something out of this class.

This is the best writing class I've ever taken! I got to work on projects that helped me in the real world and I'm actually using some of the writing I did in this class for a grant project in my career. Loved his class!

Our whole class loved Professor Kirby!! Take him if you can. Even though it's a core class this was by far my favorite class this semester. There is a couple of long essays that need to be done but overall the assignments were really easy. She genuinely cares about student's wellbeing and will ask how you are and check in on you. This professor fails to teach anything of substance, she mainly just has students popcorn read assignment instructions and then read the textbook or excerpts of textbooks for actual instruction. This class was not as difficult as others make it seem. She is clear that the correct due dates are on the syllabus although her blackboard dates are all off. Does not have due dates on BB, passive-aggressive, horrible lectures, and no real classroom activities we only go one day and its to sit and read from a PowerPoint or be expected to do our hw so there's not even a real reason to go to her class but to get the participation points

Does not communicate with students. If you ask for help she will tell you to talk to your peers instead of giving feedback. Prof Lopez is a very caring and nice person, but I would not say that she is good at teaching. The course content was very disorganized and she did not come prepared for her lectures. There were only two assignments in the course, a 10-page research paper and a presentation/seminar for class.

Prof. Dani was very nice; obviously cares about her students, but I learned absolutely nothing other than what I did a presentation on. If you want a throw-away class, take her.

Dr. Danie is a really nice and caring professor, no doubt about that. Basically, it could be a blow-off class for you if you are into that.

She can be really all over the place, I remember by the end of the semester the syllabus was just utterly binned. However, the information shared and the required readings are really relevant and she teaches them decently well, plus shes a super easy grader. Not a lot of strict deadlines or instruction on assignments tho which can be a bad thing.

recentReviews.comment: I didn't think I'd be interested in Medieval Lit, but her enthusiasm is contagious!

Dr Fonzo is an amazing professor but her teaching methods feel a little "outdated" sometimes. She requires participation which means that you will have to finish the readings and get ready to discuss in class. Also, she prefers that students use paper and pen when taking notes unless they have a valid excuse to use a laptop. Lots of pop quizzes too

I learned a lot in this class and Professor Fonzo's teaching style is very effective, but she is often condescending and treats her students like children. We were often made to feel like we were in a middle school classroom. Other than that, if you study then you will pass, though I highly recommend forming a study group.

Love professor Fonzo! She's very sweet, enthusiastic, and a ball of energy. Her lectures are so amazing and she makes class very interesting. This was one of the most fun classes I'd ever taken! The reading material is all really great and engaging, and the way she lectures makes it easy to participate. I loved this class!

I took Professor Milam over the summer for English 2332 at Northwest Vista. He is a very passionate, fair and accommodating professor, if you show up, turn in assignments and actually try you should walk out with an A.

I took Professor John over the summer for English 1301 at Northwest Vista. I recieved great feedback on my essays and lectures were helpful. Very easy class if you do the essays on time and put in an effort.

I took them two semesters in a row for ENGL1301 and 1302, they also teach at Northwest Vista college,  amazing professor! Best i've had, they are so inspirational and are genuinely there to help you. Their class is extremely easy as long as you read the prompt for essays! Excellent feedback on your work too! Only good things to say about John!

John was a great professor in my Shakespeare class! They are energetic, knowledgable, and insightful in discussing the plays. The quizzes were alright. Cons: It's a Shakespeare class & shouldn't have been as difficult as it was. The professor failed to upload assignments on time yet was strict with due dates. Pros: Non-Binary. Funny.

Prof Chairez is nice, cares about her students, & wants everyone to do well. She makes content fun & engaging during class. Extremely kind, understanding, and knowledgeable! She really appreciates when you speak up, so participation is highly recommended. Assignments are not difficult at all. Prof. Chairez is amazing! You can tell that she is passionate about what she teaches. She is very understanding and caring. Overall, it was a joy to be taught by her and I will definitely be looking for more courses taught by her.
Prof Chairez is hands down one of the most interesting professors I've had so far at UTSA. I want to take another one of her classes after advanced composition.

recentReviews.comment: Dr Drinka is truly one of the best professors I have ever had. I took her for Structures of English and she explains every concept perfectly. Her class changed my view on English linguistics. Attendance isn't mandatory, but don't miss class since the lectures are really helpful. Homework required some critical thinking but was not too difficult.
If you ask her a question regarding course work, she will likely say "Figure it out"

Every English student should take Structures of English, even if not required. The course starts off easy but builds on top of itself, so do not miss class. Dr. Drinka is extremely knowledgable about the subject and will help her students if things aren't clear. Be prepared to come out of this class with a better understanding of English grammar.

I took her Structure of Eng class Spring of 2021 and she was awesome! She is a master at this subject and is great at explaining things. She held many Zoom review sessions outside of class and they really helped me. She is super sweet, lenient with grading, and gives out extra credit points. Take plenty of notes, practice diagramming and study!

Great professor teaching teaching some difficult material. She will be honest in grading you, but she IS available outside of class to help you understand the material. She also responds to emails fairly quickly, and is overall super sweet :)

Took her for persuasion & rhetoric/environmental humanities, and for her first time teaching this cross-listed course, she did a great job. Assignments weren't too difficult and were more reflection-based. Class discussions were really insightful and opened up my worldview. She definitely wants you to succeed in her class and gives good feedback.
Totally uninspiring.

All study about race and gender with only her view allowed. Students must be eupeptic to the sinananophosy or grades fall. She asked for examples of the worst sexism existing in the world today and when one student said it was within Islam, she ignored it. Turned up to class often without PowerPoints prepared, shuffling through a mess of papers.
I really loved this professor! This was a summer course, and I had to read 4 books. They were really well chosen, and I enjoyed the work!

She speaks VERY quietly and with an online class it makes it challenging. I had to use earphones. I haven't had issue with volume any other time. Also, she made every novel about race and slavery - even Jane Austen which was quite a stretch for me. I felt that a Romantic Literature course should discuss more romance.

She will help you succeed by balancing a caring, intelligent teaching style with assignments that fit around who you are as a student. She lets you guide your ideas alongside course material while always being there to help straighten out any questions or issues with projects, life, etc. Most understanding professor I've ever had, by far.

Dr. Garza is incredible professor, mentor, and human being. She knows how to run efficient and productive creative writing workshops. After workshop, you will walk away feeling like a better writer. She gives tons of helpful feedback, offers flexible meeting times, and provides clear expectations.

I liked Garza but she talks A LOT. My class with her was from 1 PM to 4 PM and 98% of class time she was talking nonstop very quickly without taking a single breath and it can honestly get mind numbing. I zoned out many times. Still, she is a good teacher and instructor, gives excellent resources for students, and is informative if long-winded.

Participation is extremely important in this class. She's a great professor. Class is always interesting, helpful, and informative. I just wish she was more understandable/helpful with people suffering from social anxiety.

His poetry class is great--really knows his stuff. People will say he's strict about formatting, but what else is there to grade in a subjective creative arts class? Always uses all the time in class though, so buckle down for long class hours, especially if you take a workshop from him (1 PM-4 PM for me). Sometimes a lot of homework.

Dr. Vance always has good feedback and advice, but he grades assignments late. We read a lot of different poetry collections and give feedback to each other's poems. Turn in your assignments in time and write useful feedback to others and you should do fine.
Dr. Vance is a great teacher and a super nice guy.

Great professor! His literature courses work a lot like book clubs, very laid back and enjoyable. he obviously knows his stuff, he's encouraging, and doesn't ask more from you than what he knows you can handle. Overall, his courses are interesting, entertaining, and he helps you through it the whole time.

creative writing class was a sham. you buy expensive poetry books, and he asks you to respond to them, but no discussion of it whatsoever. peer evaluation discussions also ridiculous. he doesn't know what he's doing, nor does he care.
This whole course is not about learning; it's about memorizing the content. I am a hard worker and I was given no study guides whatsoever.  This class is impossible to pass.

He has an encyclopedic knowledge of literature, and the classes can be fun with the discussion. I only have one criticism, his instructions for a paper were vague, if you can get past that and do the work you will pass though. Also there is alot of reading so prepare for that.

This professor is... well, awful honestly. I had him more than once and he A.) doesn't stick to the syllabus, so will, for instance, tell you that you have two weeks to complete a novel and then expect you to finish it in 3 days for a pop quiz. And B.) he's incredibly arrogant and just spouts facts at you but doesn't teach you much.

You definitely have to read a lot for Kellman's classes, but they are in the English Department, so it shouldn't be a total shock. Kellman has high expectations for his students. It's stressful sometimes, but you feel a massive sense of accomplishment when the semester ends.

Im sure Kellman is a brilliant man but not a very caring professor. He knew very well this semester would be an uphill battle for some of his students, yet he remained steadfast in having students read an absurd amount of books in so little time. The term paper was a nightmare. And its remarkable how condescending he is to students responses.

Dr. Raymond's course in Mexican Women's Literature was, to say the least, academically life-changing. I am now able to approach complex and sensitive subject matter more confidently. Her expertise, philosophy, and care she has for her students and job make all the difference.

A TRUE GEM! This was her first time teaching at UTSA and due to COVID our hybrid course became fully online, however, she remained accessible and was truly understanding about everyone's situation. She was an amazing lecturer and I hope she continues to teach at UTSA!

Great professor. Works with his students very well and I really appreciated how he curated the course content, allowing students to submit topics that they were interested in. His lectures were always interesting and he has a very deep knowledge of American history.

good professor, you have 3 essays you need to complete for the course but they are very straightforward and easy. he gives good feedback and has great material to help you succeed.

To put this into perspective, I am a 24 year old Veteran born in the year 2000. Despite how young I am, i didnt grow up using ai. But this man has accused me twice of using it. I spent days writing both essays. I barely even know how to use ai. And the fact that hes asking me for proof and nobody else make me think im targeted for some odd reason.
90% of the assignments are writing assignments, they're not hard if you put the work in. as long as you fit the simple criteria he has for each assignment you will succeed i had a 99 in this class.
AWESOME PROFESSOR!! There is a one page paper due every chapter, I think it was. But it was super easy to do if you read your stuff! Easy grader and super caring!!

This guy is great, he emails right after his lectures even if u missed the class! took as elective. Besides that, clear, friendly, and willing to answer ANY question u have!

Professor Baumgardner is a great professor! What you expect from a professor! Professional, friendly and helpful. I took the Early American Culture class as an elective and I am glad I did. The class does require a lot of reading and you do have to put the work in, but you will learn a lot. Great professor and highly recommend!

pretty much just lectured the entire class. make sure to ask him to use the microphone b/c he talks quiet. waives your worst test grade and theres a few extra credit opportunities and some group work as well. he allows a small notecard for tests as well.

Great professor, hard to hear at times but lectures well. Loves telling stories. Lots of group assignments and McGraw Hill reading. Pay attention to what you need to study, exams vary in vocabulary and lecture material. Fair amount of extra credit opportunities and worst test scores waived. Made some great friends in his course, would retake!
He is a great professor, his exams are very easy. Even just paying a slight amount of attention goes a long way. The McGraw Hill assignments are annoying but frankly easy 100s.

Great Professor and great person. He's great at getting the class engaged and always does his best to make sure we're prepared for exams. He's also great at giving out advice to individual students who are struggling—Just ask and he's more than helpful!

Dr. Atabey is an amazing professor! He gives outstanding lectures, and I always looked forward to his classes. His essay tests are not difficult and if you pay attention you will do fine. If you participate and pay attention you will enjoy the class and get an A. If I could, I would take every class UTSA offers that is taught by him.
He's a really good professor. His exams are take-home, and he doesn't give much homework. Definitely recommend!
Professor Atabey is awesome! He is very passionate, knowledgeable, and caring. I enjoyed this class so much that I already signed up for his Ottoman Empire class next semester.

This class is straightforward. Attend class, take notes, do weekly readings, and occasional assignments once every few weeks (map-based or essays on primary sources). Exams are the hardest part, focusing on vocab and mini-essays, but the professor isn't a tough grader. You should pass as long as you show up and read every week.
Seriously a really caring guy, if I have the chance I'd love to take him again
I was a straight A student until I took her class. She is an extremely tough grader and is heavy on tests that doesn't follow the study guide
Less reading than other history clases

I have never received below an A- in any history course I have ever taken. This professor gives little to no feedback on essays. Is incredibly rude and UNCLEAR with instructions and expectations. She is the least helpful professor I've ever had, doesn't respond to emails about her one sentence feedback on an essay worth 20% that you failed.

I took this class with hope, let's just say she killed it. Everything below is true on papers on test, this entire course just felt like a trap. She inserts her opinion on everything, which leads to docked points. Her instructions are not clear at all compared to how she grades and her test and traps that do not allow you to think.

She has very high expectations for her papers even though she does not explain the prompts or details needed for the paper well, your hard work will go unnoticed. The course is extremely test heavy and she times them 1 min given per question with only 10 questions at the most, so if you miss more than a couple, you will drop an entire letter grade.
