recentReviews.comment: Dr. FG is an awesome professor.  He is extremely knowledgeable and gives exciting lectures.  He is a little full of himself but has a great sense of humor.  Lots of reading but hey what college class isn't?  Definitely recommend any of his classes.

Dr. FG is a little harsh. He knows what the readings are about and he expects you to know what they're about too; not just generals, but specifics sometimes too. If you haven't done the reading HE WILL KNOW AND HE WILL CALL YOU OUT ON IT. Only a few papers/assignments which I liked but very focused on talking about the readings

Dr. Gibson is a pretty easy grader and has rather easy assignments, as long as you read the instructions and try you will probably get a good grade. There was a technical textbook but it was not necessary to read to get a good grade, but participation in class was important.

for HIS 3103: Great structure to the class, 3-4 mini lectures every week w a short quiz and a discussion post. progress checks for final project thru out semester. quick at replying and very understanding w late stuff. had 3 papers due at the end correlating to books we had to read.
Professor Gibson has been one of the best professors Ive ever had! His lectures are always very interesting and his assignments were easy to do. Id definitely take him again if I could!

This was a really fun class. It was a super small class which led to some interesting discussions. His lectures were great and public history was fun to learn about. The organization of the class was awesome and easy to access. I'm an art history major so this was a little out of my element, but it was still a lot of fun.

I took Gibsons class during spring, right before COVID hit. He handled the transition online well. During class, I felt supported, and heard. Hes professional, and serious, but kind. Hes open minded and empathetic. If you reach out, hell meet you halfway. All round a good human. I got a C, but thats my fault bc life... Hes a fair grader.

Not a bad professor, but he does not use powerpoints or uploads class notes. He read notes off his paper, projects a picture of a map on the screen, and talks very quietly. He does not use canvas. The only material you will see on canvas is the syllabus.

Davies is by far the WORST professor I have ever had. I don't know where these good reviews came from to be honest. He shows pictures in class and talks like a mouse during lectures so good luck understanding anything. Your best bet to pass is getting with other students and trying to figure it out yourself. YOU WILL TEACH YOURSELF IN HIS CLASS.

Brian Davies is very old school and EXTREMELY quiet. He only speaks, doesnt use visual aids, and doesnt elaborate and runs through his lessons super quick. Study and read tons on your own time or you will fail, he is only good at answering specific questions you have. He honestly needs to get with the modern age and use any kind of aid for his clas

This was a seminar class on the fall of complex societies, so it was really up to us on what topic to take with our 30-page paper. Honestly, the vast amount of knowledge he has is quite impressive. My paper was over the collapse of the Soviet Union, something he has expert knowledge in, so I knew his feedback would be crucial. The best professor.

Professor Davies is by far the best professor at UTSA. His lectures are extremely interesting. He teaches every aspect of the subject matter, and goes into great depth. His level of knowledge is amazing. I have completed everyone of his courses. His courses are challenging, but that is why we are in school, to challenge ourselves.

Dr. H is very specific about how she wants things done and how the course is set up. Not sure if she does this for her sake or the students, but it can be a bit much. Her writing assignments are different from those in usual history classes, as they're a bit more creative. There's not too much reading, and she does care about her students.

The class is very unorganized and requires the student to guess if they got everything in. I had emailed her THREE WEEKS before SB that I would be unable to take the midterm on that day and no response. I got sick and missed two assignments by 1 DAY. I emailed her and she said that the late penalty applied because I did not notify her before.

The course wasn't hard, but rather tedious. In my personal experience, communicating of the professor proved to be hard. Whenever I did, I was blown off or ignored. Grades harshly with little to no genuine feedback on what to improve to make your work better. Don't take this class if you're looking for a responsive professor who provides feedback.

I would recommend not to take this course if it is not required for your major. I got all A's this semester except this class. she is very unorganized with assignments and takes forever to reply if you ask her question. Her instructions on assignments are confusing and all over the place.

Dr. Hardgrove is a good professor and I enjoyed her class overall. She is strict and serious on instructions. A lot of the assignements felt unnecessary like she wanted to just fill up our time. Towards the end of the semester it felt like too much work for the class since I took it as an elective.

This was my first time dropping a course, I did so after the first essay was returned with such harsh criticism I was shocked. He took off points for going over the word count. He is an incredibly harsh grader but does not go off the rubric provided, so I knew I would struggle on future assignments and decided to drop the course to save my GPA.

This professor is one of the worst professors I've had. I am doing all the assignments that am being asked to do but seem never to do it right. I met with him and he told me I don't have the capacity to pass his class. Instead of trying to help me understand his assignments he brought my hopes down. I walk out of his office sad and unmotivated.

he was okay. his lectures barely made sense and it was hard to understand the material. his assignments also were kind of challenging because it didn't really go off his lectures. grading was pretty quick, but was also strict

Pretty simple class as long as you pay attention to his instructions. He gives a lot of time for the reviews, which are basically open book written exams. There are 3 group projects, which was honestly the only downside to this class. He was a good professor though. His lectures were really helpful.

(HIST 2553)This is an extremely informative course. Dr. Wing thoroughly explains the material. However I just think the amount of written work given can be a bit overwhelming at times for an Intro course. Group projects, essays and writing exercises can be expected for one module. I had to write 3 pages on Chinese bookbinding, so take at own risk.

Phenomenal orator with an almost photographic memory of American history, I had a good time in his class. Probably the only professor I took this semester who seemed to know what he was doing. Very fair with grades, provides plenty of extra credit work, but the tests could be tricky. Slightly difficult, but light work load overall.

He sets a random standard of expectations that isn't necessarily made explicit. Assignments have no clear rubric, & he doesn't provide any helpful feedback. This is the only class I've ever dropped because I wasn't willing to put my sanity and GPA at risk. This is a sink-or-swim class, and a lot of the learning has to be done outside his lectures.

Avoid this professor at all costs, this man should not be teaching anything!!!  Hypocrisy runs wild in his courses and his feedback doesn't really matter since he ignores it when you accommodate him anyway.  Ridiculous!!  His grading of papers is extremely tough and illogical!!  DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN"S CLASS!!!!

Avoid this guy at all cost, tough grader who gives feedback but then adds on extra when you turn in assignments. Had a first draft turned in he gave feedback and I did exactly as he said on the final and received a lower grade. If there is anyone else to take take them avoid him at all means!!!!
She's very disorganized. If you want to learn Chinese, you probably wont unless you practice everyday (basically teach yourself). It's easy to get a good grade, but definitely not taking her again.

I don't know what everyone else was talking about because Dr. Ward is super cool. She's very personable and quick to respond when contacting, gives good feedback on discussion assignments, and does a really good job organizing and creating weekly lessons. It was honestly a super pleasant experience.

Dr. Ward is great. Her lectures are entertaining and her teaching style really works. You start off slow, so nobody gets left in the dust. She makes her own curriculum, and she knows all the material by heart. There are 3-6 homework assignments per week, so the workload is kind of heavy, and you have to memorize vocab etc. on your own. Lots of EC.

Class itself was lackluster and overall easy, however her handling of the final project was a complete mess: Emails every day calling students out by name who didn't meet expectations, vague guidelines she'd only elaborate on in her LINE group chat, unspecific guidelines such as # of slides/sources, amending expectations up until the due date, etc.

Tbh Id rather take my language course with other professors. No wonder the bad reviews are bad, heard so many things about her past students saying how her course is so unorganized. I mean shes an easy grader but doesnt mean she is good at teaching, Ive taken Chinese outside of school and its much more structured.

Dr Zhang is very knowledgeable in her field and you can tell she is very passionate about it. However, her lectures were sometimes boring and lacked engagement. We read Shakespeare's plays and had a short 5 question quiz after we finished each play. For the final, she wanted us to be creative and act out Shakespeare, which was fun.

We need more professors like Professor Zhang! I took her Sins & Punishments Seminar class and she's so articulate. Her lectures are very fluent and she responds to emails very quickly! Not only she's very articulate, she's so sweet and down-to-earth! My advice, if you're planning on taking one of her classes, DO IT!! because she's amazing!!

Kind but the Topics in LNG class was unorganized. This is a good class for Spanish speakers. He was confusing and not clear with instructions and he has been difficult to get hold of. Does not take attendance, some homework but nothing unmanageable. LOTS of reading/textbook. 1 group proj and 1 reg proj, 3 quizzes and reading guides. Nice prof.

A little tossed, Professor Requena is a good professor in the sense that he cares for his students and always gives good advice about the semester long project, which is pretty difficult, that you work on with your group. First semester is a breeze, almost didn't like there was much of a class. He's extremely nit picky with the project, confusing.

This professor is very sweet and kind! He would always try to make the topics we talk about fun and interactive. However, the semester long group project is pretty difficult, and very time consuming. However, the professor is very understanding if you are absent or late on an assignment!

The class itself is pretty easy, especially the first half. The second half of the semester just focused on a group project. The prof is usually very helpful when you ask questions. The coursework itself was time consuming, but pretty manageable and easy.

Her course consisted of group projects and at the end of the semester, the group will showcase a video that can be time-consuming throughout the semester. Her course is 3 hours which involved discussion on reading. The class felt very long.

She is okay, there would be times she wasn't clear on instructions and would be upset when no one did the type of work she expected. The course itself was interesting but the amount of time in class is three hours. You're expected to work in a group project for the whole semester but there are no tests, only weekly assignments.
Best Professor so far would rec

This professor is amazing, I enjoyed my time in his class a lot. He tells a lot of stories about his life, he's super interesting and laid back. A decent amount of work, but totally manageable if you put the effort in. Easy A if you try. Super awesome professor, would 100% take him again. He truly cares about his job and his students and it shows.

Easily the best Spanish professor at UTSA. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. His lectures are essential to success in the course. You have a lot of reading homework. It can be a little difficult since its ancient Spanish, but you will be fine if you try in his class. Highly recommend.

Such a great professor. He really cares about your learning. Goes over all the tests with you before you take it. (same setup usually just different vocab and sentences on actual test vs when we go over the review) He really just wants you to learn and enjoy class.

Stern but kind, only issue with this class, is that prof is not practical for intermediate students- she expects you to already be fluent. Talk's very fast & uses vocab and grammar you haven't been taught yet. Final group project is hard, all Japanese. The instructions on her assignments and project are sometimes not clear. You must attend class.

Fukuda Sensei is engaging, passionate, and energetic about teaching Japanese. There is a lot of HW that is due before each class, but they aren't too hard. There is one group project in this course. There are also a few large essays that are done throughout the semester too, using grammar from each chapter. Definitely recommend.

This class was very difficult compared to the course description and Fukuda won't budge on the difficulty. A 1200 word essay is due every week in the form of discussion questions. Don't take this course if you're excepting a chill anime class. Side note: some of the films viewed deal with heavy topics that can be triggering without any warning.

Fall 2021 - Great professor, tough course. Just like any other language course, you need to review material everyday. There are also quizzes every single day. Also, there is homework and videos to watch, but those are fairly simple to do. Furthermore, there are 4 exams. This professor does a great job at teaching the materials, highly recommend her

Some of the most fun that I have had in a class, even being online. Sensei Fukuda not only taught the Japanese language but would tell stories and give insight on life in Japan. Although there can be a bit of homework at times, it is easy to keep up with and complements her teaching style. I would easily take this class again. Fukuda Rocks!

I've never left a review for a professor and I am on my last semester of my senior year. This is the worst professor I've ever taken. If you don't say it exactly how she wants it, she will count it wrong. If you miss one question out of 10 or 11 you get an automatic 75! I'm afraid I won't be able to graduate bc of her!
Avoid this class please, take a different Course in place of the credit if you have to, just DO NOT sign up for this lol.

I believed that Writing about Film is my strong suit, and unfortunately, this Professor doesn't seem to agree and has noted it in her emails. If you need to take this for core, please take another section. This Professor would rather attend conferences than provide helpful or positive feedback on assignments!

The films listed in the syllabus were all interesting and historically significant in some capacity. There is a homework assignment every week and two major projects, they are very in-depth. In my experience, this professor was fair and reasonable as long as one did their part as a student.

UPDATE: Never mind, avoid at all costs.

Sabe sobre su materia, pero eso es lo que arruina sus clases. No sabe comunicarse ni organizar los trabajos, por lo que causa confusiones, y aun así es prepotente y engreída cuando le pides que te aclare un tema. Otra cosa: hagas lo que hagas, si no respondes EXACTAMENTE como ella quiere, estarás mal. Membrez, trabaja en tu egocentrismo, por favor.

group projects assigned every week. if you have a job, quit it, because all your time will be spent on this class instead. I think she just offloads lectures to her students instead of putting in the work to teach herself.
The majority of the class is homework from the textbook and participation in class.

Professor Hall is an amazing teacher, she cares about her students and will ensure that you actually learn and become better at the language. There is a lot homework and assignments but it prepares you to do good on the tests. Attendance is mandatory and she is strict on that but there are extra credit opportunities to make for that.
She uses the textbook a lot, but class is easy to follow :)

Travel in France-She seems friendly at first, but u never know what mood she'll be in when she gets to class. Will belittle u if u aren't participating & often makes comments about u in front of the class & expects u to volunteer and attend multiple events outside of class for a grade. Do not recommend. Was supposed to be an interesting elective

recentReviews.comment: The class schedule is put together very poorly. Explanations on assignment expectations are nearly non existent so you will be stuck discussing with your classmates what it is you should do. You will also be graded on attendance by A LOT so beware. Don't recommend. This class has been harder than most of the classes I actually need.

Took her for an Italian film class. Horrible at explaining things, would change the assignment guidelines for presentations the day of and hold you to that (new) standard. If you offer up a different interpretation than her own she'll passive aggressively challenge you in front of the class. Genuinely baffled by all the positive reviews on here.

You would expect this course to be easy, but you do need to put in the work to get an A. We were expected to read around 50 pages of the book weekly. Which isn't bad; however, she randomly gave us pop quizzes to ensure we were reading. We did go on a field trip, and our final was a big potluck with a video of you making your food.

this class wasnt awful but the professor makes sure that you don't have fun. I passed this class although I don't feel like I learned that much Italian. I'm mostly writing the review because she made us take our final exam at 7 IN THE MORNING. although the test was online its something you should be aware of.

Just had to share my thoughts on this Italian class. Professor is seriously the best super helpful  makes learning Italian a blast. And The class is balanced, giving us plenty of time to soak up the language without feeling overwhelmed. If you're looking for a class that's both fun and manageable, this is it. Highly recommend!

recentReviews.comment: Main complaint: so much homework. Going to class is fun but you'll do more work outside of it as all the assignments are online thru the textbook. Not sure if all of the german classes are like that or just hers, so choose wisely or find out before you register. she's overall sweet though

Overall, she was my best professor for the one semester I attended at UTSA. She is very sweet and really cares about what she teaches. She normally grades well. However, I cannot rate her a 5/5 for two reasons:
1. The book is expensive, and in my opinion, not too good.
2. The homework is sooo long, expect to spend at least 6 hours a week.

Dr. D truly cares about teaching and helping you learn German. She is an amazing instructor who will go beyond just the language and help you learn the culture. Though the homework can be a bit much sometimes, its fairly easy. Not a difficult class to pass if you just try and take the time.

Helpful, straightforward lectures, and is easy to reach out for help.  Lots of homework that is difficult, and textbook (required to access homework) is expensive.  You are required to work with classmates on various assignments.  Great professor, but be ready to do some work.
Don't

A lot of viewing of films expected of students outside of class, but honestly he does such fantastic lectures, and his focus is making each student take both a new appreciation of film and of various cultures. As long as you submit to that. Easy A.

Great Professor, took him for FRN 1024 (French in Spanish). He was very motivated and had so much energy. He focused on talking more than assigning heavy homework. He worked really well through the different level of each person's French. Lots of oral exams, final exam is a skit in French. Overall a great professor.

Professor Watson is a really nice guy, but not a very good instructor. He was unclear about rubrics for assignments and tended to grade quite harshly towards the end of the semester. He's also bad at responding to email. Don't take him, take another easy or fun honors culture course.

Professor Watson has extremely unclear grading criteria (no rubric or real guidelines to follow for assignments), never responded to a single email or Canvas message sent, and randomly graded a lot harsher at the end of the semester. Nice guy, but wouldn't recommend the course.

Terrible professor. Please do not take him. He started off nice but during finals, he suddenly started grading much harsher than before. His grading scale is also wonky and he's super unclear about what he wants but then takes off points for not including something that wasn't mentioned to begin with. Horrible at responding to emails.

Overall good professor. 5 Perusall assignments every 3 wks. Midterm and final presentation based on interviews w/ family/Mediterranean person. Readings and 6 films. Lecture and in-class discussion based. Must participate. Good workload and easy grader. No textbook. Friendly and helpful. Focuses on southern Mediterranean/Jews. Recommend for easy A.

Yu Sensei is honestly such a lovely teacher. She helped me learn Japanese really well and all her course work makes a lot of sense and is clear. Attendance is graded but you're allowed to make up some stuff if you're absent. Overall though she is awesome and I would love to take her class over and over again!

Yu Sensei is amazing. Japanese is difficult, but I would not want to learn it from anyone else. Yes, the class is fast-paced, but she makes it fun. There is a method to the madness; apply yourself, and you will do well. The textbook is free- she wrote it and provides it to you. ありがとうございます！

Best professor ever. She structures class time so effectively. There's a lot of homework and quizzes but they aren't too difficult or time-consuming, they really do boost your learning. She also provides Quizlet flashcards which are very helpful. Take this class, you won't regret it!

She is great, be sure to practice a lot and you will do just fine. She does have fast-paced lecture sessions, homework, and quizzes due in every class. Tests: you are required to have a laptop and headphones. Hard to fail this course.

Kind and patient! There is a lot of homework due in this class and a small quiz in almost every lecture. Nothing too difficult; you just have to practice and participate in class to the best of your ability. Test are easy-ish, you must practice, she does tend to speak very fast so make sure you are paying attention.

A wonderfully kind and inspiring Professor, Matsuda Sensei is probably the most helpful language teacher you'll ever have. She's keenly aware of how difficult of a language Japanese is for English/Spanish speakers and doesn't judge you for not always getting it. There is a good amount of homework and usually a group project, but nothing insane.

That Rakugo project was probably the hardest thing I've done in my life tbh. Matsuda-sensei is good at getting you to participate. Everyone gets a chance to speak and if you're having issues with the material, she is patient and helps you work through it. Japanese is a hard language, but having a good teacher kept me motivated.

Be prepared for the workload because it was definitely a surprise! There will be essays you have to write and then read them out loud to turn in as a video. She is a sweet professor and if you ever have questions go to her office hours and she will help.がんばって！

She is a wonderful professor, I had no issues with the course on her end for East Asian History. Very kind professor and an easy grader- you just have to follow the guidelines. There is a bit of reading and writing in the course, but was all reasonable.

Great professor, is kind and will respond to emails. There are no issues with the course; lots of watching East Asian Films and writing. You have to respond to other classmates' posts and do a bit of reading, but this course is nothing unmanageable.

She is very caring for her students. Her lectures are fun and interactive. She makes sure to involve students during the lectures. Her expectations are clear and as long as you do some independent studying like any other language, her class will be easy and fun! Would definitely recommend her!
Just has a really bad attitude with some students! seems like a sweet lady but is rude and condescending. I wish i could like her but nope ! The class wasn't too bad tho easy A

She is so engaging. It is clear to me that she is passionate about teaching Korean to students and wanting them to learn. Take this class with her because I have learned so much and am going to take KOR1024 with her again.

Professor Kim was a great teacher to learn from. She creates a kind and encouraging environment where she wants everyone to be involved and take charge of their learning. She doesn't go too fast with the learning so it is easy to keep up if you do the work and come to class. She was always available to help and overall just a very kind professor.

Sometimes her explanations are a little difficult to grasp, but if you ask, she always takes the time to repeat and break down the more difficult concepts for students to understand. She is also very kind and funny, and provides many resources and interactives for students to study.

recentReviews.comment: I'm a single mother, and babysitters are EXPENSIVE when you're studying and working full time, so unfortunately I had to bring my infant to Prof. Rushforth's lecture. He cried and people were mad. Rushforth carried him around during lecture, using chloroform to put him to sleep. He went above and beyond as a professor!!
He's a great professor and was honestly the best part of my week. He's really understanding and you can tell he's passionate about his job.

Very vague instructions and gets distracted in class so easily that he wouldn't actually teach much. Be prepared to teach yourself through lots of weekly readings that are graded. There are three pretty big projects and one group final project. He expects graduate level participation and knowledge despite this being a mixed undergrad and grad class

This class was really fun and a highlight of my week. We are only graded on journal entries, science fair, attendance, and some other random grades. This class is definitely helpful in developing communication and quick thinking skills. This was an interesting experience as someone who has never done improv or had an interest in it. Try it out!
Wonderful professor. Talks a lot about some experience with bedbugs in Guatemala, but apart from that pretty decent prof. I'm going to go make some spaghetti now.

One of the most understanding instructors I've had. When I was undiagnosed and unmedicated for a health condition that significantly impacted my ability to participate and perform in class, she went out of her way to make accommodations that no other professor was willing to provide. Her flexibility made a huge difference in my academic experience.
Nice person but terrible professor. Didn't learn a thing in her class. Flexible with late assignments though which is great.

If anyone says this course is easy, then they are lying. If they say the course is too hard, then they quit before actually trying. Professor Maltseva creates a comfortable environment for learning and making mistakes. The amount of assignments can seem like a lot, but they are really just clusters of small exercises to help you practice.
Always late to her own class

Very kind and good professor.  The class was HARD.  prepare to study a lot on your own or you won't keep up in class.  It moves very fast and was really hard.  The professor will tutor and help outside of class.
I loved having her! Easy grader and gave good feedback. I will be taking her again next semester.

Amazing professor. Assignments were fun and easy. It's very easy to get a good grade by doing nothing, but please make sure to pay attention as the Spanish classes above this are way harder and you'll wish you paid attention in this class.

Such an amazing professor! Can't think of a better professor you should take for Elementary Spanish. Kind, inspiration, and informative. The class does have a lot of homework assignments and different topics, but they're very manageable to learn. There's 3 oral assignments in spanish as a learner and 1 in english as a coach. Highly recommend her!

Just take her!!! I have never had a teacher who genuinely cares about her students as much as she does. So many times during the course, she emailed me about how well I was doing, and it really made me feel so seen. There are lots of assignments and homework, and the conversations can be nerve-wracking, but she is so supportive.

Extremely organized and clear in her teaching. She broke down material in a way that made it easy to understand and always encouraged questions. She gave helpful feedback, offered extra credit and make-up work, and genuinely cared about her students' success and improvement throughout the course. Accepted late work at times. Highly recommend.
awesome professor
She gives off High School teacher vibes, she's nice but she's a bit annoying in the early classes. No exams, only 10 assignments due every week on different days.

Amazing!!!! I was hesitant at first because I don't feel comfortable speaking Spanish, but my confidence has increased. Her lectures taught me a lot, and because she demanded participation and practice, I was able to put what I learned into practice! But she's very patient and funny! She is someone I would really like to take again!
THE. GOAT.

I took her heritage section of SPN 1014 by accident but it ended up being a perfect fit for me. It's a 4 credit course, so there is a lot of weekly assignments. Professor Nowlin is a wonderful person and a wonderful teacher! All of her lectures were entertaining and informative and she made me actually want to continue coming to class. 9.5/10

Amazing professor! I took this course in the Spring so the lectures were well paced. Absolutely does NOT care about his students. I understand he is passionate about this subject, but he takes it way too seriously. If you have other classes, this class will take up most of your time. Nice professor, always willing to help students as long as your willing to ask for help. The class is very informative and I learned a lot. I enjoy the group activities. Nice professor! if you are taking HUM 2093 online I 100% recommend it. Be sure to do all your assignments on time and you should be okay. Be sure to look at the criteria for the assignments because they are very important for grading. Overall, really enjoyed this course with this professor.

Dr. Adair is a very nice person. :) He was very knowledgeable about the Synoptic Gospels, and how they compare. THE GOAT, only take his class if u genuinely enjoy philosophy. Exam and quizzes arent difficult, rewards u for speaking in class.

Amazing class

Only 3 exams for the semester no actual assignments. Super easy as long as you pay attention during lecture and take your notes. He makes it easy and fun to learn! If you ever have a question or need help, dont be afraid to ask. He is great.
LOVEEE this teacher. Such an easy class, he cares a lot. He will help you if you did a mistake on an exam and is very chatty too. Love his energy. Would love to see him in my future classes.

Professor Debbage was a joy in an otherwise bland course. His passion for the subject shows through and helps the course to breeze by. Extra credit, too!

Amazing professor. The class is super easy and very sweet and as long as you pay attention, study and take notes then you should be fine. The way he grades is 3 tests (drops the lowest), final exam, and knowledge checks.

Take her online class it is the easiest A ever. There is a project that takes a lot of effort but it is worth doing over in person tx pol. Take her fs!!!

Super chill makes the class easy and fun with in class videos. Is accesible outside of class.

Professor Rhadbane is not at all a difficult teacher in terms of classwork, and he is always available to have meaningful conversations about the content (and ideas beyond the realm of the content). I felt that he directed me through learning and understanding everything I needed to know.

Update on grade situation Said she was "unable" to find my name in gradebook due to me using my preferred name on every assignment, as if my preferred name wasn't in ASAP I was not comfortable using my deadname in this class and feel that the unwarranted F could have been completely avoidable. Otherwise good professor, pay attention and participate
She's a good professor, just make sure you really focus in class. Just wish communication was better. Currently going back and forth with the department chair due to a grading error.

She does come across as very rude until you interact with her one-on-one.  I thought the same thing until I went out of my way to speak with her personally, and I found her very inspirational.  She's extremely knowledgable, and if more people took the time to connect with her, they'd think the same.  She's just misunderstood.

This professor was not clear about anything. Gave us a list of textbooks that were not accessible and was very vague about instructions for every assignment. Only gave us four assignments for the entire semester and graded them harshly. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR.

She does fine as a professor.  In order for her clasess to be passed, you need to put in the effort.  She's not a bad profesor, but she isn't easy either.  I'd take her classes again, but you need to put in the effort towards receving a better grade by participating and reading things provided.
Really was a great class, learned a lot of interesting and insightful information. Just study the materials, and try your best on the assignments!

There was a heavy amount of assignments in this summer course however if you finish it, you will get an A. She is not a tough grader but the last week of assignments pile up. There were 2 assignments, a quiz, a group presentation, and a 2000 word paper due in the last week so manage your time wisely. She responded quickly to emails and was helpful.
Her classes could use a bit more structure keeping up with the syllabus but overall the class was very doable and she was very respectful. Her lectures were very informative over the class topic.
This class was really easy and very boring at times. Aside from the tests being a little difficult, the coursework was incredibly easy and the bare minimum got me an A.

Dr. Stefanova is very nice. Attendance is necessary in order to actually pass this class because her PowerPoints don't help much. She is very knowledgeable about European politics and political economy. She is also willing to be lenient on deadlines, if you have a good reason for missing any. Be willing to speak up and add to class discussion.

Free textbooks. Midterm, Final, two quizzes, and weekly writings on chapter material. Professor is in a different country, so it's TA lead and completely self-taught. Quizzes from week 2/3 were left ungraded even by the time I withdrew in week 8. The amount of reading is insane, esp. for a lower-div course. The two exams are most of course grade.

Had a terrible incident in my life & needed extended time, every instructor offered it & sympathy but her. An exam closed once & I asked to use my accommodations. Had to harass her for a week, didn't answer when I got disability services or chair of dpt involved. TA emailed me instead meanwhile she was answering everyone else's emails in the class.

Very inaccessible outside of the classroom. All content is on lecture slides, multiple 40-page readings, and YouTube videos. 1 assignment per week with very minimal credit towards the final grade. One five-question quiz at the beginning of the class can tank your grade for the rest of the class. Midterm and final weigh heavily. I do not recommend.

Lengthy discussion posts and a lot of reading. You'll be fine if you get them done on time but you will be at a 50 if you turn in any late work, no matter if its a few hours or a couple days late. Could definitely be an interesting class but I took this class as an elective and did not expect to have lengthy weekly assignments.

This was a great course. It was challenging, but as long as you stay on top of your work, and try your best you will do great. Many extra credit opportunities. No required textbook, resources are given for each module.

Don't recommend.

His Canvas is disorganized. His syllabus is unclear in places and he blames you if you don't understand. He uses disparaging language in his announcements. Rude, unprofessional, and angry are 3 words I would use to describe him. Some of the class submitted their paper topics to the incorrect location, and he took 25% off of the final paper grade.

So when I took this class I only had to read and do the tests. He seemed to have time to write an insulting email to students who didn't do well on his tests. He always seem to need to blame people instead of realizing how he is the problem and one failing. Any time I saw him it was him just walking in circles around the building

Highly unprofessional "professor" who doesn't understand technology, how to grade, or his students. He's the type who takes himself and his class way too seriously and sees himself as infallible. He gives exams on Sunday's. SUNDAYS! He only posted 2 lectures on the first week of class that are years old. There is little direction and we are graded on few things. Professional

If he decides he doesn't like you it's over for you. There's nothing you can do to change it. And if he doesn't like you he'll make it so obvious. He won't even try to hide it. I've been taking Professor Hofferberth since the beginning of the Fall 2024 semester, he has quite the personality. His lectures are engaging, he is also very forward on ensuring his students are in attendance to really learn the material. His attendance is hard and he will count you absent if you are tardy, had a hard time with him this semester.

Nice professor, you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. Not a fan of having to buy multiple $50+ textbooks and have weekly pop quizzes attached to the books.  He always runs over class time too for some reason? I will never understand why professors insist on having students pay more and more for books they'll use once.

I found his online courses really do-able. This course is exam heavy there are no other assignments BUT he makes it really easy. The exams are multiple choice, there are lecture notes if you miss class and there is study guides. He is an awesome professor, I am taking another one of his courses next semester. When I graduate he will be missed :(.
Great class, I can't wait to take another class with him

One of the most boring professors i've ever taken. His tests are lazy. His lectures are lazy. He reads from slides and has 0 enthusiasm. He also will not budge at all when confronted with complaints about test questions. If you have trouble paying attention or if you have the ability to think critically, I recommend you take another class.

Class was ran well and I appreciated that lectures were recorded and posted online. Professor Oliva was generally really fair and generous with his exams and there was not a lot of homework, making this one of the best courses I took for the semester. Definitely recommend taking his classes if you haven't already.

Save your GPA. This is the second time i've had this professor (different classes btw), and every semester he's just as extra. first of all he's not even the one that  answers your emails or prepares the content you will study, its his assistant because he's not "good with tech", theres a reason theres a support group for this class!
The material was boring, the work was very tedious, and you needed to read the textbook at length. I'm glad it's over

Overall I just think his class is poorly ran. I took it as an online course and it was supposed to be an easy A for me like all of my online classes. This one is super heavy with assignments and the tests are put together by him so unless you read the textbook word for word you're doomed. Wouldn't recommend if you are looking for an easy A.
If you can avoid taking this class please do so, save your GPA. The readings are sooooo longgggg, you learn on your own.

He has a lecture, reading assignment with questions, and a weekly quiz. This is a very typical online class I feel. The Quizzes and Exams are proctored with honor lock and you cannot go back to check answers. This is an okay class if youre good at history and politics which luckly I am, If youre not tho i wouldnt reccomend.

Took him for contracts, my favorite class so far. I loved it so much! I am taking him again for 2 courses next semester, the class discussions are hilarious and actually help you dissect and understand the material so you know how the rules of the case apply and don't apply. We are only graded on 2 exams and a group project/final position paper.

The class was heavily graded based on two exams. The lectures are not helpful for the exams because instead of giving clear answers on what cases affect the law or create exceptions in the law, he asks his students to attack scenarios using the cases, changes the scenarios as they argue them so the case law becomes irrelevant or difficult to argue.

This is by far one of the worst classes I've taken at UTSA. It was for PAL 4233: Federal Courts. He was never prepared for class and his course objectives where not clear along with his syllabus not having the right information or dates on them and him making last minute changes. He rambles too much in class and does not stay on topic. Exams suck
Professor Paschal is an absolutely outstanding Professor.  I have had him for two courses and again in Spring 2023.

Awesome professor!! I thoroughly enjoyed his course. It was very discussion-based, which is where he got a lot of the test material from so its important to show up to class. You definitely wont get an A if you dont work it for it, but he is a fair grader and definitely makes you think. If I werent graduating, I would love to take his class again.

He's a good guy, really knows his stuff. He is now at Utah Valley University for POLS 1100. Is willing to make accommodations if you tell him if you need them. His tests are tough and only grades on the 3 tests, an essay and attendance.I like the guy he just needs to grade more so your grade isn't so heavily impacted if your a bad test taker.

Professor Brogdon was great. He doesn't do lectures so much as class discussions, but he talks through most of them. He's very knowledgeable and also very careful to be non-partisan. Very engaging speaker.

Prof. Brogdon is absolutely wonderful as a prof and a person!  He is passionate and knows his stuff. He wants students to engage in conversation and become involved in the lectures. I'm looking forward to taking more classes with him in the future, easily one of the best profs around. You will need to try but put in the effort & you will do great!

Very thorough in explanations. Best political theory Professor, hands down. I have taken him for 4 consecutive semesters and some of these comments have claimed that this is a difficult class, I would say it is just a serious class, even then he breaks everything down so that you can understand. Enjoyable classes that enable critical thinking.
I never got a 100 on an assignment but I suppose my grades were fair enough. Put in the effort and the work and you can get an A. I thought this was pretty much an average course.

I've taken, political philosophy. american political thought, and intro to political theory with her. Extraordinarily easy grader, like 70% of the weight falls on very easy multiple choice exams. She was a decent professor. I took her for Political Philosophy. She does focus heavily on the texts, and all off our exams were 75% what we discussed in class and 25% actual reading. Participation does matter; however you can probably get away with not participating if you do decent on the exams. Not for me personally, but others may enjoy it.

Awesome professor. You actually feel like you're attending university and not high school (participation based discussions). People that give her bad ratings are just used to being able to cheat and not having to actually read for a class.

Most of her courses are discussion based, so you have to attend the class having read the material to know what is being talked about. She asks tough questions that make you think but it helps you understand the material on a deeper level. I LOVE her classes because I actually feel like I am learning. Participate and go to office hours!

As long as you read you'll be all good, participate in discussions she's really interactive and it makes the class more enjoyable if you do. it can get boring if you don't read. the tests are straightforward and the study guide is practically the whole test, missing the short response.

Laracey was a decent prof, and the class is very easy and straightforward. The only difficulty I found was being able to reach him. I sent many emails through utsa outlook but never got responses back. not sure if it was a problem on my end or his because he did specify we could email him through those. Overall decent and easy class.
Good online class for A

I only got a D because I missed the entire 1st quarter. The tests and exams are OPEN BOOK. They don't say this directly, but please notice! There's a tab to find the textbook in the same page as the tests. Please look!

This prof does nothing its all on your own, but the class is pretty easy other than the fact that they are time consuming. Do a chapter each week and you should be fine because his deadlines are in big gaps.

Don't take this class in the summer. 14 SmartBooks (they take 1.5 hrs each), quizzes, and hws (each 5%), plus 5% for discussions with hour long videos. Doing the work felt useless just for 5%.

Exams are 80%, & they pull random facts from all that busywork. 
It's a burnout challenge disguised as a class. Prof made me put 10x effort it deserved.
Great class, great professor I'd take another class if I could. Easy "A"

Professor Aleman's POL1013 class was a breeze! The weekly quizzes and easy exams made it a low-stress experience. The recorded lectures were super helpful, and unstuckstudy was a game-changer for prepping. Overall, a great choice for an online GE requirement.
Interesting class. Lectures were very informational and straight to the point.

Professor Aleman did a wonderful job with teaching this course! One of my favorite classes that I have taken in college for core requirements. There was not a lot of work which I really appreciated, and the recorded lectures were AMAZING! Exams were always very well put together on canvas. Overall was a wonderful experience in this course!
The online class was straightforward. It was the least homework-heavy class I have had.

If you arent into politics, this class will likely be difficult. The subject matter is dense and dry, but Gervais is good as you can tell he tries to make the class more interesting and adds humor to his lectures which I appreciate. Exams dont give you a lot of time, you have to pay attention and take notes otherwise you will get lost quickly.

I'm someone who is very invested in politics for my age so to get a C in a class about politics is baffling to me. Professor Gervais is a TOUGH grader. Exams do not have nearly enough time for the large amount of questions either.. my classmates and I were struggling to finish in time.

He wasn't a bad teacher however his grading was odd. Professor Gervais was one of the best professors I had this semester. His lectures were interactive, and the learning modules were easy to follow along and gain information from. I personally had no problem not using the textbook, although he said it was mandatory. Tests didn't have a lot of time to take them, but overall a good professor.
I enjoyed this Professor and this class. However, hes a tough grader. Each class was mandatory and there was a participation grade.

She's OK...not really that great. not a lot of student-to-professor interaction. The class is pretty straightforward but hard to contact her. I have called during phone hours, never picked up. One time she posted a video assignment with absolutely no info, bunch of students messaged her about it and she never replied. gave us all a 100 tho ig

One of the worst professors I've had. Doesn't respond to many emails, if she does it'll most likely be non-helpful. You will have to teach yourself, literally. If you can, find a better professor, it'll do you good. You're paying for your own help in this one.

The worst professor I've ever had! never communicated with students, her office hours are by phone call only which is two hours on Monday and Tuesdays. mandatory weekly quizzes and she claims she cares about her students but good look getting in contact with her. your lucky to get a response 3 weeks later.

If I could give her negative ratings, I would. Words can't describe how bad of a professor she is. I had never before seen someone like her. She sais she's wants to succeed and that we matter yet she doesn't do crap to teach. Be ready to pay to be your own professor

If you care about your GPA and mental health, PLEASE DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS, SHE IS THE WORKS PROFESSOR I'VE EVER HAD. Weekly chapter and 2 quizzes. Does not teach or help at all. It's impossible to contact her and if she actually responds, it's not usefull and stupid. SAVE YOUR MONEY AND DONT TAKE HER

Henry Esparza is demeaningly disrespectful toward his students and expects an unmatched level of respect to be given. Just do not take him.

DO NOT TAKE HIM. I wake up every day dreading to walk into his lecture. I have cried so many times already because of him and it has only been 3 1/2 weeks.

Great professor, very passionate and respectable. Grades based on 6 exams, no extra credit opportunities. Engages with students and occasionally opens the floor to small debate. I missed a test due to a medical emergency.  For some reason it was counted as unexcused and he would not let me retake the exam even after detailing the situation. This class is only graded by around 4-6 tests. Not very much room for error.

Grade based solely on 6 tests. Does offer small extra credit, and lets you use cheat sheets for exams. Exams can cover material not in the lectures, which is frustrating. Overall a good human being and solid teacher
I did not try for this class, it was the easiest thing I have ever done in my life.

Loved this class! Each week there is a 5 ? quiz, and discussion board. 3 exams in total, and the review is exactly like the exam. I took her for texas government and she was great. She was very communicative and provided a bunch of resources. She records lectures and gives out study guides. She lets you retake exams and quizzes. Stay on top of the discussions and you will pass this class easily.
I am not good at politics and she made learning the topic very easy. You'd have to try and fail to actually fail this class.
They weren't very passionate but it was very easy to glide through the class. They did leave midway but if anything it just made it easier. Would take again.
She made it super simple! Would totally take another one of her classes.

Pretty good professor while it lasted, she liked to ramble on sometimes but mostly enjoyed what she was teaching. I only saw her for a couple months but she had to leave due to health problems. Hope you doing better big S

Thick accent, not really sure what kind. Poorly organized and miscommunicated concepts, her "corrections" on your assignments are basically just her trying to write for you, didn't seem like a case of "you should do this" but a case of "replace this and im not gonna tell you why"

I do not recommend this online class or professor at all.

She's accessible outside class but we'd rarely have class.

She is very nice but she is not looking for original work. Also, since her class is online she must have working technology so we students won't struggle to hear her. She's considerate at best.

I took course 3363 and he had us buy 3 textbooks with the first exam covering an entire textbook all 17 chapters. We learn by ourselves online, and in person all he does is review, no teaching. On top of that there are only 4 grades for the whole semester, all exams and essays so if you fail one it's basically it.
Boring and plain. He comes off as he knows what he talks about but he can't even argue with students who oppose his opinions. I avoid this one and take any course Jon Taylor teaches in POL instead.
took civil rights in america and texas. he's an ok professor, lectures are plain and dry, class is kinda boring. sometimes you'll get in groups to go over reading, but really not fun class.

I took this professor's online flex course, expected it to be difficult. was doable, course consisted of module quizzes and assignments. the professor seemed to be a moderate grader, gives good feedback when grading and his online modules consisted of recorded lectures, lecture slides and provided extra reading material which were very helpful.

Wilson is a very easy grader and a really engaging lecturer, but there are very few grades and a lot of participation in the class is needed to pass and do well. He likes short answer tests and class discussions.

This class was incredibly weirdly structured, confusing for no reason, and not flexible in any shape or form. I passed and Im happy that its over now, but just dont take the course unless you like being confused and bored.

I know that Dr. Ang's grade is low here, and that's because her Designing Research class is hard, and you'll have to 100% work for that grade. But this is my 4th year at UTSA, and, from experience, most of the POL/PAL professors don't care about their students. But Dr. Ang did. And she worked hard for me. And I'm grateful for that.

Doing the work was so no problem, however she is a very tough grader and is not always clear on what exactly she wants. So this made some assignments confusing and could hurt your grade if you dont fully understand.
Just do the work and you'll be fine

Prof. Ang is complex in the way she explains. She grades pretty hard and there was a few miscommunications we had. Probably the hardest class I will ever take as it's complicated to grasp what she means and confuses me with how she words assignment instructions. Has also forgotten to add important info for certain assignments & gives hw every week.

recentReviews.comment: This man has gotten A LOT of flak, and he deserves some of it. He doesn't allow food, laptops, or phones, and he is not good at engaging with his students. I would not retake him, but he's not all bad, he's an easy grader if you pay attention and know the basics and clearly cares. If you aren't afraid of hard work and want to learn he's for you.

Hes not an lenient teacher, all he gives is 4 exams for the whole semester so you have to really study for his exams and he will not help boost your grade up whatever final grade you receive even if you failing he dont care he take his job to serious.

He is not very good about responding to students. It is also very easy to fail given the fact that the only grade you will have are exams. I understand COVID-19 has changed a lot of our lives, but it would be nice to have a professor that cared about his students learning and he simply is not one of those.
He is a good teacher but nonetheless, his course is difficult, probably one of the hardest I have had.
Lectures are long and he often goes off track. Tests aren't super hard though as long as you study from the book and from notes. He also takes attendance.

I'm so glad I had professor matta as my first chem professor. The lectures were easy to understand and she was very clear on her expectations and what you must do during and outside of class to succeed. If you listen and basically just TRY, you should do very well in this course. ALEKs was everyday but honestly you get in routine after a while.

Dr. Matta is an okay teacher and gives you an idea of what you're getting into. That being said, get ready to study. The main issue is the daily grades on ALEKS throughout the semester including weekends and breaks. She also hides the total grade calculation from you so either do it yourself or just sit and wait for the end of the semester.

If you are not religious, get one and start praying. She is completely unintelligible up to 4 rows back, and she is incapable of personally aiding you if you have any questions. The TA's were basically the real teachers.

I absolutely loved taking this class with Dr. Matta. She genuinely wants to help the students understand the concepts. She works through problems and explains well. She also is very good about listening to the class. If extra help is needed she stops to explain in more detail. This class just requires focus and continuous practice.

I absolutely adore this teacher, she's extremely intelligent and an absolute sweetheart, but I did absolutely awful in this class. Chemistry is a hard subject and I feel like I didn't have enough time to go over most of the material. We are forced to do Aleks every single day which makes it hard to study for the stuff we are actually learning.
Difficult class, great professor. I doubt a better chem professor exists at UTSA.
Chemistry is hard, especially here at UTSA, but I don't regret taking Davidson. If you do all the ALEKS and attend lecture you will be fine.

Best chem professor here, only reason to take another is his sections fill up so fast. He doesn't write exams however, so the reason to take this class is his slides, explanations, and examples are easy to follow and understand.
Love his enthusiasm. Hes very nice and chill.  He goes over things well the only thing I didn't really like was that it was all powerpoints I wish he was more hands on.

Professor Davidson assigns a lot of work, so make sure to stay on top of what's due (ALEKS included). Though the class itself was a bit difficult, he was very helpful when it came to reviewing material for upcoming tests. He explains concepts rather quickly, but just make sure to study a little a day, and you should be good.
