recentReviews.comment: Definitely one of the better professors in the chem department, very nice and caring and will take her time in class to make sure everyone gets the questions before moving on. She's more of a "beginner friendly" professor. Exams can be difficult tho due to the volume of materials. GO TO STARS TUTORS, they'll give a lot of tips and tricks on exams.

Chem sucks but she made it less sucky. For the lab lecture final quiz, she let us collaborate with the person sitting next to us. Every class has a quiz using Iclicker at the end. She really just reads off slides during class, but if you miss a class its a zero for that day. Besides that she is probably the best and easiest chem professor at UTSA.
Horribly tough grader and is unreasonable at time, a reflection of this poor department

PICK HER!! she is so caring and is always willing to help you with anything you need. obviously chem is hard, and the tests are hard, but just redo all the quizzes, and you should be good. she gives good lectures. take it from someone who hates chem :)))

Class is not difficult at all if you put in the effort. There are a lot of extra assignments for basic chem that are annoying but really easy. Also, there are assignments due practically every day on ALEKS, so make sure to constantly check that. Exam questions are pulled from the iclicker and quizzes in class, so not that hard

He's a nice guy like if I was older I would say we could be friends. HOWEVER, in class he's just talking. You have to learn everything by yourself and if you want someone to kinda guide you through ochem he is not the right person to take. Its like he is at the finish line saying hurry up but not really taking your hand and helping you get there.

He is a nice guy, but he does not offer much guidance. You are mostly going to have to figure out what he and his TA's want from trial and error. I am honestly surprised I pulled out a decent grade. I liked him as a person, he seemed like an interesting guy. However, many failed due to the course to how he orientated it. Be cautious taking this.

Took for ochem I and he was great! He truly loves the subject and is very willing to help u outside of class. I was intimidated due to his low ratings, but this class is hard, and u NEED to put in effort. He's very kind and caring and wants his students to do well. I studied everyday. If u know how to do the problems in the book you'll be ok.

Dr. E is a chill guy, but very disorganized. The TA for this semester was no help. There will be homework's quizzes may be random and not very tech savvy BUT his exams are like the book so practice those, did do curve on final and does like spectroscopy. You will pass if you practice! I'm taking him again due to knowing the structure of his tests.

Lectures well, ask questions or for examples. Read textbook chapter before class. PRACTICE. Exams are your whole grade. DONT MISS CLASS. Study for ACS from the start of the semester, it is mostly Ochem I. Attend exam review sessions w/TA. Go to office hours as often as possible! If you bomb the first exam, just drop.

Do not take this Professor does not care and dismissive when asking questions. Treats every student as if they have taken chem 2 before. Take Professor Davidson so much better, started to go to his lectures over this Professor

Had him for gen chem 1&2, he's very understanding and flexible with his students. The exams are hard but it's not his fault he doesn't write the exams. He has a sense of humor some people don't like but I thought it made the class more fun and engaging. If you're taking him just be prepared to STUDY.

Compared to other professors, he is willing to help students when they are having difficulty. if your miss an exam he allows you to still take. I had him as my lab instructor over the summer. He grades lab reports carefully, so make sure your reports are complete, well written, and follow all the instructions.
He's fine but be ready to pull your weight in class. I really can't say much beyond that.

If you plan on passing chemistry, I'd recommend looking elsewhere. He spends most of class reviewing basic material, then rushes through new content in the last 5-10 minutes. The class leans heavily on jokes rather than instruction, which makes it difficult to actually learn the material.

Dr.Zapata is an easy going professor and seems "cool", but I did not learn anything from him. He had review sessions for exams the night before the test and he hadn't even made the exams so we had no idea what was going to be on there. He gave out the list of topics for the exam an hour before it was time for our test. Sounds bored when teaching.

Dr. Zapata is by far the best Chemistry professor to take. GenChem II seemed very intimidating because I am not good at chemistry but by the end of the semester, he made me love it. He gives great examples and explanations and is available to further discuss topics if you don't understand them. He is a fun professor with great lectures. 10/10

This was my 3rd time taking this course, so my grade does not stem from the professor at all. DO YOUR ALEKS!! By just getting 100%s on your Aleks and doing the 30 mins a day to get extra credit, this will put you in a great spot even if you don't do well on any exams. Honestly, I failed pretty much every exam and still was able to pass the class.

Taught as if we already knew the material & provided no resources to practice. Tests came out of left field & were made day of, so it was unsure what we would be tested on. "Weekly quizzes" turned out to be only 1, that was graded by attendance. Took forever to grade. Had to curve 3/4 tests out of 120 & final out of 140. ALEKS gave +10 each test.

He is fun, and listening to his lectures in entertaining, he's a funny guy. My only complaint would be that he is slightly disorganized. He moved a lot of test dates, he takes a while to grade thinks, he shifts his hours around a lot, but overall, he is a good professor and the class isn't too difficult.
be ready to wake up to a surprise exam

he hides your grades with the hopes that it would somehow magically help you lock in in an already difficult class. Very hands off. Does not teach, he reviews. Tests look nothing like the review we do. Objectively he sets everyone up for failure. Couldn't recommend this teacher any less.
lab reports for every lab there is pre lab and post lab reports. one mid term exam and final exam.

I had taken Mamiya for lab lecture ochem 1 over the summer. He truly is as harsh as he is hyped up to be. He is very down to the hair on grading, harsh deadlines, and there is no room for discussion. He keeps your grade hidden as to avoid arguing with students. Lack of accountability on his end.

he is hated by most but he is a great teacher and forces you to learn proactively a huge shock at first for the work load but if you take the time and follow his modality of teaching you will get the score you want would take again
Great professor overall, really likes what he does and teaching the curriculum. Class is relitivly easy if you show up.

Best professor I've had hands down. His lectures are informative and full of passion, and the work load is super doable and easy. The course is literally designed for you to pass as long as you turn in the assignments. There was no final, all of the tests and quizzes open note. Quizzes are unlimited attempts too, and the labs weren't bad. 10/10

Dr. Frederick is one of the best instructors I've ever had. The concepts are hard but he makes them easy to understand with the lectures, softchalk lessons and the office hours he offers. Virtual labs were a big thing but he was always willing to help us out if we had a deficient team.

I enjoyed this course. Some comments mentioned his frustration with lateness but they missed the part of students repeatedly being 30 minutes late and causing distraction. He is not a tough grader and he provides extra credit opportunities. The tests are easy to pass if you manage to read the lessons ahead of time at least one day before test due.

He was an ok professor but if you are late to his class, don't bother showing up. He would regularly call students out for being late and got upset when no one showed up to class. The class can be done all online but attendance is graded.

I was in this class for less than a week and he already ruined chemistry for me. There is no reason he should be as rude as he is to people who needed help. Also... an exam on the 2nd day of class? Hard pass. Switched sections in a heartbeat. Please choose a different professor. You'll hate chemistry if you stick with him.

gets paid comission for students using ALEKS. he makes comments to TAs about how seeing students again because he knows a lot of ppl fail this course. he'll drop you if you miss 5 classes, need to provide medical excuses and even then he might not accept them. the class is purposely designed to be difficult. it can be done but he's not a good prof

Everyone has a different experience with this guy, but for Gen Chem I Lab you will not be seeing a lot of him if that helps. Your TA will be who you interact with the most. Just study for the iClicker quizzes, show up to class/lab on time and hand in your work before the deadline. You'll be okay, I promise.

I only took Arman for lab lecture, and he can be intimidating at times. The lab is a good amount of work with hefty prelab videos and he'll do iclicker right at the start of lecture for attendance. I'm in gen chem 2 lab right now and I actually miss him. If you study what he provides, iClicker questions, and procedures you'll do good.

Dr. Arman is smart, and he has a passion for chemistry/crystallography, but he expects too much from Gen Chem I students. His lectures are okay, but you have lecture, then a video assignment (30+ minutes), then the TA in lab explains again. He gets into crystallography and organic chem towards the end of term, which is not Gen Chem I relevant.
This is the worst professor I've ever had. If you like and respect yourself just don't.

The professor is completely unprofessional. Expectations are high for such a general course. This member of the faculty looks down upon his students and acts as if he is god's gift to chemistry. General chemistry has an extremely amount of busy work for some reason at UTSA. Lab manual are required which are not even used fully. Good luck.

Cons: -He's unclear and occasionally straight up wrong in his lectures. 
-He loads you down with a ton of homework. Expect 20+ hours of work/week. 
-Many of his materials are poorly written and confusing, including test questions.
-He yells during exams.

Pros: -You'll learn acid-base neutralization reactions very well.
-Goofy Star Wars references.

Dr. Arman gives a quiz virtually every day on material from ALEKS and the daily videos. Be aware that the videos can be up to 2 hours long and that the ALEKS will take a lot of effort every day. It's not impossible to get a good grade, but it is not easy and other professors tend to be a little less intense.

This guy sucks. The courseload is unreasonably heavy, and every time I went into the tests thinking I understood all the material I would come out with a grade of 75. The learning program he uses is really expensive ($140 if I remember right) but is completion based so it's a good grade-booster. Also if you email him prepare to be ignored.
Her accent is very strong so you won't be able to understand her at all. She's very strict about no laptops or phones. She runs away when students come to her after class.

Took Dr. Reeves for both Organic I and II. She is the bomb, simply put. Yes her class is hard but organic is supposed to be hard. She gives you all the resources under the sun to use and doing so makes the course very easy. Practice exams similar to the real ones. Show your initiative and she will see you as a better student. Be FOMO for Ochem

she's sweet but overall, genuinely do not take her. there's a reason why your TA's and tutors feel bad whenever you say you're taking reeves bc she has a reputation of being the professor with the most to give in such a small amount of time. for reference her ochem 2 class is taking 3 exam in a span of 7 days bc she can't manage time…

We were pushed to the maximum in a minimum amount of time. We were given a test within a week of a previous test with 2 weeks leading up to the final. Timing in this class is poor, and sympathy from the professor is low. The only positive is the test reviews are similar. These reviews are divided into 1 & 5 stars, it is not a risk worth taking.

Not once, have I rated anyone here, keep this in mind, in all my years of school, I had never failed a class nor see half the class drop until I decided to take her (that should tell you a lot). Exams were not even 50% of what she would provide for reviews, quizzes, every week, Be ready to study and dedicate your life to this class. Best of luck!!

What a massive HEADACHE this professor was. Would expect us to read the book before lecture but admitted she has not read the new book the department switched to. Did not know my grade ALL SEMESTER! Exam questions were written like riddles and some questions had more than one right answer but she would still mark wrong. Watch nerd ninja to do well.

This professor was the biggest head ache. She was never on top of grades, doesn't understand technology, and is extremely boring in lecture. She doesn't answer emails and doesn't listen to her students. I had an assignment that I missed one part of and suddenly I had a 25 on the paper? Makes no sense avoid her at all costs PLEASE.

Please listen to the reviews that say do NOT take her. Exams always had material that she said would not be on there. She posts assignments without announcements. please do not take her (I am NOT usually one to complain about a professor but she is the worst professor I have ever taken in undergrad).

Awful lecturer, doesn't actually teach during class. You will have to look for outside resources to learn the topics. Doesn't care at all about her students. 0/10, I hope the Chem Dept. will reevaluate her abilities and contributions to students/academia. Would NOT recommend taking her class.

Terrible in every aspect. Wastes lecture time rambling about topics that are not relevant. Misguides students on what to expect on exams via vague and inaccurate study guides. Assigns homework that is not relevant to what concepts will be covered on the exams. Barely answers emails. 

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

Clearly intelligent and a very nice man. However, extremely difficult to hear him and understand what his notes say. takes forever to upload things to canvas and its extremely unorganized anyways. I was unable to finish, mid semester I decided there was no way to pass the class. You have to have lots of free time to teach yourself..

He's probably the smartest man I've ever met, but he is not a good professor (at least not for Gen Chem One). He knows what he's talking about and is very sweet, but you'll have to teach yourself most of the content, but ALEKS can help with this. He's very soft spoken and likes to go on tangents, maybe better for higher level courses.

Dr. Ermler is a nice guy, however I feel that Gen Chem 2 is not the best subject for him to teach (talks about subjects in detail equivalent to higher level chemistry). He does attendance by iClicker, but it was always the same 1 question quiz. Overall, he's alright. Definitely read the textbook to supplement his lectures.

Ermler is a very quiet, soft-spoken, sweet old man. He is very intelligent, however, he teaches to explain the content but he doesn't go over anything enough to actually absorb info from his lectures. 

P.S. His handwriting sucks (respectfully, but it sucks)
Reads directly off the slides and his handwriting is completely illegible. You WILL have to teach yourself all of the material.

Professor Gorski is very straightforward, really nice and funny. Does talk the whole time during lectures but exams aren't that difficult since it's straight from the slides he provides. So mainly if you pay attention and attend class and do some practice you'll pass.
Really awesome professor. If you follow/study his lectures, you will pass! His exams were exactly what was on the exam, no curveballs. He is super approachable and kind.

Gorski is a professor that wants you to succeed. I wish he taught every form of chem because he's the best professor I've had so far! His lectures are extremely helpful for taking the exams and he's a very kind soul overall.
He was one of the best professors I had! His exams are based on the lecture slides and will say what will be on the exam so it won't be a surprise.

Dr. Gorski is such an amazing professor for GC 2. His exams are super easy as long as you study his slides. He is very fair professor and explains the concepts very well during the lecture. Very kind professor. If you get an A on his final, he will bump your final letter grade up by one full letter. TAKE HIM!!

Easily the best ochem professor at UTSA. He is not only an exceptional lecturer, but genuinely cares about the success of his students. My advice: go to his office hours & TA sessions to prep for weekly quizzes, read the textbook (there's a free pdf version so don't worry about having to buy it), and complete ALL textbook end-of-chapter problems.

There is quiz every other week, you have to buy a textbook. If you don't want to purchase the textbook watch this guy on YouTube, he goes over the same textbook as the professor "Chemistry Professor." Exam review is provided that is exactly like the exam. your grade is based on Quizzes and exam. No curve, no exam drops.

I passed but he is unfair. Much of the class needed to retake since his exams are removed from what he teaches over. He is charismatic, which is likely why he gets such positive reviews. However, he does not drop exams, and the extra credit is good on the normal exams, minimal on the final, final was unlike all other exams. Take someone else.

Ochem is really hard but Dr. Aguilar understands that and is here to help. 20 extra credit points on each exam and syllabus has grades shifted, ex. A = 86+. He makes everything as understandable as possible. Take advantage of TA recitations, they're like a saving grace. Quizzes are not horrible if you study. The final is incredibly difficult.

If you are wanting or needing to learn Organic Chemistry fairly then Dr. Aguilar is the man. Attendance isn't mandatory but I just don't see how you would pass without going to class. Pre-read is mandatory but he will make sure you start off where he left off, always prepared.

Awesome slides. His exams reflect exactly what to expect on the ACS standardized final. His quizzes and homework problems are also very similar. Provides suggested textbook problems to study for exams. Extremely intelligent and caring. Gives his exams online so you find out your grade immediately. Ask questions AFTER class or at his office hours.

OChem is a hard class, to begin with. His exams are set up to your benefit, and as long as you practice outside of class then I think you should be fine. His lectures aren't the greatest, but his slides are decent and easy to review. I think the biggest thing is just doing end-of-chapter problems outside of class. As long as you do those, your fine

Organic chemistry is already a hard course to begin with, so I would suggest taking any other professor. . He often gets irritated with students and expects them to know this subject as well as he does. Don't bother asking questions during class, because he will make you feel stupid. Exams were extremely difficult and he does not drop or curve.

Han is not a bad professor, just not the best option. He goes over slides and does not go over examples or walkthroughs which is not helpful. 
He offers no extra-credit, no curving, no dropping assignments.  He does not have an assigned tutor. The 4 exams are worth 70/100 points. If you struggle with mechanisms, I suggest taking another Professor.

Dr. Han is very knowledgeable in organic chemistry. He explains reaction mechanisms well but the tests have questions that aren't in the notes so you need to live and breathe organic chemistry to make an A. Homework is highly weighted and doesn't show what you got wrong. Asking him any question in his office he will rudely tell you to study more.

Dr. Schanze is genuinely a great professor. He teaches with pre-made notes that are posted on his BB and they have examples on them. Organic chemistry is an incredibly difficult class, so you will have to do the work outside of class. No matter who you take I recommend getting 3-d chemistry model sets to better see what's happening.

He makes you work for a nice grade. I learnt a lot in this class. The tests were not extra hard and he also gave a pretty nice curve. He gives a lot of homework which helps in getting prepared for the tests. I would give him a 10/10

No extra credit, no partial credit, does not spend time going over concepts. He assigns a ridiculous amount of homework on Connect(2 or more due each week, 50-80 questions with multiple parts.) His exams are between 4-6 pages front & back, with about half being written answer. Doesn't announce quizzes, so attendance is req'd if you want to take it
Will not work with you in the events of an accident. Gives some room to still pass, the letter grade range for tests depend on how well the class as a whole does. WOULD NOT take this professor again.
Hes a solid professor, Just have to focus on core concepts and I think essentially you should be fine through out. I havent had any issues this semester with him to be totally truthful.

Dr. Doyle is passionate about you learning the material, but his lectures and the exams are incredibly different. Throughout the semester the class averages were from 20-30's and he would blame us for not knowing the content, but if the entire class failed the exam, is it really us that failed? Even reading the book I barely passed with a C.

Dr. Doyle is a brilliant professor, but his exams were nothing like the textbooks. His lectures were 100% based on the textbook, but the exams were far more difficult than the textbook. He is a very nice professor and is willing to work with students outside of class.

I can tell Doyle is a very intelligent man, but how he teaches is very unclear and very outdated. Although the textbook used for this class is amazing, his tests are nowhere near the material from the book. All grades are based solely on the exams. Students averaged 31-42 on average test (thus far). His response is "this is quite depressing"... ok.

Save yourself the heartache- DO NOT take his class. He lectures in a way that is only understandable to himself and it showed on his exam averages. Exams are tenfold more difficult compared to examples in class. He consistently negatively criticized the textbook and supplemental instructors, so reaching out for help outside his class is pointless.

Doyle runs through lectures and doesn't take the time to break down difficult topics. In comparison to other prof, he was always 2 chapters ahead and his class averages reflected the lack of time spent explaining the material. Thus, if you take him, BE PREPARED TO TEACH YOURSELF FROM THE BOOK IF YOU WANT A GOOD GRADE. Grade is based only on tests.

Biochemistry is hard, but Dr. Liu makes it simple. Even though attendance is not mandatory in his class, i highly advise you to attend evey lecture to ace his tests, because all his tests are based on what his powerpoints and the lectures. He gives no homeworks or quizzes at all, his class grade is 100% weighted on the test grades.
Would give a zero if there's one

If you want a prof. that belittles you, this is the one for you. Wants students to ask her questions, but the moment you come up to her with any, she will make you feel like dirt on the bottom of her shoes. There are a lot of radical reactions happening in her brain, and I hope I'm correct. 80% of the grade are from exams. no curves/drops/mercy

Having her for Organic II lab was awesome. Provides so many good resources to prepare before coming in to lab. My favorite thing is that she will tell you how the experiments you are conducting actually apply to real life, which is always nice if you actually care about chemistry. Her laid-back nature makes the lengthy experiments go by easier!

This professor and her minion TAs must live a sad sad life. Constantly yelling at students to belittling them whenever asking about points missed on exams, questions over concepts, or refreshing ochem 1 topics. If you have a kink for being degraded you would LOVE her class! Takes a lot of thick skin to not let her words get ya but you can survive.

Makes mistakes often, so expect to teach yourself. Tough love taken too far. Many students would rather take a lower grade than ask questions because she snaps unpredictably. She'll probably call us "gutless," reading this but maybe be more approachable. If you take her, keep your head down, do well, and avoid talking to her unless you have to.

The exams are fair as long as you put in the work. Do all the practice problems, stay on top of the material, and study consistently. Organic Chemistry is not an easy class, but if you dedicate enough time to it, you'll be fine. The professor is not the most approachable or friendly. I highly recommend watching Professor Dave on YouTube.
A very good professor and overall not a hard class if you put in the work.

Honestly, most of the bad reviews are due to students that refused to put in the work. This is Organic Chemistry II after all and so it is a difficult course. Dr. Larionov is a great professor who was always available for any questions I had. If you actually put in the work, I promise this class is not hard. One of the best Ochem Professors.

Dr. Larionov is the "old school" professor that you would normally think of. Long lectures, quizzes after each class, and a monotone voice. I did like that he did practice problems after each topic in his lectures. If he was a bit more approachable, then I would feel comfortable asking him more questions.
Proctored exams and quizzes. Ochem 2 is def not a class you want to take without guidance from the professor, and he was MIA the whole time.
Gave no direction. Confused the entire course and had to teach myself. Exams were multiple choice but still impossible.

Class had no structure whatsoever. Every exam was cumulative, and Pearson assignments rarely correlated with exams. The lab was unorganized. Towards the end, he didn't even grade over 75% of our Pearson assignments.

He is your go to professor for mass spectrometry . When I asked him some mass spec questions he lashed out and cursed me with the f word multiple times because of my apparent lack of the fundamentals. Always approach professors prepared with the questions you ask but his violent out lash was uncalled for and I felt unsafe. I would not recommend.

ANALYTICAL CHEM! I love Bach. You will have to work for your grade & of course you will be finding yourself with heavy material, lab, & HW. But Bach's personality helps the Genuine Chemist find more passion into Chemistry with his real world application on concepts. If you don't like it don't pursue chemistry. Having a cool lab partner helps.

This class was brutal!  This man clearly is not interested in his students.  I believe he harvests the tears of students to feed his ego, because he clearly thinks he's amazing.  Unfortunately, if you have to take analytical chem, he is the only person who teaches it, so pray to your god now!

I like to think of Bach as the professor who applies your chemistry knowledge to the outside world. He always asks useful questions that seem annoying at first, but the questions he asks are for your own good. Tests can be tricky. If you work in the chemical field (bio majors gonna hate) you'll thank Bach for provoking you now so you succeed later

I like Frantz but there are issues with his teaching. First he uses powerpoints which are inefficient in a class like this. Second he goes through materieal way too fast for a 16 week semester. Finally he didn't adapt well to online. This included quizzez with exam level question that needed more than the thirty minutes he gave us to complete them.
hard class and professor ever
His is a nice and professor. He knows a lot. Test are hard. I felt bad because I study hard and I cared a lot for this class and ignore my other class for this one. And it wasnt worth it.
DONT TAKE HIM!!! HARDEST PROFESSOR EVER! his test are hard as hell. I study 15 to 18 hours a week and it wasn't enough for his test. You are never prepare for his tests.

Dr. Frantz was my toughest professor ever. He was also the best professor I've ever had. His class gave me better work ethic. The exams were very challenging, in comparison, the Ochem 2 ACS exam was a cakewalk. I was in 92 percentile. Only 9 people passed the class, so it meant that much more. STUDY!!! Has in class quizzes, so ALWAYS read ahead.

recentReviews.comment: Dr. Tonzetich is the most outstanding professor. He is both passionate and laid-back at the same time. He is always willing to provide answers to any questions you may have. Although Chemistry could be daunting, he provides clear guidance on what to expect in the exams. He encourages his students to think critically beyond the classroom curriculum.

DESCRIPTIVE INORGANIC CHEMISTRY! Dr. Tonzetich is just simply amazing and his passion for Chemistry is highly contagious to the Genuine Chemist. Of course chemistry is going to be difficult no matter what level. He gives a review prior to his exams and is very clear on what he wants on there.

He provided us power point slides that had all the info you need on them. He's very clear and knowledgeable. You can try to stump him in chemistry but has all the answers. Chili pepper from one man to another

For CHE I he was challenging, but not impossible. After hard work and some studying you'll get an A. He knows what he's doing and he's a brilliant professor. If you do go to his office hours, he's actually very helpful.

Great Professor! Take him if you want to LEARN Chemistry. Its not a free A and if your not used to reading your text book before class or practicing problems on your own, don't take him. Very helpful.

Had for Molec Therm. Read off of slides (not her own), and didn't really teach at all. Course is based around another Professor's materials, showing Xu's seeming lack of care towards the course. Would have preferred chalkboarding and no slides. 

Course isn't that hard, but also not stimulating/interesting. No real world applications shown. Dry.

The chem department at UTSA is a BIG disappointment. The main heads don't care about helping the students succeed & expect us to understand challenging topics the first time. Fang, however, did her best to prepare us for the exams. If you understand the topics, her iclicker & pdf q's really help-usually similar to exam q's. Would def take her again

Xu is not a bad lecturer, however she cannot really prepare you for tests because Arman writes them and doesn't tell the other professors what's on them. She is nice though and is accessible during office hours. Attendance is mandatory and taken using iClickers during class, but that's true for all the chem classes.

She is an overall good professor, however, since none of the Chem professors know the contents of the exam they cannot prepare you as well as Arman the professor that makes the exams. But if you pay attention and finish the home works you should have no problem finding success in this class. PS all tests average in the 50s, so study hard.

Gen Chem I content and tests are determined/written by Dr. Arman. Dr. Xu knows her stuff and is a caring professor who will take the time to explain a topic during her office hours. Her homework doesn't necessarily correlate with the tests however it serves as good practice. ALEKS is the only source of extra credit but she is lenient.
