recentReviews.comment: Hi there Mr. Heaps
Best professor ever, i had a extremely bad grade, but he helped me bump it up, taking him again next semester :)

Lectures are absolutely amazing, the best part being that they are uploaded to YouTube after every class. The assignments were also pretty fun to do. He also gave us lots of advice going into the CS industry that can help us with future endeavors outside this class. Overall an amazing professor that I hope to take for CS3343.

Dr. Heaps is a very caring professor. He is great in office hours, as he will help you on projects without giving answers. Also, he is very flexible and will always give extensions if you ask. He also asks the students what kind of teaching style they would like.

He never answer emails or was available outside class. Easy class but unecessary, we learned things we don't really use for other classes inside CS. Waste of time and I didn't learned. Also I felt the classes were too short and the professor had to rush, however great at explaining and giving examples. Great professor, useless class.

Had videos uploaded for all classes, assignments were like building blocks for the Labs. Labs were time consuming. Was the easiest class on my schedule when taking 17hrs. Well-structured class. She's a sweet and helpful lady. Had infinite support as there were many tutors available almost all the time. Felt like a very easy class.
beware if you have mental health issues or a sudden death in the family, this professor does not display empathy.
Easy class, I don't know why English or business majors think this class is hard, easiest class I had while taking 19 credit hours.

In person class but attendance is not required. Uses one class day to go over powerpoint lecture and the next day to walk you through assignment. Gives a week or more to finish each assignment. Tutors and professor are accessible outside of class for questions. Has powerpoint and videos to walk you through assignments as well.

It's not hard if you divide the workload and plan ahead. Watch the videos and follow along to complete exercises while taking notes. Screenshot finished exercises, highlight code, and make side notes, takes ~15 min and saves hours. Grading is fair; if you do well, you could even fail the last lab and exam and still get an A.

This professor was extremely rude when I asked to reach out, and was really mean when I asked questions or got something wrong. DO NOT TAKE IF YOU ARE A HANDS ON LEARNER, the entire class is pretty much trying to figure out what he is talking about in lectures and getting thrown in the deep end, with little to no grace for your grades.

He failed me by one point. He was very difficult to talk to and he was aggressive when spoken to. He would release in class assignments, not lock, release so we would have to wait for our web pages to refresh but only had 5 minutes to complete the assignment. No grace was ever given and hard to understand when learning.

One of the worst classes i have ever taken. he doesn't respond to emails even during office hours. The lectures are horribly put together. almost all content is off Zybooks instead of lectures as he talks about stuff not related to the class and waste a ton of time that we have little of. do not recommend.

Professor Gomez is caring and reasonable. If you stay disciplined and complete Zybooks on time, you'll do well. Lectures are recorded, and extra credit is offered. No late work, but he's helpful if you reach out. Three exams and a group project are hardest. Attend class—quizzes are frequent and heavily weighted. he even drops 2 lowest grades! Cmon!

Do not take this class if you are a hands on learner . He reads everything off a PowerPoint with no examples or problem solving . He makes up random theories and rants all class . DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS TRUST ME YOU WILL REGRET IT!! You will be given assignments with no clear understanding making it easy to fail his class.

I don't know how she has a low score she is awesome. Her examples are just like the homework (there's a lot) so all you have to do is basically copy it. Go to the computer lab to do your homework and if you are stuck her ta's will help and they will. The course does need some time outside of class but which classes don't? her lectures are fun

I have never done any of coding until I took this class, but as long as you follow the instructions it is easy to pass. All her lectures are uploaded to blackboard, and she has very detailed instructions for each assignment. The class was very organized, and it was very easy to find, and complete all assignments and labs.

Even though this is an Intro to Data Mining course, if you don't have any Python experience or aren't comfortable with coding this course will be very difficult. The professor is lazy and all of the material including the lesson code is outdated and incomplete. This professor shouldn't be teaching this course at all.

Assignments are out of date and have lots of errors. We had to constantly ask for clarification b/c they just don't make sense and assigns things that weren't in the book or readings she assigned. Got an 89.8 in the course and she didn't round up to an A. If you've never learned any programming language in the past, good luck.
I learned so much from this Data Science course she is highly recommended.

Software engineering had a semester-long unguided project. Having a good group mattered, but was not something you could control because they were randomized. The class was entirely theory. Be prepared to do a lot of self learning. You'll need it for the project. He cares about his students and is funny, but the lectures themselves are a bit boring
Tests are very important, lock in on them. Rest is zybooks.

I do not know what my academic future holds but I doubt there will be a professor as terrible as professor Dogru. Mumbles some words off of a slide for his lectures and intentionally puts trick questions on tests with multiple correct answers. Does not give the tools necessary for projects and tests, had to teach myself C. Do not take this class.

This was my first time taking him and I wouldn't do it again. I don't feel that this class adds much value to the degree overall. There is a group project which is awful. He also mentioned that in previous semesters he let students choose if they would rather do a group project or an additional exam. I definitely would've chosen the exam.

It's a nice class. I learned a lot from this class. The professor is very accessible and understanding; he was flexible with granting extensions on deadlines when needed. The course is project-heavy, so you should definitely start assignments early. Overall, I'd definitely take his class again

In a course called Data Structures we were not taught anything about them until around November 8, twelve weeks in to a sixteen week course. Most of the course then was loading text files into a C struct. Assignments were not graded until months after being given. Multiple mistakes were included in project instructions.  

Avoid him at all costs.

Worst professor I have ever had. Has a "flipped classroom" so he does not have to prepare for lecture. Lectures are incredibly disorganized, on-the-fly, & confusing. CONSTANTLY changes project expectations, due dates, exams, etc. bc he is so unprepared. Does not compile his code in class because he would not be able to fix it. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

The professor is passionate about CS, but he is not an organized instructor. The assignments he wrote were far too vague to be understandable and he had almost no communication with his T.A. or grader, leaving his students wondering about grades and progress.
Mr. Jointer was the professor that extinguished any passion I had left for CS.

Worst course I've ever taken at UTSA. No communication between the professor, TA and/or grader. Went 3 months without grades feedback. Class-time was spent seeking out information/clarification in past course material, resulting in little faith or confidence in the professor. The Flipped Classroom felt like it was only for the professor's benefit.

Jointer is great as a person, but needs work as a teacher. Jointer's class as a whole is disorganized and lectures along with assignments/tests can be very vague. However, he does give a good amount of extra credit opportunities (at least in my experience) and he is pretty avaliable outside of class.

You can never go wrong with either of the Sahba brothers. Ramin is very willing to answer any questions you have, and the assignments don't take very long to complete. He does tend to speak in a quieter tone though, so definitely recommend sitting up front.

Very nice and approachable professor. Lectures get a little boring but also no one really participates. About 5 relatively short homeworks, one solo project (C), and you get 2 attempts at exams including final, which were all multiple choice questions. I've heard good stuff about him from peers that took him in person too.

I liked the online class, there were lots of student presentations, deadlines were kind of short notice on everything, but doable. Hopefully you get a partner/group who contributes to the work and not freeload. Work piles up at the end of the semester so work early to avoid stress. Attendance only mandatory for presentations. Grades leniently.

Dr.Sahba is an absolute sweetheart. Very kind to students and is always happy to re-explain concepts and answer any questions. He's good at breaking down complex problems so they're easy to understand. If you struggle with math and will need a lot of help & patience, go with Dr.Sahba.
Attendance isn't required, but definitely recommended. There's not a lot of assignments, so everything is worth quite a bit.

databases async: lacks the ability to teach and only uses outdated pptx as lectures. Gave group project requirements a month before its due and does not even provide SQL tutorials other than the textbook. Little guidance from him. Labs were harder than expected due to his lack of input/lectures. However, exams are like the quizzes and proctored

Labs weren't super difficult, but the 3rd one lacked necessary orientation from prof. He expected us to google as its done "in industry", and he forgot we paid to at least get some technical guidance. This entire course was a lackluster exchange of buzzwords/business talk with a final project that required technical skill and QUITE the writing.

Given I don't think assignments were too difficult they were just a lot with little guidance. Lab 3 was easy after classmates found a guide to follow that was not provided by the professor. He also surprised us by requiring a write up of each chapter of the book in addition to our group project to make a search engine to handle 1 million users...

Labs 1 & 2 well-received. Lab 3 lacked crucial demo (3-node setup, connection). Students struggled to connect nodes, impacting Team Project readiness. A well-explained Lab 3 could have remediated student issues.

My only complaint was that this professor's assignments were just easy busy work. All the assignments and discussions were easy. The 3 labs were as simple as installing some stuff on VMs and following instructions from google. Lab 3 required a little finessing. I feel sorry for anyone who thinks this class was hard. He shouldnt have been so lenient

A hall of fame professor as they say. Homework and exams reinforce what is learned in lectures and the lecture slides themselves are full of great examples and step-by-step guidance towards the weekly topics being learned. Never skip out on an Amin Sahba course here at UTSA
Very nice person and easy to follow in lectures. I really enjoyed this class and learned a ton. He was very generous on grading and seemed to really want people to do well.
The best professor out there. Please take him, the tests were really easy.
Mostly reads off the slides but is a caring professor. Homework's are helpful for understanding the material and exams are not bad.

Attendance only mandatory for student presentations (there are several). Deadlines were kind of short notice, lots of homework, quizzes, etc, but doable if you stay on top of it. Hopefully your partner/group contributes and doesn't freeload. Work piles up at the end of the semester. I would have preferred zybooks for programming exercises.

MAKE SURE YOU KNOW JAVA SYNTAX before taking this class!!! It's a weird thing with course changes and not his fault. The assignments are the hardest material and while they're not worth much of your grade they're your best study material going into the exams. SHOW UP TO TUTORIALS if you're struggling, they helped me and they'll help you too!!

CS1063* Up until chapter 7, I had forgotten that Professor Byron Long was making videos for each lesson. The use of self-taught methods are vital for this 100% distanced instructional course. I found that the material was easy to understand, and the projects being presented for the class were within the scope of what was being taught. Great course.
Does not even slightly convey course material. He expects you to know before you are taught. Exams are the only way for points in this class and basic class work does nothing to help.
nt next time, might have to lock in. gg go next
Not good communicator, no notes posted online, no extra credit, doesn't round grades even by .03.

Professor Hend is incredible! I took her for Apps and knew I needed to take her again for Database Systems. Super caring professor who wants to see you come out of the course with applicable skills. Class itself is relatively easy if you pay attention, do your work with integrity, and ask questions when you need help. Great class!!

Everything is so clear and she makes it very easy to understand. We get fun assignments and she is engaging. She sets you up for success, so if you do badly it defintatly was on you. We get so many examples in class, she'll go over theoretical and practical things with a focus on preparing you to have critical thinking and a good foundation

Professor Alkittawi is an amazing professor. She genuinely cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. If you pay attention, participate, and practice the material outside of class you will have no issue in the class. Group project is manageable and she is very helpful throughout the process.

The actual lecture pace could be better especially with two times a week lectures. But the lecture slides created and material made around topics and the resources included automatically put her above other professors here at UTSA. So long as you take good notes and utilize what she puts up in canvas you will do fine.

Overall, she was OK. My only concern was that many deadlines were clustered together, and she was often not open to adjusting them. We would sometimes have several assignments due back-to-back and then no work at all for more than a week.

I can't speak for how well this professor teaches in-person, but I will say this: do not take her classes online, and definitely do not take her summer classes. Only a few weeks into the course, and a good portion of my classmates were already "resolved to just kinda teaching this to themselves," because her lectures barely taught us the material.
She's very sweet and accessible by email or during office hours but I felt as though she didn't actually "teach" any of the concepts we were expected to know.

The professor was not the best, it seemed like she didn't really care about this course. We missed maybe 5-6 lectures throughout the sem. Class was structured very strangely, we had 2 exam the last 2 weeks of schools which did not follow with the schedule on the syllabus, I really hope they change some things about this course.
terrible professor, just doesn't know what teaching is and doesn't know what she is doing it seems, very hard to follow, just do the homework and move on.
Pretty alright teacher to be honest. She grades pretty hefty on the homework. If you want an ez A you take her but if you want to be prepared for comp arc then take another professor.

He was okay. He had his office hours in the syllabus but most of the time I went he wasn't there. He never responded to emails too so I just gave up and tried to get through the class. Disappointing because I heard a lot of good things

Decent professor, knows what he's talking about. However, it doesn't feel like he's teaching students rather he's talking to himself along with the slides and expects you to follow along. Sometimes he'll skip entire slides just to move on to other concepts. Plus i wish he could slow down the pacing of his voice.

The guy is down to earth and will answer any and all questions you may have. The unfortunate thing about Systems is that the graders sometimes ghost the professors, don't grade, or just don't grade right. IF you're to experience that, just bring it up, he'll grade it. Otherwise, the class is very test heavy, but because of that so are the curves.

Systems is a difficult class, but if you put in the work and study you will be fine. Professor Silvestro is extremely knowledgeable. Pay attention in class, follow along with his examples, and study hard for the exams!

He is very knowledgeable on the topics he teaches about, grading schedule can be here and there and isn't the fastest especially towards the end of the semester i felt a lot of up and downs seeing my grade move around. He does teach a little boring but it gets the job done. He's not a bad teacher by any means and his assignments are kind of fun.

You will get your money's worth out of Dr Harrison's class. The workload is pretty insane, but if you're up to it, incredibly rewarding. There is so much you'll learn, and its fun to boot. Perfect for anyone aspiring to work in cybersecurity.

If you liked CS3433, take CS4353. 

Perfect for any cybersecurity, forensics, and programming enthusiasts. 

Similar teaching style. Focused on relevant demos and specific notes as opposed to traditional lectures.

Only graded on roughly 9 challenging and technical assignments.

His classes are somewhat unorthodox, but among the best I've taken.
Good prof, his teaching style is like a riddle. No test or project, just beefy assignments. Don't expect free time and don't expect hand-holding. Other than that, pretty cool class

Professor answers questions and helps with projects; easy to contact. Recommend class to those who enjoy challenging resume worthy projects and low level comp sec. Only critique is that this class emphasizes self study(custom class notes). May be good for some,but for others who prefer more traditional classes, may be hard to follow some lectures.

His class is extremely difficult, but very rewarding. The grade is only determined by a few assignments, which are hands-on and super technical. He doesn't really do traditional lectures. You're expected to learn a lot on your own. However, he is super helpful when needed and dedicates a lot of time to answering questions and doing useful demos.

She is a great professor! She is good at giving feedback and wants us to succeed. I will say that some of her lectures take forever to get to the point, as she spends a lot of time going over things from previous classes and over assignments coming up. She also does not revisit material often and expects you to look over it again yourself.

If you know Java, take her. If not, pick another prof since you need prior Java experience. I only knew C++ and Python so learning Java in Data Structures was rough. Dr. Hosseini is kind, responsive, and  very accessible during office hours. Lectures aren't mandatory, but help review material and prep you for the assignments, quiz and projects.

Wasted time and slowed down too much at times, due to this we did NOT cover everything in the syllabus. She is very kind and easy going. She is extremely understanding, most would say too understanding. She is always available through email. Finally, there is a group project in the course, be extremely careful with who you pick as your group mates!
The professor is intelligent and kind, but she wastes time going over material that students should already know. She thoroughly goes over material during lectures and is lenient on grading though.

CURE is one of the best classes I've ever taken and Dr Fern does a great job teaching it.  Every lecture is something new, we have group activities and guest lectures.  All around it's an amazing class, if you're interested in research TAKE THIS CLASS.  This class is a lot of work, so take at your own discretion, you read many many papers.

She is a phenomenal instructor. Her grading is fine, there's a lot of work to do in this class because it's an introduction to research. Her timelines are very realistic for what's expected. She does a great job building a foundation and helping the students learn the role of researcher. Ignore the reviews saying otherwise, they wanted an easy A.

The CS Course-Based UG Research class which isn't listed here (CS-4593) was awful grading the research assignment. Half of the grading for the project literally was not possible with the finite time given, especially relying on information that is not easily obtainable.

Death by powerpoint. So many slides. Feel like she is a good teacher and great at answering questions, but this isnt really obvious except during the rare moments when she's not lecturing from her slides. Struggled to stay awake for this reason. IMO its a lot of material for one semester. With no previous Java background, I struggled to keep up.

Shes ok. Her lectures come from PwrPt slides. Slides have contradictory info at times especially on UML stuff where one slide says an arrow goes 1 way, but the next it goes the opposite. Dont underestimate the HWs as they tend to take longer than expected. SceneBuilder isnt taught enough in class. Overall her class isnt bad if you study the slides.

Engaging speaker but brutal grader. Followed the itemized rubric perfectly, but he personally graded it and took 30 points for adding '/hw#' to a path on working code. When I politely appealed, pointing out the rubric criteria, he said he would 'happily' make it a 0. Completely unreceptive to feedback and not professional.

I do not care how tough classes with him may seem you need to take him. Any class taught by him will actually give you something real that will get you to a real job. He understands sysadmin in depth and even though it may seem like gibberish at first, you will begin to understand things. I graduated and am rewatching his lectures even now.

He's a great professor, you'll learn a lot in this class! He really cares about students and their mental health as well, he's very understanding and a great guy all around. Go to class everyday, do the hw right away, and you'll be fine!

i love this guy. seriously. valadez is extremely passionate about sysadmin style stuff and you can spend HOURS talking to him about computers without feeling bored. valadez cares a ton about both his students and his topics, so i promise if you give him respectful energy, you'll be astonished.

Professor Valadez was very solid overall. He put heavy emphasis on the WHY when it came to what we were learning. He cares very much about his students and their success, as long as you're willing to put in the work. Though he's a great professor, he loves to challenge his students on the exams. He's very caring and understanding when life happens.
They were okay. Just okay. Their lectures felt pointless to attend, and the assignments were not especially difficult, though the midterm and final take up a lot of the grade.

Uses scanned notes for lectures which can come off as a cookie-cutter approach, but makes studying relatively straightforward. Encourages doing homework in pairs (though is not required) and exams make up a hefty portion of your grade. He's a nice person, understands personal circumstances, and wants to help students succeed. Zybooks is optional.

Discrete Math can be hard to grasp at first, but he explains it well. Just pay attention in class and take notes, then look up anything you don't understand so you don't fall behind. Don't be afraid to ask questions, he may come off as a little rude but he truly wants you to understand the concepts.

great prof and detailed lectures. hws consist of getting output from small programs. focuses on C and lisp towards the end of sem. only complaint is that exams are heavy on your grade and lacks extra credit, and reviews do not help for tests. although, tests are open notes/unproctored but tough

The assignments can be tedious and time-consuming, but basically are the class activities (which are used for attendance). He really seems to enjoy this class. The group project grades can be changed at the end depending on how team members rate each other, so slackers can get called out. Creating an e-commerce site is not easy, start early.

The class is hard, but Korkmaz is good. He's friendly, understanding, and helpful. Lectures are heavy & fast-paced, with a lot of information to go through. The workload is fairly difficult, but meaningful in a way that doesn't waste your time. He strikes the perfect balance between wanting you to learn and wanting you to pass. Best choice for OS.

Prof. Korkmaz is very amicable, and makes the subject of OS intriguing at best for the curious mind. Unfortunately his teaching falls short in terms of impact and retention, as he tends to breeze through material quite often. Provided textbooks are very useful and can help learn beyond his limited teaching scope. Assignments/Exams are manageable.

The hardest fought B+ of my life. Took OS with Korkmaz over the Summer, and he is a great professor but be prepared for a lot of work. Workload may be more manageable for Spring/Fall since there's more time to do everything.

Probably the hardest class ever taken. Korkmaz is highly respectable, but his way of teaching is very messy, especially w/ his diagrams! Grades every assignment and test very harshly, though I luckily managed to pass with a high curve at the end. Unless you're insanely smart, C/Java savvy and/or have no other option, please avoid him at any cost!!
deducts points for incorrect questions in tests. tons of difficult projects.

Opens all assignments (5), quizzes (3), and exams (1 mid 1 final) so you can complete everything early. In regards to grades: Very easy course. He seems to prioritize you understanding the material over worrying about grades.

OS was a super easy class with him. Assignments were easy and straightforward. He records all of this lectures, and his tests were honorlocked, open-note, and relatively easy. Take this class if you want an easy time in OS, but don't expect to retain much of the information. Many students felt they didn't learn or take away anything from the course

Took him for OS. He was just okay when it came to teaching. Lectures were boring and a lot of times it was hard to hear him. He is a very calm person tough. He made the class very low stress. The material also is not overly difficult.

He seemed like a good guy. I like his concept that we should focus more on the material than the grades. The assignments were easy, mostly following along, which was definitely beneficial for my workload, but I don't feel like any of it prepared me for the exams.

He was a fine professor who focused more on getting us to understand the concepts of the material, rather than having us endure difficult projects and exams. Unfortunately, his lectures never felt worthwhile, and consisted of a fair bit of repeated phrases and rambling. That said, if you pay attention and do the work then you likely do just fine.

He is an awesome professor that seems to care a lot about student understanding. Tests are pretty difficult but he offers a ton of extra credit and prepares you well. I would highly suggest taking this class if you want to get good at C.

CS 2713 (updated #)
Personally, the lecture style didn't connect with me well. The professor mainly worked through sample problems during class. The tests were harder compared to the study guide, which was easier since the problems came from Zybooks and labs. That said, he does offer a good amount of extra credit and is accessible outside of class.

The professor is very strict and often responds to questions in a short or dismissive manner. Lectures are dense and sometimes repeat the same points without much added clarity, making it harder to follow. More over, the class structure is different from what other professors teaching the same course use, which creates inconsistencies in learning.

His class is well-structured and easy to follow as long as you are participating and he is available outside of class through email and Slack. His lectures are very understandable as long as you have prior experience with the previous class(CS 1083) or have a programming background.

Hard class, coding some algebra for computer vision. The main gripe is why is Linear Algebra expected as a prerequisite when it isn't on the degree plan and really doesn't count for credit except for elective. Add linear algebra to the CS degree plan if it's expected knowledge. They used to have it, need to add it or don't expect people to know it.

When I took this class, the rules and expectations seemed to change throughout the semester, which made it difficult to keep track. The exams were extremely difficult and the TestTaker system made submitting assignments, talking exams and reviewing grades more complicated and stressful than necessary.

If you don't have a Windows computer, don't. Professor uses a self-made program for homework, exams, & feedback that's only Windows-compatible. You can't actually see homework questions without downloading/extracting a zip. You're welcome to use AI & notes, but he makes exams so difficult that you'll need to answer the topics from memory.

Ortiz is a good professor overall. This class is not easy at all, you will have to work hard. The exams are hard (2nd and final are the hardest imo), but the past exams are a huge help. He answers emails very fast and is willing to help you understand concepts outside of class. Don't take him if you aren't prepared to cry at least once.

This has been a really tough course, but you will learn so much. Ortiz is tough, you better be ready to put in the work. But he is a really kind and caring professor too. He encourages all students to ask questions, he is easily accessible through email too. 11 homeworks, 1 group project, 3 exams, 1 final. Insane? I guess. But this prof is worth it

Ortiz is a different beast. His ADHD - which is either unmedicated, or entirely too medicated - was felt in every aspect of this class. Yet, underneath the chaos, true knowledge shone through. He is the CS department's equivalent of an eldritch being. His methods? Foreign. Goals? Alien. Take him if you seek knowledge. But prepare for insanity.

This is a comprehensive, hands-on class with many in-class activities and quizzes. It can feel overwhelming since the number of graded tasks isn't always clearly defined. it's practical than most courses at UTSA and focuses on packet tracer rather than just theory. keep up with his assignments, lenient grader, should be okey

doesn't teach much of what appears on homework or exams, gives a timed and proctored pop quiz at least once a week, doesn't respond to emails, wastes class time trying to figure out canvas and zoom, and is one of the toughest graders i've ever had. i had to drop this course because i just couldn't take it anymore.

assignments were posted with little notice and less time to complete them. midterm 1 was after the drop date, midterm 2 was at the very end of the semester, three days from the final. syllabus was completely inaccurate. prof was rarely available for office hours despite claiming to be available regularly.

All of the reviews that are above a 1 star are outdated. The grader is horrible and just lets Canvas auto grade unless enough people argue with them, and the professor is so hard to listen to and takes so long to explain a point that you can walk away from the lecture, come back in 30 minutes, and he'll be saying the same thing.

The class isn't difficult because of the material. It's difficult because the professor gives as little information as possible before giving you assignments with the most vague questions possible, and decides what the question meant after. 

Not only that, but he talks so incredibly slowly that he needs 2 hours per class to say anything. Miserable

Professor has all course lectures recorded and posted from day 1, loved that.  This class is pretty tough even for someone who is tech savvy and likes low level programming.  Make sure you attend his lectures, he does Q/A for people with questions so make sure to ask.  He is very responsive and will try to help you.

Hard tests, invasive camera requirements for tests (online class). A previous professor used to let people do projects in groups, not this one. Last project includes writing a long paper. He ended up being good, but didn't like how he acted overboard on the cameras for tests.

Best professor!! Take his class if you need some inspiration on CS. He breaks down the tough subjects into easier ones and cares for students. He's talented and passionate in this area, with industrial and academic experiences.

Class material for Computer Architecture was difficult in general for me but he seems passionate about architecture and gave many extra credit opportunities. Gave fast email responses to assist with assignments, which was very appreciated. He is very understanding, forgiving and patient. A great professor!!!

Wang is a straight-forward, fair professor. Exams in Comp Arch are very straight-forward (no trick questions) and study guides provided are actually helpful. Assignments are not too difficult and Wang covers assignment answers in class. As long as you keep up with the course material and complete assignments, Comp Arch with Wang is fair. Take Wang.

This class took more effort than I thought it would. Labs are long and sometimes confusing. Personally wouldn't take again but my opinion is based on the class itself. The professor and graders are super lenient and understanding. You're given the opportunity to turn stuff in a week late with no penalty which is nice.

I think this class is tough as it covers so many concepts, and in technical detail, that its hard to keep up. The professor though makes the grading very forgiving, we were given a 1 week forgiveness period for late work, and majority of the grade is through assignments. However, there is A LOT of them, sometimes many in one week.

Lectures are long, boring and hard to understand be ready to study a lot by yourself. Now onto the worst part, the day grades are due he forced the grader to be more strict on the lab TWO HOURS before grades are due, making most of us in the class fail the lab and making our overall grades fall. If that sounds fun then take him, otherwise dont.

I felt like I learned more test-taking skills than the actual material in this class. The poor lectures, which led to lots of self-studying, and the weekly quizzes, which led to lots of workload and stress, made it extremely difficult to learn anything in the course. At least he was decent with criticism, he gave us more time on the final.

If you have four other classes, or a job, do not even consider taking this class. Even if you are graduating, take an extra semester to avoid this class. The workload is absolutely absurd, and was just overwhelming for me. Thankfully there is lenient grading, but it doesn't make completing the often lengthy and confusing assignments any easier.

CS 4223.courseName: Bioinformatics I: Algorithms for Biological Data

Fall 2026.title: Bioinformatics I: Algorithms for Biological Data

recentReviews.comment: His homework assignments were not difficult, they just required a little bit of time. His tests weren't bad either. He is very open to questions from Students and will take the time to explain a topic further until the student(s) feels satisfied with the answer. His lectures were sometimes hard to keep up with, but still enjoyable.
He gives more homework than others for this class. He is helpful during office hours but there's a lot of work. Tests are not easy. I don't feel this is an "easy A" class.

This class is an easy A. You will get to know python well and learn about pandas, numpy and data frames. Lectures are a little hard to understand if you don't ask questions. Seriously, really easy class don't fret over this one.

Professor Ruan LOVES data science and clearly knows the ins and outs of it. Lots of HW but it's not hard if you pay attention in class and ask questions when confused. If statistics and computer science had a baby it will be Data Science, so know what class you are signing up for. Very understanding and caring professor. Always smiling and cheerful

Fast talker and does have a bit of an accent but hes a really fair and caring professor. The class is kinda tough but prof Ruan tries his best to help and explain topics. Would say hes a solid alright pick wouldnt mind taking his class again
Don't take him recommend to get a different professor.

4233 is a really tough course but Professor Alperen makes it manageable. He gives credit for just showing up to class. Quizzes are take home and usually have problems from the lectures so if you take good notes you should be fine. Exams are also questions from the lectures. He does grade somewhat tough and the content is difficult.
Not a very good professor at all. Avoid

Professor Ergur has a very thick accent, so it's sometimes hard to understand what he's saying. I tried to follow his methods, but I found that Khan Academy helped more in understanding concepts. Homework assignments were also NOTHING like the exams, but the reviews the TA posts are somewhat similar to exams. Overall, very sweet professor!!
Not a good professor take anyone else over him.
Good professor, look at utsa bluebook for previous syllabuses

Dr. Slavin was an awesome professor who is always accommodating. Grading is not that harsh as he gives out plenty of extra credit. His exams are a little tricky, but slow down and read what he is asking carefully. Homework's can be vague, but he will update it and clarify if you email him. Lastly, he guides by example when covering materials.

Professor Slavin and this course are really great; his lectures are extremely in depth and detailed, but he doesn't over complicate anything. He gives every student the ability to give their input and ask questions. This class is an easy A, but you also get to learn a lot about security principles. Not an easy A where you don't learn anything.

First and foremost, Dr. Slavin is a fair professor. He is a tough grader but he gives you specific direction to follow and what is expected. If you have any question or want to "fix" your grade on an assignment, he is available during office hours for you to go over your assignment and potentially make adjustments. I would take again

Extremely confused on the good reviews on this prof. Honestly, he "seemed" like a good prof but has impossible grading standards and blamed me for his lack of grading assignments on time. I would not recommend taking his class to anyone. I tried to get help from him and when I brought up concerns he turned it on me. NEVER TAKING THIS GUY AGAIN.

Not sure why Assignment 2 patterns is graded so hard, but the other assignments are better. Tests usually have coding questions so study code from lectures. The workload isn't bad, but not an easy A class either. Great professor and responds to emails/office hours but kind of vague, won't give you answers. Overall would take any of his classes.

Appreciate that he recorded lectures, although he can be slow to post them. The first project is a lot of work so try to start early. Might need to look up how to run JUnit Tests on your own, and follow his class Fibonacci demo. Midterm was harder than expected but seemed to curve a little. Would take again, is a nice professor.

Compilers seems to be a UTSA graduate CS gateway course for whatever reason (why? It's not useful for most of CS). The project is very difficult and confusing, especially the final part. Having the project at least compile and run will go far, even w/errors. He doesn't respond to many emails, & grades hard on tests, but has a little curve overall.

If you are struggling with the project, good luck. His emails were helpful with directing what to do, but that's when he actually does respond. Brutal on the exams, especially on questions like automata and miss one thing on it. Hopefully if the catalog is changing, this class would become optional, and I recommend against taking this class.

Validation as a class is known to be boring, but I enjoyed going to his lectures. He recorded them so reviewing for the exams was super helpful. His second project was actively being built during the semester, and it was missing critical steps and really difficult to build, even following the directions. Slow project grades. Both exams went well.

I took this class in the summer. It was very organized. The professor did a good job of laying out all the requirements. The Professor also did a good job of balancing direct slide reading with further explainations and experiences. Test reviews were helpful and there were no surprises. The project was fun, and I learned new skills ! Great job !

Nice guy. Bought us pizza. Lots of labs with a robot. It's fun.

The issue with this class is that the lectures are a bit detached from the labs. The HW prepares you for the test. It can be a bit hard to understand him at times, but just give an effort and you should have no issue.

Must attend! You can miss a few but be careful.

He has an extremely hard accent to understand and will go through slides that are gibberish when seen outside of lecture. Don't even attempt to study outside sources because it seems like he makes up information as he goes. Would not advise this class

He's an incredibly smart and kind, but his accent is through the roof most of the time, and he talks a little fast. He will help you whenever you need him, and he tries to help you if he notices you're struggling. I did not do well in this class at all, but that's because you need to start your piles of homework ASAP and pay attention EVERYDAY.

This is a weed out class. If you you don't do the work or have a solid foundation in another language, this class will be incredibly difficult. Partial credit is given, but tough grading. He does have an accent and can be hard to hear, but just ask him to wear the mic. Very acessable outside of class and knows the subject.

He has a really horrible accent. YOU CANNOT understand anything. This course is very, very difficult and this professor makes it worse. I failed the class because I really never understood anything... and I tried to go to the tutoring center, and tutors were never there. I am a Math major, and I have no idea on why I have to take this course.
He is just brilliant

Professor Jadliwala's Practical Attacks class was among my favorites in my education so far. No tests or quizzes, just 8 hands-on labs using Kali Linux tools to compromise target VMs and 3 essays summarizing a recent research paper from a specific theme. Very rewarding class with a good workload balance... it's not small, but manageable and fun.

Very knowledgeable about crypto. Very responsive to questions and willing to engage the class. Quizzes seemed a bit strange. Seemed to be flexible in grading assignments as to not fail people. Workload was above average but manageable. 6 quizzes, some java programming and a paper and presentation are your grade.
Quizzes were hard until kind of figured out a better way to study. The grading scale is fairly generous but it's easy to fail quizzes.

The lectures were okay, and the assignments weren't that bad, though they were tedious. For the group project, though I learned a lot from it due to it involving whatever your group wants, was still very difficult and time consuming, especially with the project requirements and deadlines. Know what you would want to do, and plan accordingly.

Class participation is part of the grade. Class was mixed with undergrads. Difference between grad and undergrad is a paper presentation and grad students work with other grad students on the project. Project had clear milestones. Very clear teaching and grading criteria. I found him approachable and willing to answer questions. Would take again.

Laid back guy, very helpful in office hours and easy grader. Graphics can be difficult if you have no background in C++ and linear algebra on vectors. Class consists of 3 prgm assignments using C++/OpenGL, some HWs (mainly math), in-class activities due by midnight, and a group project for a simple game. No tests! Offers extra credit opportunities.

Quarles is a great professor and taught a great class. He's one of the most easy to talk to professors in the whole CS department. I took him for User Interfaces and it was great. The only grade in the class is a semester-long group project which you have a LOT of freedom for being creative with. I would take him again and recommend him to anyone.
No exams, except homeworks, project and presentation . I like this course as professor will not pressure you at all. Class activities are fun.
I had Dr. Cannon for every semester in my undergrad for geosciences. He is an amazing professor. Clears up any uncertainties. He is also a very down to earth, understanding person.

Dr. Cannon is really sweet and has a genuine passion for what he teaches. The course consists of lecture days, work days, and projects that we mostly do on our own time. Overall the difficulty isn't too bad but there were a few times that I got some points off for not answering things very specifically. But overall its a good and interesting course
he's a nice professor but lectures get really boring really fast. do not recommend if you're not interested in geology.

I graduated from UTSA with a B.S. in Geology. Dr. Cannon basically teaches all the mandatory GEO classes, including field camp (where you spend 6 weeks straight with your teacher&classmates). He's excellent! He cares, Is available outside of class, has a subtle silliness, genuine, and over 4 years with him one of the best professors I've ever had
Pretty easy class. Only downside was the boring lectures. Weekly quizes with a few tests and projects all done online. Overall easy.

she's really nice and actually knows what she's talking about. There is discussion and homework grades which were due every week but super easy to complete. She lets you use your notes for the exam. I have nothing bad to say. She is also eager to help you if you have any questions, and super caring :)  you don't really need the textbook either
Nothing fab or bad about this class. Very typical online course, as long as you do the work you'll get a good grade. Prof responds quick too
Textbook is pretty much useless. Nothing to complain about the professor, simple online course.

Above decent if geology is not your strong suit. Kinda lengthy lectures, an (easy) participation quiz each class. Exams are open note. The project that replaces your final is known to be difficult, I had trouble but still ended with an A for it. She's sweet so this class is worth taking if you gotta fulfill a science credit.

Professor Cannon was excellent! Her lectures are interesting and fun, and she cares about her students. She understands science may not be everyone's passion and tries to make her classes interesting for everyone. All assignments and exams are open note, and the textbook is really not necessary. I highly recommend her classes.

I found 3rd Planet to be an amazing class. Professor Weissling is very personable and enjoyable to talk to. You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches which makes sense given his expireince in the field. As long as you pay attention to his lectures (which were always very entertaining) you won't need to read the book.

Weissling is is a tough professor but you can tell he really enjoys what he teaches and he goes on tangents that make it more interesting to listen to the lecture. His exams are pretty hard, but I learned a lot from his class and he makes sure his students understand the tasks he puts out. You can tell he really wants the students to succeed.

His class is very easy and he doesn't give a lot of work. I don't know why his ratings are low, his grading is good and the material is not that hard and as long as you do the work and ask questions, you won't have a hard time. He puts up a lot of slides and gives extra credit. You can also tell he cares and is passionate about what he does.

No idea why such bad ratings. I absolutely LOVED him, if you show up to class and just pay attention it's all online and the easiest class I've ever taken probably in my life. He is funny and provides slides during lectures, half the time when I looked around everyone is on their phones or watching something on their laptops...

he's a chill guy, but throws around a lot of passive aggressive remarks to the class. lectures are overall fun but he releases the submission links hours before theyre due, which makes it hard to turn things in on time when a lot of students are at work before they can submit. gave the exam review an hour before the exam, lots of grades to drop.
he will be undercover in the group me and makes it a pain to ask anything in them because he'll reply, sometimes not with the best attitude.
The professor is very nice, but I don't think he realized how difficult the material in his class was. His lecture slides were not detailed enough for me. And the iclickers were hard

Excellent and hilarious professor, don't let the other reviews scare you. His course is definitely difficult, but if you stay focused you'll do fine. Loves telling stories and engaging with students. Daily pop quiz but only keeps your best 10. Challenging but interesting course material. Overall very solid course, would retake!

Pretty good professor and is funny, the class it self isnt too hard you just need to get ready to memorize things. He mostly does quizzes for attendence so study before class. Exams are mainly just the exam review.

Great lectures and a teacher that really understands what he's talking about. Very funny guy and definitely tries to add a lot of life to his teaching, unfortunately he lost my homework assignment and didn't provide me with any other options to make it up.

recentReviews.comment: This class really only serves as a roadblock in the way of classes that actually matter
I hate this class. So much busy work! If you can find someone else, please take them. Honor lock. Microphone and camera needed BTW!! idk why ppl like her. I feel insane.

Her lectures are very clear, not long. But there's a lots of work to cover every week. If you're taking this class just for credit, consider this course. Her assignments are time consuming. This class will not work for you if you got other classes that you're struggling and you need extra focus on those, it's that bad that I considered dropping

She's just....she's so nice. I had some personal problems and she was nothing but understanding and kind. We have a decent amount of assignments, but it's not that bad to knock em out. No writing either. All short answer and multiple choice. You can afford to miss some assignments. And late work is graded for a while afterwards.

I love her class. It's very easy and she gives enough extra credit to help with your grade. The skeletal notes and exams are A LOT of questions but it's not so bad because you can have your notes out to help you review. She's very helpful and understanding and gives enough time for due dates.

Overall the course is not hard but you have 2 attempts for the quizzes so if you don't do well in the first attempt you're not shown what you got wrong and if you do worse on the second attempt that score is the one that's kept instead of the highest attempt which I think discourages students from wanting to understand what they got wrong.

Overall it's an easy class but be ready to read and read. Some of the quizzes from the Investigations you do are not the easiest but you can work through them and you get 2 times to try. If you are interested in Climate Change, I would recommend taking this course because it has current info!
He replies to emails relatively early and gives good feedback too. Exercises and lectures are sent through email, so you need to keep up with emails but all in all, enjoyed taking him.

Paleo & Lab at UTSA I took a couple years ago. Dr. L was frequently late for class coming disheveled & w/ excuses. He would walk in and say Ill be back in 10 min, leave, &come back 10-15 min later. He had few assignments in lecture so if you miss one your grade could be affected. He never once showed up to lab. Not once. I felt bad for his TAs.

I loved his class, he knows he stuff, made class really entertaining and he answers questions really well too. If you attend his lectures and read a bit of the textbook you'll get an A no problem. he grades his test comparatively so whoever does the best he ranks the test based on that, which really helped me. And all of his test have a bonus Qs
Great prof...really knows his stuff..not easy subject but if you go to class and write all his notes you'll definitly pass with atleast a B. Its not an easy A but if you really try you'll get there.
nice guy, hard class!  But, it was good for something! I met my fiancee in this GEO class

This class requires a prerequisite in Python Programming to begin with. The professor refused to use current materials: remained with Python 2.7 in a 3.8 world. Almost zero of the disorganized coursework pertained to GIS. Apathetic attitude. Poor explanations. Those familiar with Python said the professor was very inefficient.

The professor was completely unfamiliar with both the text and the assignments. Students had to correct and guide him repeatedly. Apathetic attitude. Buy the book and perform the exercises on your own. Save the time, money and frustration.
He just reads from a PowerPoint of 100 slides. Also doesn't seem like he knows the material very well. avoid if possible.

He promised for extra credit but didn't give that. Gave a mail with pride and said, "I am curving your grade" and everyone got .5% curving!!!.  I got over 80 without that curving as some of my class mates but below 85 is just a B- (2.67!!). My friend got 89.6% and its a B+(3.33!!!) But he described the grading as A90, B80 in course syllabus!!!
He's a very nice teacher. The class is very useful for professional research. learning programming and software need put a lot of effort but that's worth it.

recentReviews.comment: Teaching is horrible, the homework doesn't correlate to what is shown in class. His lectures are very boring. The homework assignments are very tough and you have to self-teach yourself on how to complete them due to it not being shown in class. No feedback on what was wrong with the homework. Cool dude but just a bad teacher.

Mr. Whittington is really compassionate and interested in what he does. He works as a Volcanologist in the field when he's not actively teaching. He wants people to use critical thinking in his class, and thus gives difficult and lengthy homework because of that. He does not go over how to actually work through equations though. Homework is hell.

Best professor ever! Very informative in lecture and gives real life examples that help apply memorization and principles. She will work with you for exam extensions or early access if needed and is helpful with feedback for what you got wrong or didn't give enough of answer wise on exams. She has as well established a good grading system.

she gets off topic so much, I could never keep up. the information was very confusing to hear from lectures but when reteaching yourself outside of class it made more sense. homework wasnt bad, and tests were pretty difficult.

Do not take this class. She gets off topic a lot, so no point of attending her class cause she'll only get through 4 slides and for the project she was EXTREMELY strict, giving many questions and wanted it detailed but with a very low word count allowed and didn't give opportunity to fix grade on it. It brought down many people from my class grade.

Professor yells at students a lot, yet also allows students to talk over her during class, making learning in lecture impossible. You will have to teach yourself from the book. The head coordinator for BIO 1 makes the tests and she acts as if she has no idea what we will actually be tested on. Lots of material on tests that aren't on the reviews.

Terrible teacher, can't figure out technology for the life of her. Exams are somehow able to be retaken and not, depending on the person, hinting towards favoritism. Posts 6-8 assigments on any given day without being on the syllabus.

This professor was great! His grading scale was very helpful. Slides are most important for understanding the exams! Very little/no homework at all. His reviews are due to other students lack of effort. This is a 3000 class..ofc nothing will be spoon fed. Seriously such an easy course! Just talk to him and he will give you feedback/help out

This course was very frustrating. We received the textbook late and had our first exam a week after getting it. Material we were told wouldn't be tested was included. Lectures were mostly slides with little explanation, making it feel self-taught. Take this class only if you're prepared to learn on your own.

absolutely HORRENDOUS. If you love your sanity, take this class at a community college and save yourself hours worth of CRYING and STRESS. There is a quizlet for all his exams, but now it's locked, so good luck.
Exams are all in person!! He has an english accent and I can not understand him. Also doesnt put very much energy into the lectures.

Dr. Saville is a horrible professor. I would not recommend anyone to take him. He doesn't answer emails, gives no help for exams, and answers questions rudely. He also ignores certain things (ie. disability accommodations). He also shows up late every single class and speeds through every single slide. This is basically a teach yourself class.

Had a great semester with this professor, she had very clear expectations and interesting lectures. She does a good job keeping the class involved in the lectures which made it easy to stay engaged and actually retain the material. There's only 2 tests, final and midterm which she has provides multiple forms of study guides for. Would take again.

I love this professor. Extremely clear instructions and criteria for everything, her lectures are interesting and very informative. Only two tests in the class, the mid term and final which she gave excellent study guides for. She does have a thick accent so if you have hearing issues be aware. There are pre/post lab assignments and one project.

Dr. Adelani was an amazing professor. She made the lectures interesting by tying them back to her life and was always there to help out with the procedures as well. Only 2 exams throughout the whole course that are relatively easy as long as you go through the material beforehand.

took her for lab and lecture for micro , she's amazing very straightforward with exams and quizzes , no homework . its impossible to fail her classes. she's super sweet and loves to engage her labs for so interesting . sometimes she does go fast and it can be a lot but other than that great.

Dr. Adelani is an incredibly sweet professor who is very easy to get in contact with. During the labs she is extremely helpful and grades the data sheets relatively lightly. Theres two exams throughout the semester that aren't the hardest but do require studying ahead of time. Overall she's a great professor who you wont regret taking.

recentReviews.comment: Dr. Nuckels is pretty nice and very straight forward on his guidelines. Not too much homework either. The tests were manageable (just make sure to study the slides) and he curved every single one. However, exams are 60% of our grade, none are dropped, and they are taken in class. His lectures are boring though, mostly him just reading the slides.

He has very clear guidelines on what day and time things are due. Everything was done through McGraw-Hill Connect, though, so be prepared to buy the textbook. He also does not respond to emails (in my experience). Easy enough if you read through the book and keep up with the slides. He also requires Proctorio for all exams.
This summer class was easy going. The professor was clear since the beginning regarding tests and hw due dates.

All assignments and tests are on McGraw Hill. The tests were weighted at 70% so if you made one bad test your grade goes down a lot and it's difficult to get it back up. Attendance wasn't required and barely anyone went. The lectures are very boring and didn't help much. I don't recommend this professor, you basically have to teach yourself.

I took the lab and it was super chill. Labs were about an hour long. Homework, lab assignments, etc. were pretty simple. He only had quizzes for us, no exams and the quizzes were exactly like his reviews and based off labs we did. Attendance not required, but you should go because you will need information & pictures for your assignments.

recentReviews.comment: Wouldn't recommend this prof. She's nice to students, and the labs weren't difficult, but they weren't enjoyable, either. If you actually want to learn: look elsewhere. Other than that, the homework isn't much, 5-question quizzes due weekly, and the exams were fine. She doesn't give guidance in terms of what to review prior.

Dr. Guerrero is extremely caring of her students in the lab. If I ever had a question regarding an experiment she would clearly answer and guide me in the right direction. While the labs may be long or hard, as long as you read the procedure and follow instructions carefully it isn't too bad. As long as you try each week, you'll do well.

You have to try. That's all. She's really nice and if you ask she'll help with anything you need she's always willing to help and explain concepts. Usually ends lab early which is a perk. I understand most things in bio because of her explanations and lectures. Would take it again.
This class was really easy. Professor is very helpful and answers all her students questions, she doesn't just tell people to refer to the course material.

She is very easy going when answering questions and help students with feedback when needing. I also like the fact that when she is teaching, she tells students what is going to be in the test. She keeps students attention at all times and encourage them to participate in class.

recentReviews.comment: The professor is awesome very knowledgeable and the lectures are recommended if you don't want to feel lost. Very open to accommodating students however the McGraw hill assignments are tedious and due dates are final normally. The professor is a cool dude and pretty funny I would take again.
the reading McGraw hill was the only downside but would take again for the professor he's very chill and knows his stuff

Super exam heavy. No late work, no corrections, no extra credit, no grade drops, no sanity. Honestly the worst class I have ever taken. Lectures are super boring and it's super hard to learn directly from the professor. There's a problem if a majority of the class is failing the exams and still offering no incentives. Avoid at all cost.
Be prepared to teach yourself everything

Professor Andrew was not present. This lab is taught by TA's and it really depends on which one you get. I got Sam and she was the best TA. The class it's self isn't too hard even if you got no information from the Bio lecture. The practicals are hard if you didn't pay attention to the lectures, which I didn't, but I still passed.

The grade is based on exams and iClicker questions, with no homework or extra credit. Exams are curved and include multiple choice and one free response. The final is cumulative. There's no textbook. It's a difficult course, as expected for a 4000-level, but the lecture notes are detailed and easy to follow—study those and you'll be fine.

Dr. Jaffe is BRILLIANT. He has a hard shell and does not accept mediocrity from students, and I loved this. He engages with a multitude of questions and is incredibly passionate. He taught quickly and with precision and is THE teacher I would want for all med school classes. Don't be quick to judge someone who does not present as warm and fuzzy.

Do NOT take this professor for Neurobiology or Neural Circuits. Take any of the other professors. He doesn't enjoy teaching at all. He may be a fantastic researcher but it does not translate to the classroom. You have to teach yourself, and he often mixes up test answer options, counting wrong ones right and only fixes it when it's pointed out.

Avoid Dr. Jaffe. His lectures are very confusing, he jumps around topics without clear explanations, mostly overcomplicating simple topics. He's also downright rude, dismisses students, and acts like we're wasting his time. The class is painfully boring. Office hours are useless and online only. Save yourself the stress and headache.

Class itself is difficult, Jaffe made it harder. Do not recommend. He's passionate about neuroscience, however doesn't care or even try to act like he cares about teaching or his students. I sat in front row, actively participated, perfect attendance, yet wouldn't round 0.01% up to a B-. Also very boring. Just take someone else if able.

Very nice man who was so understanding that we also have lives outside his class. He did go a little fast during lectures, but I would take the time to read and understand them outside of class. My exams were online lockdown browser; I'm not sure if he still does that though. Overall cool guy he wasn't heavy with homework either.

Dr.Ozturk is very knowledgeable and it is obvious he knows a lot about biology, but his exams are kind of difficult and there are 5 exams plus the final. He drops the lowest midterm and he does a lot of iclicker. You have to purchase a McGrawhill textbook and do the assignments each week. I would not recommend if you are not a science person.

about the CURES course: you will get out as much as you put in. I recommend it if you're ready to put in the work and dive into the world of research. If you're pre-med and just want to say you did research, you may want to chose something else.

I wish this guy taught all my science classes. He was so happy all the time, legitimately seemed to love teaching and his students, his Gimkits for the tests are awesome. I miss this class all the time. Don't even bother with other bio professors. This guy blows them all out of the water. He is so kind and understanding.

Best biology teacher that I have ever had. His lectures are well-given, and he will explain topics in depth if you are confused. Prof Ozturk will help you and will give you extra credit. Top Hat is used in class, and you will have chapter assignments due every Sunday. Tests are multiple-choice, and he offers extra credit on them.

Dr. Perry is an amazing professor, he explains basic biology very well and offers engaging lectures. He always makes sure students don't have questions before moving on, and he won't shame you for not understanding something. He's down to earth and incredibly intelligent. He also offered me an undergrad lab position after I emailed him inquiring.
Dr. P is great and very kind. All assignments are typically in McGraw Hill and he will help you succeed. He is clearly very interested in what he teaches which is very encouraging for students.
Talks a lot, but is an amazing person, I would definitely recommend.

PAY ATTENTION TO LECTURES AND READ THE CHAPTERS BEFORE CLASS. That is the most important thing for this class. Professor Perry is an amazing professor and explains topics in great detail. Paying attention to his lectures and using material from the TA(s) is how you succeed in this class. I never took AP bio and yet I still performed exceptional.

Goated professor. Grades aren't necessarily free because you do need to study for exams. Dr. Perry goes slightly in-depth during lectures because he encourages you to read the textbook before class and learn more content during class. Reviews made by TA are pretty helpful. 10% curve on almost all exams. Attendance mandatory. Best Bio 1 prof imo

Good professor, wants you to do well if he sees genuine effort. Very easy to talk to outside of class. Exams can be a tad bit difficult--Biggest tip I have is to start studying for exams a few weeks in advance. Overall, if you put genuine effort the class is pretty easy.

This teacher is not accommodating at all. PLEASE do not take him. He does not care about any issues you may face and is not helpful. He is also very confusing when explaining material. I would not recommend this class.

This class is mandatory for attendance. He does not give no extra credit, nor does he drop any low score for tests. Alot of McGraw-Hill readings and assignments. His test are Claude Ai questions many questions are questionable and are not in the lectures or assignments he assigns. Too much Ai used in this class DO NOT RECCOMEND taking this class!

Tons of energy and a great human being. However, his knowledge of the material was questionable at times and the tests often didn't reflect the lectures. Overall decent experience, but be ready to teach yourself.

Awesome guy, awesome class. Willing to hear you out on exam score changes and you can tell he enjoys teaching. I would say to be careful if English isn't your first language, because his accent is pretty thick, but even despite that he was able to keep the attention of like 100 20-somethings for over an hour twice a week so yeah. Good luck!

recentReviews.comment: Honestly one of the best professors I've had at UTSA so far. He is very charismatic and eager about the topics he teaches. Would highly recommend to anyone looking forward to taking his classes.

Professor Rogers is a really cool guy and is fun to talk to. He is passionate about certain topics and will go more in depth on them in lecture. The tests aren't hard, just study slides/review material he posts. The group project isn't too bad either. However, if you take him for lab he is a strict grader

He was my second choice for bio lecture and he is very under-rated. His lectures are so fun and engaging, and you only need to review slides for the exam to pass. He would randomly drop hints about exam questions so actually pay attention to the lecture.

Had him for Bio II lab, but we had a graduate student teaching the class. The grad student was awesome, but the material was just okay, could be hard if you don't understand it, but if you know what you're doing it's a breeze.

His exams are so heavily weighted 50%, and his assignments are just 25% He's good at reading off his slides. His assignments are easy and the group project is wtv. He also gets sidetracked a lot is what I noticed. Just please if your not a great test taker than don't bother with this guy specifically.

She is a really good professor, she responds to emails quick, she'll still give you credit for tophat even if it wasn't working, you just have to ask her. The TA makes helpful study guides for the tests and even made practice questions once which helped even more. Just study the slides, take notes and you'll be fine!!

Overall amazing class, this professor will always make time for you if you communicate with her. She sometimes gives out extra credit on her exams too. I will say that the homework's can sometimes be overwhelming with how much they have but if you have good time management you will be fine. Study, listen, and take NOTES.

Dr. LaPenta was a good teacher. She really cares about her students. I came out with a solid understanding of this subject. She delegates a lot to her tutors and TAs to help students in the class. I found memorizing the lecture slides was the best way to get an A on the exams. The tutors reviews were wrong in several places. I would take her again.

Dr. LaPenta was amazing. Her syllabus was very relaxed as your lowest exam gets dropped, homework is completion assignments, and her lectures specify what you'll be tested on. She leaves out slides that she won't test you on, and writes specific things to study on the board which correlated to exactly what was on the test. Use her practice exams!

All of her lectures were great and well put together. The material was not too hard to understand and she did a good job of offering supplemental material and study times for students. Seemed to really care about her students

Worst professor ive ever encountered. Class time consists of NO TEACHING, while we have to do in class activites that are not worth any points. Before class we watch lectures that are unlocked only two days before class that are 2 hours long!!! How is a student going to be successful??? He doesnt Actually teach!!!!!!!!!!

The lectures are very monotone and difficult to stay engaged with. Since full lectures are posted online, class often feels unnecessary when the same material is repeated without much interaction or demonstration. Adding more visuals, practical examples, and discussion would make class more engaging and worthwhile.

All he does is read off a PowerPoint which is in canvas btw. You can barely hear him speak EVEN with the microphone attached to his chest. You get an extra credit quiz every class before lecture only worth 2 points. But if you go through the notes yourself and study then you'll make a decent grade.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! His lectures are some of the most boring you will ever see, as all he does is whisper into a microphone and read of slides. This is supposed to be a class for non majors yet he goes into so much detail about random things that are not on the exams. NO ONE passed exam 2, the highest grade was 69.2. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!

I've never failed a class before, and this is the first time I'm most likely going to. Attendance is mandatory and he reads off the slides. Honorlock is required and tests tend to be 76 questions long. He provides study guides but what's on there is a fraction of what's on the test.

He talks really fast so trying to write anything down from the lecture can be very hard. there are 4 tests, but he drops the lowest one (covers lecture slides). you get two lectures and a quiz a week unless there's a test. Also, the curve is really good because you can get b's on all the test and still get an A if your other grades are good.

Be prepared for in-person tests, but what was great was that all the exam material came directly from the lecture slides; He does rush through the slides, but he posted them to the blackboard after class. He also was very generous by dropping the lowest test grade, and there was no final for this class.
Prof Wanat is average. I got a B+, there are 4 tests (he drops 1) and then some homework. Overall kind of easy but he doesn't round grades (boo).
Not too tough of a class especially if you remember bio from high school. He drops your worst grade so you can be done with the class with a month left.

He has slides, but the slides are exactly as what is said in the textbook. It is hard to take notes in his class because there is so much on the slides and he speaks far too quickly. If you choose to note take what he is saying, you will not be able to note take from the slides and vice versa. best bet is reading and following the textbook exactly
Dr W was super engaging and its super easy to get an A in his class! All exams are just the hw questions re used. Hes amazing

Class is tough by material but lots of study resources are provided which outline the entire test. Going to TA sessions gives good info. Lectures give good info and test hints. Very easy to talk to and funny, wants his students to succeed. Lessens homework load when he knows it's a lot. Extra credit for every test and no final test (for physiology)

Professor W is an amazing guy. Sadly the lectures follow the McGraw Hill slides format that all science classes at UTSA follow, but he makes it as interesting as possible. He is funny and cares about his students. Despite the boring McGraw Hill slides class format, I looked forward to attending his lectures because I love Professor W.

Great professor who really cares about his student. He has extra credit opportunities for low test grades if you're  willing to put in some extra effort. I love how his content seems to excite him and it makes for a fun class that allows discussion.

Prof W is the best professor ive ever had. Gen phys was challenging, but he tells you what youre being tested on and has his ta give a good review. Smartbook heavy, but manageable. Gives extra credit opportunities on all his exams. Available through email and office hours always. I had him at 8am, and he was my most enjoyable prof. 11/10

Content-heavy, but the material itself isn't difficult if you stay on top of it. He provides all of the slides from the start of the semester, and every exam question can be answered with them. My biggest advice is to make Anki or flashcards and review them CONSISTENTLY. Do not rely on the reviews sheets. Homework- time-consuming -not on the exams.

canceled consistently one of the two days i had his class every week this semester. in person class btw. no extensions no make-ups. sassy remarks when being asked a question. proctors exams with extra sensitivity and room scans. explanations, reviews, lectures, and answers were ALWAYS vague/broad. says to "know everything" for exams when questioned

This was the only class that fit my schedule. He could come off as condescending, especially since our class held him to high standards like he did with us. He didn't post the first exam on time, and after someone contacted the dean, he seemed upset and kept bringing it up in lectures. So the class felt extremely uncomfortable.

Dr Garza has been by far one of the worst professors I've had. This was an online course but he doesn't seem to be very tech savvy, multiple exams where posted hours after they where supposed to open and where given barely any extensions. Avoid this professor if you can
If you take him be prepared to get your extra credit and exam reviews taken away. Whether its 3 or 20 people caught cheating he will punish the whole class. I'd take another professor if possible.
