recentReviews.comment: Mrs. Trevino is amazing! She provides so many resources that actually help on exams and is truly caring. A&P is already difficult so she is very straight forward and if you do the practices that she creates for the class and you study you will do fine. It even helped me for my lecture.

Prof trevino genuinely is the best professor! Anatomy is a lot of memorization. Make sure to stay on top of things and study early; you will be successful in this class. Trevino is super sweet and always ready to help and give feedback. Gives a clear explanation of the materials and makes them easy to understand.
She is an amazing professor!

She was honestly one of the best Professors I've had. she was very caring and made lectures very engaging as well. She cared a lot about the students and found ways to make it easier for us to study for exams. She was very sympathetic as well. The reviews she gave for exams were very helpful as well. Would 100% recommend taking her.

Great teacher, passionate about anatomy. Very kind and caring lady. Took A&P I Lab over the 5 week summer term. Assignments were easy and extremely manageable. The lab assignments were done on a monitor in groups. Only downside: A LOT of googling is needed to complete labs as the resources we're given do not cover the topics in the lab questions.

This will be an easy A if I study good for those practicals, in which they're pretty simple. She could have an attitude occasionally but other than that she was in a good spirit...just didn't do too much teaching.

The course is structured as practice in class and learn outside class.The "learning" was videos that were easy to follow but had no depth to the activities done in class. I suggest reading the textbook and taking good notes, that will help alot. Technology is NOT her strength and she will give you attitude when you try explain an issue on her end.

You learn through a bunch of video that were unhelpful. She makes the exams, very poor word choice when she made exam questions. Would put a wrong answer as the correct answer, when you would email about it she would throw attitude which was very unprofessional. Thinks everyone is out to get her when emailing about it which is simply untrue.
Always ill prepared for lectures, throws in random “fun facts” on exams. High school teacher that the most, definitely NOT a college professor by any means.

Don't take her. She's super unorganized, doesn't teach well, and is overall a mess. What she teaches in class is barely in the tests, she says textbooks are optional but the tests are very textbook based. She would forget to post what we needed to go over before her class. There's just so much wrong with her class. Don't take it.

recentReviews.comment: amazing proff

Loved Dr. A this semester! Her class is incredibly well organized and easy to understand. Graded by pre-lab, playposit lecture, lab assignment, and exam. Super informational and will answer any questions. Really amazing and passionate professor!

Professor A was a great professor. She lectured very well and made the lab very engaging. She knew exactly what we needed to know and her study guides reflected that. Anatomy is hard, but she breaks it down to where it is easy to understand. Attendance is Mandatory, but that is for all the labs. Don't show up late. Take her if you can.
Natalie's tests are so easy, its crazy. that's all I have to say. PLEASE take her if you want an easy A.

This professor is amazing!! Her lectures are very helpful. Her extra credit helped my grade get to an A. Her exam reviews are exactly like the test, so if you study those, you'll do great! I'm so glad she was my professor.

A is easily attainable because class is out of 109, but the sheer amount of work for this class is ridiculous and SO tedious! Disables copy and paste, but all of his questions are from internet. 6 assignments due each day for 30 days + Quizzes, Vocab exercises, & other unnecessary assignments. Please take another elective, class is a waste of time!

Professor Phelix assigns so many assignments that if you do all of them is it impossible to fail this course. The assignments are all fairly easy too. He also posts a lot of his stuff online, so it is more convenient. I would definitely recommend prof Phelix.

Very nice man. Attendance matters very much be on time tonclass because online quizzes are due within 15mins of class. PPVQ are due before each class which are very long but not hard. Exams are taken at home and are all due at the end of semester.

This is a very detail-oriented class. He makes it a point to spend at least 15hr/wk on his class alone. I managed to get an A by doing almost every assignment given. His lectures aren't very engaging but he does care about his students. I didn't pay attention in lecture too much so I used the powerpoints he posts with each lesson to help me learn.

Dr. Phelix is a really great professor. If any concept is confusing you, go to his office hours, and he will help guide you through the concept until you understand it. He really tries to make sure that his students are learning, and the work may be a lot, but at the end of the day, youll actually learn by the repetition.

I took Professor Degen for the CURES MDAD Lab. She is one of the best professors I have ever had. Truly a gem. She genuinely cares about all of her students and is great at explaining concepts. She's very knowledgable and will meet you where you are at, she's very receptive to feedback as well.
Took her for the CUREs MDAD class best professor I ever had. Very understanding and gives good feedback . Helps you on your research process and documentation.
She was a good professor, I would take her again.

She is really funny, and was really helpful during the online part of the semester. Truly amazing, and she grades exactly what she says she will. She is also more helpful than the TAs, obviously. She explains things very simply and is pretty lenient if you don't understand the first time. Also, she lights the burners for you if you're scared to. ;)
Avoid her like the plague. She tends to forget shes teaching a freshman level course that only gives you 1 credit hour. She makes this class harder than its supposed to be. Youre warned, kids.

I really enjoyed her reasearch class. Amy was always reasonable with grades, and her lab was a genuinely great learning experience, especially if you like microbiology, as you learn many important laboratory techniques.
Worst professor I've ever had. She has no compassion for her students and often comes off as entitled. She doesn't even know how to answer basic questions so your only source of help is the TA's.
Amy is a great professor!!!! I loved the SEA PHAGES CUREs course, it is an amazing introduction to research and Amy puts her students first.
I LOVE AMY. She's such a sweetheart. I had her for CUREs GEP and she made it so fun and easy to understand.

molecular genetics lab with Amy was pretty easy. As long as you do the assignments and show up to lab you should be fine. You definitely have to study for her quizzes. Amy did not provide any help for her quizzes, but I was able to get study guides from Kalin Skinner which was EXTREMELY helpful. Amy's class is fun, but I would pick Skinner.

This class is pretty straight forward. It's easy to do well if you keep up with the lectures and virtual labs. Dr. Hopkins responds to emails quickly and seems like she genuinely cares about her students doing well. Glad I waited until summer to take this class with her.

Dr. Hopkins is AMAZING!! She breaks her lectures into smaller chunks that have questions and videos, and has a way of explaining things that make them easy to understand. I'd take any class she teaches.

Honestly the best bio professor I've had so far. She is super supportive and made times to meet with me outside of her office hours since they conflicted with my work schedule. She has so much knowledge in her area and you can tell she really loves teaching the material.

Loved this class! You have to keep up with it, but it's one of the few classes where I actually enjoyed listening to the lectures. The assignments are organized and she is a fair grader. She just released her grade distribution and over half of the class got an A. I would definitely take her again.

recentReviews.comment: Mrs Gdovin is kind despite seeming a little scary. She can be strict, but in the end it's what you need. Absolutely attend lectures, as most tests rely on her notes.

Mrs Gdovin is amazing!!! She's old school so if you think a grade will just be handed to you, you're wrong. Go to class. She gives in class assignments sporadically. If you go to her office she's willing to help and easy to talk to. Attendance is taken.

Gdovin is the best lecturer I've ever had. You CANNOT miss lectures. Be sure to take thorough notes. STUDY for this class!!! It is challenging, but doable. If you are a bio major, don't take this elective just thinking it's an easy A. It's not. But... If you actually like ecology, go for it. She curves exam grades. My only complaint is Packback.
Never again

Memorization is key as 70% of the grade is quizzes every lecture. Herbarium project is very time consuming, and the 4-hour lab rarely ends early. If you're willing to devote your spare time, that's fine, but I wouldn't take her again. She gives off mean-girl vibes, & previous students have an advantage on the quizzes and final, which feels unfair.

Kareem is funny, very relatable and always willing to help. Not the best with emails but if you go to his office hours he will help with whatever you need. Course is excel heavy so be ready. I will say that he does not give clear feedback on assignments so you don't know what he takes points off for but again go to office hours and he will tell you

Professor Kareem is very caring but his class has too many problems to begin with he is unreachable outside of class, he is such a nit picky grader that he will dock points for the most littlest things and worst part not even show on the rubric what he took out or leave comments what he docked don't take him if you are not an ES major.

I liked Kareem at the beginning of the class; he was funny, relatable, and shows care for his students. Unfortunately, outside of class/lab, he is completely unreachable. Sometimes he isn't at his office hours, and won't reply to emails. Also, he doesn't fill out grading rubrics or leave comments on assignments to indicate why points are taken off.
Kareem is a great Ecology lab professor and is very funny. I wished he taught other classes so I could take him again! Unfortunately, the lab is very excel heavy, so its a lot of homework.
Never responds to emails and is rude to students. Do not recommend.
Easy A. Best bio prof hands down.

My fav prof @ UTSA. Only 4 tests & 5 simple quizzes. Attendance not mandatory but you must attend if you want to know exactly what is going to be on the tests/quizzes. Lectures are super easy to follow. 3/5 quizzes were two vocab questions and exams consist of m/c, short answer, and vocab. nothing is dropped. Easy A+ if you go to class and study

I took this course online Professor Wang is very organized and provided prompt communications via email. This course is lecture heavy and difficult to sit through sometimes. However, the exams are directly from the PowerPoint slides and she allows you to use your own notes for the exams.

Professor Wang is amazing! Taken him for Spring 2021, but you are graded solely on the exams, of which there are 4, so that is the only thing that is a bummer since one miss up has a huge impact on your grade. However, the test is fairly easy and is multiple-choice, and the lectures, practice questions, and the book do prepare you for the test.

Dr. Wang is an amazing professor! Take her class! She gives you big hints as to what will be on the exam. She also gives extra credit quizzes. Her lectures are engaging. She is personable. Tries to get the names of all her students even in a large class. No homework. Four exams in total.

Sweet old British lady. This is college, your professors aren't gonna babysit you. She teaches the material, most people just straight up don't listen and then blame her. I definitely stayed up late reteaching myself her slides (very helpful for the tests btw) because I didn't pay attention in class. I ended with a 98 easily. Take her!

Dont listen to any other review than this one! 

TLDR: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS 
While Professor Sponsel is a very nice woman, her lectures are tough to get through. They are very slow and not engaging, and not useful to the test. If you are a senior FIND ANOTHER ELECTIVE or take earlier. This class WILL put your GPA at risk.
Everything is a group assignment. Lecture heavy but informative. Just let her know whats working and what isn't, she's very flexible with her teaching methods.

My favorite BIO prof at UTSA. Her plants and society class is so interesting and she is a very inspirational person. She tells cool stories in class and all of the content is super interesting and useful information, not just to do well in class, but to know in life. Everyone who says this class was hard is just not good at memorization imo.
Worst Professor at UTSA

When he messes up on quizzes or exams, he does not fix the mistakes instead, he acknowledges them and doesn't do anything to help the students. The only people who are trying to help the students are the TA's. . His exams are also not created by him so he does not know what the exams are on just expects you to know

Lectures consist of PowerPoint readings and nothing more, really. Be prepared to fully teach yourself the material. It is not difficult material, luckily. Forced to use McGraw Hill slop assignments and textbook.

He's a great guy, make sure to form a relationship with him and go to office hours after tests wink wink. He doesn't make the tests, his lecture slides are available outside of class and explains questions very well.

Professor Ramos is very caring and lenient with his students. Let me turn in multiple assignments late because of personal issues. His grading is fairly simple, not too much homework or exams. His lectures can tend to be a little boring but overall the class is easy and the professor is great.

Ramos is great but he is the type of professor that reads directly off the slides. Recommend that you establish your unassigned assigned seat in the front because he tends to speak quietly, mumble, or speak only to the people right in front of him. Tests can be a bit difficult if you don't study and know the functions of everything.

recentReviews.comment: Writing this 5 years later because this was by far the worst class I've ever taken. Completely disorganized group labs with no support when members dropped or didn't contribute, leaving most of the work to one person. Repeated Proctorio issues led to unfair zeros despite constant outreach. Retakes weren't even posted and no flexibility was given.

Dr. Akwar is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. You work in groups and work hands-on on assignments, with there being two pre-labs & two labs per week. They are very informative and interesting! He gives a summary of the lab in the beginning of class, and he helps whenever he can. If I could take him again, I would. Thank you!

Took for physiology lab, amazing professor!!! Super kind and sweet. He is really thorough and clear on what he expects from you. He made this lab super fun, and I really enjoyed it. I'm glad I got to take him for my last semester!!
Kind, but a little hard to understand accent-wise. Tough grader. Brags about few people ever making an A on the tests. 10 points automatically added due to this. Only exams are 1 midterm and 1 final.

I truly did enjoy his lectures; he checks his students for understanding. He says "are we good" after every other sentence. He provides an exam review at the beginning of the semester and also designates time for in class review to prepare students for the exam. He's understanding and will provide extension, if need be (don't give a bs excuse).

You can do good but a lot of things just rubbed me the wrong way about this prof. I remember there was one day he had his class read out all his bad rate my professor reviews and asked people to make negative assumptions about who wrote it so he can be in the right and then made the test with inspiration from the reviews so the writer could see??

If I could go back in time, I would break my computer so I couldn't register for his class. Beyond being the rudest most entitled professor I have ever taken, no matter what everything will be your fault if you try to communicate. You are only graded on test. Hellen Keller must have hired this man because literally any other option is better.

This class is extremely difficult. Exams make up the entire grade and are proctored with Honorlock, as are the extra credit assignments. The tests include material not covered in the textbook, and no study guides are provided. The professor rarely responds to emails and posts videos that barely cover the basics. Avoid this class & professor.

This class (neurobiology) is exam heavy, for the first exam the average was a 44 and it didn't get better throughout the semester. He doesn't respond to emails, and uses honorlock for homework which are only for extra credit. The only grade for this class is for each exam and there isn't a curve.

I wouldn't recommend unless you are passionate about neurobiology. If you take this class be prepared learn from the book. Professor is very nice and passionate about his field. He really wants his students to understand the material instead of recite it to him.If you can do that you will be rewarded with interesting active lectures and fun dialog.
funny dude, interesting class. Overall i'd take him again he's funny HOWEVER he's a tough grader. Has a clear criteria and likes things the way he likes them....

I can NOT imagine having him for more than 1 class. This lab was actually HORRID. Would consistently word questions on exams in the most trickiest way, and if you didn't respond in the way he said word for word (even though it was right), he dock points. Constantly lets anger get the best of him, and will call you out in lab for any little thing,

He tells you what is exactly not going to be on his exams so prepare for that. About 1/3 of what he says he will test on will actually be questioned. Lectures he will tell you what to know but you can go over slides yourself you don't learn in class its all on your own. The exams would be better if he was clearer on what to focus on.

I had him for 2 classes this semester and I am writing first for his Neurolab class first, he was lenient with attendance as long as you communicated. He can be very inconsistent with grading he goes off of his opinions and not whats actually on his rubrics which is really frustrating when you are trying to get full points .

Dr. Hanna was honestly one of the best professors I have had. He is nice and funny, and in terms of the course, he is lenient and offers tons of opportunities to excel. His lectures run parallel with the textbook, and he is available outside of class. He gives great feedback when you ask questions, and I would take his class again, no doubt!

Dr. Renthal cares about his students and the material of the course, but his lectures are incredibly dry. 88% of your grade in the course is taken from exams. There is no graded homework, the textbook is terrible, no STARS or SI tutors, and only one TA. For a class that is arguably more difficult than OCHEM II, students are grossly underserved.
The grading is very disappointing. Any extra boost in grade should be given to all or to no one at all.

Daily iclicker attendance and questions, 4 midterms (lowest dropped), and 1 final (recycled/slightly adjusted from midterms). Very kind and laid back, exams are very similar to reviews, provides optional homework, posts all exams and key afterwards for studying purposes. lectures can be dry but he gets the job done!

Dr. Renthal understands that not every student that comes into class is striving to be a Biochemist, and while his lectures aren't the most entertaining, you can tell he really wants you to pass the class and he wants you to understand the material. His practice exams are similar to his tests and as long as you know the concept, you'll do great.

Best biochem prof!! Gives out a practice exam, which is VERY similar to the actual exam, before the exam date. Fully understand all the concepts tested on the practice exam and review the PowerPoints he post. Also, attend class, he takes iclicker attendance. His lectures are kind of boring, but he is so kind.

oh my god avoid this guy at all costs. he's so old he can't even manage his own class on canvas because he's so technologically incompetent. The entire semester he told us we ONLY had 3 exams, which I thought included the final. No, it was 3 exams + final. He just drones on and on and his class is so incredibly boring. People stopped showing up lol

Everyone passed who showed up, but almost everyone got C's. You have to try extremely high to get above a C, so if your goal is to just graduate and move on take him. If you don't want to tank you GPA take someone else

Does not care about student success, provides little to no notice about almost daily quizzes. No partial credit given. Has the nickname "chainsaw chambers" and a reputation with students who haven't taken his courses which shows just how awful he is. Provides very dense notes and is often very off track with his lectures. Stay away if you can.

He is really hard. When I took him whatever the final was, is the final grade. There are quizzes but they don't count against you. He is a really smart dude, you just got to talk with him and work things out. He didn't fail anyone. Even people who got 50s on the final. He was a pleasure to take, and you just have to work hard.

Chambers is not a good teacher so if you take him get ready to be thoroughly confused in every lecture. His quizzes (no partial credit given) had no correlation to the textbook study material and half the questions on the final exam (worth 60% of your grade btw) he pulled straight from his butt. Definitely the worst class I have ever taken.

recentReviews.comment: Hated this class there was so much information thrown at you. You had to read the whole chapter before class but he would assign three chapters worth of questions and expect you to dedicate so much time while he could NEVER finish a single powerpoint. Exams literally every other week. Powerpoints are filled with info but he does offer alot of ec.

Its ALOT of exams back to back. But if you actually study the material and do all the extra credit it bumps your grade up. I was so close to my B dropping to a C but the extra credit bumped it up to an A! He drops an exam and extra credit points goes towards exam points.

very test heavy in microbio, tests were 95% of your grade, but he gives TONS of extra credit throughout semester, even enough to boost a whole letter grade if you do most or all, he also does Iclicker questions randomly so show up for easy bonus points. He's very nice, just have to show prepared for tests.

Super content-heavy and definitely tough if memorization isn't your strength. That said, the extra credit made the subject actually fun if your creative. Very smart guy despite not being very tech savvy.

I would never take his professor again. your grade is worth 95% of exams , he has no exam review session , and he only post powerpoint slides. He will literally give you 300 slides and says good luck. he doesn't even finish teaching throughout class. please save yourself and take guentzel if you actually want to pass.
Very bad and rude professor! I have never had such an unprofessional teacher! Do not even take any courses with him.
He has attitude and he does not care about students learning! I had such a bad time having him as a professor! Very rude and unprofessional. Very slow in email responding as well.

Prof Zhang is one of the best profs at I've had at UTSA. he is extremely caring and understanding. Just shoot him an email and he will get back to you quickly. attendance is mandatory but if you cannot make it to class, just email him and he'll understand. Exams were online and they were all from his PowerPoint. He's really flexible with exams.

had a difficult time understanding something due to his accent.didn't quite grasp the assignment rubric in class.I emailed him for clarification, but he never responded.When I asked him to elaborate in the next class,he ignored me, insisting it was straightforward. I blame UTSA for hiring such a professor; I've heard he's unsupportive as an advisor

5 Exams, 4 "extra credit" assignments, attendance 15%. All assignments & Exams online. Lectures pointless & hard to understand bc of heavy accent. TA sent all announcements & graded assignments. An A is a 95 but grade goes up to 105 hence "extra credit". Uses a sheet of paper for sign in attendance & allows you to fill in last time if you forgot.

Only read off the slides and was not engaging so he was hard to follow and learn. Attendance isn't mandatory but it counts as extra points towards the final grade. Exams were online and worth majority of the grade so be sure to study. Very few assignments in the course.

He is the worst professor I have ever had. Extremely rude and doesn't care about his students. I regret taking his class, especially during a virtual semester. He didn't care about technical problems with her tests or meetings. He always seemed irritated and had no patience for students who simply needed a bit more of an explanation.

Took her 5 week course.we have a notebook to use for the quizzes and the quizzes are exactly about what she goes over in lab.the problem is that she does not wait for you to write everything down. when you want to try to study at home the powerpoints online dont match hers in class. you HAVE to study for the final. labs were fun tho for me.

Grading scale is unfair. Two skills tests, 6 quizzes, midterm, final, and a Tiny Earth Research group project. I completed all extra credit opportunities & reviewed the videos posted to BB before lab. Not allowed to take home notes due to safety. Lowest quiz grade dropped. Highly recommend taking with another instructor if possible.

No assignments, just one group project and 4 exams. Exams are not multiple choice. He does not take attendance. If you want to pass the class, go to class, because during lectures he will throw a question that will be on the exam. If you have the option of taking another professor, then do so this class will make work hard as if this is a OChem.
Sweetest professor ever. Class was super easy! In addition, all you need to do is pay attention during the lectures.

Dr. Seshu is a professor that genuinely loves UTSA and its students. His course covers A LOT of material and I would not recommend taking it if you have not yet taken Microbiology. His exams are open ended and other grades depend on group work. Love his course!
Cool.
He is a really good professor and really knowledge. He cares a lot about the success of his students and is willing to go above and beyond for them inside and outside the classroom.

Not a bad professor. He knew what he was talking about but you also needed to read the book before class to help you understand. lectures were boring, grades were weird but he tried to communicate and was really nice. Exams were not as hard as the material seemed to be, no practise exams and we had a quiz of the previous chapter every thursday.

Deadlines posted and accepted were two different things, slides were largely filler, very textbook heavy however test content was random. Emails were frequently sent to the wrong student, or class cancellation emails were sent only to some students. Very stubborn professor, only things that can be trusted is the syllabus. Often went back on words.

Professor is fine, doesn't believe in reviewing previous material. Lectures are extremely boring and slideshows are very underwhelming and are not descriptive at all. Truly, the entire course is taught by the textbook, read it and you'll be fine. Tests are based almost entirely on one topic that is picked by the professor and often it was random.

Reads off his slideshows but he expected you to read the textbook before class and already know what he is going to review. Offers no test reviews and only curved the first three exams the last two he did not curve. Exams were 50 multiple choice questions however no amount of studying makes you feel prepared. Gets made if you leave class early.

This professor cannot teach a class properly, his lectures barely go into the detail that he has on his test. your grade is based on 5 test during the semester and thats it, he curved the first 3 tests for my class because they grades were so bad but for some reason did not curved the last two which made a lot of people fail. Don't take him.

Attendance not taken, there are random quizess which are online not proctored. Exams online not proctored. if you attend the lecture its not boring you'll learn alot. There is no assignemnts Just quiz and exams. Easy A.

Currently taking him for Plant Cell Bio and he is probs the best professor I have had at UTSA. He is extremely lenient (dont take advantage tho), attendance isn't mandatory, online exams (3) and quizzes(8), not proctored, and no "assignments". It is pretty difficult to fail this class lol
I would take him again hes super chill, and gives very good lectures.

Please do yourself a favor and take him for both Cell Biology, and Plant Cell Biology. He is an amazing professor and he deserves a raise. I'm not kidding, his waitlist is super long, but well worth it if you end up getting in.
Great professor take him!!!!

Dr. Carless was straight forward about what was important to understand for the exam in her review videos and provided plenty of extra credit. She broke down difficult concepts into easy pieces. Dr. Carless is also a very supportive person and genuinely wants her students to succeed.

Dr. Carless was awesome, and I highly recommend her! I had the textbook but never really used it. Super easy iClicker quizzes as long as you pay attention. Open-note exams helped A LOT, though I still recommend studying beforehand. She offered up to 3% EC towards your final grade, so DO IT! Drops the lowest test and the 3 lowest quizzes/attendance.

Class is so easy, the content is a little hard but open note exams help a lot. she's wonderful and really cares, if you don't understand something she explains really well in office hrs. shes awesome, class is insightful, i definitely learned something.

There was no outside HW. The tests were open note. Each lecture she had an iclicker quiz but as long as you paid attention during lecture, you will get an A. She offered lots of extra credit. The tests are lecture based, no outside materials. Super nice and would take her again.
Great professor, does iclicker for attendance+quizzes. Lectures can be boring! Exams were in person, though she let you bring notes.. THEY HELPED A LOT.

recentReviews.comment: Wild Life Ecology is discussion heavy and requires being able to read and understand the material quickly, followed by being randomly selected to present the information. Not a lot of hw, but the readings are technical. Everything is group work, and an occasional individual quiz. Dr. Bush is very knowledgable but has high expectations.
class is hard and it teaches you how to study because exams are concept focused.

This class is difficult, but Dr. Heidner is an excellent professor who lectures very well. His lectures are 100% the topics on the exam, however you must understand the concepts to do well on the exams. I did not use the book much at all. Exams are 90% of the grade and 30 points of EC possible. Highly recommend even if hard.

This was by far the hardest class ive ever taken. I thought ochem was hard and recieved an A in that but this class i almost got a D. If you have the time to study and work extremely hard then go for it but its an extremely hard class and dont take this with other difficult classes. You may think you did good on exam later to find out you failed it

"Which of the following is false?" is his favorite question to ask on exams. Not to mention tests are 85% of your overall grade, there is no homework to cushion your grade only tests and TopHat questions which saved my grade (take those seriously) had D+ before! Be cautious on what classes you take while taking his class. I learned a lot though!

To anyone reading this, I will start by remaining completely honest: both of Dr. Heidner's courses (Immunology & Virology) are certainly the toughest classes I've taken in my academic career thus far. However, I promise if you pay attention in his lectures, ask questions and meet with him regularly, you will do fine on the Exams. I believe in you!
definitely took a lot of my time, but follow the objectives and study all sources related to objectives, ask questions regarding material if you're unsure
She is a great professor, but her lectures just suck and her tests are doable but require a ton of solo studying since you won't get anything from her lectures.

Fall 2022 took class the only homework was inquisitive assignments due Sunday book needed they are point based can get all 100 only three tests 40% FRQs that are done in class and could use notes she graded lightly only taking off a point or two of 10 the 60% was the multiplechoice exams if you got lower than 70 could take the same test on weekend

So Immunology is a challenging subject all on its own. I remember reading the book but I also found Dr. Cardona's lectures to be so helpful and clear. She is a wonderful teacher who really cares about her students. I found that because I took this class, immunology was so much easier in medical school. Really recommend it!!
HORRIBLE PROFESSOR!

This class gave me anxiety on an Ochem level. She does not post any lecture slides on time so you need to go to class, the TA does not provide practice questions to help with exams, your grade is mainly exams and they don't put out exam grades until a day before your next exam. She and her TA made this course way more difficult than it needed to be

Super nice and sweet, would take her again. She made the material really easy to understand. Attend all her lectures and you will be fine. Lots of group work but it is relatively easy, she does give some articles to read outside of class. Curves the exams. Drops your lowest exam and group work grade. No book just power points.
Go to lecture. Read slides. Give time to the class. 95 for an A. Extra credit is only 1 whole percent if done. And you will do lots of group work.

Lecture off of powerpoints. Ensure you read the readings given and go over powerpoints for tests. Tests are multiple-choice, short and long answer. Super compassionate teacher who made the material digestible

I recommend reading ahead of the lecture, but you should have neurobiology under your belt before taking her course. She did not give her powerpoints until after the lecture, so I recommend writing side notes during the lecture and then going over the slides later. Make sure to reach chapters of the second book accordingly. Tests are free response

Really kind and understanding professor. The entire class was reading empirical articles and presenting them in a digestible manner. It was a little tough if you are not used to reading these kinds of papers but he helps guide you through your presentation to the class.

Great professor. His course consisted of different cycles of scientific/ news articles. Students were to present 3 articles throughout the semester, he took these presentations for a grade as well as attendance.  He was available for help on how to approach the articles. Easiest A I ever earned for an Uppr. division. !

This is for his Neuroscience and Our Future class, which is co-taught with another professor. Basically, the class consists of you being given online articles to read about neuroscience, you critique the article from a scientists perspective, re-write it to have more scientific accuracy, and present it. Easy A if you ask for feedback on your edit

Dr. Wilson is a nice guy who genuinely cares about his students. So much so that I was allowed to retake an exam that I missed due to being sick. The only complaint I have about him is that his lectures are done with slides that are all visual aids for him, not for you. It can be difficult to tell what to write down, as he talks about everything.

Extremely fast speaking. The class is a pretty fast pace as well. If at all possible read ahead before EVERY lecture, attempt to take notes during lecture, print out slides, and re-read chapter and in class notes.

recentReviews.comment: Only exams no assignments, will grade very harshly. Does not offer any corrections, make ups or extra credit. Will take off points if your code is too advanced and/or for things that are out of your control like technical issues. Is very rude when asked about these things. Most grading is based on how he feels. No lecture material to refer back on.

Taught you everything you needed to know to understand the material, wonderful teacher. go to class, you get extra credit for showing up. exams are easy if you search the notebooks, he posts everything after class. genuine guy, great professor, easy class. i had no coding experience before this data science class, would recommend.
Very nice professor. Accent can sometimes be hard to understand. Very picky with test answers, but you have multiple days to take it. If you show up to class then he explains everything very well

One of the best professors I've had. Super smart guy and wants to help you learn. He goes over Exams after they've been graded so you know what you missed and why it was wrong. Interactive course where you work through problems together during lecture - made it easier to do homework problems and exams. Genuine person too

recentReviews.comment: She is the best. She's so caring, and the classwork isn't alot. Plus, she gives you a lot of time to complete it. She isn't teaching at UTSA anymore :(, but I loved her.

Had her in the honors section and she's great! Very understanding and eager to see her students grow. 3 essays and a group project, with minor assignments in between. The deadlines for essays/rough drafts can sneak up behind you, so just be on top of your work. Definitely recommend her, she makes writing approachable and interesting. Free textbook.

Even though the class was difficult for me at times, I felt like her feedback helped me immensely in my writing. There are a few papers that will need to be pretty long but doable. Peer-reviews as well. Group presentation towards the end of the course as well.
Professor Ratcliffe is the best. She makes you enjoy the class and her lectures are amazing.

She is the best writing prof at UTSA. I took her with the Honors section. She is very caring and will help you no matter the situation. There are three essays and 1 group presentation and 1 final portfolio so it is not the most difficult class at all. Don't hesitate to take her if she is open. You will not regret it!
His lectures are kind of boring, and he also goes pretty fast with them. The tests are all based on the book, so make sure to keep up with the chapter hw that he gives every week. Hes funny though.

his lectures can be a lil boring but hes super nice and can be funny, tests are mostly over textbook stuff, group infographic proj but its super easy, weekly textbook hw on mcgraw hill, overall not super hard but there is weekly work and going to class helps you understand whats going on and theres tophat questions some classes for a grade

This was a easy and fun class. In this class there were quizzes and and iNaturalist assignments that were easy to do. And the exams were based on the quizzes. Attendance is mandatory in his class for a grade. I recommend taking this class!!

not the best at explaining the difficult units, but to be fair, anyone would have trouble explaining photosynthesis. funny guy. slides were disorganized and hard to use for studying purposes. goes through slides way too fast but he'll slow down if you just ask. enough hw to boost up your grade if you're a bad test taker. still wouldn't take again
Professor Eddy is understanding, he is really accessible, he doesn't go by deadlines. He has review for his tests. Overall it's an easy class if you put the effort to engage in class.

Professor medrano obviously is good with computers and tech. The problem was that he would refuse to help with questions for the program (ArcGIS) and instead would give hints. He had a "question limit" and would get very aggravated and degrading. He made me feel like I was too stupid to use computer programs.

He seems annoyed when you need help, even through emails. I met him in person and he created a very hostile learning environment, teaching does not seem like the job he should do. Try to take another prof if you can.

I think as a person he is nice  but as a professor he is not great. I would take the other GIS professor if possible. Medrano does not like to help his students, and is often rude. Don't expect him to be inspiring either, despite GIS being a really interesting class.

If you are good with computers you should be fine, just don't assume Nick will help you if you aren't. He can sometimes be very short and unwilling to answer questions. The class is very organized though and you know what's expected of you.
Overall a good professor but will want you to do a lot of the work on your own.

will blame you for all of her assignment issues and provide 0 extra help. dont expect mercy from a professor who thinks she's too good for her class. Barely accessible outside of class so if you're stuck on something, just kiss the rest of your day goodbye. I'd rather be slowly eaten by 500 fire ants.

these reviews are mad inflated. most of her high ratings are from a different time. she's completely redone her class to be painfully annoying. She shoves like a year of lectures into the semester and every part of it comes up on the exams. I wouldn't wish this professor on my worst enemies.

Attendance is definitely mandatory! She's awesome I was just ill prepared. There is a group project that lasted all semester which sucked, but it was fairly easy. Her test are somewhat hard, so make sure you are taking good notes and pay attention closely.

If you take notes and know how to study it is a relatively easy class. Group project lasts all semester but doesn't actually require much work. She is really sweet, engaging, and friendly, her lecture videos are fun even if you don't particularly care about the subject. Def one of the better online courses I've taken.

Professor is so sweet and you can see her passion too! The exams were a little bit challenging, but other than that the class was chill. There is a bit of homework for the class too and a group project at the end. Everything is relatively easy and she's not a difficult grader at all (:

I am not a environmental science major and still found his class interesting. He gets off topic very often but always gives you the information you need. He's pretty funny, and it's fun to make fun of him, and he is very understanding of any situations that may come up. You have to work for your grade, but the work is never overwhelming.

This is for the Geology Lab and doesnt have anything to do with professor Willmot.

The TA just plain out sucked, didn't really give good information over the lab, cared more about her goofy y2k inspired outfits rather than firmly understanding the material. She did have the answer sheet so if you asked she'd help you out.

Geo Lab: The TA assigned for the lab sometimes didn't know how to explain certain questions which was hard to understand but overall it was an okay lab as long as you ask the TA questions. The quizzes are timed with little time given but later you get the hang of it.

The course consisted of 3 writing assignments. The last one being a group writing. Attendance is mandatory since it consists of iClicker questions. Every week there is a timed quiz on the lecture covered. The only thing that caught me off guard was the time quizzes at first since sometimes it consisted of 1 minute per question.

Spring 2023: As a business major taking his class for the science credit, he put in effort to make the lectures engaging. Pretty funny and a sense of humor, too. It's not a complete blow off class, so be prepared to study at least a little bit, or pay attention. At the time he used iClicker for in person quizzes to make sure you paid attention.
The midterm and final exam reviews are not helpful, definitely study for weekly quizzes as they are better reviews for both midterm and final exam. Textbook is provided on canvas, free.

I took him for Environmental Remediation, which is ES 3053. It was a great class and I learned a lot about the engineering and chemistry of remediating contaminated sites. If you are interested in management, this would be a great class to take! This class does put a lot of weight on exams though, and there are weekly quizzes.

He is great! He made stats easy to follow and dropped the lowest lecture grade. he gets off-topic, but usually, he's pretty good. Attendance was mandatory, but idk what percentage of the grade it is. Overall a funny man who teaches a boring subject. He did assign hw that was due the day after Thanksgiving break, so that was evil but he was cool
Jason is such a great teacher! He really cares about students and makes stats very easy. He is also very funny!

Jason is a nice guy but his class is kinda chaotic. You can tell he cares for his students but be prepared to be confused a lot. The nice thing about this class is that the lab and test count as the same, so as long as you do good on the labs you'll pass.

One of the best professors in the ES department. I would 100% take them again. They strive to see you successful, assignments aren't too heavy, only like three group projects for the entire semester and then no more, so don't even sweat about being in groups. The one bad thing was the access code-locked textbook.

Professor Matiella is a super kind and nice professor. She does assign a good amount of work every week and there are tests once a week. The class is easy if you study and stay on top of your work. She also offers a lot of extra credit so take advantage of it because you can earn up to 15 bonus points per test!

Best professor, I enjoyed her lectures so much and they were very easy to understand. She made me get into environmental science more and is very sweet. Homework and other assignments weren't difficult at all, I suggest taking her!
The professor makes this class super easy to follow. Science was never my strong suit, but Dr. Matiella made it easy to follow along. She also offers an abundant amount of extra credit.

Awesome prof. She posts lectures online that can be long but worth it. Make sure to get the book, the tests can reference case studies in the book asking questions specifically for those studies. Group projects within the semester, and always gave extra credit opportunities. The tests varied in difficulty, some easy, some much harder, so just study

For me personally, I thought this class was okay at best. Attendance matters a lot so if you are one to skip class a lot I would not recommend her (about 60% of your grade). Her lectures were okay; she was very monotone. Lectures were 70+ slides at times and the quizzes after were only 10 questions. 3 group projects which are fairly simple.
pretty funny teacher, test were easy. she did group projects but graded ppl individually (aka slackers do bad) good professor.

If you like working in groups this is the class for you. you will make your group in the first day and be stuck with them through the whole semester. Also she is very lecture heavy and you have to spend $150 on a textbook. Attendance is mandatory and she will email you asking why you have missed class.
Very easy class, clear deadlines, reasonable amount of work, very slow speaker very frustrating for me how slow she taught, but she is very caring

The lectures she gives are super helpful for the exams, so pay attention to them. There's also a bunch of group discussions during this class, and if you group up with cool people, it makes the class super fun. Overall a really great professor to aim for when taking this course.
He is the most understanding and kind guy. I'd definitely take any of his classes again. Super knowledgeable and easy to listen to lectures.
he is the sweetest professor i've taken and is very understanding when things come up. if you talk to him and do the work, you should get a good grade. plus he's really funny

I took this class over the summer, not many assignments and tests are worth a lot of the grade but are very easy. There were a few projects but none of them were that hard, I highly recommend taking this class!

he is so sweet and caring. there are only 4 test which are in person and homework online. he is a fast grader and will give you extra credit before a test. there are also group test before the actual exam

Be prepared to give a group presentation and possibly an individual presentation. The class is very chill and almost guaranteed an A as long as you do your group work and show up for the few tests. He is very understanding and nice to talk to.

recentReviews.comment: Great professor, and her class is easy to get an A in. A textbook is required, and attendance is required for iClicker. You will also have to work with the group that she will assign throughout the semester, but it's not bad. She makes time for her student, and you'll only fail if you don't do the work.
Very sweet and made the lectures very interesting. There were a lot of group assignments, but they all could be done in class!

As a freshman taking BIO, I was very nervouse. Proffesor Juarez is amazing tho! She will do her best to help you not fail the class. She has a lot of extra credit opportunities that are really not that bad and she is very good at giving her lectures! Would 100% recommend!
The sweetest woman ever! Class is super easy if you are failing then its definitely a you problem. Theres group work but its easy, iclicker quizzes and exams are unproctored.
Professor Juarez was one of the best professors I have ever had. Shes extremely underrated and sweet.

Lecture heavy, there's no textbook to refer back to and PowerPoints are only provided after he finishes the unit taught, is encouraged to be there but not required. 2 group projects that are a bit heavy, especially the 2nd project.

For GIS he was a very hands off teacher, so come to him if you need any help, Prof himself was amazing but the course was rough the online textbook was a little not accurate to the website, Prof does do everything in his power to help all you need to do is ask. And for GIS assignments I cant tell if its actually hard or Im just dyslexic.

This professor is very good at helping you with the assignments without giving away the complete answers. He also gives plenty of class time for assignments, so you basically won't have homework. You will mostly be reading from the free textbook and applying the steps on it from the GIS application.

One of my favorite professors I have had. He is very knowledgeable and will help you be successful in this course. Has 2 group projects, 2 essays, midterm, and cumulative final. Other than that there's quizzes and video question assignments. Just put in the work, Global Changes is pretty much what our major is all about!

I recommend Professor Grunstra since he is a very chill professor and if you have a question or concern he will answered rather than ask you more questions. Attendance is not mandatory but I recommend to set time out of class for assignments.

Study the slides!! Not really accessible outside of class so best if you talk to her after or before class! She has somewhat of a bias towards students. Also some of the comments here got deleted so (keep that in mind)

this class was a lot harder than I was expecting 😭 Absolutely you have to show up to class every time and study really hard for the exams. They are moderately difficult but they're weighted heavily so you can blow your grade if you don't do well. Couple of homework but mostly lectures, exams, and group pres. Grad students got the same exam as UG.

Dr. Veach is a very knowledgeable professor with a big background in microbiology. I'm glad I took this class, as ES majors aren't given much other bio and microbio exposure. The exams can be a little tricky but you just need to study hard. Also, she is pretty strict on attendance and only lets you miss one class without an excuse.

The worst class I have ever taken. Professor and students wouldn't wear masks in class during COVID. Professor was extremely boring and monotone, class was NOT mandatory, there were about 50 students and only 6 would show up, she would be extremely unfair to students and rude. She's just mad no one would show up because of how terrible she was.

Really amazing professor, He was able to make a subject like soils actually interesting. Attendance is not mandatory but its almost necessary to attend class, theres weekly quizzes on the previous weeks material and a few hw assignments. Tests are difficult and require alot of studying but he has in class reviews and is flexible with office hours

This was a tough class but worth it and Dr. Brigham does a great job making the content as interesting as he can (it's soil after all) lol. Exams are difficult but he provides review material. Show up every class and study the powerpoint and you will do well. Exam are multiple choice but require you to apply what you learned. good luck :)

The lab was given by the TA Claire Littlefield and she was very clear in lab reports and provides lots of great feedback that helped for upcoming reports, there is no midterm/final exam rather it's a group presentation.

The course requires lots of time outside of class, there is a lot memorization and understanding of the material. The professor is accessible outside of class. The textbook is required but not necessary as most of the info. is given in class.

Soils may seem like a very difficult class but if you attend class and do the homework then you should be fine. Dr. Brigham tries to make sure that every lecture and assignment is helpful and will either boost our grade or further our understanding of the material. Overall, he is a great teacher that is motivated to help his students!

Study the slides!! The class is very lecture heavy, I personally can't learn just by reading slides for exams but if you can, good for you, you can skip bc he doesn't take attendance. He has an optional cumulative final. Accesible outside of class. Be specific in exam answers! Would take again just to get a higher grade (STUDY!)

This was a super fun and eye-opening class to take. The creative content paired with the professors easy-going, yet formal teaching style created a very positive learning environment that I felt comfortable sharing in. After completing the course, I can confidently say I know how to write a clear screenplay.

I may be biased since I love screenwriting, but Professor Smith was one of my favorite instructors this past semester. She's very laid-back and funny, and gave solid, objective feedback when you needed it. Her understanding of the material speaks for itself when she does lectures, and they help you look at scripts & films more analytically.

Professor Smith is very passionate about birds, and the class is very interesting. However, if you are an undergrad you WILL be held to grad student standards. She teaches mixed classes with grad and undergrad students, and for the most part, everyone does the same amount of work. She grades very tough, and never curves or offers extra credit.

She is a very intelligent woman who is passionate about birds. The class is very interesting but it is a very intense course. There are two quizzes every week, and bird observations. There is almost always a class discussion post, or assignment if not both due every week. This is a class you take if you like a challenge, but you cannot slack. 2/10

Very informative class, weekly discussion post that are easy to do. A semester presentation that is very easy to get done, as long as you are prepared and follow rubric. A professor that is very understanding of his students.

Intro to Env Risk was an excellent class. One of the best I've taken at UTSA. Eddie is a great instructor and gives student lots of space to express themselves. I feel very informed about pesticide regulation after this course. Eddie is very easy going and wants you to understand the big picture therefore discussion and application is v. important.
The course is very manageable and the professor is very understanding of its students, he also gives a lot of extra credit so it is possible to end the course with a high grade.

Professor DeLeon was fantastic! I really enjoyed his online risk assessment course. I thought it was going to be difficult since I was not too familiar with the course materials, but it was surprisingly easy. Plus he always works with his students to give you additional time. The content is SUPER interesting and I learned a lot.

I could not find this professor on any app so I'm sure she's either new or no one's made a review, I honestly could say that her way of teaching is not it at all since day 1 I've been confused on her assignments I would say it was just me, but others have been confused too.
Absolutely avoid this  professor , can never understand his handwriting , does not teach well in a way math should be learned

Professor Olivarez definitely knows his way around math, but when it comes to translating his ideas into clear and meaningful, step-by-step processes is where he fails. It's good that he is available after class, but he often cancels his office hours for no apparent reason other than that 'Something Important Came up'. Get ready to self-learn.

I believe this professor could be more personable and helpful to his students. Most professors don't want their students to fail but I don't believe he cares too much. He doesn't want to offer help for students who are failing or struggling grade wise. His handwriting is not the best and made it very difficult to understand the content on the board
Doesn't care about students. Teaches super fast and doesnt explai

This is the worst professor I have had at UTSA. He mumbles, has very sloppy handwriting, and explains material out of order without clearly showing steps. Emails go unanswered, and while he helps in person, he can be condescending. The only positive is his fair grading and exam retake policy, which saved my grade. Avoid taking him at all costs!!!

Professor Dyas is pretty good for math-averse students. The online lectures are helpful, but unstuck AI and other resources like the textbook can be just as useful. Attendance is mandatory, but worth it for the extra practice opportunities. Overall, a solid class if you put in the work.

she was a very kind professor but didn't throughly explain things. im not sure of it is because of how fast paced the course itself was or not. if you miss a class it does feel really hard to catch up

Very sweet, and really cares about her students success. Lots of homework and extra credit. Had office hours and even took some time before class if anyone had questions. Attendance is mandatory, and I would take her math class again!

Professor Dyas was a very understanding and sweet lady. However, we would frequently fall behind on the notes which made assignments confusing, but she would extend the due dates. Lots of homework on web work/written assignments, and requires you to submit your work for exams. Overall I would recommend this course to people who are patient.

There was a lot of homework but she had office hours or you can set up an appointment & she can help you. Attendance wasn't required but it does help with understanding the material. Tests were good if you're good at math. There are practice problems before the test & count as extra credit. Also, writing assignment problems can be more difficult.

Barakat's class is structured very well. He goes over many practice problems during class. Tests are 80% of your grade, but he offers 10 extra credit points by completing the test review. The tests were easier compared to the assignments on Webwork and grades them very lenient. Overall, he's a very good professor, and I would recommend taking him.
The GOAT and was very helpful and his lectures were great! Explained things very well. Wish he taught other math courses as well. One of the best professors I've ever had

One of my best teachers overall, very helpful and kind. My grade could have been better if I ever did the homework (I got ~40 in the homework section). Grade mostly relies on exams, all of which were fairly easy. Just focus on notes and try not to fall behind!

Barakat is a very good professor. Exams are 80% of your grade but, he teaches well and the reviews he offers are almost identical to the exams. Also, he offers +10 points on exams if you do the review. He grades lenient and fair. I would recommend taking him even if you're not good at math.

One of the best math professors I have ever had. Very clear instructions and lectures very well. In-class assignments, 10 extra credit points for each exam. Fair grader, allows room for error. Study guides actually contain material on tests. Teaches math in a way that makes sense. Overall an amazing instructor, would retake in an instant!

there's 12 modules throughout the semester. each section per module has practice and preview assignments per section in the module. as the course went on we ended up doing multiple modules a week and having around 10 or more practice and preview assignments due throughout and by the end of the week.

She is VERY kind and lets people turn in late work with minimal penalties. I had a death in my family this semester and she was VERY accommodating and helped me get back on track. She's also very easy to get a hold of and is overall a very good professor. Her class content is easy to understand and isn't overwhelming.
I would say the course is very time consuming, due to trying to get credit for TSI. As long as you put in the work you'll be fine.

If I could give Vega 6/5 stars I would. I could not recommend her more. Dr. Vega knows her stuff and actually has the passion and care to make sure all of your needs are met. She is the most gracious, accommodating, and patient prof/teacher I have ever met.

There is a lot of mini assignments and homeworks, but as long as you are on top of your work the class should fly by really fast. Really engaging in class and the class was overall a fun experience for me. Tests are straightforward and open note. Overall, I feel like I can take away from this class and apply stuff we learned to the real world.
I recommended this professor

He's a nice and funny person, but if you need help with the class material, you would end up teaching yourself. Test heavy, and there are 2 group projects, with the 1st one being very complex. There is no textbook, attendance is not mandatory, but there is a lot of work for this class, especially if you're not already good at Algebra.

Great prof if as long as you show you're trying. His lectures are based off of going through the homework questions. You can ask questions during lecture, and he will be more than happy to help you. Office hours are so helpful as well. 4 exams, one final, make sure you attend lectures, he tells you what questions are on the exam.

Professor Perez is absolutely hilarious. He'll give the most off-hand, unexpected stories and analogies in the middle of lectures and it really helps keep everyone awake and focused because college algebra is not fun. I failed with a D+ in this class likely because I tried to coast. I also found him a little hard to talk to, but he's a good guy.

Great professor really knows how to explain things in a different light. Will give extra credit to those to attend class but the attendance isnt mandatory. Also you need a scientific calc for this class.

DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!! he will go on 20 min tangents about nothing relevant to the class. I had to teach myself the math. The way he teaches and explains things are so confusing. He'll ask a question about a new concept that we have never covered and wait 5 min expecting a genuine answer.

Bro yaps about nonsense 75% of the class, speaks very little about the homework and the tests, exams are hard and never have anything related to what he tells you to practice. If I had to take him again I genuinely might drop out. Very frustrating class. My class averaged below 50's on all 3 exams and there still was no curve on anything. DONT TAKE
First class I ever failed. Very boring , hard to learn from this course. NOT RECOMMENDED!

This professor is by far the worst professor they have at UTSA! He takes months to grade exams and lies about them. I even reported him to the department chair and they just took his side. Do not take him ever find anyone else to take him don't make the same mistake I did.
I wouldn't recommend this professor. His class alone made me re-consider my choice of going to UTSA.

Professor Luna is okay. The class itself isn't super difficult but you definitely have to study hard. She seems as confused as us students when lecturing. Her feedback on exams aren't very clear or helpful.
If you're not that good at math you will struggle. she doesn't really teach but is a very nice professor
Simply do not take this class if you do not remember math from middle school. Her "teaching" style is too fast and if you can't keep up you will definitely fall behind.

She's very friendly and quick to respond to emails. The class moves fast, so if you don't learn quickly, it can be tough to keep up. There are about two homework assignments per week and exams with 5–10 problems. Attendance isn't required, but showing up definitely helps.

Professor Luna is SO SWEET! She helps you if you're confused and is very good at explaining concepts. She's patient, kind, and overall amazing. She only counted attendance on Fridays, but I rarely skipped Mondays and Wednesdays unless I had to because the class environment is chill, welcoming, and doesn't treat anyone badly for being confused.

He outlines expectations well and provides resources to help you. I highly recommend going to each and every lecture and looking at all the supplementary videos if you're not going to the math gym/office hours. Any difficulties I had during the class were self imposed. Calc II is known as one of the more difficult, so be prepared mentally.

took him for Calc 2 which in general is a difficult class but he does give very good lectures the only thing bad I could say about him is for exam review days he does not go over the practice exam himself.  He lets you do it with your peers around and at the end he just gives the answer key and thats it.

He is amazing at giving lectures, but they are very test-heavy, with each test accounting for 20% of your grade. There is also a decent amount of homework that, if you actually sit down and do it, takes time. I would recommend this professor, just be ready to pay attention and study for tests, as he isn't an easy test grader.

Very nice guy! Not much partial credit given; however, that means you'll be able to actually gauge how much of the calculus knowledge you've learned because of that. I had him for Calculus 1, so it was not much of an issue; with harder courses like Cal II, it might be more challenging to score higher. Very humorous guy I enjoyed his lectures.

Definitely would recommend Brucks. He is amazing during his office hours and I have been going to them for Calc II as well and he is just as good as he was in Calc I. I can tell he cares a lot about his students, current and past. He has everything on canvas so you don't have to worry about missing class.

She genuinely cares about her students. If you are struggling with her class, do not worry. She has office hours. She grades her tests as modules. You will be tested individually on 11 modules; you can retake up to 5 at the end of the semester. Same questions as previous tests. Only the numbers change.
Professor Bentley is the best, I highly recommend her for MAT 1133.

Dr. Bentley is one of the best professors I've taken to date! She explains this really challenging subject in a way that makes it simple to understand. I loved her teaching style. She always responds to emails and is willing to help you succeed however she can. You can tell she loves her job! I HIGHLY recommend taking this course with her!

She's definitely a great professor and teaches well, and you'll understand the material better if you go to class. However, the way exams are graded are really intense, which brought my grade down extremely. If you're a bad test taker, good luck. At least retries are given out in lieu of a new final. But no extra credit or rounding is offered.

Dr. Bentley is great. This is the first time I haven't needed a math tutor to pass a math class. 1 webwork assignment and guided notes due each week along with a quiz. 3 exams. Exam retries instead of final for up to 5 questions. A lot of challenging concepts but she explains them well. If you need to take business calc, take Dr. Bentley.
Amazing professor, super caring and compassionate and gave ample opportunities to earn points on the exam and the lectures were great.

I had Chris for my Algebra and Number Systems class, this being my first experience taking a proof based class, and it definitely made the experience so much better. If you are ever struggling with the material or simply want help with your work, office hours were always the best! Also never be afraid to ask question. Definitely my favorite prof!

Don't take Chris' class if you want your all-time favorite teacher to be nocked off their pedestal and replaced with Chris. I have never understood a math class better than Calc 1 of all things because of him. Not only is Chris an exceptional communicator, they're also super fun and thought-provoking.

Exceptional at communicating to the class about what to expect for the exam, in terms of material, as well as a timeline. The explanation of course material, for what looks intense, was impeccable and made learning both fun and easy. I would recommend taking her class again, if not for Algebra & Number Systems, then for another class.

i had chris for cal1 fall 25 and they are by far the best professor ive ever had. i'm back here to mourn the fact that i can't take any other classes with chris because if i could, id take them all the way to calc3. gives as many partial credit points as possible and with the extra points from doing reviews, i never made less than a 100 on a test.

dont take this guy if you dont already understand the material. all questions you ask will be taken as you not paying attention, and he will let the whole classroom know. if you are prone to skipping class or submitting things late, you WILL fail. i took 2 of his classes and he was a consistent 0 stars.

Professor Nasr is one of my favorite professors. He does want his students to succeed, as long as you show up and put in the work. SHOW UP TO EVERY CLASS! Write everything down and practice the questions he gives you to review before a test multiple times. He is a good professor but you have to actually learn. Tests are 55% of the final grade.

I asked him to clarify a small concept two seperate times. He yelled at me for not paying attention and said I should have known the answer. It took way more effort to yell than it would have to just answer my question. I would've just Googled it, but he would scold us for that too. If you must take his class, don't bother asking him questions.

at first i tried to give him the benefit of the doubt but he's MEAN. take him if you alr know everything bc if you're coming here to learn, this is not the class. be ready to be belittled and traumatized. the way i feel ab him is how kendrick feels ab drake. he comes off as cute at first but… be prepared to get. your. feelings. HURT. don't take him

I have never taken such a bad professor. He DOES NOT teach anything, he expects you to learn everything from the textbook, homework does not match the exams. Everyone in the class seems loss. Very passive aggressive and if you ask a question he will get visibly frustrated. Does not help you at all and does not explain things.

Professor is good overall. Online class is structured weird. Lectures are watched offline and class time is spent doing Amplify activities which imo, should be flipped. Lectures should be on the zooms to cover topics and open up to the class for questions/help. Amplify makes me feel like I'm in elementary school during COVID.
Wants the best for his students, always willing to explain concepts and help you succeed!

Professor Schurmann is awesome and makes tough material easy to understand. Assignments are clear and manageable. If you do the readings and work, you'll do well. Quizzes are graded tough, so study, but you get notes and a second try. Tutoring sessions are very helpful—use them if you struggle. He is a very reasonable and patient professor.
Is very strict on grading quizzes, but funny guy and helps a lot.
strict grader when it comes to quizzes

This class was easy. She allows quiz retakes, and the retake is the same quiz with different numbers. You're also allowed to bring a page of notes. The only downside is that there is a lot of homework.

her reviews are really negative so i was worried but she was not that bad at all. not the best teacher and you have to learn on ur own but its just algebra. lets you redo all the quizzes and lets you have a page of notes so not hard to pass. It's not a hard class as long as u do the hw and study before or have a good page of notes for the quiz.
