This class is very difficult. Professor Chen tries his best to thoroughly explain the concepts and give examples, but he expects you to know every detail about every theorem. Homework was graded only on completion and we never received any feedback. Midterms were 50% and the final was 40%, and Chen is a very strict grader.

This class is just overall difficult. The professor is nice in his office and try's to explain material so that we understand but proofs are challenging in general. He wanted us to memorize everything taught but considering this is a very difficult class, it felt impossible to remember every single thing. I didn't enjoy this class.
His lectures are all speaking in theorem. Very few examples and gives an insane amount of homework. 28 assignments on top of three quizzes and two midterms. Each homework is minimum 15 questions.

Just a really chill guy. Maybe too chill? Literally had 3 things graded the whole year which is good if you pay attention and bad if you don't. Really soft spoken, but is good at explaining things if you need it.

Dr. Norman is really easy going in his lectures and takes his time to explain topics, this makes class much easier to follow. He's always up to reiterate things as needed and won't make you feel stupid for not knowing something even if you went over it 100 times. He really just wants everyone to learn and won't just let you fail.

Professor Norman is interesting. He's rarely prepared, often late, but it's clear he knows the material. Just not how to convey it properly. For this course, with materials ripped from Boppana's Math Found class, it became clear how unprepared he was to teach it. He's a sweet guy, but I got by by using Boppana's much more concise notes. Would avoid

Professor Norman is a funny guy. His lectures pretty much come straight from the book. One of the annoying things about his class is that he was never really prepared for class or never seemed to put effort into it. He never assigned things so he wouldn't grade them and when he did it took him he entirety of the semester to. Tests are easy though.
Not always coherent. Tends to simply execute a problem without addressing the concept that is confusing students.  Tests were not scheduled ahead of time, and syllabus did not include all chapters.

I loved taking this course for differential equations! Lectures were thorough. Homework's were great for practices. She always makes sure you are prepared for your exams! Very helpful in office hours. 100% would take again.

She is amazing. Lectures were clear. She always had everything ready and she was always ready to teach. We took 3 exam and the final was a take home which was really helpful. She offered extra credit here and there which was also very helpful. Overall very good math teacher.
An incredible professor who really cares that students absolutely understand the concepts taught in Foundations of Mathematics. Would absolutely take her for any other mathematics class.

Professor Stamova is one of the best math professors! Her lectures are extremely helpful to do homework, exams, and the final exam. She only gives you a few homework assignments and you have a month to complete problems in each homework assignment because they can be difficult to solve. 100% RECOMMENDED if you are taking Differential Equations I.

She's the perfect balance of making it easy, but you still learn. I really wish I took her for earlier math courses. Hw can be challenging but you have forever to get it done. Tests aren't bad, and she reviews a lot. Great BB content.

Foundations of Math was literally just presenting proofs every single day. He expects everyone to get up and present a proof to the class but also allows for people to present in his office hours. He is one to go on and on about specific things, sometimes 1 proof can take up an entire 1hr and 30min class. But he is always availbale in office hours!

Overall a good easy going professor. Show up to class, do the textbook problems and you most likely will be fine. He grades very generously and drops an exam grade! At times, he might not be very clear, Make sure to ask him questions and go to office hours; he is always available to answer questions and clarify hard/confusing topics.

As long as you go to class you will know what is going on in the semester. If you don't know just email & he will get back to you but this may happen during student presentations because they are back to back presentations in each class. You do have to study based off presentations & the review is very helpful to your success in the class.

Dr. Richardson is a great guy and professor. He grades the 3 highest exams so make sure you show up to class, do the example problems, and study. Overall, he graded super easily and wanted everyone to pass. Definitely cannot go wrong taking him. Diff Eq was easy!!

Very detailed and interactive lectures. There is no graded homework but he will give you problems to practice from the book and other websites to help guide you. If you attend lectures and try to follow in class you will be able to learn. It is test heavy but he doesn't try to trick you, he will tell you what types of questions he will ask.

This professor is an incredibly compassionate and passionate person. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He can be a tough grader and a little nit-picky, however it's for the sake of improving the student, and he allows for makeups. He can be a little scatter-brained so self learning is necessary.

The course itself is very difficult and the professor didn't do much in-depth teaching. He is a extremely hard grader but he let us redo the homework to get a better grade. The graduates students had to do a presentation and he interrupted many times that made it difficult to understand what the graduates students were actually teaching.

Iovino is a great teacher. He is always willing to take time out of class to answer questions and work out examples if you need help understanding the topics. He also gives you chances to revise homework assignments before he officially grades them. Very caring professor who genuinely wants you to succeed in his class.

I took him in a 5 week semester. I really don't recommend it for Modern Algebra unless you're highly skilled with proofs already. Decent won't cut it. He looks for any reason to dock points on the test. If you do go for the 5 weeks, make sure you're not taking any other class. Even then I probably wouldn't recommend it.

This is a very difficult class as it is & Iovino makes it worse. Hes knowledgeable but his teaching method is terrible. Expects proofs to be perfect but struggles w/them himself sometimes. Syllabus says to spend 2 hrs/day on HW, not including studying/reading. Graded only on exams & his grading is unreasonable. Im taking it again w/ someone else.

Back to back projects, heavy comfusing lectures, completely inadequate, and not good at explaining, I too went to other professor's lectures to learn the bare minimum. I would never in a billion years take again.

The professor provided engaging lectures and offered detailed explanations if asked. The test reviews were identical to the test. For the projects, follow the documentation, and you will easily receive a 100. He does focus on theory, so make sure to ask him to go through practice problems. An amazing teacher overall.
Too many projects, too boring lectures. The projects cooked us so hard with 2 projects back to back in finals week. Might be wraps.
YAP YAP YAP

I agree with other reviews—it's not that bad if you take charge of your own learning. Lectures aren't necessary to pass, as his teaching style is confusing, directionless, and ineffective. Toward the end of the semester, though, he assigns back-to-back projects without adequately preparing students. He fails to take charge of his classroom.

Very sweet and super fun class, she is very experienced and has lots of great advise. If she offers feedback before you submit an assignment, take the offer to ensure you get full points. Revise your work!!! Very constructive and offers great advice to help you grow as a student. Lots of partner/groupwork but it's not difficult.

She's amazing!! Very connectable and will always give you advice. Its actually impossible to get anything below an A in this class unless you just don't show up or don't do work. She's very understanding as long as you communicate. 10/10, she's the best.

Professor Weissling, is an amazing professor and in general person to be around. Her lectures are always engaging and she is an inspiration to all future teachers out there! Definitely would take her class again!
Great feedback on assignments. Interact with her when she asks questions as she likes to get to know her students. Very respectful professor!

Her lectures were always super fun. She is super nice and loves talking to us, and answering questions. For the most part, the assignments were clear and easy to understand. She made learning super fun.
She's the sweetest and absolutely crazy about math and helping you to understand it. She makes math easy and explains it in a way that just makes sense.
Take this class!
She's the best. She makes you want to learn. She loves math and goes out of her way to help students.

She's literally one of the best professors at UTSA. The staff likes to give her grief because if you have 2 or fewer absences, you get to skip the final. She goes the extra mile for her students. She available outside the classroom and will put in the effort as long as you do. My only complaint is that she's too lenient with her student.

I had her Fall 2015 and she was honestly very nice. Attendance is mandatory (especially if you don't want to take the final). Class work and homework were super easy and she goes over everything so that everyone will understand. Sometimes she does for some reason think that like math is the most exciting thing and that everyone loved it.

All while she is a great professor, her lessons were generally hard to follow and didn't give clear products of what she expected us to grasp from the lesson. To be honest once we stopped having to read the assigned books and just focused on any articles that were given in class it was a lot more enjoyable.

I was scared reading the reviews on here but Dr. Emeneha's graduate course was actually really good! Don't get me wrong, there was a lot (and I mean A LOT) of busywork and papers to read, but nothing impossible. She really took the time to get to know each of us, which I appreciated. She was very nice and I learned a lot, actually.

Please do not take. I feel so bad that nobody was happy in her class, but she made it that way for everybody. Although I got a high A, she was still very passive aggressive in emails about genuine questions I had about the course/assignments. She told us from the beginning the final was going to be difficult and proceeded to not give us any review.

I have a feeling shes putting in reviews for herself (sad), her feedback is so broad it was pointless, had us do a 20 Q final with no review (it was over 16+ lectures, 3 books, and additional readings we had) just told us to use our notes weve taken. When we gave feedback she just seemed aggravated and offended. Really not worth the stress!!
Lots of work, but everything is really easy! She was very supportive and the weekly Zoom meetings were very helpful

(NDRB2113)Great professor, but doesn't curve grades--I finished the class with a 89.73 (B+). Other than that, he's very passionate about the class, and he allows a notecard for the exams. The study guides SAVED me, they're extremely useful. Lot's of homework, but it's really easy and serves as a good grade booster if needed. No McGraw Hill.

(NDRB 2113) Dr. Troyer is a professor who cares about his students and love what he does. He is always excited to teach a class and he will provide you with everything necessary for you to succeed in the class. Very generous grader, easy to talk to, and he is quick with responding to any questions you may have.

NDRB-2113 Use the outlines he provides as exam reviews and you'll do fine! He even posts review videos going over all the key points. I was a little overwhelmed in the beginning, but he's really clear about what he wants you to focus on. Generous grader and a couple opportunities for extra credit.

Troyer's tests are hard but not unreasonable if you study well. He is a good teacher and cares a lot about his students. He offers extra credit and opportunities for success that make the class manageable. He was nice and understanding. He also graded our final in literally 2 hours which was great.

I love this professor. He grades on a big curve and makes getting and maintaining an A very easy. There is extra credit and he records reviews before all the tests and the home works are short but help you get ready for the test. Just a fantastic professor who will really get you excited about biology

Professor Troyer is a better professor than people make him out to be. He listens and gives great feedback to students. However his tests are quite different from lecture so best read and look at supplemental sources he posts.

His tests are super specific so I did not get above a B on any of them, however iclicker, homework, and extra credit will save your grade. He definitely really tried to help us out with our grades as much as he could so I respect that.
TERRIBLE, worst calculus professor whoever taught biology. 10/10 do NOT recommend

It was hard to find a consistent way to study. I failied two exams and passed the class with my grade with perfect attendence, a decent lab grade, he drops the lowest exam, and making 100s in all of the online quizzes. Take advantage of the office hours and tutors. His questions on exams are specific so memorize the powerpoints word for word.

nice guy and always open to questions but his lectures are very unclear and the test are pretty rough. there is extra credit and the homeworks should bring up your grade. it is easy to pass this class but to get an A will require a good amount of work. you cannot slack off.

Dr. Gamblin is easily one of the best professors at UTSA. He will tell you exactly what he tests on. There are lots of opportunities to become familiar with the material before the exam (practice exams, multiple opportunities for homework, discussion boards, iclicker questions). He responds to emails very fast and is receptive. Take him!
Very good professor. Elaborated on topics which made it easier to understand. Requires Tophat and McGraw hill. Had Group Concept Maps due every week.

-if you're a procrastinator i wouldn't recommend this class at all. 9 assignments after the first day, very tedious-
took me 2 hours to do only two assignments
-he also goes pretty fast, he does lecture style with group work and doesn't take any lates grades or assignments
-attendance is also mandatory 
-textbook is also very expensive

Graded participation w/top hat questions in class. He was responsive to emails. Very kind and knowledgeable guy. Classwork was all Mcgraw Hill which was super easy. Screen proctored exams were sometimes rough but never made below a B. Would've made an A if I went too lecture more. Easy to talk to in class.

Dr Anantua is a tough professor and expects a lot from his students, especially those within the physics department. He has an open ear, and made himself available for me to explain how much was on my plate and how I could help myself in class. Putting in the effort is CRUCIAL to passing any of his classes. I took PHY 3513, not PHY 7903 (no option)

Review for Electrodynamics:Fall-24
Class was challenging, as it should be.Electrodynamics is conceptually easy and mathematically brutal. When I put in the work needed,results and knowledge happened. Some of my classmates wanted a covid era rubber stamp and they didn't get that.

IMO, Prof did everything possible to make sure we grasped the topic.

Despite the challenging nature of the course, I definitely learned a lot. Professor Anantua's teaching style is clear and effective, and he always made sure to explain complex concepts thoroughly. Professor Anantua is dedicated and knowledgeable, making the difficult material more approachable and engaging.

Took his advanced PHY 7903 GRMHD course. It was math heavy and give out a lot of homework. However, he grade very lightly and his feedbacks from them are great. He made the course very enjoyable and entertaining. We even watched interstellar for 3 days! Would take him again.

Great instructor, very wise, and actively listened to the feedback given to him from his students. Though attendance is not mandatory he does seek for class participation. Only one assignment per week, an open note midterm, and no final made this class pretty easy and almost impossible to fail. Idk why others are being so harsh.
We are covering difficult material a week before being tested on it during an exam.
not professional what so ever. Interrupts already difficult material to bring up her cat. cut it out.
Dont take this course. I promise no matter how interesting it sounds its not worth your time unless you're majoring in it
Talks about her cat and breaks the flow of instruction. Too quiz heavy. Im not learning. Im struggling.

Deadlines are enforced too strictly. I tried to access a quiz less than a hour after it closed and immeditarly contacted the professor, but no late attempt was allowed. Students should avoid her or plan ahead and treat every deadline as absolute. In my experience, there was little flexibility for minor lateness, which made the course more stressful

He gives out a lot of free and easy assignments. A lot of group projects too. Tests are group projects, so get a good group at the beginning and you'll be set. Attendance isn't mandatory, and while his voice is boring, the slideshows are good enough. I didn't pay much attention and even missed some big assignments, and still passed.

You can tell this teacher really cares about what he's teaching. I thought the course was pretty easy but he does have some projects/papers required that require some amount of brain power. Really cool guy.

You can tell he loves what he's doing. It was hard because I honestly thought I was failing the whole time but in the end he let us redo all the quizzes with unlimited attempts and I got an A-. I never understood what was going on in his class but he was fun to listen to. The man knows what is is doing.

Class is relatively easy, but professor is REALLY boring. It was not even slightly interesting. Really bummed about that.

Pros: 
- Credit back from corrections on tests
- Attendance not mandatory

Cons:
- Tests not based on info taught
- Test Qs don't make sense or on topics that weren't covered
- assignments are often confusing/pointless

AST1013 was definitely one of the best classes I've taken and it's mainly due to the professor. He is very passionate about what he teaches and wants students to succeed, his lectures made me actually want to go to class. Almost all assignments are group quizzes, and theres no exams besides the final which is bonus points.

Very nice professor who clearly cares about his students. Lectures can be a little boring, but he tells you exactly what's going to be on the exam, so worth going to. Grade is 25% homework and 25% each of 3 exams, no final. Tests are 7 questions, 4 mcq and 3 frq which he gives partial credit for. Would definitely recommend taking him!

Dr. Botez is a very kind and passionate man. He made physics an interesting class bc he himself was very interested in it. Incredibly generous with grading, but very fast paced in his lectures given that the amount of material. I asked for an extension on 1/3 HWs I missed, and he extended all of them, and said "Good luck in your future endeavors"

Currently taking this professor and hes amazing! You can tell hes really passionate about what he teaches. Attendance not mandatory but sometimes taken randomly for extra credit.Breaks down problems step by step.Exams are in person with about 6/7 questions.Mock exams are very helpful and theres only one homework each week.Enjoying this class a lot!

Professor has great lectures and explain concepts well. Open to answer any questions. Attendance is optional. Exams are 7 questions with easy concepts if you have basic knowledge of concepts taught before and know how to solve problems.

Physics is hard so don't expect much learning from just watching her lectures, which are around 20 minutes long. You have weeks to complete homeworks and are only given two exams and a final. Exams are not proctored and you're given an extra try per every question if you get it wrong the first time, as well as the homeworks.

Be prepared to teach yourself and waste countless hours watching her lectures just for the material learned not be reflected on the homework at all. The only good thing I can say about this class is that she is very reasonable with assigning homework. So it gives you enough time to do them but YouTube was the only reason I passed this class.

Be reading to watch YouTube to teach yourself. The course is easy to follow, lecture vids, hw,  2 exams and a final! The exams are worth a lot but she does give you all day to take it and two attempts per question! You do need to buy Cengage, it's nice bc you get your grade right away! (no make ups and no extra credit)

For an online course she was a good professor. Not a lot of assignments and the due dates were reasonable. Her videos to watch can be time-consuming, as well as having to read the book on top of that. She communicated with us frequently though which I appreciate and was willing to help answer any questions regarding the homework.

I took her online and it was a mess with the synchronous sessions! I also couldn't really understand her accent. Be prepared to use Youtube and teach yourself to learn if you take this class. I wouldn't recommend taking this class. Find another professor if you can.

recentReviews.comment: Can't teach to save his life. Just make sure you remember how to do math and take the easy A+, he literally doesn't care what you put on homeworks, just that you do most of them and submit them as a single PDF.

Class formatting is : watch the lecture videos outside of class and in class we work on practice problems. There were no midterms, just one final, and attendance was not required. The class is hard to fail. Pick him if you are just trying to get your physics credit in but if you are actually interested in physics pick a more experienced prof.

He doesn't know how to teach yet. He sort of changes his mind a lot about the practice problems he does in class. His in-person lectures topics don't really match the topics on the homework. He will often introduce topics expecting students to already have an idea of what is going. If you want a good understanding of physics take another professor.

There were a lot of lectures videos that taught the subject but were not useful for the homework. The homework was hard and time consuming. He did hold zoom homework help sessions and was easy to reach out to which helped a lot with the difficult homework. No midterms just 1 final exam over all topics.
should make it easier to study in the class. Average professor, answer emails fast though.

Prof Fuller is not the greatest professor but keeping in mind this was her first semester teaching physics 1 she was not that bad.  There is defenetly room for imporvement but her exams were fairly easy.  If all other prof. are taken this would not be a bad option

I took the PHY 1611, Algebra-based physics 1 lab. The labs are very easy. The labs explain exactly what to do procedurally online and the math was fairly simple to figure out. Make sure you include units in your math and answers.

recentReviews.comment: There one is lab and quiz due every sunday. You have the whole week to work on it. The labs are really easy to complete. If you want to get easy A then take this class.

You have to get lucky on your TA tbh. I didnt like my TA, but it depends on who you get ofc. Attendance is mandatory. You're allowed one missed lab; it doesn't matter if youre sick, save it for the end when motivation goes down. No exams, but lab reports every week.

This class was fully online. Every week there was a quize, and a lab to do which was very easy to complete. I got B in the class bc I missed an assignment to complete. The quizes and assignments opens in the beginning of the week and are due sunday 11:59. There is no Final. No exam. Just quiz and one lab to complete every weeks.
Take his online course! They are taught by TA's I got a great one.

it wasn't a bad lab, it depends on ur TA really, since chris dunn wasn't actually there teaching. you have to take a 5 question quiz in the beginning of EVERY lab which really sucked, some TA review the material before u take it which is really great. make sure you get in a good group. your lowest lab worksheet and quiz is dropped thankfully.

The class was easy to navigate and the exams were 50% based on the HMs. The HMs take a bit of time to finish but worth it. Professor was very nice and cares about this students. I took the summer course so we had 2 exams and 1 final. It was okay, just make sure to study and ask questions. Highly recommend his office hours!

The subject material was too tough for my course load this time around. His lectures were okay, you just really have to keep up with them and stay ahead in order to keep afloat in the class. Weekly homework due via Cengage that can take a few hours to complete; 4 open-book exams using some questions you will have seen before.

Dr. Mobilia was a very average professor. He had session that we could attend if we wanted but the homework being due every single week on Friday even during the holiday's made me sick of this class. I really did not appreciate the amount of homework assigned each week.

Dr. Lopez-Mobilia is amazing if you are a Physics Major. His PHY4983 (Unifying Concepts in Physics) is focused on a discussion/lecture environment similar to that of a master's course where group discussion on the topic at hand is essential + term paper due at the end of semester. No exams, 30% HW/30% Discussion Participation/40% Term Paper.

Dr. Lopez-Mobilia is extremely smart and amazing at explaining physics. Taking his class at the same time as the physics lab helped so much during his exams. Lectures are a little boring if you're not in love with physics but he is a solid choice if you want to learn. Would take him again.

recentReviews.comment: It honestly wasn't bad, but it also could be because I took it in the summer. Just get through the homework, and for tests, focus on the examples from class and clicker problems. They are very similar to what he will show on the test. Even if you have to memorize them, it'll help a lot.

I loved Dr. Konno but he definitely is the toughest teacher in the Physics department. He has high standards and really wants everyone to know the material before moving on. If you show work, you will get partial credit. Brush up on your math and make sure to do the examples ALOT. The testing will become second nature if you really practice a lot!

Hes not good at teaching. Exams are very predictable, he only writes questions similar to the questions he goes over in class/posts on canvas. If you spend a week studying all of his example questions and learn how the concepts work, you can get an A on every exam no problem. Treated the class like a self study with an occasional exam and was fine.
Just a nightmare class tbh
Failed me by 0.5 points away from a C- , now I have to retake the whole class and was not caring for students at alllll, literally 0.5 points away from a C- DO NOT TAKE HIM AND DELAY YOUR GRADUATION

Extremely passionate professor and is very open to questions. SO NICE AND SWEET. His lectures can be heavy but he explains materials well and does many examples. Only garden with exams but exams are open note and always include extra credit. Attendance is taken every lecture.

No hw assignments, but attendance is mandatory or your grade gets reduced. Lectures are very blah, he uses an old school projector & his hand writing is difficult to read. Exams are online, open book, & always has bonus question. Boring class atmosphere but you can tell he is passionate about Physics, would take again cause it was an easy A.

SHOW UP TO CLASS if you miss two classes you start dropping letter grades. Other than that the exams were easy they were online pdf file that you print out and do on your own. The book offers really similar problems like that ones on the exam. Do not use chegg the grader will catch you and its easier to do your own work then use chegg.

Very passionate about physics and is willing to give lots of extra credit. Truly wants his students to learn and doesn't want them to fail. Attendance is mandatory, but that's only due to the fact that many people just weren't coming to his classes initially and were failing his tests because they didn't come.

He's a nice guy and very knowledgeable/passionate about his field. However, his lectures are really dry and monotonous. Weekly homework is given for practice, not for a grade. Read the syllabus and make sure you understand the attendance/grading policy so it doesn't catch you off guard. Review Physics 1 concepts bc he doesn't cover them at all.

Professor Capps was a good professor, but it seems you're teaching yourself the material. He is available after hours and is willing to schedule a time with you, but he will respond in a couple of days. All of his lectures are on video, and I feel they do the bare minimum to teach the material. There's nothing really that goes into much detail.
Jeremy Capps was able to make complex concepts into 2-3 page summaries that explained everything perfectly. Super easy exams if you read what he puts out!

with all due respect, jeremy capps......  IS THE GOAT, STOP PLAYING. you want a good grade? you have a stacked scedhule but need to take phsycis? you suck at physics (proabably)? then look no further, As Dr. Capps is quite literally the best option for physics, he is caring, responds fast, and is hilarious. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!!!!!

He is awesome! Such a chill professor, attendance isn't mandatory. All hw's are due at the end of the semester. All hw's and 3 exams are done online and not proctored; he doesn't care about how you complete it. Final is optional if your 3 exam grades are to your liking. Easiest A in a physics class I've ever taken!
there is not much to be said besides the fact and with all due respect HES THE GOAT FIYTB!!!!!
Great class definitely recommend and took this in the summer.

around 60% of the grades are from exams, but most importantly, you won't make less than a 75 on them, she makes you enjoy and actually understand the material, I never liked physics, but she makes a good effort for you to understand and get the material, also makes reviews for exams and uses cengage for coursework.

An amazing professor! Her lectures are amazing and help with the exams. Doing the homework helps a lot with the grade and the exams are easy. If you do the homework and go to class, you're going to get a B or higher in the class guaranteed.She is so nice and is very passionate about physics and helping students! 10/10!
I honestly loved Modern Lab, I wish there weren't as many equipment issues, but I know that wasn't Dr. Shepard's fault, she did her best for the class. She graded very light, which was very helpful.

recentReviews.comment: Dr. Chen really cares about quantum mechanics, yes, it is a really hard class, but he does his best to make it more interesting and actually teaches you the things you will need in the real world. Dr. Chen cares more about you learning the concepts, rather than how good you are at math.
best. teacher. i. have. ever. had.

Pop quizzes are easy 100s, just show up to class. He emphasizes problems that will be on test. Tests are multiple choice/free response w/ cheat sheet. He gives partial credit. Lots of HW but easy 100s if you attempt it and turn in. Class was disorganized. Had our two days/wk of instruction cut to one day so quality of instruction wasn't great.

If you want a easy A DON'T take this class. You're gonna have to work. He wants everyone to be successful in his class through. He often curves tests and he goes over exam questions in class before we even take it. He is super nice but his way of teaching physics isn't for many people.

Only grades are 3 tests. Almost no calculation examples given in class. Most questions on the test were theory based and didn't include any numbers. Youtube will be no help. Lectures were confusing and hardly learned a thing. I got an A in phy 1 but couldn't pass this class.

I'm not sure why people complain. Professor Hamby does not answer questions. He is responsive to questions, even the night before a labs due. He's firm with grading, and his comments can be vague, but the class is easy overall. Just read the prelab notes, make sure your graph is correct, and answer all the questions. He's actually an easy grader.

He is a stickler for sig figs, but he has all of his grading criteria laid out in Canvas that basically tells you how to get an A+ in the class (I found out too late). I submitted the procedure with the lab for the first few weeks, and he was pretty passive aggressive in his grade comments lol.
Pretty decent for a physics lab online. He's pretty strict about graphs so be careful with those and with sig figs. No real complaints though, online labs are stupid but its an easy grade I guess.

Counts off for the smallest things. Instructions are not fully clear and examples tend to not help at all. Don't expect any type of useful notes unless it is for the easiest thing. Would not recommend taking unless you want to write a whole paper for each lab.

I took his physics II lab and he was a good TA. Answered my questions within the day and is an easy grader as long as you follow what the lab requires you. He gives you many resources to help you with the lab and the quizzes for each lab are meh (make sure to study the first part of the lab).

He was very sweet and the projects aren't very hard unless you don't study the material. Also HW is a huge part of your grade but you can work with your classmates so take advantage of that. I love this class and I'm looking foward to taking physics 2.

If you need Physics 1, you should really take him. I took him in the covid times, but I believe his in-person courses would be very similar. Extra-credit is intrinsic to the course; you get bonus points for various things that you can use to redo an exam, make up homework points, or bump up your final grade. Your best exam is worth more points.

Dr. Brancaleon is the best PHY prof at UTSA. Allows 1 take-home Exam. Tiered exam grading (BestExam25%,2ndbest15%,worst10%). Fully explains topics and their relation to their physical connection thus allowing retaining information to be easy. I am taking a 5 week thermal with him just because its him teaching it. Take him, thank me later.

I work full time and am an intern on campus. I recommend making it to the lectures, they help a lot as he covers similar questions to the homework problems. Homework is due weekly. The professor does post old versions of test to help you prepare for his tests. He also has great tutorial videos that you can watch anytime through his class page.

Luckily I'd previously taken this course in high school, because he explains things in a very confusing way. I found his lecture to be boring, scattered, and unorganized. HW is MasteringPhysics online which is 10 problems due weekly. DO THE BONUS HW. It'll give you up to 8 points to your entire grade. Tests are easier than HW.

The instructor was excellent, and the lectures were always engaging. They were readily available for questions, and I enjoyed the topics and learning the new simulation software in an open and positive classroom environment. I can tell Dr. Large cares about his students and truly enjoys teaching this class.

I wanted to understand the topics and do well, it just didn't happen. Not because of Dr. Large but because I've made some bad choices. I just never thought participation grade was going be the final nail in the coffin. I really appreciate Dr Large's teaching, he is really amazing, He is patient and care for his students. I hope to have him again.
I was pleasantly surprise with this class. I figured this would've been one of the most difficult classes I have taken yet I found the class to be very easily understood.

Dr. Large was prepared to teach every lecture. This and his organized notes made the class easy to follow as well as understand. He also made the topics of course more intriguing which encourage me to study the topics more in depth in my own.

This was a great class. Dr. Large really did a great job at explaining things in a way that made sense to me.
Exams are straightforward if you work on the practice problems and homework. Dr. Large was really engaging and it was the best course I took this semester. The grading policy is very fair and give flexibility for late homeworks.

recentReviews.comment: The tests with this teacher are often based entirely upon 1-2 questions and a failing grade can be reviewed if you do not get those 2/15 correct.

Classes often start late resulting in incomplete lectures and no time for practice problems. Mandatory group work for concepts never taught before. Homework assignments are posted late and she is impossible to contact outside of class time. The homework assignments often include questions that haven't been covered in the course. All around AWFUL.

Professor Mayer was very difficult to reach. Emails would go unread/unanswered for a week. When students asked questions in class, she was unable to answer or simply responded “we'll get to that later” without providing any context. Classes start late because of lack of preparation. This would lead to unfinished lectures. WOULD NOT TAKE AGAIN!

Very caring professor, but does not have the best teaching method in my opinion. I find I learn better with example problems over slide lectures and constantly found myself lost if I tried paying attention. She is very open to criticism though and does make an effort to make the class more interactive.

Professor Mayer is very smart and very kind, she definitely wants you to learn and ask questions! The subscripts she uses in the equations can get very intense so make sure you take good notes! Test are a awkward mix of being super hard but also super easy. Pairs you in groups for entire semester but it helps! Shes great!!

As some folks mentioned earlier that She Really Doesn't Help Students Succeed Much.She doesn't care your obstacles outside of school even you told her. If you get closer to C-, she will let you stick with an D and so on. Participation not mandatory but counted as grade percentage. She will not do nothing to let you go through.  Piece of advie: RUN.

Lectures in this class did not really adequately prepare me to tackle homework or exams. Most of the learning I did in this class was done on my own time using outside resources. She is a very kind and caring professor but I cannot recommend her for this class. She isn't a super tough grader and gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit though

While she may be a nice teacher who means well, you need to be prepared to teach yourself as well as being extra comfortable with Calculus. Homework was long and the graded quizzes attached to her lectures only allows one attempt. Resulting in you being punished if you don't quite grasp the concepts yet.

She is a good prof and assigns grades very fairly, but you will have to do most of the teaching yourself. Homework was excessively long, and lecture quizzes do nothing but hurt you since they are graded for correctness. An A is very attainable, but be prepared to take matters into your own hands.
Dr. Sooby is very sweet and caring. While her tests can be tough, she wants you to succeed and will help you along the way. Homeworks help a lot too and she does do some extra credit.
rhbfbnhdfgh

Professor is not a typical teacher and it can either make or break this course for you.  That being said the higher you go in academia , the more you have to teach yourself.  His lectures are all heavy with derivation but if you treat the textbook as a guide you'll do fine.  Great course and very enjoyable.

C-word legitimately just cannot teach. Maybe it's his accent, maybe it's how he simply throws math at you without guiding you through concepts, or maybe it's his use of a grad level textbook. Read the Taylor textbook instead of Goldstein and you'll be surprised that it's actually possible to learn this material when you have a good teacher.

God this class is hard, and Dr. Chabanov has super high expectations for the students in his class. He teaches it like a graduate level course, and its hard to adjust, read the book, use the internet as much as you can, and you will do well in the class. The class takes a ton of effort, but you will make it.

Just read the textbook, do the homework, and don't show up to class. When he asks a question in lecture no one answers because he gets mad if you get it wrong. The tests are pretty easy all things considered and he lets you use your own formula sheet. There was no comprehensive final for physics 2, just learn and forget; easy grade in general.

recentReviews.comment: I really enjoyed having Professor LCT Ball. I will definitely take his class again. I really enjoyed class discussions as well as humor. He does have a Midterm exam as well as a final exam. He does assign readings but not too difficult then it will be discussed in class.
A KING!!!! I learned so much in this class in such a short period if him teaching. I highly recommend he is an amazing mentor.
Cavazos is so sweet and caring. The course is super project-heavy, but if you have a decent group it's easy.

Professor Cavazos is an absolute angel. She is so helpful and you can tell she really cares about her students. She provides so much help if you ask for it, and is always willing to give feedback. Definitely take her for AIS if you can!!

Prof. Cavazos was one of the most caring people I've met at my first semester here at UTSA. Assignments vary per week, but very rarely took long at all. She took attendance everyday, but if you literally just show up you're fine and do the work before it's due you're golden in this class. She was overall, amazing!

Professor Cavazos is a very caring educator. This course is based on two projects, one being individual and one being a group project. She assigns 2-3 assignments each week, however they are relatively easy. She is a very easy grader. Attendance and attending peer mentor meetings is required.

In the class, you have to do an individual portfolio and group project throughout the semester. Attendance is for a grade, so definitely make sure you go, however, if you are late she doesn't take off credit for that. She genuinely cares and is easily reachable by various methods. I would totally say take her class if you can- she's great.
its ok, be prepared to write a lot
He very obviously valued what he taught, and wanted us to learn it. I think it's fine as a transition from high-school, but very jaring if you already have experience in college classes.

He isn't a bad guy and seems to mean well, but his overall style comes across as pretentious and overly critical at times. He's a tough grader and sort of nitpicky, but there is lots of extra credit. His lectures are alright, but since there's not much room for class participation you'll feel constantly reminded that you *have* to be there.
He was rude and snobby whenever you tried to talk to him, probably because he has a doctorate. He was also a hard grader and barely let you be one minute late to class.
Really good professor. Work was manageable and he is very passionate about teaching. The class was 50 minutes and he keeps you engaged. I can not say there were any cons.

He was an ok professor, his lectures are heavy and standby for a lot of homework. He will help you out if needed, but you would have to be the one reaching out for the help. All that being said, I did take his fast paced 1314 College Algebra class during the summer. On a good note he allows you to use your notes for your test and quizzes.
Became very rude at the end of the semester. And didn't appreciate it.
He's an okay professor. He's not bad, but not extraordinary either. Just go to class, do the easy busy work, and you're guaranteed to pass.

I had Candelario, I can firsthand say, that this guy isn't bad at all. Many people say his tone is a bit monotone, and while he is, it does not make this course hard or difficult in any way. He gives you everything you need to succeed, and grades fairly easily. Just make sure to turn in assignments on time, and you'll get an A.
Class was not difficult, especially at the beginning of the semester. While the information presented in the class is useful, it felt like a lot of busy work.

Lauren is genuinely such a sweet and caring instructor. I took this class at 8:30 AM and still found the content to be really enjoyable. Just show up to class and do the extremely easy assignments and this will probably be the easiest 100% of your life.

Lauren Riojas-Fitzpatrick taught several lectures that I will remember for the rest of my life. Completely unbiased opinion, this course is the only course that I feel provides any real insight on how you are supposed to attack life after college as an individual. Amazing professor and am excited for anyone that takes her class in the future.

Professor Lauren is truly great. Despite her being laid back, she tries her best to have an organized curriculum. Some of her assignments felt like busywork, but I loved her Goal project. It really set me up for success in my first year.

I loved having Lauren my first semester here at UTSA. You can tell she genuinely loves what she does and cares about her students. Her lectures were very informative, and she always made sure to keep them interesting. This class wasn't just a blow-off class; I was able to learn a lot for my academic career and personal life.

Lauren is a great professor and makes her lessons very relatable and also  very real. It's rare that professors can make lectures fun but she found a way to do it. She is very good at making students feel invited and welcomed. Not to mention, she is very funny!

What an awful course and professor. The structure of the entire course is very poor. The professor is actively trying to fail you so be in alert mode throughout the entire semester. If she sees an area of weakness, she will attack and bring you down. Very viscous. I'm very surprised the university is ok with the quality of this course.

She is a harsh grader and is not empathetic. She has an all or nothing grading criteria and is a very rude professor. If you make a tiny mistake, you get a zero. She shouldn't be teaching if she hates students. I accidentally didn't name my files exactly as she wanted on one hw and she gave me a 0 which made my grade go down from a 99 to a 79.

This class is a very easy A. You literally have to try to get anything below that. She has clear instructions, clear expectations and is not there to baby her students. This is a business class and you must have a business mindset. You are not going to be walked through life.

Absolutely horrible and rude professor that clearly does not want to do her job.
All of her "lessons" are low effort slides and she never actually gives ANY context on assignments. If you so much as get ONE instruction wrong (which she never tells you WHAT to do) you get a zero, not even a partial grade for the work you did.

The assignments themselves weren't too difficult. She is very strict about following her guidelines, so you just have to be attentive to what she expects from you (which isn't even clear most of the time). She doesn't give much feedback so it's kind of hard to know what you're doing wrong and what you're doing right.

This class was pretty simple. There were weekly in-class assignments that could be completed before the end of class. The only major assignment was the Career Readiness Portfolio which we had around three months to complete. If you start the project early, you should have no problem getting an A+ in the class.

AMAZING PLEASE TAKE HER IF YOU CAN!!! you can submit anything and get a 100% but the only tough assignments is the semester long project, which is mainly community service projects and you have to present it.

Only really major module in this course is the semester-long project but even that is pretty issue. You could probably knock it out within a month if you wanted. Besides that, her class helps you discover every resource that UTSA offers and how to use them.

Very minimal assignments (one a week, maybe an hour max) and an easy final project you can work on the entire semester. Quite a bit of groupwork but nothing that is for a major grade, just in class participation. Very easy to talk to and understanding, will give extensions if you give her a good reason. Nice to have a conversation with in general!

She is very easy and the class is all about what UTSA has to offer to their students. All of the assignments and discussions are extremely easy. Final project is about activities geared towards career readiness and she gives you the entire semester to complete. Don't hesitate to take her if she is open. You will not regret it!
Super sweet lady, class is fun and easy. There is a semester-long class project you do which isn't too bad, and there is a lot of group work

Dr. Laborde is one of the most caring professors there is. You are put into 2 groups throughout the semester which you work in. Attendance is mandatory, but it's just submitting an assignment as a group during class and then another one at the end of the week-totally doable. Main focus is big project you work towards throughout the entire sem.

Laborde was an absolutely lovely mom teacher to have this semester. I made a lot of great friends in her class and the whole semester revolves around one actual project, so curriculum is pretty easy. I highly recommend taking AIS with Laborde.
She is so cool.

This class is great!! 9.6/10. I would recommend this class to anyone looking for an AIS class. She does a great job at getting the class connected. This was one of my favorite classes at UTSA. Attendance was a bit strict but it's mainly easy group work. One end of the year project very simple.

Camargo is very unclear with her grading and takes forever to grade the assignments. I constantly found her making small mistakes while teaching us, if it be with the equations or the text material, which made it very hard to learn the material. If you care about your GPA, I definitely wouldn't recommend taking this class.

Takes more than 2 weeks to turn in grades, which is against UTSA's rules. Took half a semester to start grading papers (and that was only because students went to the department chair). Is not clear on what is expected of us in our lab reports. Goes through pre-lecture notes too fast, so hopefully you have notes from Biomechanics lecture.
Awesome professor. Please take him. He's very responsive, easy grader.

He is a really nice and understanding professor. The class itself sucks, but if you have to take it with anyone take it with him. He made it as engaging and interesting as possible and the group project we had were really enjoyable. Attend Class!!

I took this class in a hybrid format. On the days we met on campus, he presented slideshows that were relevant to the online assignments. The class is super easy, and there were only two projects, one service project and one group project. He was easy to reach and gave great feedback. Attendance is mandatory.
He was very sweet and passionate! His instructions were always very clear and he is very understanding about deadlines.

He's a really understanding, and kind professor. He just wants you to succeed! Usually 1-2 assignments a week, and then there is a semester long group project. Super interesting and informative. I genuinely enjoyed learning about the topics each week since they are extremely relevant to today's world. You NEED to participate in class.

Dr. Taylor is very understanding she gives extensions on homework, she is an easy grader and be prepared to give 2 speeches on projects which are not difficult and she is very nice and accessible outside class.

recentReviews.comment: I had an extremely easy beginner data science course with professor Schroeder, the homework was occasional and easy to complete. Just keep up with your assignments, a very accommodating and kind professor.
She was super kind and communicated well. Her assignments were clear and it was a good class overall. Take her!
easy class and great professor. one group project for the whole semester and she's super understanding.

She was very kind and understanding! I took her for AIS and we had a group project that lasted the whole semester, but it is very easy and you get to make it about whatever your career interests are! Overall, she was an amazing teacher and very sweet!

she is so nice and a super easy prof for ais, we only meet once a week and shes so understanding if you have any problems. there are sm extra cred opportunities, but there is a group project that you actually have to do some work for (volunteering, tabling, presentation) but overall its pretty easy. only hw is online modules that are easy
AIS is a pretty stupid course, but the work is easy. Dr. S is very nice and accommodating if you have any trouble.

AIS is a very boring but easy class. She does weekly modules with one or two assignments to do and you can get them all done within a day. Worst thing was probably the signature experience n rowdy service project which are semester long but that's just bc theyre long n also boring. Easy class to get that first year credit

Dr. Schroeder was an amazing professor. AIS is the most boring class and a worthless class but she manages to make it fun and engaging by doing scavenger hunts, group projects, etc. Really recommend her for AIS.
This class is basically a semester-long project. If you can pull your weight, you will pass with flying colors. She is very prepared and knows how to help. Great person overall!

I love how Professor Dones always tried to bring the class together. She encourged us to talk to each other in class and meet with our groups and that is needed now more than ever. This class is all about participation. She made everything very clear and simple, and it's practically impossible to fail unless you don't show up or talk to anyone.
As long as you know what's going on in the class, and willing to participate you will get a good grade.
There is one group project and you kinda work on it through the semester. But its one of those classes that if you show up you know whats going on but if you don't thats on you.
Shes very specific on how she wants certain things answered other then that shes pretty chill and understanding

Love this professor, not only is she SUPER understanding but she's also very passionate about what she does. Even though it was an intro to college class I learned so much and also received great feedback! She also leaves the sweetest submission comments.

Dr. Vikesland is so sweet and seems genuinely interested in everyones education and lives. She always left private comments on each assignment responding to what we did. She was always very encouraging, supportive, and engaged.

Attendance is strictly enforced. I missed two classes due to illness and my grade dropped six points with no chance to make up the work. She is very stingy with grades. On my final presentation, all feedback was negative, which felt discouraging since I struggle with public speaking anxiety. Overall she was pretty passive aggressive.

First of all attendance is MANDATORY if you do not go she will make up random assignments that she will never till you about and you will get a 0 for them. She is some what laid back but she will be towering over watching what you do and criticize and nitpick at anything and everything you do if its not done in her way.

Aside from some weeks being repetitive, such as interviews with peers for around 3 classes straight, Dr. Vikesland is a good professor and helpful with assignments. The class itself is very easy, as long as you show up for attendance. Group work didn't really occur until the last four weeks of class, but the project is doable.

Such a unique and amazing course to take with her and to experience. She is a planner, and knows exactly what she wants and HOW she wants it. The final project she said we would have creative freedom but it reality she didn't facilitate that because her rules were so so specific. Loves student participation and for you to speak up in discussions.

Professor was a kind person just a little harsh on grading. Class honestly wasn't THAT hard just a lot of work. Took a lot of time doing my AIS work than other classes. Really specific on what she wants for assignments. A lot of group work but was overall not too hard of a class

Professor Engates is a very nice and professional woman. Attendance is graded, and I believe that is so because your presence or lack thereof can affect other people's grades too. Half of the course is building up to a final group project that is presented at the end of the class. She is a very stingy grader, losing marks if you dont dot every i.

The teacher is from a military family, so she is tough on details and deadlines. Instructions for homework are expected to be done exactly and instructed, but instructions are very thorough. First half of the semester is networking and talking with people in class. Second half is a project for your final. Lots of group work, attendance is 100% need

She is not a terrible professor but she makes the class a lot more tedious than it has to be. She yaps the whole class which leaves very little time to finish the busywork she assigns. Also her attendance policy is strict and if you miss too much you're capped at a C. Too much for a freshman year course

This class is basically one big group project but a doable one. A lot of work! That being said, I appreciate that Professor Rubal was clear with what she wanted from the very start. As long as you don't stray far from that you should be good.
She just takes this class a little too seriously and makes it take up more time than it should.
Honestly I wish the class wasn't mandatory so that was probably my biggest issue this semester but she did an oaky job at leading it. You'll have to take initiative in this class but she was okay.

An unnecessary amount of busy work for a basic university class. Grades every little thing and comments about it, allowing you to make corrections. However, she takes a significant % off each day you don't resubmit. Don't know if all the other professors are like this, but definitely recommend finding a better one.

They type way too much for little assignments, doesn't look twice at assignments when grading, and even with all the words they type they still fail to effectively explain assignments. This class is comparable to a high school English class atmosphere, there's way to many words and now enough basics.

recentReviews.comment: She is the sweetest professor ever! She makes sure you are understanding what is going on and actually cares about her students. The class was very easy and the final group project was also not bad at all. I would most definitely recommend taking her for this course.

Professor O'Brien is a great professor to take for AIS. She keeps the class easy and doesn't require much work. There is a paper due every Sunday, but it is so easy, and she is an easy grader. There is a group project at the end of the year, which is actually interesting. Highly recommend her!

Hands down best teacher I've had. I actually was bummed this class was only once a week. She's a fun interactive teacher and really got involved with the class instead of just lecturing us. Her project was also really fun. 10/10
great class to take your first semester of college this professor is great and easy I would take her in person if you can but online is great too,

AIS is one of those dumb classes the University forces you to take, and I imagine how boring it must be for other classes. Thankfully Professor O'Brien is super caring, super understanding and does her best to make the class an enjoyable experience.

Zybooks course but I love them even though it's a lot of reading. Zybooks has so much coding practice and detailed explanations which is great. You can keep working in zybooks by accessing it online, can bypass waiting for it to be released on Canvas to get ahead. He was responsive to emails very quick. I liked this class a lot.

Professor Bergeler wasn't my favorite. The class had potential, but the material felt outdated, and the projects weren't engaging. There wasn't much useful content, and I didn't feel motivated to attend. Could be a better experience with some updates and more effort to inspire students.
A bit of homework but not suffocating. They will let you redo homework as much as you want and is very understanding. Communicate and you will pass.

She changed our schedule in the syllabus and forgot that she did that months ago so she still taught the wrong unit. She also was a poor communicator over email. I would email her about an issue and she would just respond with confusion. I would try to clear it up for her but she wasn't getting it and wouldn't response anymore after that.

Toward the end of the semester, she stopped caring about the Canvas page and our assignments because she had messed up the due dates and submission settings. So, instead of fixing it, she just gave up and gave us the credit. What a mess.
Took her for intro before and thought it would be different this time around but no. She still can't get it together. Still had to remind her time and time again to open assignments on Canvas.

I always had to email her and keep reminding her to unlock assignments and extra credits because she would always forget almost every week. She would make the excuse that she is a very forgetful person and wouldn't change her habits. It got old and exhausting. Honestly, don't take this class cause you are just going to end up doing her job for her.

I had a death in my family and had been sick but she wouldn't excuse late assignments whatsoever and would barely excuse any days that I missed class. She's pretty strict about everything so she's not my favorite and can be snarky when you try to email her.

This is not class related but it's something else. I rather say she has come off guard whenever she repeats the question when I'm trying to answer during the interview. However, I'm very neurodivergent and that is my concern. Yet, Elizabeth Pople comes off rude with her rolling eyes at me. I wish things were getting better but NOT with her.

very bad teaching ethics! she doesn't respect her students in the slightest and is very unclear when it comes to explaining new material. calls out students to single them out when she feels like they are confused or behind, just to not help explain but get the class to teach! just very disrespectful and discouraging all around.

recentReviews.comment: Meritz is a tough grader who rarely explains point deductions. Feedback is vague or missing even when scores drop below the top category. Extra credit is required for anything above 90, where the top 25% of the class is tightly packed. Grading feels arbitrary. Easy to get a B+, nearly impossible A. You basically have to teach yourself.

For the kind of person who has trouble caring to do the work, or setting aside the time to do it, this is who you are looking for. Prof. Meritz motivated me to write as best I could, do better than the last time, and made me want to be in that class.

Prof. Meritz was an alright professor. It's good if you just want to get this credit out of the way. If you want to actually improve your writing I wouldn't take him. His feedback wasn't great; and generally took weeks to grade assignments. He was a good guy and loves his job; just wasn't that great at lecturing; usually reading off slides.

He's a nice guy and always willing to help, but not the best for if you want to really improve your writing. It takes a while to get feedback on assignments, so it's hard to know what to work on for the next essay. Not too difficult, but attendance is pretty important for your grade.

Didn't give good feedback at all for the essays we wrote. Also wasn't helpful throughout the writing process and would mark things or critique them after previously saying they were good in a draft (even if you didn't change it at all in the final version). Kind of frustrating, he's a good guy and clearly likes his job, but bad feedback.

recentReviews.comment: She's a kind and respectful teacher who cares about her students. There are several essays, but she lets you redo them if needed. She communicates well, and the workload is manageable if you stay on top of assignments. Overall, she's supportive and wants her students to succeed.

She was an amazing professor! Only about 7 major assignments, but she tends to grade very tough and will take points off for small details. There is only a few minor assignments but they're mainly for participation points.

This professor is good. For the first few assignments you will receive low grades but don't worry she is not as tough as you will think. She gives you many attempts to redo essays to get a better grade and will provide tons of feedback. Email her or ask her to revise, before submission, your essay and you'll get a good grade. Don't fright too much.
Super tough grader, but it helps you become a very successful writer!

her class was tough plus she's a tough grader. i don't recommend taking her class if you have more than 4 classes. she gives out alot of essays to do. My big thing with her is that shes never satisfied with any essay. plus she always goes off topic on the zoom calls

This class was okay, I appreciated the writing that we did and the feedback that she would give, but at times I felt like the class was too much on me. She is a hard grader but allows you to turn it in again when your essay has been adjusted with her suggestions. Attendance matters, there is a small group presentation but it's easy.
She cared about your development as a writer and will give you plenty of opportunities to raise your grade. Your grade is dependent on the work you are willing to put in.

Very good professor; she knows her students, she gives good and clear feedback and wants you to succeed. While I wouldn't say attendance is 100% mandatory, I don't think you'd have an easy time if you didn't attend class.

Taking a course with Dr. Shaw-Tillmon is one of the single best decisions you can make if you care about your writing skills. You will thank her for the rest of your life, truly one of the greatest professors I've had.

Great professor and extremely caring. Gives unlimited revisions on every assignment, so you can learn from your mistakes. recentReviews.comment: DO NOT take this class if you dislike writing, don't want confusing, overly wordy assignment instructions and titles in Canvas, disorganized Canvas set up, nit picky grading for a freshman writing class that you aren't even majoring in, or having assignments due barely an hour after class when you have other obligations immediately after class

This is by far the worst class i have taken all year. At one point she told me I did an assignment incorrectly as well as other students because she failed to explain the assignment correctly. She assigns so many thing throughout the week and overall the class feels very overwhelming, I would never take this class again.

Professor Mahan is an amazing professor. There are 3 major papers to write. She isn't a tough grader but she can take a little while to grade especially when it comes to rough drafts which she grades the day or night the paper is due so it doesn't help. There are plenty of extra credit opportunities and the class overall has a great vibe.

She is absolutely amazing! Very caring of her students and their success. She talks a lot in class but most of it is irrelevant. There are usually three papers and she is very specific about it so just review the formats she sends out, those tend to be EXTREMELY helpful.

Professor Mahan is probably very sweet personally but when it comes to the education of her student she falls severely short. She takes forever to grade to the point that rough drafts are not given back in an appropriate amount of time so much so that it effects the grade that you could get on the final draft due to lack of time to edit.

Would not recommend this professor for USC-2011. He is a very strict grader, and is one of those professors who does not give As. For a 1 credit course, you are doing the work of a 3 credit course. Good luck.

I took Professor Sano's course back in 2024, and here I am 2 years later getting on here to give him the praise he deserves. He is the kindest professor I ever had throughout my 5 years of university. He was very good at explaining the content while making sure you left with all your questions answered. TAKE HIS CLASS IF YOU CAN!

Professor Sano was great! The only homework we had was a journal and a paper (5 each) due about every other week or every 2 weeks, as well as a digital storytelling project for the final. This class was the easiest and the lightest with the course work. If you need a filler or just need the class, take him for UCS2011. :)

Great Professor! Has a respect for higher education and values a quality learning experience. Inspires you to work hard for the grade. Took in the summer and was very accessible outside of class. Reading before class is mandatory and necessary to pass. Be prepared to discuss and write research paper. Be engaged during class time, it helps!

I have taken two classes with Professor Sano and he is absolutely amazing. He is a great Professor. He is very knowledgeable and he is really nice and approachable. His lectures are very insightful and you actually feel like you are learning in his class. You will have to read and you do have to show up to class every day.

Not too bad, but prof. didn't follow his own syllabus and sadly struggled a bit on an online class and tended to fall behind :/ Instructions aren't always clear. Long lectures. Mandatory attendance. Helps your professional development. Good advice and ideas. Get opportunity to research major pathways a lot more. But wouldn't recommend online.
It won't let me say what needs to be said.

For the love of good sweet god, do not take WRC1013 with Professor Cruz... Only low grade I ever had my freshman year, not only does she grade tough, but she grades vague. Once you realize you got a low grade, have fun trying to decipher why. She certainly won't tell you. Oh, and never let her know her score on here or she crashes out. I was there.

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR.She is so disrespectful and unfortunately very self centered. She will constantly brag about how amazing she is as a teacher and how she's the best professor you'll ever have. She takes ages to grade. I can guarantee you won't have your papers graded till finals time. Because of this professor I loathe writing

Professor Cruz is a sweet person! But her teaching style is not easy. She's an extremely hard grader. Not only did she teach me so many new things, but, she helped me love writing again. If you meet with her 1:1 you will understand her personality better and see just how great of a professor she truly is. It isn't an easy class but if you put in the work, don't slack off, read the rubric, and genuinely put in effort, you'll do great.

Honestly the best professor of a class I have had so far in UTSA. Exceptional, not strict, and your best friend when It comes to being helpful.

Literally the GOAT. I love his class so much, because you can just tell how much he cares about each of his students. You can also tell how passionate he is about writing and English as a whole. Four papers, and weekly informal writing prompts. I would take him for WRC 1013, AND WRC 1023.  I absolutely recommend him. He cares so very much.

really nice guy! tries to make the best of classes by finding ways to connect and relate to students ! no homework only had one quiz, grades are on papers and warm up like writting (easy a)  . This teacher wants you to pass

recentReviews.comment: Professor Miller was very kind and understanding. Attendance was a part of your grade but overall the class was well structured and easy to follow! Definitely recommend!

Highly recommend Professor Miller! She gives great feedback, responds quickly, and is super understanding. Workload is manageable, just attend all lectures, participate, and follow her slides closely. Show effort and you'll do great!

Professor miller is always accessible outside of class, encourages students to ask for assistance, and genuinely cares for her students. Although your schedule might revolve around this one class, she can give you an extension without penalty to get you caught up. Great teacher & great class!
Really excellent professor. She is a tough grader, but she provides clear feedback on papers. She is really sweet and caring, so I highly recommend this professor.

Attendance is taken for a grade but class is unbearable because she's so unorganized. She would spend almost all of class switching between tabs because she doesn't know how to operate technology. She also never graded any of the essays until the end of the semester which is annoying because she would just keep assigning more. She's nice though.
She grades papers once in a while, she expects you to already know a lot of things, shes very hard to impress, tough grader as well, you can do better so def take another one lol

Ms. Karen is a nice professor who gives good feedback on your paper. Go to office hours for guidance and better direction towards papers. There are 3 main essays in which she gives 2 weeks to complete which is plenty of time for a paper. She responds to emails quickly and drafts are graded by competition and on time submission.
She disagreed with a topic I put in a paper, gave me a failing grade, and would not let me back into class. Very unprofessional. Do not take her.

Honestly, this class isn't hard. if you do your work and spend some time on it you should get an A. The bad ratings are just your average student who doesn't care about their studies and just shows up and expects an A.

I would 100% recommend Professor Smith for WRC1013. Before this class I didn't know any proper MLA or APA citing rules, but Professor Smith did a great job teaching it all. There are a few assignments each week as well as a few essays, all of which are simple and easy. As long as you can write well and follow instructions, her class is an easy A.

Professor Smith was honestly a ton of help. It wasn't hard to pass her class at all. She is always answering emails and is willing to meet with you over zoom or in person at reasonable times. you have about 4 or 5 essays but they're pretty straight forward. attendance is mandatory but you have a couple absences before it affects your grade.

Professor Smith is so kind and genuinely cares about her students. She gives so many opportunities for getting assignments turned in and different ways we can get help if we need it. She's very open to meeting outside of class for help and gives great feedback. The book we read is interesting and there is weekly blog posts. Attendance is graded.

Professor Smith is amazing! very hard to not pass if you do what you're supposed to as a student. You have weekly chapter readings, but the book is very worth reading. You also have weekly blog posts which are super easy and she is very open to what she lets you write about. She truly wants what's best for her students in and outside the classroom.

She's super nice! However her grading on essays seems a way too harsh(meeting all expectations is a C). Her instructions aren't very clear, which is why I would advise you to ask her questions whenever you can. Attendance is mandatory but she is lenient at times.

Professor Williams is nice, just show up to class and participate. She likes things pretty particular when she's grading but, the expectations are voiced many times so its hard to miss. Turn in your work on time and do your best, and you will get an A.
There are better professors. Don't make the same mistake I did.

Before taking her class I definitely thought she was going to be a professor from hell based on the other reviews but she wasn't. I will say she is extremely passive-aggressive. Other than that as long as you follow the rubric this class is easy.

She is a good professor and provides instructions fairly well, so you can ask questions if you aren't sure about the guidelines. It is very hard to understand her lectures, and she will give you a big essay due within a few days and no explanation on how to write it. I found it very difficult to do well in her class.

As someone who loves everything English I did not enjoy this class. I thought she was very boring and I would often find myself zoning off as she spoke. She is a very strict grader when it comes to essays and projects.

Very understanding regarding extensions and explains the grading criteria well. Only complaint about the course would be that the major grades are all put close together within the second half of the term but otherwise would 100% take again, easy A
i would reccomend getting another prof but shes the one to chose if you have no choice

Professor mainly focuses on grammatical errors more than anything else. Has no connection with her students whatsoever and her instructions always seemed to be unclear and vague. Honestly, she only grades like half of the things she puts online. Decent prof but a hard grader on grammar. I swear she doesn't even read the essay, she just past attention to the grammar.
Slow talker. Bables on. Does not explain well. She grades easy though.

She has an accent and speaks slowly so her classes are really easy to zone out in. Doesn't even talk about essays for more than a day but expects them done so pay attention to the syllabus. I'm sure Maike is a sweet woman, but her class was a drag to go to... she lectures the majority of the time and speaks slow and has a monotone voice. the work load is not heavy at all though. if you're willing to take time to write the essays and sit through class once and a while, i'm sure you could get an A.

She grades really harshly, where the mean falls around 15 out of 25, and gives homework constantly. Do not take her if you are later in your college career cause it is insufferable.
