Can take a while to grade, but it isn't that big of an issue. Also forgiving when it comes to late or incorrectly submitted work.

She responds fast to emails and is very kind and understanding. Overall, her class was very easy and not too much work; however, her Canvas is confusing, and she sometimes gets the dates mixed up. She gives lots of easy assignments that help boost your grade.
She was very sweet and was always willing to help and give feedback, but sometimes would not be clear on instructions.

Loved this professor; they have very creative assignments. She does use AI a ton for her class, which can be a double-edged sword. Very caring for her students, and the class was very centered around conversation.
The grading feels harsh. If you care about your GPA don't take this professor. You would most likely not get an A.

Relies on videos to explain what he wants and does not want for essays. His explanations are very broad and not detailed enough, especially since he grades very harshly and takes off points for every minor mistake. I recommend taking someone else or at Alamo colleges if you can.

Prof. Longoria refused to honor my documented accessibility needs until university administration stepped in to enforce my medical waivers. Good professor that is very understanding and helpful. If the class for the week was going over an assignment that you already did, you could leave early. Prof. Piña is super nice and understanding! She is very good at explaining things so I could understand them. She is very good at reminding you of due assignments. Amazing writing prof. Her topics are fun and easy! She isn't a tough grader at all just get your papers done on time and this class will be an easy A. Also for the group project, make sure to communicate with your group members!
Overall she was good. She definitely picks favorites so just be on her good side and show up to class.

AMAZING CLASS! she's super chill and very easy to talk to, she cares a lot about her students. She does grade papers a little hard, but as long as you listen to her feedback you'll do better. She's an amazing professor who loves her job, and loves a talkative classroom.

Newcomb was great professor she was kind, funny, & kept it real (in a good way)! Professor Newcomb has been the best professor I've gotten so far. She very nice and cares for each and every student she has. I would not have taken a different professor and cannot recommend her enough to anyone else taking this class.

Avoid Christina at all costs. Even if you follow Christina's rubric to a T, she will find an arbitrary reason to lower your grade. PICK A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR. It's really a shame that I have to give her a low score because she truly is so nice. Very tough grader that floods you with work and assignments. I'm coming back to this post to address how sloppy of a grader and professor she is. Debra Pena is a great professor who genuinely cares about her students. She offers extra credit for attendance, essay revisions, and more. Honestly when I say take her, TAKE HER. She's so sweet and caring, she even helped me with my speeding ticket and court issues. I love her. I absolutely adore this professor so much

Prof. Pena is a nice professor when you dont have to interact with her that much. When asking for help she tends to come off with a snarky attitude, which could make you feel belittled in a way. Professor Long was fair. Be sure to support your claims with cited details from credible sources. If you use genai,  be sure to tell it not to revise your papers. I could have gotten a better grade but I was graduating, and all I needed was a C. It was a fun class, if you still need to take Comp II.

Good discussions and the timing of assignments is manageable. She gives feedback on drafts and helps you learn to revise multiple drafts so you can do your best work. You get time to write in class and you make friends during group work. Just stay up n homework and you'll do fine.
Interesting class because she makes sure the assignments are relevant to your life and goals. The assignments are challenging but not too challenging. She gives you support and plenty of feedback.
If you would like to actually learn good skills this is the professor you need to take. She cares about her students and will help you if asked.

Professor Abdo is amazing!! She cares about you a lot and tries to help and teach you as much as possible. Professor Abdo is a very knowledgeable professor who stays up to date on current events. The grading is abstract. She holds you to outdated standards bc shes a stubborn older prof.

She has been by far one of my favorite professors. It is easy to tell that she cares about her students on a personal level. She has entertaining lectures and gives helpful feedback. I would recommend her out of all the writing comp professors.

Best Professor I've had at UTSA so far! Super down to Earth and doesn't treat her students like normal college kids, she genuinely cares about you and your well-being. Overall, Ms. Morley is a good professor who genuinely cares about her students. She doesn't try to make things difficult, and really gives good feedback. This is an easy course to pass if you put in the effort and turn in assignments. If you want to improve your writing and need credit in writing and composition, take this course.

If you asked Professor Morley for help formatting an essay, she would make you figure it out yourself and not lend any help, other than to direct a student's questions to anyone but herself. My emails were never answered & her morley meetups are pointless. Would NOT take again!!

Take another professor. Wants you to go to his office hours but has very limited appointments. I told him my midterm was in conflict with his class and told me if I even wanted to still be there. If you haven't basically written a book before good luck. Was a waste of my time and money.

Please take another professor! Wants you to go to his office hours, but only has very limited spots. He graded super hard & doesn't know how to give feedback w out being rude or making you feel stupid. I'd attend his office hours and writing center and still he'd find something wrong , and towards the end of the course he just didn't respond to canvas messages

If I could write more than 350 words.. I would. Professor Helton is an interesting character, he's quirky but not in a fun way. recentReviews.comment: This class is not easy.  There are assignments throughout the semester that are due and there is also a group project due that you must work together on.  If you stay on top of the assignments you should be good.  Professor Romero always answered any questions via email outside of class and is an easy grader if you put effort into your work.

I took Dr.Romero for assessments and internship 1. All I can say is she is there for her students, she listens to what her students are saying and she is very accessible out side of class she will make time for you. I would absolutely take her again. She has made internship a pleasant experience.I'm not sure about the negative reviews.

Dull pre-recorded lectures, in-class time feels pointless. When questioned, offers more information instead of clarification. Group project based on 80+ hour tv soap opera. Book is a slog but good reference text. Avoid.

Online classes has been tough for me during the pandemic, and Dr. Romero was not very good at it. It didn't feel like a "true" lecture. When I would ask her to demonstrate a math equation for a test, she didn't feel comfortable showing it online and I'm a visual student it just made the class tougher. Stay away.

I have taken Dr. Somody for a few classes for my clinical mental health degree.  There is a quiz every week and each week we would meet to practice for our recording that we would have to do throughout the semester with our groups and then do a reflection paper. You also meet in a group from 7:30-8:30 each week as well.  Attendance is taken.

She was a welcoming professor and the class was easy. You did meet in groups each week to practice material, and had some assessments on that. There is a textbook but she provides the pdf. You did not learn much in lecture together, as the book material was learned on your own and the lecture time was spent mostly in groups.
I really enjoyed her Introductory class. Very kind Professor, was very helpful and understanding when I was ill. Assignments were not difficult, exams weren't too bad.

The previous reviews are way off target about Dr. Somody in my experience. My class and I LOVE her. She has never had a negative comment leave her mouth during our meetings. She gives you all the material needed to do the tests (which are online and easy). On top of that, shes extremely caring and kind. I really hope I am able to take her again.
Do not take this professor if you can avoid it. She is terrible and potentially dangerous.
Such an awesome and knowledgeable professor. I would definitely recommend him! Its an easy class if you put in the effort, he gives excellent feedback!

He knows a lot about the subject and has a lot to give. He is cocky though and if he is in a bad mood he is incredibly rude to his students. He uses humor at the student's expense during his negative moods. He also tells so many personal stories that important information is left out that students have to learn on their own.

Great professor! Would def take again.

I love Dr. Juhnke! He is positive and brings life to his lectures. I would take his class a million times over! He very knowledgeable and his explanations are clear. One of my all time favorite professors! He is knowledgeable, experienced, passionate, & great story teller! He is clearly passionate about counseling and training new counselors. AND he personally called EACH student at the beginning & towards the end of the semester to introduce himself and see if we had any questions. He instantly won my respect!

If you didn't know he is a MAC (Master's Addiction Counselor). He used to work at state jails and hospitals and has a FULL understanding of what he is talking about. He used to be a hostage negotiator as well. These are stories that you can't get from anywhere else. If you want a wonderful and helpful experience go with Dr. J the exp is 10/10

I took Dr. Juhnke for Career class here at UTSA. He has so much knowledge of counseling and what to do with it once we graduate. Many of my classmates hadn't thought of what would happen once we graduate. Where do we find jobs? Dr. J knew. How do we negotiate for jobs? Dr. J knew. Never was there an unanswered question, bcs he knew just what to say

Dr. Juhnke is one in a million professors. He is super knowledgeable and you won't find a better in class experience. From funny videos he produces to the stories of past experiences there he is always cooking up something new and exciting. If you have to pick between him and another professor 100% go with Dr J. You won't be disappointed! I wasn't!

Dr. Sullivan is perhaps one of the most helpful, organized, approachable, and straightforward professors I met in the School Psychology program. Course expectations are always clear.
The most organized teacher I've ever had. Follow his grading guidelines and rubrics and you'll do great! I wish he taught ever single course. Definitely recommend this teacher. 5 stars!

Dr. Guerra is a fantastic, caring prof who genuinely loves teaching. She will work with you, respond to emails quickly, and do everything to ensure your success, assuming you put the effort in. Dr. Guerra is a sweetheart. You know from the moment you meet her, that she cares about her students, but the downfall about this class is that I walk out not learning anything. Assigned seats, starts early, doesn't ends on time. Doesn't get through all the content in one class.  She is not clear on the content that she's teaching; jumps from topic to topic. PROS: She's a nice woman who obviously cares about her students & how well they are doing in her class CONS: She's boring, her slides are boring, the class is boring. Dr. Carmona-Dominguez  was a caring professional who took the time to clarify assignments when asked.  She takes her craft and subject matter seriously, so be prepared to respond in kind.  Lots of work and outside reading, but I learned a lot as a result.  I respect her professionalism and in depth knowledge & would take another course with her.

She was incredibly unclear all semester. Syllabus had to be altered (in class) several times, and she was never specific about what she decided, until it was too late. Horrible at communicating. Didn't grade anything until the end of the semester. Literally the last day of class, we got grades. Ridiculous.

She is a terrible professor! Everything we did in class was completely pointless. She never went over the syllabus or assignments and always left us  confused each class! It is clear she has never taught this course before.

Dr. Proffitt was awesome! I took her Fall 2021 and I remember the assignments being fairly easy. We used google classroom for our assignments, don't know if she uses it. There were no weekly meetings, just the journals. She gets back to you as soon as she can and communicates properly, and very helpful. I definitely recommend her!

This professor puts in a lot of work into her lessons and makes this class so easy to navigate. However, she does indeed expect you to put in the same amount of work as she does so be prepared for that! Overall her lessons were so interesting and you learned something new everyday! Such a relatable professor I recommend taking!

Great professor! She uses the course to help develop our understanding of the world around us, and how our teaching can be influenced and shaped around what is happening within our society. There are a couple group projects that aren't too tough. The class does involve participation and being able to talk about our thoughts and opinions.

Took this course over the summer and overall he is a great professor, he is quite approachable and was always willing to answer students question and easy to reach with the whole online dynamic in current times. He would clear up any confusion on assignments and concepts that the class was unsure of, and is overall just a great character.

Well organized and understanding. The course has a solid workload, but he does everything he can to help you succeed, especially if you reach out. I appreciated his professional interaction in and out of class and lack of ambiguity on all assignments. In short - he cares.

Dr Yuen is very helpful and nice. I had a hard time in his class but just because CS was not my best subject. If you have the chance to take him, do so! He gives extra credit and revisions for tests, which is very generous.
Dr Yuen is an excellent profesor. He teaches topics step by step, very caring.

He was an excellent professor. His lectures were very helpful and he went over the topics in detail. There are only two tests, three projects, and the textbook is mandatory. Extra credit is given, and revisions are optional. Would recommend for beginner computer science.

She was a very difficult professor. Her grading was harsh and often unclear. She was also rude in her communication and did not allow students to use the restroom during class, which was unreasonable.

This professor grades based on opinion. She has her favorites in the class. She doesn't upload grades on canvas, so you don't know what your grade is. She hates cell phones! She has you turn in homework by email.

If you have your phone out she will be rude. She doesn't use canvas at all so good luck with knowing your grade. She was unclear with assignments, it feels like she grades based on opinion. Will last minute assign readings. She has favorites and if you aren't one can come off very condescending. She hates all technology being out even note taking.

This professor grades based on opinion. She definitely has her favorites in the class. Don't take your self phones out or she will call on you. Don't be late to class! Doesn't use canvas to uploads grades. All assignments are hand turned into her and given back later. She does call on you to participate, read texts, or help her with stuff.

This professor definitely has favorites within the class. Unclear grading criteria. syllabus changes every now & then according to how she's feeling that week. Sweet most of the time, but she ultimately has to benefit in some way. Tends to drone on about concepts unrelated to the lecture. Most of the year, everyone is lost & has no idea what to do

She is kind of confusing, but she was not a "hard" professor. Lesson plans for tutoring due every week, which are like 3 pgs long and are only worth 4  points. Follow the rubrics and examples word for word and you will get great grades. If you do well she will give you more points than possible (ex: 12/10). Attendance matters and do not leave early

LOVE LOVE LOVE Dr. Boon. He is the most understanding professor I've ever had. He works with you on anything you need and helps to explain things clearly. He understands that people have work, family and school and tries to make things work around life. Can't say enough good things about Dr. Boon.

LOVED Professor Boon. There was an assignment/quiz/discussion due every Sunday and a good amount of reading, but as long as you did it and put in work its an easy A. Professor Boon replies and answers all questions quickly and kindly. loved this class for summer 1 online!

Great teach that actually cares about students. Yes you have to read the book and take quizzes and do discussion, yet all the work is laid out in the book. He responds quick to any questions you have. Very go with the flow kinda teacher.

He is very passionate and loves what he's doing. He is ready to work with you andf very understanding. He talks a lot, but I love listening to his stories. He is a very interesting individual and makes things fun. He has been my favorite professor.

Very woke and arrogant.  For reviews that say he is caring, I witnessed none of that.  
He should retire, he's outdated.

ARC2156 - Sophomore studio. He pushes every student passed their limits and helps you grow as a designer. Lectures are lengthy, and he will go on philosophical rants. You will be expected to spend quite a bit of money, but don't be afraid to challenge him or talk to him about your concerns. Genuinely a person who sparks imagination.

Say what you want about Marky, that man cares a lot about his students and is absolutely passionate about each and every one of them . He was the only professor who really gives an opportunity for students to redeem themselves and I am really greatful that he believes in me because I honestly would have dropped out if it wasn't for him.

Mark Blizard. Where do I start? Disclaimer: first and for most my opinion is my own and my own alone and experiences and preferences are subjective. Mark Blizard is not a an accommodative Professor. He will make it very hard for you to meet on one on one or have an office hour with you especially this COVID happened. He tries so hard to be cool.

Professor Baron is a good professor but unless you're interested in minor details or a subjective view of architecture, may not be your best bet. Two tests and a few quizzes, grades attendance and appreciates participation.

Attendance is taken in every class. Lectures are kind of boring but simple. Dry sense of humor and can come off a little rude but I don't think he means to. All info is posted on blackboard. You have TWO exams total that is 90% of your grade. The other 10% is weekly quizzes... yeah. Doesn't post grades until the end.

Great professor, interesting subject (although he strays a bit too much in lectures, more modern examples would be nice). His grading made no sense IMO. Lectures were a bit dull at times, but when I look back I learned a ton and am applying it to the architecture I design.

Just a warning, there's literally a reading quiz every other (if not very single) class from like six different sources (not an exaggeration, but all the books should be about $20), plus they're pretty interesting. Some have the impression that he's a "snob," but truly he isn't; he just has a peculiar way of speaking & is always willing to help.

Went on the Honors trip to Italy and took his class. He explained everything in excruciating detail and had us out "studying" all day every day on the trip. I did everything I was supposed to, and I still got an A-. Do everything and do it well, especially the drawing. The trip is great. This professor has pretty high standards. Employ caution.
Pretentious professor and extremely tough grader.

He is not very patience and gets irritated easily. This person does not understand every student has a different strength his job is to help the student to excel . Does not want to repeat himself giving instructions or the guidelines again or simply expecifing one more time what he meant ! Mentor and Guidance come in mind but not with him!

I loved the architectural conservation class with Dupont. He makes the content so interesting and knows so much about the material. A lot of the work is based on student groups and student led discussions so if you read and understand the material, speak up and put some effort into it.

Fun engaging class to learn about the theory of preservation. I learned a lot in this class and will use this valuable knowledge gained throughout my career. He's proven to be very knowledgeable in this field and will share his opinion on any controversial matter in the current events.
Abstract yet practical. Relaxed teaching style which is nice until grades come around and you're not sure why/how you recieved it.

Professor Norouzi pushes you to strive for excellence, she is tough but fair. As long as you give your very best and are looking to improve as a designer, you will definitely benefit from having her as a professor. No other professor within this department will put more time and genuine care into their students academic journeys & future endeavors.
Her class was one of the hardest classes I took but it got me in the right mindset for grad school.

I have taken Professor Norouzi both in my undergraduate and graduate studies. She always pushes her students to go past their limits, which is why I enjoyed taking her. The design style she promotes is research based, where every decision needs to have a backed up reason. If you want an easy A she is not the one. Take her class if you want to grow.

I consider this course to be one of the most challenging in my graduate program at UTSA, but it set a high standard for my expectations for every project afterwards. The professor is highly knowledgeable. Beyond the classroom, she goes above and beyond to help students gain experience. Overall, a great professor and a harsh course.

Dr. Neda Norouzi was an excellent instructor for Studio focused on  Healthcare. She is highly knowledgeable in healthcare architecture and consistently provided valuable research resources that strengthened our design work. Her guidance created a strong, research-driven learning environment that greatly enhanced the quality of our projects.

Sometimes asks "guess what I'm thinking" questions in class, but his courses are easy and light on reading. Lectures are 10/10, absolutely no notes, incredible teacher. There isn't much to say... he's good at what he does. Fair grader, knowledgeable about Shakespeare, good fun in class, and big assignments aren't hard.

He will absolutely make sure literally every person in his class gets a good grade on every assignment and test, come hell or high water, no matter what. His lectures can be shaky but trust him and youll pass every test with flying colors. You get an attendance grade and the midterm + the final are most of the grade. Reading comprehension quizzes.

If you take notes during lectures, read/watch all the plays, and review the notes and powerpoints, you should do excellent on the quizzes and midterms. And for the final essay, you get to choose your topic. The professor likes for his students to participate during lectures, so try to participate if you can. (all plays are free online)
So much reading, not really enough time to absorb modules if you didn't want to fall behind, though to be fair it was a fast-paced class. Some extra credit. I'd go for another teacher.

Sometimes he would post entire modules due within the day with no warning. Only two exams that are 50% of the grade. I got a 100 on almost everything, but since I got 80s on the exams my grade was lower. I did everything (even not required stuff) and still was quizzed on stuff I didn't learn. Only got feedback when I emailed.
Find any other professor to take this class with. Spends more time threatening your grade than actually teaching the course material.

He crams you with information every week. With a quiz each Friday, only 10 questions (10 minutes) on anything you learned that week. It was hard to get ahead, as he grades heavily. His quizzes are from the videos so get ready to take lots of notes. He doesn't give you an outline to help you study. His SI helped. There was not much guidance on study

Luckily the final was not cumulative and just covered the last couple chapters. Lots of homework. Tons. Chapter reading, several video lectures, and primary source readings given each week... all of which are tested on. Sometimes the teacher will refute information in textbook so definitely don't forget to watch the lectures.

recentReviews.comment: I've never felt so defeated, disappointed, and stressed in all my college years. Professor Clinton is just awful, unbearable, unprofessional, and unethical. Her feedback is vague and inconsistent. God forbid you ask for clarification or correct her because she will retaliate with bad grammar and outright threaten to lower your grade. HIS3023

Reads from a manuscript her lectures so it feels like you are in first grade being read a story. Power Point lectures dont match the lecture and dont add to the assignments but are mandatory. Grading is confusing and unclear. Three books were mandatory but I only used two and one of these two I only used one chapter.

Get ready to read multiple books that are required by her. cruel at grading and harsh. the most minimal mistake on a paper will get you an F. Heavy lectures with little directions. she uses a lot of exclamation points when addressing the class. way too much homework.

Clinton is by far the worst professor I have ever had. She is incredibly vague when describing her standards for assignments, but expects work to fit her specific criteria. Attempts to clarify will often fall flat as she does not respond to emails or the like. She is very rude to students and attempts to embarrass them in front of classmates.

Don't take a class with this professor. Please don't. She is very rude and does not teach well. Classes were very dry and boring. Couldn't even see my grade until the week of finals. I felt belittled frequently as well. Do yourself a favor and take this class with another professor.

Professor doesn't teach. You have to read through slides and learn from those, yet they are almost identical to slides from the previous cyber class so you won't learn much. Labs were canceled and instead our grade relied on large papers that felt unnecessary. Getting an A isn't hard but I felt like I wasted my time in this course.

It wasn't the best experience. Grades inconsistently and doesn't even grade according to the rubric, implying bias as a means for grading which defeats the purpose of having a rubric in the first place.

This class was such a waste of time. Dr. Rutherford doesn't teach you anything about cyber security. The way he grades papers is insane, worse than any writing class you've ever taken. His pretentious personality shows through his emails and feedback on papers. You will not benefit from anything in his class. It's all useless busywork.

Prof Rutherford is not very interactive, but as long as you watch the lectures and do the assignments on time you'll pass his courses easily. Unlike many CS courses, there is no programming projects, but you are expected to write several papers throughout the semester, most of them are fairly easy as long as you understand the material.

Dr. Rutherford has high expectations for his students while giving minimal effort. This class was entirely online and consisted mostly of reading through the previous instructor's slides. Be prepared for arbitrary points off such as him failing to actually use the plagiarism checker or just because he doesn't care for your particular writing style.

Great professor for any data science oriented course. Main portion of the total grade is the group project which you need to focus on the most. Really helps making each lecture and tool for data management very easy, esp. to use for the project. Take her!!
I got a job offer on the basis of the project done in Dr. Arora's class. This is an excellent class to build practical data management skills.
Just ok
Changed the project scope so it became a ton more work at the end of the spring 2021 semester.

We have received only 1 homework so far. 10% of the grade is based on a quiz, 20% is based on two assignments, and 70% is based on a group project selected with the approval of Prof. Arora. This is a great class. I usually do not leave reviews for professors but seeing a false review about "Lots of Homework" I thought to set the record straight.

Only a half dozen homework assignments, and three tests, though final is optional. Some extra credit opportunities. Lectures aren't super engaging, but she does a good job at simplifying otherwise complex concepts. Tests are also fair, and as long as you attend class and understand the homeworks you'll do fine.

Professor Xie mainly uses the lectures and powerpoint slides to teach the class, however most of the grade is determined by the tests. There are two tests. Neither the lectures nor the slides go into deep insight on the topics covered on the tests and reading was "very lightly" reccomended, there was no guidelines on what to study for tests.

Xie as in "see". Decent amount of homework and 2 coding projects this semester. She has knowledge and the concepts are applicable to industry. She is a tough grader on tests which are hard. She allows a cheatsheet for exams, which she had us turn in with the tests without warning. Appreciates attendance but not required.

Besides sometimes wishing we'd spent more time on some topics over others, I really enjoyed the class and felt things were very fair. She's really good about answering questions, clarifying material, and setting realistic expectations about exams. Sounds like she's changed the class since previous semesters after feedback to make it better.

This class is test-heavy, 50% of grades from midterm and final. Surprisingly, failing exams won't prevent an A. On my first exam, got 20. Prof curved all grades above 70. Same with final. Do all homework, attend pop quiz, and you can't fail the class. Highly recommend this professor!

Pretty straightforward introduction to C. Reading both the zyBook chapters along with his provided slides make the content easy to digest. Really nice to have a professor you can email and give you feedback on your code for assignments, projects, etc. Make sure to always start projects early as they can be a bit difficult.
This is an easy class that teaches C. The zybook will help you alot but don't slack on projects. You will have 3 and the second one is kind of hard. Otherwise should be an easy A.
Dr. Gao is a very good professor. Knows his stuff.

professor Gao was pretty hard. He doesn't seem to care that 99% of the class is only there for a science credit. the tests were extremely difficult and I'm confident saying I learned nothing. If you're looking for an "easy" science credit, 100% do NOT take this class.

I took Remote Sensing with Dr. Xie and gained a wealth of new skills for my project, his deep expertise shines through every lecture, and the hands-on exercises introduced me to powerful tools and techniques I hadn't encountered before. Dr. Xie's clear explanations and real-world examples made complex concepts accessible. Great class, learned a lot

I took him Fall 2022 and got a B. It's a difficult course but it's very straightforward and you receive all the tools you need to succeed. Professor Xie is very helpful and he had knowledgeable TAs, there was one presentation we had to do on a major project. Overall he's a good professor.
Very unclear.   Tests are hard to follow and don't seem to follow the course.

Dr. Xie is a tough nut.  It is extremely difficult to understand him, he uses class time to lecture about things that are easily looked up elsewhere, and he lies about funding for students.  If you take his classes, plan for LOTS of your own time to figure out what's going on. If you're his student, find your own funding.
Good professor. DO THE SMARTBOOK ASSIGNMENTS!!!! and you will be good. Tests are easy if you attend lecture and actually do the smartbook hw.

Underrated professor on here. He can be lecture heavy and have overwhelming topic. He does like to apply concepts to real life. However, grading set up is very favorable to us. He wants everyone to do well and I do 100% recommend to take him. Just be ready to read the textbook. He is very passionate about what he teaches.

I really learned a lot from his class and he explained all his assignment guidelines very clearly. He also could work with your schedule and if you needed a small extension on something, he was able to accommodate.

His tests are all online and as long as you go to class and answer the clicker questions, you will do fine.The clicker questions matter as they effect your grade so don't blow them off.  He drops your lowest test grade. Basically his tests come from the homeworks and iclicker questions. I actually enjoyed his lectures and he is funny!
Online Lecturing was good. Could've been worse, underrated on here

Graduate lvl Principles of Molecular bio. 2nd lecturer. Everyone failed the practice exam question. Lectures are good but the exam questions are confusing. 5 Qs written, open note, but it doesn't help. He wants very specific things and takes points off for not mentioning exact things he wants. He is kind and knowledgable, but so unbelievably tough.

This is an extremely difficult course. Dr. Hermann teaches it at a graduate level for sure. I would recommend taking only if you see yourself as a future PhD in Mol Bio or an oncologist. Exams are half M.C. and half free response. The book was horrific (Lewin's Essential Genes). 1st exam was over half the book. I'm not kidding. Good luck
Dr. Hermann is a VERY good teacher. He is the coolest, nicest, and funniest professor I've had! Defiantly one of my favorite professors at UTSA! :)

You can't understand him. He speaks super fast and mumbles. His lecture slides only have figures from the textbook and random websites. The quizzes are only 2 written questions with each being 5 points, but he does give partial credit. Just study his slides and don't bother with the textbook. He uploads lecture slides after class

Vague, not helpful when asked questions, breezes thru PPT slides, no info on slides. Exam didn't fully resonate with what was addressed on his lecture + when asked "whats best to not focus much on" for his exam, was told "IDK, Good luck on the exam". I'm an A-B student + did amazing on all other courses the same semester so this is a him problem.

Professor does not seem to care for the success of his students. No EC, dropped HW or exams. There is so much material in each chapter its difficult to predict what you'll be tested on. Tests were difficult and there is no guide to help with studying. Your best bet is to review the HW questions.

He is a nice professor, the class is a little boring. There are only exams and then small 10 minute easy group assignments every so often, so make sure you're present as much as you can for class. He does not give any exam reviews so the exams are lowkey HARD in comparison to the vague power points he goes over. Didn't hate the class, didn't enjoy.

Dr. Lee is a nice guy, but I solely relied on the textbook to study for exams, and his lecture slides weren't the best. He took attendance daily, but I don't think it was graded. Random in-class group quizzes, so showing up to class is important. He gave a generous grade boost at the end that was equal to a letter grade, so that was really nice.
I took her for Principles of Microbiology. Amazing class. Not too difficult. You'd be doing yourself a disservice by not taking this class.

Took this class online during COVID. Dr. Hung is a great prof. She really does try her best to engage her students. Study her slides and you will be set for her exams (5 of them, they get progressively harder)

Dr. Hung is very passionate and dedicated towards ensuring you receive the best microbiology experience. Dr. Hung has 5 exams which you have to read the textbook to make a good grade, but also provides practice questions for her exams. I would say towards test 3 and 4 to study more because immunology is difficult to grasp at first glance.
Study for the tests and go to class because of pop quizzes

Dr. Hung is really great, she's really enthusiastic and wants everyone to succeed. You will need to study for her exams and always be going over previous lectures because she gives pop quizzes as attendance. Theres an extra credit project towards the end of the semester that can really help you.

He is super nice & I really enjoyed the class. I had to study outside of class at least 20 hours before any test because each test is a cumulative one page-double sided exam where it is all free response and half involves drawing a molecular interaction. Also he has in class assignments every class for attendance, sometimes they're pop quizzes.
Would not recommend taking any classes with this professor

Prof SCL is a great person, but he lectures as if he were speaking to PhD students, expecting you to know any and all background information. The test average for my class was a 70 EVERY test and no extra credit or curves are given. I always felt prepared for his tests then left the room feeling horrible. Take someone else if possible.

Dr. Lee is a decent professor. Quizzes are worth 40% of your grade & Exams are 60%. He drops your 2 lowest quizzes & your lowest exam grade. HOWEVER. His exams are tough only because he gives you an hour & 15-20 minutes to complete 48+ questions w/ half being free-response & a third of those having multiple parts. You have to be able to type fast.

The participation quiz assignments given after each lecture are a large portion of the grade, so as long as you stay on top of the reading it's an easy A. His exams and homework questions are very straightforward from his lectures and slides. Fast turnaround on grading.

The exams are pretty much straight from the powerpoint lectures that he goes over in class, which can make the course easy to follow. While the material isn't easy, an A is doable as long as you study the powerpoints and participate in the group activities at the end of class.

Great professor, interesting lectures. 2 iclicker quizzes per class and he drops the lowest one at the end of the semester. There's also groupwork at the end of every class. 3 tests and a final, but the final is optional: he'll take the average of your 3 tests and that'll be your final exam grade.

Env. Law was more organized than the assessment class :/. The 2nd exam we had in-class review that was hard to follow, group project had no rubric! Some classes attendance was taken and some weren't, he sometimes didn't show up. Overall this class was disorganized! & DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK (I miss my $30)

He is very knowledgeable about environmental law, however, he rambles a lot and often about things that are not important to the exams. It often felt like class was not helping me learn, as I learned most of the content from the book and study guides.

Great professor, he's very intelligent and experienced in Environmental Law. His lectures can be a little slow, but Thompson is a really likable guy and the material isn't challenging if you apply yourself and read a little. Definitely recommend.

Professor Thompson definitely takes participation seriously. Would not recommend him to any introverts! Course work is very easy, quizzes every week are good grade boosters! Old school style lectures, and tests in person. Don't think his style is for everyone but if you enjoy discussion this is definitely the prof for you.

If you don't make an 'A' in this class there is actually something wrong with you. Best old school styled lecturer there is, read a chapter from the book and the discuss it in class, Exams are just like the exam review and there's some writing assignments. only 6 items in the grade book lol. Also shoutout the TA Stephani man she was a real one fr.

No homework graded, only exams. Very difficult class. Not very nice either.

If you think his class is hard then you may want to change majors. His class was a breeze compared to other instructors. Exams were so easy I barely studied. it very hard

Honestly one of the best math professors I have ever had. Although tests are weighted heavily, they are not difficult if you show up for class and take time out for your day to study. He always says "You can't win a marathon by watching others do it, you must practice yourself". Communication was iffy sometimes but most likely covid related.

He's was my college algebra for scientist professor last spring before covid happened. I took a 3 hour lecture per week and they were enjoyable! If you plan on going down the computer science or engineering route, I definitely recommend taking his class!

All homework and midterms are online, while the final is in person. Attending the lectures seemed to not teach me much, only a few points being made in over an hour. I'm not sure if he always does this but the final consisted of writing your own questions and proving you understood the concepts (we were given 4 blank sheets of paper, open note).

I personally did not like his teaching style, however I do think he's a great professor and I enjoyed learning about physics. Overall great just not my style

I would not recommend him to anyone. Although he's nice and seems to know what he's doing, he does not know how to teach. From the beginning, he expects you to know already what he's talking about and will rarely explain his steps. The final was very confusing and essentially required you to create the questions. Essentially, don't take this class.

Professor Chen is very educated and knows a lot about his field of study. However, he is not good at explaining concepts, and it is very easy to get lost in his lectures since he does not explain any idea or concept and instead just starts deriving formulas without telling us why he is doing what he is doing.

The class is super easy. Tests are online and based on HW questions, and final is open note. HW isn't too tedious either. His lectures are pretty engaging as he's a nice, funny guy but its hard to follow what he's saying. He's not good at explaining concepts. Easy to pass but I didn't actually learn a lot besides memorizing formulas & procedures.

The jokes aside, he's a cool professor. He explains things okay. He does lectures on Excel, the textbooks he provides are outdated but can help, and the open-book tests can be really hard. Each point is worth A LOT and you have to show work and do the problems carefully, but you can manage to pass. Thank you SHARAD (ACCOUNTING).

After taking SHARAD (ACCOUNTING)'s class, I am now making $4.3 billion per year eliminating overhead costs for a major firm. Thank you SHARAD for teaching me everything I know, even things Dave Ramsey hasn't discovered.
SHARAD (ACCOUNTING) is very accounting
I expected no less from the Minister of Accounting.

Graded on 4 tests, attendance, and 1 homework assignment. The tests were completely openended, but he doesn't show you how to do all the problems. I had to teach myself this course and barely managed. There was barely any teaching sometimes, just mindless excels that didn't teach you everything. I was frustrated constantly, don't take if you can.

Most of the class is run by his TA, and he changes the syllabus constantly. The syllabus itself is very confusing and often worded weirdly. Nearly every single assignment is group work so it can be a hassle.

Professor Beebe was rude, changed assignments last minute, and loaded on a heavy course work that took up all of my time. By the end of the semester I was utterly exhausted and didn't even care if I passed the class, I just wanted out.

This class is an elective. DO NOT take this class. She gives little to no directions and expects you to already know everything. She has an attitude most of the time and is rude. Labs are very hard and she doesn't provide enough material to be able to complete them. She does not teach at all. I dropped the minor bc of this class.

The worst professor I have taken at UTSA. Unorganized and always made revision a day or same day of due date yet accuses students of having "bad time management". Does not teach. PowerPoints and quizzes does not make sense. She expects everyone to know how to use the tools needed for the labs. No clear instructions nor answers to your questions.

Professor Beebe is extremely unorganized and her wording on the Labs and Quizzes is awful to say the least. Constantly is changing and updating the labs last minute after most of the class has already turned the lab in, and is unable to complete it. The quizzes have horrible wording as well. Really would not recommend her as a professor.

Took her for online and I must say the worse class I have ever taken! Most of her powerpoints are not made by her, no clear explanations or directions, everything is mostly self taught or from the textbook. Unhelpful and outdated materials when it comes to downloading the required software, labs always had an issue that got fixed last minute.

Great professor, very straightforward with the criteria. No assignments, only 6 quizzes (one dropped), extra credit for class activities, and 3 exams. Exams are exact examples used in class and very simple, not tricky questions. Lectures are decently interesting, and notes are allowed to be used on the quizzes.

she is an amazing teacher! my class with her was a hybrid so you do have to watch the lectures but she does also go over them and do some experiments regarding the lectures in class. there are many opportunities for extra credit in the class based on attendance so GO TO THE CLASSES. very accomodating for mental heath, just have notation for it.
Lectures are boring, if you miss class you'll probably be missing a quiz. and if you're late she probably wont count you present.

Love her! She's super sweet and she explains the concepts in a way you understand (at least for me). Tests are easy because they are all based on her powerpoints, so if you just watch her videos, you'll be good. We take quizzes as well as get plenty of extra credit opportunities if you attend class. There's no reason to fail this class.
Easy A. Just watch lectures and you will do ok. Lectures can be kind of long but nothing too bad.

I like Dr. Lewis but his class is confusing. He never had his assignments on canvas so you wouldn't know when the due date was. You had to send him the assignment through email, which sometimes he would see your email but forget about it and you had to resend. His tests are kinda difficult but you get a cheat sheet and can argue for extra points.

Professor Lewis was my favorite professor for the Spring 2025 semester. Our course was made up of module quizzes and 3 tests. We had group mini projects throughout the year and our final was a group project. His lectures were entertaining and the textbook he used was free. The best part was we were able to "fight" for points back on tests in class!

Take literally any other professor. He creates his own exams despite using the book for chapter quizzes. Never know what to expect to be on the exam because he can make up any question he wants. The highest grade someone got on an exam was 88. I show up to class every day and study, He is an awful professor, judgmental. He thinks he hung the moon.

The professor himself was a cool guy. Chapter quizzes are done thru Pearson & not loaded to Canvas until the end of the semester(just the average). He made the exam questions himself, so the tests were tough. Gave the study guide the week of(2 days to study). Doesn't teach anything from the book. Shows favoritism. BIG on the group project.

He is by far the worst professor I have ever had. His lecture videos have to be watched multiple times because of all the 'uhs' 'ums' and long tangents that don't pertain to the video. The quizzes are very hard, he wants you to think exactly like him. He has you read wall street journal articles that are pointless. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!!!!!

She is very accessible outside of class, responded quickly to emails and text

AWESOME TEACHER... I loved her class(Cultural/Lng Div-Plurastic Soc) ... This class is easy and there is a lot of class interaction,,, VERY INTERESTING PROFESSOR and SUPER SUPER SMART and very open minded... I WOULD RECOMMEND HER and wish I could take her class again...

Took this class in a 5 wk summer course, and I didn't have any interest in the subject matter.  After taking Dr. Sanchez she truly opened my eyes with the interesting class discussions & her intense knowledge. She is a great instructor and really cares about her students-she learned all of our names (about 40+) in a 5 week course! Would take again!
Awesome professor! I dreaded taking this class, but ended up really enjoying it:-) She is very helpful and all around good person. If you have to take this class, take it with her!

Dr. Sanchez is a fantastic professor! I thoroughly enjoyed taking her qualitative research class. She is very knowledgable and professional. Gives great feedback in timely fashion. I highly recommend her:)
I would take her again if I could.
Dr. Duffey was an awesome professor, very receptive and willing to discuss issues openly with students.  It has been a really fun class considering the material can sometimes be quite dry.
Great Lady & a phenomenal prof.
Dr. Duffey is a phenomenal professor.  She exhibits a genuine interest in her student's learning.  She has a wealth of knowledge and is willing to share.
Extremely knowledgable and helpful. Very interesting professor, with a wealth of experience in counseling practice and in teaching. Highly recommended!

The classes are very engaging Prof. Bhaganagar makes the subject very interesting. The exams are very manageable and as long as I followed the class notes and homework, it was ok. She is very concerned about the students and she answers any questions with care and respect. It is very important to attend the classes as she does a lot in the class.

I am taking fluids with Dr. Bhaganagar. I love her lectures and her teaching style. She gives plenty of examples to practice. I am liking fluids a lot after this class. She knows the subject really well and that makes a lot of difference.
Professor Bhaganagar is the laziest and most disorganized professor in the entire department. I did not learn anything from her lectures

Her class prepared to tackle problems in real life. She gives students lot of confidence to tackle problems step-by-step. I can say that good students who are serious about learning like her class and find it useful. THose who want to get through it like other UTSA classes might find it demanding.

Nothing positive to say about Bhaganagar............. She doesn't care, period. She is proud of her horrible research and brags about empty data............ I have talked to previous students in her lab and there is no positive comments......AVOID! If you plan to do any fluids class take Combs or Finol, they do care
She is literally the best. The course is hard, but she works hard to make sure that you are on the right track.

Super nice!! She's very approachable and wants to help you pass. Tests do require studying but she tries to give you hints as to what's on the test. Keeps class fun and makes you want to come to class. YAY! I would take her 10 times again! One of the best professors I've had yet and plan on taking her for Relationships!

If only there were more profs like Dr. Weston! Crystal clear lectures. She follows a PowerPoint with all the notes you need & waits for everyone to finish writing before moving on. You need the textbook, but she'll tell you which sections you need to know for tests. Very friendly, accessible, & her lectures are always interesting! AWESOME prof :)

She is a great teacher!, she applies the stuff you learn here in class, to real world problems, and solutions. She is helpful, and the class is easy to follow. it odes require some work, specially reading wise, but she makes the effort to connect concepts, so that its a easy grade. Will recomend
I took her this past spring. I thought she was outstanding. She loves what she teaches, and she does her best to get the class involved. TAKE THIS CLASS.

This class has a point system of 3 exams (x50pts), and 5 pop quizzes (x3pts - only 4 count) for a total of 162pts. There were 6pts of extra credit available. Some of the exam content is online, but the pop quizzes are a pain and are open ended so it's hard to get full credit. It's not worth it IMO, take couple and family w/ Dr. Scott instead 10/10.

You have to take as many classes as you can with her. She loves to teach, take advantage of her knowledge and ask a lot of questions. Book helps for the exams, they require some thinking but are not there to trick you. Read carefully and don't overthink the questions. I used the free PDF Book of the previous edition than she required and got an A
Dr. Morrisette is very nice and smart! She is also very easy to talk to. This class is not easy but if you work hard you can get an A.
Dr. Morrisette is so smart and has so much knowledge on this topic! she is also very understanding and easy to talk to. But this class is not easy so be prepared to work for an A!

Dr. Hum is an awesome professor who really encourages participation/discussion in class. There are lots of extra credit opportunities so make sure to take advantage of that! She replies to emails very quickly. I feel like the old negative reviews don't reflect her accurately. Also, dedicate enough time for her class and you'll do well.

Dr. Hum is incredibly supportive. As far as your writing goes, prepare for a major upgrade. I've never written more clearly and I've been at this for 6.5 years. There are so many pluses to working with Dr. Hum, including the breadth of her courses. The camaraderie I've been able to take part in thanks to her seminar is unbeatable.

Dr. Hum is a super nice and kind lady. I'm not sure why she has a couple negative reviews on here because my experience with her was overwhelmingly positive. Yes, you have to do the work to get a good grade, but college isn't supposed to be a cake walk. If you manage your time well and ask questions when you need clarity, you'll be okay.

I took professor Hum during Summer I. She's very nice and doesn't mind answering any questions you have! I bugged her a lot when it came to our essays.  You have to be lazy to not pass her class. Show up, do the online discussions, write the EASY topic essays, and you're good. Open book quizzes were plus!!!! I would love to take her again!

she is really good at teacbhing rather than reading off of the slides

Where have I been?  Dr. EF must be great in classroom, but glad it was at least possible to hear and see him online.  What a voice!. This is an easy A, with many extra credit opportunities.

Overall, I enjoyed her class. The work was fairly easy and you have time to dot it. There is 3 projects, which 2 were in groups and one was a volunteer project on your own. She made the class feel very comforting and she's understanding and easy to talk to. I definitely recommend her!

I took her for Consumer Health, she is an amazing professor and very kind. Her class is very student friendly, paced well, and has assignments that encourages critical thought. I would highly recommend you take her; you are missing out if you do not take her. Her course was lots of fun, and I would highly recommend.

Professor Bradford is one of the best professors I've had at UTSA. Her class wasn't difficult at all. Assignment load is very minimal. Besides a weekly discussion all we had was 1 very easy project and we were able to use that for our final. I would highly recommend taking her as a professor, she was amazing.

Professor Bradford is passionate, inspiring, kind, understanding, and compassionate. I took her special studies in health course, and it was very educational, relevant, and inspiring. You won't regret taking one of her classes.

Professor Bradford is one of the best professors. I signed up for this class on accident but fell in love with public health once I started class. She is very knowledgeable & passionate abt public health. Lots of extra credit & assignments are very straight-forward. Attendance is not mandatory, lectures are always exciting & she is very funny.

Awesome professor! She made lectures fun. This is an intro class so she does an amazing job of explaining public health. She is really big on participation so be sure to participate. Overall an amazing course and professor.

The amount of reading for a simple 5-10 question quiz was absurd. The outdated online lectures that were given to us through PowerPoint and the "class project" were confusing. Emails were not answered for up to a week, multiple times when hw was not opened on time, the instructor was oblivious until she finally read and responded to the emails.

Great teacher overall. Sometimes she doesn't know how to explain her thoughts, but she always gives reviews & is very fair. I would just shorten the test criteria, studying 13 chapters for one test is a bit much. She also takes very long to grade. A project took 3 months to grade.

Had everything we needed for each chapter when we needed it. She also responded to emails fairly quickly, which with an online class I believe is a major plus! Overall great class, enjoyed all the extra materials given for the chapters and the quizzes really prepped you for the exams.

She's really nice if you need her to answer questions, emails or personal situations which she can help. She has a bad rep but she's a good professor and person. Try to ask her questions when confused instead of talking bad about her. Cross read between book and power points. Third time taking her as the professor.

I took her this summer (2015) for the first summer session online and it was a pretty easy class. I did not have any problems and we had an homework assignment every week with homework every week as well. I believe we also had a quiz every week too, but for a summer course it was clear and I got an A.
Super easy class, I got an A. I think its pretty hard to fail this class. We do get a group project and with it being no set time it can be tricky to get ahold of everyone in your group.

I had him for Health Care System online and I got an A. There should be no reason you should not get an A as long as you do your work and follow the instructions. However, the course you teach yourself and he does not respond if you reach out to him. The course is still easy but there is a group project that he grades a little tough.

very easy class as long as you show up. he cares about student wellbeing and sometimes will have extra credit for coming to class or give out quiz/test answers in class. There are some group projects, and it can suck if you have nonresponsive group members, but they aren't too hard as long as you can write and decently understand research articles.

His expectations and deadlines for group project work are not well-explained. It was difficult to know when things were exactly due, and his assignments were confusing. He never responded to my emails :/. Quizzes started off weekly and then became biweekly, you can use the slides for them and they are pretty easy but timed. Same goes for the exams
He cares about his students wellbeing, his class is easy. I would take again 100%

She is very clear on her expectations: read and prepare notes before class begins and actively participate in discussions. LOVES group projects, she makes all of her classes do one every term. She genuinely enjoys seeing participation over memorization or knowledge of content. She brought guest speakers and made this class very interesting.

The best professor I have ever taken. Her classes are tough but she helps you rise to the ocassion. The structure of the class is also great with weekly assignments and you're working the whole semester on what's going to end up being your final paper. Highly recommend!!

Awesome prof! There are weekly quizzes on readings (has freebies). Clear on paper requirements and there's also a neat research project. She provides fast, easy-to-understand feedback. One of the readings is her book 'Durable Ethnicity', which is a qualitative study, super interesting especially if you're into qualitative methods. Highly recommend!

She is new and that shows, but she is enthusiastic and clearly loves talking about anthropology. There was a lot of homework, but it was easy and was consistent throughout the semester. She was kind and easy to talk to if you need it.

You will need to buy a vantage textbook to complete all your assignments for this class, so just beware of that. Otherwise, her lectures were easy to follow and would help in the quizzes from the textbook. She does take attendance so keep that in mind. Overall a pretty easy course, and there aren't any exams just weekly quizzes.

Teacher is kind of nice. I asked questions through email. She and I had discussed a project. Other students had trouble with the project. She told me I was impatient and counted off one of my grades by 15 pts for asking questions.

Loved taking her Cultural Anthropology class! Took Fall 2023, Prof. Trevino is super nice! Had assignments that actually related to the course and that were easy, along with lectures that very clearly covered the material. Great choice if you're focused in anthropology or if you just need a core social/behavioral science!

She is the best professor. Super young and super sweet, really easy class. The weekly online quizzes were a little bit difficult but only 10 were mandatory all semester. Final project was easy and she brought food. Love her! Take her if possible. Super understanding.
Yesss i love her! Loved biological anthropology and her research on primates was fascinating. Very kind and sweet
shes very cutesie and its suchh an easy class

Loved taking bio anthropology with professor Lucci! She clearly demonstrates interest in the subject and loves sharing pictures and information from her own fieldwork working with primates, which I found very interesting. The class is quite easy especially if you're interested in the subject or if you have background knowledge. I would recommend.

She was a good professor overall but had trouble with grades. I had an 89.99 and she stated on the syllabus that she would round it and never did, so I received a B+. I emailed her twice and never responded to me in regards to the grade. I didn't think it was fair.

She's an amazing professor and is really passionate about anthropology!! She gives out a ton of extra credit as well so her class is basically impossible to fail unless you don't study. She gives out a weekly online assignment but they're not hard, shouldn't take more than an hour to complete for the normal ones. Take her!!

It was hard to get work done because the class spoke over him everyday. We had two quizzes every week, 3 tests, 3 speeches, and a group project. We were constantly confused by the instructions, test questions, and assignments. He is easy to contact outside of class but isn't understanding. If you do the weekly reading and quizzes you'll do fine,

The work load was fair. Very understanding if life happens and things are turned in late, you have to communicate. His notes are simply and lets you know the important information. He is also a very interactive teacher, class discussion are always encouraged in this course. He makes this course very engaging and fun to learn. P.S very funny.
I loved having him! He felt as present as a face-to-face professor would be. I also appreciate how unbiased he is.

Was a decent professor and did updates every Monday, which is nice.Tends to be a bit passive in the discussion boards but I think it helps with critical thinking about the subjects that are talked about. Also replies fast to emails but again a little blunt/ passive when replying.
Great Professor for 3083 Theory it was not listed as one of his classes but I took it online.  I would recommend to anyone who needs this course.

Cabrera will call you out in front of the class abt not turning something in. However, that's the vibe of his class, he builds a strong connection and makes everyone feel comfortable in class. Uses funny jokes, fun activities, and when the speeches roll in, they don't stop until the end of the semester, but they are easy if you follow his outlines.

This was an 8 week course so each week you had doubled the quizzes. Questions were easy (questions and answers straight from the book, which you would think was easy but many right answers were marked wrong!! Easy course but be alert. Takes like 4-5 days to answer emails.

Course was "Editing". We did no editing & learned no copyediting processes. In the syllabus it indicated what you might expect, but in reality it was more like graphic design & a commercial for Adobe - we used InDesign, XD, & Audition. We were also required to hand code a web page. Emails went unanswered and assignments cancelled last minute.

Professor Jim Dalglish is super caring, very funny, and passionate about teaching. He is really understanding if you miss class due to illness or a flat tire -- life happens! He even lets you email him assignments (like speech outlines and essays). However, it is a public SPEAKING class, so attendance and participation are essential.
Took her museum fundamentals class, many students didn't like her but I personally thought she was nice. The lectures are lengthy but the assignments are so easy. Just be respectful.

Kindof boring, she reads from the textbook so... its pretty straight forward. The reviews are a bit broad so be prepared to study a bit more for the quizzes. Other than that its pretty easy, quizzes are pretty easy, I forgot to study a few times and got A's. But there's a new extra cred opportunity every class! Great professor though!

She has a monotone voice, she changes the slides way too fast, but she does post the powerpoints on Blackboard. Quizzes every two weeks over the chapters discussed in class. You also have to go to the museum to write an essay over a piece of art. I feel like she singles out some students; don't be late/use your laptop. Will call you out for those!

three tests, two papers, one project, and three in-class activities. VERY strict no phone & laptop policy. lectures are hard to sit through, but if you talk to her one-on-one she's actually nice. I talked to her when i was not happy with a grade I received on a few different assignments and she changed them no problem. takes attendance every class.

The class itself might be interesting with a different professor. She speaks with a very heavy accent that might make it hard to understand her and not only that, she is very monotone. Which lead to me falling asleep for most of her class. The tests she give are not hard, and even let us use our notes. fairly easy class if you do notes on your own.

Took her class as my first English class for my degree, she's so sweet, a little awkward but I feel all English people usually are. It's very hard to fail her class as she actively tries to help all her students; provides extensions when needed and zoom calls if you can't make a lecture, so super accommodating. Great reading selections as well.
She cares so much and is so considerate of her students! read some great texts both popular & more niche. love her!

Prof Bradley is great at teaching and always comes prepared for her lectures. I will say that her lectures lacked engagement meaning that some of her lectures were boring sometimes. However, she is passionate about her field and gives great feedback on assignments. There are around 3 short essays and a lot of discussion posts, which were also short
She is one of the nicest professors I ever had, such a sweet person who loves to expand your knowledge on literature. Gives amazing feedback and is clear with assignments!

She is such a sweet professor, the kindest I have ever had! She is a grad student professor so while her availability outside of class may vary she is so quick to get back to anyone! She also provides very detailed feedback for each assignment. I would absolutely take this professor again! No required textbooks she provides the pieces to you.

she allows people to use AI which makes no sense for a decolonial/postcolonial theory professor. she gets annoyed when the class doesn't know new topics, and instead of lecturing, has us google it(or use AI..). going to this class feels like a humiliation ritual. she has a very confusing/strict grading rubric.
Don't take if you like structure and clarity.

This professor is fine if you know exactly what she wants for an assignment, as she really only grades your aptitude with MLA formatting. Unfortunately, understanding what she wants is incredibly obtuse. That fact, accompanied with her overwhelming incompetence on a technical level, makes her one of the worst professors I've had.  Stay far away.

My class had some issues with Professor Afzal, but I think going into her class understanding a few things can make it easier. There is a LOT to read, but you really need to pick a key idea and be ready to interact. Brush up on MLA and citation skills, and be ready to have your ideas challenged. That said, she knows the material and you can learn!

She is a lovely professor. She shows real care for her students and tries her best to get grades out fast and have the lectures easy to understand for all. She gives references to certain local politics or events that are well known to give an analogy that can actually be understood.

Good person, okay professor. She's kind and extremely knowledgeable, but is all over the place. Late to class, forgetting to put up assignments (or assumes it worked without double checking multiple times). Provided lecture notes but sometimes wouldn't load them up. Class structure was odd as she uploaded of modules the day before class

Fantastic and engaging professor, passionate about the topics she covers and has the experience to back up her expertise. Genuinely wants her students to succeed, and will give you constructive feedback on papers. You will need to purchase textbooks, however but you can always find them for cheap online. Overall great professor!

She is super scatter brained she has on multiple occasions assigned something then took it back. I get absolutely nothing from her lecture, she does not explain things well, has no structure and is unclear. Her BB page is messy and her tests are confusing. She gave me a bad score on my essay for using info SHE gave me. I hate this class

Do not take any of Professor Catherine Nolan-Ferrell's classes. She is a scatterbrain. Her lectures are all over the place. If you like test base class then you will like her class. She is a very unorganized professor, Scatterbrain professor. One of the worse professors I had ever taken at UTSA. How does she still have a job is beyond me?

Very sweet, the instructions for assignments aren't clear, but honestly, she doesn't really care what you submit as long as you get the general concept in your submission. Always accepts late work and encourages her students to succeed. She will send us inspirational emails sometimes lol. A lot of hw but expected for an online course.
No tests or quizzes only homework. Lots of group work and class participation. Opportunities for extra credit. Easy grader.
